News.title: Woman in her 30s ‘raped’ in GP car park as four men arrested
News.content:
'RAPE' HORROR Woman in her 30s ‘raped’ in GP car park as four men arrested







Next

FOUR men have been arrested after a woman in her 30s was “raped” in a GP’s car park.

Cops said they were quickly able to nick two 21-year-olds, a 20-year-old, and a 19-year-old following the alleged attack outside Great Western Surgery in Farriers Close, Swindon.



The suspects were currently being questioned, police said at midday on Tuesday, following the attack just after midnight.

Forensic police were at the car park on Tuesday morning and had cordoned part of it off, pictures taken by the Swindon Advertiser showed.



The GP surgery was initially closed before the cordon was reduced so the practice could open several hours later.

Detective Inspector Tom Straker said: “We recognise the concern that this worrying incident will have had in the local community.

“We were able to rapidly locate and arrest four men, two of whom are aged 21, a 19-year-old and a 20-year-old, in connection with the investigation.

“We are not currently looking for anyone else in relation to this. You may notice an increased police presence in the area. If you have any concerns, please do approach our officers.”

If you were in the area shortly after midnight, or may have recorded dash cam footage, please call 101 quoting log 54260123495.

News.title: Serial sex offender thanks Andy Burnham for letting him out as 650 lags are freed early by Labour
News.content:
Next

CRIMINALS freed early by the Government celebrated in the streets yesterday as they made their way home — and thanked Andy Burnham.

Among the 650 offenders whose release was brought forward was Arasad Azad, 66, who had previously been jailed for committing sex acts in full view of children.



He has been freed 45 days early after being sentenced to 20 months. Asked what he thought about the scheme, he punched the air and replied: “Very good. I’m happy to be released. Thanks to Andy.”

Reports show Azad, from Halesowen, West Mids, has previously been jailed for outraging public decency and was caught committing a sex act in public three times in a day.



On one occasion the offender, let out yesterday from Birmingham jail in Winson Green, was in full view of members of the public including children.

Outside Durham prison, another criminal punched the air in celebration and when asked what he thought of the early release scheme, said: “F***ing belter.”

Yesterday was the second wave of early releases. More than 5,000 lags are expected to be included in total as the Government tries to free up jail space.

Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy said: “Prisoners are cheering. Their victims won’t be.”



The Tory added that the majority of the freed lags are not being tagged.

He said in the Commons: “The Justice Secretary told the country that proper safeguards would be in place with a presumption all released prisoners would be tagged. He called it the toughest tagging regime in history, but that was nonsense.

“I have some advice for him — it is better to work out how to implement your policy before it starts, not after.



“We know a majority of prisoners are not being tagged before release, and we know reoffending is off the charts already.”

Domestic Abuse Commissioner Dame Nicole Jacobs said she is “still very concerned that protections for [domestic abuse] survivors are not fit for purpose” and added that we need to “create a justice system with victims at its heart”.

Labour says the expanded early release scheme is needed to prevent the justice system from collapsing.

Criminals are excluded from the scheme if they have been jailed for certain serious offences.

The next tranche of early releases is on November 10.

News.title: Housekeeper, 71, cleared of stealing princess’ wedding ring & other irreplaceable jewels from London home
News.content:
CLEANER CLEARED Housekeeper, 71, cleared of stealing princess’ wedding ring & other irreplaceable jewels from London home







Next

A HOUSEKEEPER has been cleared of stealing a princess’ wedding ring and other irreplaceable jewels from her home.

Jordanian Princess Firyal Irshaid, 81, left the UK during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.



While she was out of the country, part of the jewellery collection was taken and put up for sale at an auction house.

Maria Virgelina Taborda Henao, 71, was accused of stealing the items after she was left to look after the property in posh Belgravia, central London.



She has now been cleared of a charge of theft by employee at Southwark Crown Court.

The cops found the princess’ wedding ring, a pair of earrings and a jewelled metal necklace during a search of Taborda Henao’s home in Fulham, the court heard.

Taborda Henao, who is also known as Lina, gave evidence through a Spanish interpreter.

She said she had worked for 30 to 35 households, including the late businessman and peer Lord Anthony Jacobs and a Belgian countess.



Taborda Henao told defence barrister Manveer Cheema that staff found relations with the princess to be “very hard”.

The princess would sometimes accuse staff of being thieves before later calming down, jurors were told.

Princess Firyal married the younger brother of King Hussein of Jordan, Prince Muhammad bin Talal, in 1964.

Their marriage lasted 14 years.

Previously, the court had heard that her pal Pierre Jeannet, a partner at luxury jewellery maker JAR, which had made her engagement ring, called her on November 21, 2020.



“He asked: ‘Are you selling your jewellery?’ And I said: ‘No, what are you talking about?'” she said.

“He told me my ring, made specially for my engagement, was on the cover of a catalogue in an auction house.”

During the early stages of the pandemic the princess had allowed Taborda Henao’s sister to move into the property and later agreed to pay her a salary.

Taborda Henao’s nephew, Julian Ramirez, acted as a “key conduit for the sale of the stolen property,” the court heard, and transferred £17,835 to her between June 23, 2019 and November 28, 2020.

When asked if she knew any stolen items were being sold, Taborda Henao replied: “No.”



She also denied any involvement in their disappearance.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Taborda Henao had worked for the princess for 11 years.

It is thought Ramirez flew to Colombia in October 2023 while on police bail.

News.title: How Trump is facing a huge battle to save his legacy as crunch polls risk leaving him a lame duck for last two years
News.content:
Next

MILLIONS voting in US midterm polls on November 3 have a chance to send the White House a message – and look set to turn the air Democrat blue.

It will also tell the world how Republican titan Donald Trump’s latest term in the Oval Office will draw to a close over the next two years.



The stakes could not be higher for 80-year-old Trump, who risks being rendered a lame-duck President.

Should he lose control of Congress, he will face a huge battle to save his legacy and defeat bids by his enemies to even impeach him.



Congress, housed in Washington DC’s Capitol building, comprises lower chamber the House of Representatives, similar to our Commons, and upper chamber the Senate, a bit like our Lords.

All 435 seats in the former, where members represent districts within US states, are up for grabs in the latest midterms. But just 35 of the 100 Senate seats, elected by state, will be decided as elections for that chamber are staggered.

Bookies reckon the Repu­blicans’ chances of keeping their wafer-thin hold on the House of Representatives — and the legislative agenda — are near zero. The Democrats need a net gain of four seats to seize a majority.

But the battle for the Senate is far tighter, with a handful of key states likely to decide Trump’s fate.

Even losing just the House would see the President’s remarkable comeback end in bitter partisan probes, battling accusations that he and his family have enriched themselves to the tune of billions while normal Americans feel the pinch.

In 2024, Trump was elected on a promise to drive down prices, seal America’s borders and untangle the globe’s most powerful military from “forever wars” in the Middle East.



Fast-forward two years and he faces a historically low approval rating — and what was meant to be a “four to six week” war on Iran is, six months later, an embarrassing stalemate with record prices at US fuel pumps.

Headline inflation may be far lower than when Trump’s current term of office began in January last year, but prices of household basics such as coffee and minced beef have soared by nearly 20 per cent.

While Americans feel pain at the tills, the rest of the world waits for its own fallouts from the final acts of the Trump show.

Insiders fear a President neutered at home will escalate his meddling around the globe as he battles for relevance in his last days in power.

His recent easing of the Western boot on Vladimir Putin’s throat, with a deal to buy diesel equivalent to 2.25million barrels, may be just a prelude to the disruption wrought by an outgoing Trump with little left to lose. Beware an old man in a hurry.



He insists he is still a boost to the Republicans, pointing to the 2016 and 2024 elections where the party got a significant bump when he was on the ballot.

But even some of those closest to him fear the stardust has now worn off.

Yet are the Democrats blowing their shot at revenge for their humiliation in the 2024 election? Since that defeat, they have been reeling and they now stand at a crossroads — pursue the traditional centrist route or shift to the hard left to woke progressive younger voters.



Since the election of socialist New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani last year, the woke fringe has been on the march.

But their current crop of new left-wing candidates bring with them truckloads of baggage — delighting Republican strategists who feel the radical left-wingery might work in urban coastal areas but repel voters in rural and southern America.

Criss-crossing the country over the next three weeks, Trump is back on the rally circuit as he attempts to brand his party as being on the side of common sense versus extremist-captured opposition.

But the numbers would suggest the Republicans have left it too late and a Blue Wave is now heading their way. To seize control of the Senate, the Democrats must hold their Senate seats in Georgia, Michigan and New Hampshire.

They also need to turn over four states from a list of competitive ballots that includes Maine, North and South Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Alaska, Iowa and Kansas.



The pollsters have the Republicans holding South Carolina and the Democrats sweeping away the rest.

Some of the numbers currently being pushed out point to a Democrat victory in the Senate of humiliating proportions for Trump.

Data has them flipping the crucial states of Iowa and Ohio, as well as Maine — despite the latter’s long-time Republican incumbent, Susan Collins, defying the pollsters in five Senate elections over the years.

The numbers folk say deep-red Kansas is also in play for the Democrats — and Republican stronghold Texas which has not sent a Democrat senator to Washington in more than three decades. Such defeats would be a body blow to the White House and likely spark a massive backlash from the President’s own party.

But the pollsters have been very badly wrong before and many Democrats fear they are wrong again, while those in the Oval Office hope.



Republican strategists, candidates and commentators insist things are much tighter on the ground than the numbers suggest.

Polls said Hillary Clinton would defeat Trump at the 2016 election and Kamala Harris in 2024, and there is little evidence that their methods have changed.

Voter survey companies have underestimated Trump’s popularity ahead of the last three presidential elections — including the 2020 one he lost to Joe Biden — as they struggled to reach large parts of his white and male voter base.

Pollsters always promise things will be different this time, and that this time they will nail it. But you would be a fool to put too much faith in them, especially if you are a punter.

Warning signs are already there in key races such as Michigan, where progressive muslim Abdul El-Sayed was predicted to cruise to a double-digit win in the Democrats’ primary vote to select a Senate candidate but ended up scraping through by barely a mere one point margin.



If a historic trend of Democrat overperformance in pre-election polls in the US was repeated across the country, these midterms are a lot closer than the numbers guys would have you believe.

Even if the polls are out by just three points, the Republicans would hold the Senate by 52 to 48, according to broadcaster CNN.

In the House elections, pollsters are even more bullish in their opinions that the Republicans are heading for a bloody nose. That’s despite having a half-billion-dollar war chest built up to support their candidates — and a ten-seat buffer thanks to controversial redrawings of seat boundaries in a number of key states.

Key battleground House races are playing out in Arizona, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Alaska, Michigan, New Hampshire and Texas.

Tipsters and pollsters suggest the Democrats will pick up between nine to 19 seats in those contests.



Even at the lower end of expectations, that would give them 223 seats — and up to 233 at the top end of predictions.

Either would leave them with a majority in the House of Representatives — 218 seats out of 435 being the crucial number to reach.

Winning the House means seizing control of the political agenda — and congressional committees.

Not only could the Democrats block spending, they would also head up the House Oversight and Judicial Committees which have sweeping investigative powers.

Witnesses can be summoned to give evidence, documents can be turned over and those who attempt to block their inquiries can be jailed.



While publicly the White House administration are insisting they are confident the polls are wrong and they will keep their tiny majority in the House, behind the scenes their legal department is on a hiring spree.

They are tooling up for Trump’s administration, and his own family, being dragged into hand-to-hand legal combat, day in and day out, over the final two years of his latest term in office.

Most election battles end on polling day — but should the Republicans lose next month, their war in Washington will have only just begun.

Here we look at key battleground states and poll percentages so far in the fight for control of the Senate . . .



TEXAS

MOST-watched Senate race is on a knife edge.

Republican Ken Paxton has been hit by corruption claims and a public divorce.



Democrat James Talarico is struggling after claiming God is non-binary, and “white men, climate change and capitalism” are world’s biggest threats, and Texans must eat less meat.

MICHIGAN

REPUBLICANS fancy they could pinch this seat after the Democrats’ Abdul El-Sayed, a radical hard-left Muslim, beat traditional centrists to the party’s nomination.

El-Sayed is plagued by connections to extremists such as blogger Hasan Piker, who said America “deserved 9/11”, as even some of his own party despair at his past comments.

He is charismatic – but black and Jewish voters are voicing concerns, very loudly.



MAINE

A REPUBLICAN win here would all but dash Democrat hopes of seizing the Senate.

And the Democrats have had a nightmare so far.

Their original candidate, Marine veteran Graham Platner withdrew over his tattoo resembling a Nazi symbol, and claims of sexual assault.

It then emerged his replacement, Troy Jackson, had fathered kids with his second cousin.



He remains the party’s candidate.

IOWA

WHILE everyone watches Texas and Michigan, this is another must-win for the Democrats.

Their candidate hoping to bring home the win is Josh Turek.

This race may lack the star quality of more box-office battles but is said to be exceptionally close.



GEORGIA

PRETTY-boy presidential contender Jon Ossoff is the youngest current US senator at 39, but the Democrat star’s financial backing for the mid-terms dwarfs that of his Republican rival.

The Democrats are very confident of holding this seat with Ossoff on the ticket.

NEW HAMPSHIRE

THIS is an open seat after the Democrat incumbent, Senator Jeanne Shaheen stood down – and on a very good night the Republicans could flip it to red.



But only the most devout of Trump believers reckon they could have that very good night.

OHIO

DEMOCRAT Sherrod Brown has been in public office for 50 years but lost his Senate seat two years ago and wants it back.

Polls say Sherrod will squeak it but Republicans ask what he ever achieved in office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

ALASKA



THIS toss-up on the final frontier sees Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan up against Independent Dan J. Sullivan which could allow Democrat hope Mary Peltola to come through the middle.

Trump won here by more than 13 points at the last presidential election so a party loss would be tough.

News.title: Burnham must come clean about his dealings with Man City… or he risks being engulfed by the scandal himself
News.content:
Time to Man up







Next

ANDY Burnham’s relationship with Manchester City’s football cheats gets murkier by the minute.

The Prime Minister promised to come clean about his dealings with the club’s mega-rich owners after his ill-judged remark that it would be a “terrible loss” if they were kicked out of the game.



But he seems to have suffered a serious bout of political amnesia on Monday when he coughed to just one “formal meeting” with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

In fact, as we reveal today, he dined twice with him in a VIP hospitality suite before two Premier League games at the Etihad stadium.



It has also emerged that two months after the first dinner, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority — of which he was then mayor — approved a £24.5million taxpayer-backed loan to a housing venture between Manchester City Council and the club’s owners.

The PM must come clean about the full extent of his dealings with the club.



Otherwise, he risks being engulfed by the scandal himself.

On scrapheap

BRITAIN’S runaway benefits culture isn’t just a drag on economic growth, it’s a tragic waste of lives.

It is a national disgrace that our proud nation — once branded the “workshop of the world” — now has 9million Brits stuck on the jobs scrapheap.

Many were simply “written off” by successive governments as they flooded the market with cheap foreign labour.



British nationals accounted for just one in five of the increase in payroll jobs since 2014.

But the situation has been made worse by the sicknote culture gripping the country, with an estimated 300,000 people dropping out of the workforce every year.

Meanwhile, ministers demand even more foreign worker visas.

The welfare crisis is one of the biggest challenges facing the Government, according to a report by the Centre of Social Justice.

We simply cannot afford to import thousands of foreign workers while paying people to stay at home.



When will the Prime Minister give this crisis the attention it desperately needs?

Doing it for kids

WHILE the Government idles, Britain’s bosses are stepping up to help give our youngsters the future they deserve.

Companies big and small have responded with gusto to our Jobs Army crusade to tackle youth unemployment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Household names like Octopus, British Airways, Hilton Hotels and Severn Trent Water are among those providing nearly 100,000 vacancies and apprenticeship opportunities, plus 61,000 work experience placements.

Labour is still scratching its head but our Jobs Army is already on the march.

News.title: How Andy Burnham has become the ‘yeah but no but’ Prime Minister as he flip flops on issues from Russia to Brexit
News.content:
Next

U-TURN king Andy Burnham is fast becoming the Vicky Pollard of politics.

His flip-flops on a string of policy positions have left him metaphorically mouthing “Yeah, but, no, but . . . ” like the Little Britain character.



The Prime Minister’s latest about-face followed his claim on Sunday that Russia interfered with the EU referendum of 2016.

The inference to many was that the Kremlin had swayed the result.



Just 24 hours later, Downing Street was forced to clarify that the Leave vote had been “legitimate”.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: “The busiest job in Westminster is running after the PM with a dustpan and brush, sweeping up whatever he said five minutes earlier.”



Here, we look at some of his other corrections and clarifications . . .

WASPI WOMEN

CAMPAIGNING at the Makerfield by-election, Burnham pledged to “stick by the Waspi women because they deserve some recompense for the unfairness”.

Burnham said he felt “uncomfortable” when politicians were all holding up the Waspi Women’s banner and then got into government and didn’t do anything.

Some 3.6million women — who were left out of pocket after the state pension age was equalised — appeared to have discovered their white knight.



Just 24 hours later, however, his spokesman revealed Burnham now considered the £10billion compensation case was closed.

PERSONAL ALLOWANCE

AFTER winning in Makerfield, Burnham indicated that he might increase the personal tax-free allowance that has been frozen at £12,570 for five years.

Shortly before moving into No10, Burnham insisted it was “the thing I heard most on the doorsteps”.

Soon his team were frantically backpedalling. A source said the PM had shied away from making an announcement because of the cost.



A Burnham ally then added: “What he was saying is that people are feeling unheard”

DRINKING AT FOOTBALL

EVERTON fan Burnham suggested a trial on allowing football supporters to have a pint in the stands.

Describing the current drinking ban during men’s games as “discrimination”, he added: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out”.

Our leader highlighted that fans watching rugby league at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium were able to drink alcohol in the stands.



However, the idea was swiftly placed on ice after the UK Football Policing Unit warned that violence and disorderly conduct from some fans was fuelled by alcohol.

SCOTTISH INDEPENDENCE

THE PM appeared to open the door to another Scottish independence vote if there was “majority public support”. Burnham was accused by the Scottish Tories of “pulling the pin on a constitutional hand grenade”.

For more than a decade, PMs have rejected demands for a fresh referendum.

Burnham swiftly changed his mind and said a fresh poll was “off limits” after all.

REJOINING THE EU

WHEN he was fighting the Makerfield seat, Burnham insisted that “the last thing we should do right now is rerun” the Brexit arguments.



He added: “Britain will be stuck in a permanent rut if we’re just constantly arguing and people are pulling away from each other.

“It is time, surely, to bring people back together . . . ”

Then last month Burnham suggested that Britain might “go all the way” and rejoin the EU, despite Labour fighting the 2024 election pledging not to.

This week he has talked about little else — despite war in Europe and the Middle East, and a raging cost-of- living crisis.

The suspicion is that he is flirting with Brexit now to win back voters from Remainiacs who have switched over to the Greens or Lib Dems.



MANCHESTER CITY

BURNHAM triggered a huge row when he insisted he didn’t want to “lose” Manchester City’s mega-rich owners, after the club were found guilty of more than 100 financial breaches.

He added: “They have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force it is.”

Accused of political interference, No10 had to clarify that the charges against Manchester City — which the club denies — were “serious” and “there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The extent of his ties to City are still emerging. The Prime Minister had insisted he only ever had one “significant” meeting with City chief Khaldoon Al Mubarak while serving as the mayor of Manchester.

But a Sun probe today uncovers two entries in a now-deleted register of interests revealing Burnham dined twice in a luxury hospitality suite at the Etihad.

News.title: Dad killed with wife & 2 boys in ‘petrol bomb’ arson days after statement to gardai as neighbours reveal horror screams
News.content:
Next

A FATHER who died along with his wife and two of their children in a suspected petrol bomb attack had recently made a statement to gardai.

Philip English reported that his car had been set alight, The Irish Sun can reveal.



Innocent Philip, 50s, wife Kim 30s, and two of their sons, Callum, 12 and Jayden, nine, died after their home on the outskirts of Waterford City was targeted in an arson.

Two other children, a girl and a boy, are in a critical condition at Children’s Health Ireland in Crumlin, Dublin, following the horror blaze at Birch Avenue in the Birchwood estate around 5am on Tuesday.



Devastated locals — who heard screams of ‘I’m on fire’ as the blaze raged — could only watch as emergency services attempted to save their lives.

A quadruple murder probe is now underway as the main line of inquiry is drug debt intimidation.

Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan said: “This shocking event has had a very significant impact not just on the people of Waterford but on the whole country.

“There is no place in a civilised society for such a heinous act of violence.



“I am confident those responsible for this brutal and heinous act will be brought to justice to face the full rigour of the law.”

The Irish Sun has learned how the English family were subjected to a campaign of terror at the hands of what cops believe is a dangerous mob.

Philip had sat down with gardai just ten days ago to give a statement on what was the latest in a string of incidents in recent weeks when their car was set alight.

Investigators believe that today’s deadly arson is connected to and part of the same intimidation.

And as part of the cops probe two raids were carried out on homes in the Waterford area tonight.



It is understood the family had been targeted due to a connection that Philip, who had no involvement in crime whatsoever, had to a man who owed a debt.

Pals of Kim also told us how she had expressed fears for her own life and that of her family’s.

The couple and their four children were in bed when their front door was hit with a suspected petrol bomb at around 5am.

Locals were awoken by a huge “bang” as the property was quickly engulfed in flames that also caught their car parked at the front of the house.

A woman whose home is on a road behind told us of her horror.



She said: “I heard the bang and ‘I’m on fire, I’m on fire, I’m on fire.’

“And I heard it and I just thought, ‘someone is going to be f burnt to death in front of me.’

“My poor son ran over, jumped a wall to get in but he couldn’t see his hand in front of his face the fire and smoke was so strong.”

A group of Kim’s pals revealed how she had expressed fears for her life.

They said the ongoing intimidation included paint thrown at the car when they were sleeping, and even a social media account set up to target the family.

Kim had sought to be moved home by the city council, it was claimed.



One of the women told us: “They should have moved her when her house was first targeted.

“She made numerous complaints to Waterford City Council.

“She was in fear for her life. She was in fear for the lives of her family.”

Another one explained: “It was heartbreaking watching Philip and one of the boys get carried out in a coffin.

“They didn’t deserve this at all. But I will say that Waterford City Council did fail them.



“She was in fear for her life for months.” A third neighbour added: “There was a social media account that was taken down magically last night that Kim had asked me to report.”

One of the women fumed at those responsible as tears streamed down her face.

She said: “No matter who they are or where they come from, they’re the lowest of the low. Absolute scumbags.

“And they need to be held accountable for their actions.

“They took out a family. And if them two children wake up to no father, no mother and no siblings, was the money they were paid worth it? And what they have done to the community here. Was it worth it?”



Bishop Alphonsus Cullinan, of Waterford and Lismore, said of the kids who died: “They should be running around the yard there now, and yet they’re dead, and two more then in hospital.

“We pray for them — and it is amazing to see the community around here gathering, supporting and comforting each other.

“We just hope that we’ll gather tomorrow. We’ll pray together and see if we can make some sense out of all of this.

“And God rest all those who have died and all those who’ve been affected by this huge tragedy.”

Sinn Fein TD David Cullinane said that Waterford is “a community in mourning” and the murder probe added “another level of shock to what has happened”.



He said: “What has happened in Waterford today is beyond shocking. There is an enormous sense of grief, trauma and heartbreak across the entire community.

“I knew the family very well and I am utterly devastated. Like so many people across Waterford, I am struggling to find the words to describe the shock and sadness we are all feeling. The loss of life is heartbreaking. The fact that children are among those who have lost their lives makes this tragedy even more difficult to comprehend.”

The Garda investigation into the multiple murders intensified last night as searches were conducted around Waterford city.

Detectives backed up by armed officers carried out raids on the homes of two criminal figures.

The two men are connected to the drugs trade and are suspected of being heavily involved in ­drug-related activity and drug debt intimidation.



As of last night, no arrests have been made. Gardai also said that they have received good co-operation from the public and that all contact will be treated confidentially.

Chief Supt Anthony Pettit, of the Waterford/Kilkenny Garda Division, confirmed that huge resources, including national units, have been drafted in to help with the probe.

He said: “This investigation is being coordinated from an incident room at Waterford Garda Station under the direction of a senior investigating officer.

“The investigation is being carried out by the Serious Crime Unit at Waterford Garda Station, supported by divisional resources and the Garda National Bureau of Criminal Investigation, and all other resources as necessary. An Garda Siochana believe that the house was attacked by a person or persons unknown and that the fire was started deliberately.”

Chief Supt Pettit also appealed to anyone with information to contact investigating officers.



The investigation team can be contacted at the incident room at Waterford Garda Station on 051 305 300, the Garda Confidential Line 1800 666 111, or any Garda station.

Post-mortem examinations are due to be carried out at University Hospital Waterford.

A GoFundMe has been launched to help the English family with the costs of funerals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It reads: “With the heaviest of hearts, we are reaching out to ask for help following an unimaginable tragedy that has devastated our family.”

Over €16,000 had already been raised at time of publication.

News.title: Cops probe new theory after celeb BBL doc assassinated in clinic as ‘hitman’ refuses to answer questions
News.content:
Next

A NEW theory on the assassination of a celebrity BBL surgeon is being probed by cops – as the alleged hitman refuses to answer questions.

Dr Alexander Aslani, 57, whose clients included Towie’s Chloe Sims and Love Island’s Hannah Elizabeth, was shot dead at his Marbella clinic.



Detectives believe a furious patient may have hired a hitman after a row over cosmetic surgery and have launched a probe into the horror.

An 18-year-old Swede arrested on Thursday admitted to gunning down the surgeon, according to Spanish sources.



The alleged killer – who has since been remanded in custody without bail – is reportedly refusing to answer questions.

A judge ordered on Saturday that he be held in solitary confinement pending the probe.



He was cuffed less than 24 hours after the deadly shooting which took place in front of horrified clients last week.

Police are focusing on a new theory Aslani cancelled an operation with a client halfway through after deeming her psychologically unfit.



The doctor then refunded her and refused to continue the procedure.

Another line of enquiry is that one patient became disgruntled due to the outcome of the surgery.

She then allegedly went to the clinic and threatened the doctor.

Four days after this is said to have happened, stones were thrown at the clinic’s windows, according to El Debate Andalucia.

Reports claimed Aslani received angry messages and threats over mobile hours before he was killed.



A major hunt has been launched for the dissatisfied female client – with local reports claiming she has fled Spain.

The suspect reportedly left Spain to her home country in the Persian Gulf, according to local outlet Okdiario.

She is said to have left the country with her wealthy husband – who allegedly previously visited Aslani’s Cirumed Clinic to “issue warnings to staff”.

On Friday local outlet Sur reported Aslani had gone to cops in April to complain he had been receiving “work-related” threats.

It was not clear whether he had pointed the finger at named individuals in his police statement or not.



Investigators said the masked gunman entered the clinic with several customers inside and opened fire before shooting Aslani in the head.

The shooter was reportedly dressed in black head-to-toe, fleeing on a motorbike driven by an accomplice.

Aslani’s clinic claimed to have carried out more than 14,000 operations, but the surgeon also faced complaints from former patients, including one who accused him of botching three procedures.

Influencer Paulina Sobierajska claimed she needed reconstructive surgery and warned women considering using Aslani: “DON’T DO IT.”

The Sun revealed Aslani had been embroiled in a bitter High Court battle with the influencer.



Aslani successfully sued her for libel after she failed to defend the case.

Mr Justice Saini awarded him £40,000 damages in 2021, saying the sum reflected the “total falsity” of the allegations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops have ruled out an earlier theory that Aslani was killed in revenge for a patient dying during surgery, after finding no evidence of any such death.

News.title: Inside tiger attack victim's child acting career as 'proud mum' shares heartwarming stories
News.content:
Inside tiger attack victim's child acting career as 'proud mum' shares heartwarming stories

William Chapman was a former child actor featuring on both the BBC and ITV with his mum sharing how 'proud' she was of him in heartwarming stories from his childhood

View 4 Images Chapman appearing in May Contain Nuts (Image: YouTube)

The man who was horrifically killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park was a former child actor, with his 'proud mum' sharing heartwarming stories of his time on set.

‌



‌



William Chapman, in his 20s, has been revealed as the victim of the tiger attack on Saturday.

‌



He starred in the ITV production May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson, best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films, as well as playing Edward Jenner as a young boy in the BBC series True Stories.

‌



View 4 Images Chapman starred in shows on the BBC and ITV (Image: BBC)

An old blog post written by William's mum shows a glimpse into his life years before the attack.

The post, published just over 12 years ago, says William was "passionate about acting and drama" having attended a performing arts school in High Wycombe since the age of four.

‌



The Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire have posted a heartfelt tribute on their Facebook page after William was revealed as the victim of the attack.

The post reads: "We are deeply saddened to hear of the passing of our former student, William Chapman. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with William’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult time.

"We loved watching William grow, both as a person and as a performer, during his time with us. It was a privilege to be part of his journey, and he will be remembered with great fondness by everyone who had the pleasure of knowing him.

‌



"William will be truly missed, and he will always hold a special place in our hearts. Rest in peace, William."

View 4 Images Chapman appeared in two shows as a child (Image: Not known)

In his mum's blog post she described William's mood in an audition in London for the ITV show 'May Contain Nuts' at age five as "unburdened by the nerves he can sometimes suffer from these days".

‌



She added: "He seemed to relax and thoroughly enjoy himself."

His mum continued to add that working as an extra on Pan, a prequel to the Peter Pan story which starred Hugh Jackman was a 'wonderful experience for him'.

The post also includes an extract written by William himself from this time. It says: "Once on set we were sheltering from the pirates under the ship's floorboards and we had to be terrified! Our chief gets shot by Blackbeard (Hugh Jackman), so remember to look out for that scene if you watch the movie.

‌



"After lunch we just did more tutoring then we went back on set for a retake of the earlier scene, but we were lucky enough to meet and say hi to Hugh Jackman! We gave him a high five, awesome right?"

View 4 Images Chapman filmed the tiger from inside the enclosure before he was mauled to death (Image: Not known)

William's mum continued to detail other roles William has played, expressing how 'proud' she was. She said: "Being a proud mum I couldn’t resist showing off his efforts as the young Edward Jenner for BBC Learning."

‌



William's family paid tribute to their 'amazing' and 'warm' son on Tuesday evening in a heartbreaking statement. The statement said William suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and was given "strong medication".

It continued: "William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back.

"The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened.

Article continues below

"The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did."

News.title: First picture of man who fell 200ft off rollercoaster as horrified family watched on
News.content:
First picture of man who fell 200ft off rollercoaster as horrified family watched on

Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, died after falling from a giant rollercoaster as his son sat on the attraction and wife and daughter watched from the ground.

View 4 Images Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, died after falling from the 200-foot tall Goliath rollercoaster (Image: Facebook/Hassan Kariem)

A man who tragically died after plummeting from a rollercoaster during a family day out has been named and pictured for the first time.

‌



‌



Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, died after falling from the 200-ft Goliath rollercoaster at Six Flags in Georgia on Saturday, as his son sat on the attraction and wife and daughter watched from the ground.

‌



Horrified witnesses recounted how Hassan made eye contact with them and hit three different coaster cars as he plunged to his death from the "hypercoaster".

‌



The Goliath attraction, the tallest in the state of Georgia, opened in 2006 and reaches top speeds of 70 mph during the ride. Hassan was mid-ride with his son when he somehow slipped out of his lap restraint before landing on the roof of a haunted house below, witnesses recounted.

View 4 Images The man fell from the Goliath theme park ride (Image: Six Flags Over Georgia & Hurricane Harbor﻿)

The violent fall was captured on official souvenir photos available to other riders, while disturbing photographs shared on social media appear to show Kariem flailing upside down as other passengers screamed in terror.

‌



Four other riders were injured in the incident, while many on the ride were covered in Hassan's blood.

"He didn't fall directly onto us. He fell onto a girl two rows in front of us. He fell and hit the cart three different times," one woman who was on the ride told 11Alive.

View 4 Images One witness said the man fell and hit the car three different times (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"He was in our pictures," she said. "His son was right beside him … his son watched it all."

The woman said that park employees refused let everyone off immediately.

Parkgoer Logan Conner, who was riding Goliath with his fiancé, said the man "started levitating in the air sideways" as he tumbled through the air.

‌



View 4 Images It is understood the man may have slipped from his seat before crashing along the cart a number of times (Image: Six Flags Over Georgia & Hurricane Harbor﻿)

Fellow rider Fred Sowemimo told NBC that Hassan's safety harness appeared to become "dislodged" while on the ride and "he flew out".

Fred's wife, Vanessa, said they initially thought it was a prank.

Article continues below

The incident remains under investigation and the ride remains closed.

Six Flags, the biggest amusement park company in the US, shut down its nine large "gigacoasters" like the Goliath across North America "out of an abundance of caution."

News.title: New dinosaur species which preyed on humans discovered from Isle of Wight fossil 'overlooked' for 100 years
News.content:
New dinosaur species which preyed on humans discovered from Isle of Wight fossil 'overlooked' for 100 years

Scientists have identified a previously unknown long-clawed predator that roamed Britain 120 million years ago - and say humans would have been the perfect size for it to hunt

View 2 Images The new species was identified from part of a fossilised skill acquired by the National History Museum in 1924 (Image: Sergey Krasovskiy and Pedro Salas/PA Wire)

A long-forgotten fossil has revealed a new species of long-clawed dinosaur that roamed Britain 120 million years ago.

‌



‌



The tiger-sized predator has been named Invictibellatrix amberina, and scientists say it would have viewed humans as perfectly-sized prey. The remarkable discovery was made from part of a skull found on the Isle of Wight and acquired by the Natural History Museum in 1924, where its significance went unnoticed for decades.

‌



Scientists have now established it belonged to a previously unknown species of megaraptoran -a mysterious group of agile, two-legged meat-eating dinosaurs closely related to tyrannosaurs, including Tyrannosaurus rex. It is the first evidence that the group, which is thought to have originated in Asia, once lived in Europe.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images The fossil's significance went unrecognised for decades (Image: The Trustees of the Natural History Museum, London/PA Wire)

WW1 soldier's tragic love story told over 100 years later after bloodstained diary found in rubbish tip READ MORE :

Dr Cassius Morrison, who led the research at University College London (UCL), said: “It was not the apex predator of its time, but for humans this dinosaur would have been more dangerous than a T.rex. We would have been perfectly sized prey, about a third of their body weight.

‌



"They definitely would have chased us. A T.rex would not have bothered, as we would have been too small. It is a real mystery that this fossil was overlooked for so long, sitting in a drawer for nearly 100 years. Lots of bones are found on the Isle of Wight – who knows what else is waiting to be discovered.”

Invictibellatrix is thought to have measured between three and four metres long and stood just over 1.5 metres tall. Rather than relying on huge jaws to take down its victims, the feathered predator is thought to have used powerful arms armed with curved claws measuring up to 20cm.

Dr Morrison said: “Based on what we know about its closest relatives, Invictibellatrix would have been three to four metres long and just over a metre and a half in height – about as tall as a human. It would likely have had feathers, and its claws might have been about 10cm to 20cm long. It would have eaten small dinosaurs, lizards and mammals – occupying a similar role in the food chain to the hyena today.”

‌



The fossil was originally discovered at the foot of a cliff on the south-west coast of the Isle of Wight by amateur palaeontologist Reginald Walter Tooley. The dinosaur’s new name also carries a special meaning. Invictibellatrix translates as “unconquered female warrior”, while amberina is a reference to amber found in the rocks where the fossil was uncovered.

Researchers said the name was chosen with the intention to “give hope and strength to all those who are bullied, discriminated, victimised, and oppressed that tomorrow will be theirs and not to give up in face of such odds”. Scientists used CT X-ray scans to peer inside the fossil and create 3D models of the skull before comparing it with other meat-eating dinosaurs, including tyrannosaurs, spinosaurs and raptors.

They spotted a unique combination of features, including an oval opening where the spinal cord entered the brain and an hourglass-shaped crest, which helped identify the remains as a previously unknown species. The discovery has also given scientists a crucial clue about how megaraptors spread around the prehistoric world.

‌



The dinosaurs are thought to have originated in Asia before moving through Europe and eventually reaching Gondwana, the ancient southern landmass which included present-day Africa, South America and Antarctica. Study co-author Charlie Scherer said: “This new species is the first proof we have that megaraptorans were also present in Europe and that they reached Gondwana this way rather than island-hopping further south.”

Megaraptors were widespread during the Early Cretaceous period, but appear to have disappeared from the northern landmass of Laurasia tens of millions of years later. Meanwhile, those living in Gondwana went on to become enormous apex predators, with some developing claws up to 35cm long.

Scientists believe changes to the climate or environment, or competition from other predators including tyrannosaurs, could have contributed to their disappearance from the north according to researched published in the journal Royal Society Open Science. Senior author Dr Paul Barrett said: “Despite over 200 years of collecting, the Isle of Wight continues to surprise us with new dinosaur species, and finds of carnivorous dinosaurs, such as Invictibellatrix, have been particularly elusive.

Article continues below

“Work like this shows the exceptional value of working with historical museum collections where there are still many discoveries to be made.”

News.title: Pub that opened during Covid crisis is in final four for Britain's best boozer
News.content:
Pub that opened during Covid crisis is in final four for Britain's best boozer

Bosses of The Cockpit in Chislehurst, Kent negotiated lockdowns during the coronavirus pandemic — but the micropub and shop owned by the community is now thriving

View 4 Images The Cockpit is among four finalists in Camra's Pub of the Year prize

A pub which only opened during the Covid crisis is among the final four in the running for Britain’s best boozer.

‌



‌



The Cockpit in Chislehurst, Kent, began serving in late December 2020, in a former shop, with the pandemic in full swing. It was able to start operating more normally the following summer as lockdown rules were eased and quickly became popular with the local community.

‌



And now, just six years after opening, it is in the race to be the Campaign for Real Ale’s National Pub of the Year 2026.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Licensee Adam Miller called getting down to the final four “boggling news”. He added: “It has caused a frenzy of frenetic jubilation amongst us staff and stalwarts at The Cockpit.

“This is a pub stripped back to basics, where the pristinity of our ales, ciders, food and wine speak to the uncompromising standards of the producers that grace our floorboards, along with our punters’ intangible whimsies seasoning the atmosphere so dotingly, it is a truly treasured environment to serve such a convivial community.

‌



View 4 Images The Cockpit micropub in Chistlehurst, Kent, serves pints...and flowers

Over 110 Brewers Fayre and Beefeater restaurants reopening across UK – all the locations confirmed so far READ MORE :

“Thank you to all the stagehands that keep the wheels in motion, both on the jump and behind the curtain, and thank you, CAMRA, for recognising our little boozer with this accreditation; what splendid company to be in.”

CAMRA describes the Cockpit, which is shared with a florists, as having an easy going, chatty atmosphere, “with a £1 fine for using any mobile phones or foul language.”

‌



View 4 Images Landlord George Greenaway, who started the Tamworth Tap with wife Louise in 2017, has already won a string of prizes (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

The other three finalists are The Turks Head, St Helens; the Countryman’s Inn, Hunton, Yorkshire; and the Tamworth Tap in Tamworth.

The Turks Head has been a previous regional winner, while the Tamworth Tap will be fighting for a record-breaking fourth National Pub of the Year title.

‌



The Mirror has long championed the cause of community pubs through its Your Pub Needs You campaign.

View 4 Images CAMRA's celebration of Britain's best pubs comes against a backdrop of widespread closures (Image: Getty Images)

However, it comes amid ongoing tough times for many in the sector, with figures this week showing pubs were closing at an average rate of one every day this year.

‌



Andrea Briers, CAMRA Pub of the Year Coordinator, said: “Despite the well-documented challenges facing our pubs and brewers, these licensees have not just survived, but thrived. All four are amazing places that are definitely worth a visit, whether you want a top-quality pint, or just a brilliant community-orientated vibe.”

Clare Harrison, licensee of the Turks Head, said: “To say we’re over the moon is an understatement. We’re incredibly proud to have reached the final four pubs, and to be representing St Helens at this level is honestly a dream come true.

Dan Male, licensee of the Countryman’s Inn, said: “We are absolutely delighted to have made it to the last four. In our fourth year of community ownership the pub continues to grow, and we are so proud to be recognised by CAMRA in the work we are doing."

Article continues below

And George Greenaway, landlord of the Tamworth Tap, said: “We’re absolutely thrilled to have made the final four again. It honestly feels just as exciting as it did the first time we became finalists. We were keeping everything crossed.”

News.title: Car insurance firms slammed for charging 'poverty premium' to drivers who pay monthly
News.content:
Car insurance firms slammed for charging 'poverty premium' to drivers who pay monthly

Paying monthly for car insurance costs more as it is essentially a credit agreement, meaning drivers are charged interest or administration fees for spreading the cost

View 2 Images Car insurance is more expensive if you pay monthly (Image: Getty Images)

Which? has slammed car insurance firms for charging a "poverty premium" to customers who cannot afford to pay upfront.

‌



‌



Paying monthly for car insurance costs more as it is essentially a credit agreement, meaning drivers are charged interest or administration fees for spreading the cost.

‌



It means you end up paying more over the long term, compared to paying for car insurance upfront. It also appears on your credit report.

‌



This type of loan agreement is known as premium finance and it is estimated that 15 million UK customers use this to pay for car insurance.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Always search around for the best car insurance quotes

‌



DWP paid out record £170million to dead pensioners last year READ MORE :

Which? says many of these drivers are under financial pressure do so as they cannot afford the price of the insurance upfront.

The consumer champion launched a mystery shopping investigation involving 30 car insurance providers and brokers. It found five companies offered what it considers extortionate interest rates which are above typical credit card APRs.

The same customer profile was used, and included the customer being a 42-year-old motorist based in Sheffield, driving for 10 years with no claims or incidents in the past five years.

‌



The highest APRs came from insurance brokers. Car insurance brokers can charge their own interest rates if they arrange a premium finance credit agreement for you.

City Insurance charged the highest interest rate (53%) followed by UDrive Cover Ltd (50%), Sterling Insurance (38%), Rightsure (34%) and Acorn (33%). City Insurance told Which? it is currently in the process of reducing its APR to 36%.

In cash terms, these figures represent as much as £367.75 added to the typical car insurance bill, turning a £2,583.23 annual policy from Rightsure into a £2,950.98 one.

‌



The median APR across all 36 quotes analysed was 26.2% - in comparison, the median credit card APR is currently 25.9%.

The consumer champion found just 14 providers charged interest under 25%. Only two insurers, Marshmallow and Motorcade, charged 0% APR, though Which? said this does not mean they were the most affordable providers overall.

Quote Detective added the most to its quote for paying monthly. Its total monthly cost of £1,756.03 was £244.76 (16.20%) higher than the annual premium of £1,511.27. An APR figure wasn’t provided as part of the online quote.

‌



It comes after the FCA concluded a market study in March 2026, where it ultimately ruled out a price cap or ban on charging interest for pay-monthly policies. The regulator claimed that its current rules were sufficient to address cases of poor behaviour among insurers.

Rocio Concha, Director of Policy and Advocacy at Which?, said: "Too many consumers have already been pushed out of driving or into financial peril because of these unfair pricing practices that we’ve found can charge less wealthy customers more.

“Our latest investigation exposes the consequences of the regulator shying away from its responsibility to ensure competition works for consumers.

‌



“The Prime Minister has pledged to create more ‘breathing space’ for consumers, and that’s why we’re urging him to use the upcoming budget to announce a ban on two-tier pricing for motor insurance. We believe it is the best way to create a fairer, more competitive system that doesn’t punish the customers least able to pay.”

Highest car insurance APRs for paying monthly

City Insurance - 53%

UDrive Cover - 50.67%

Sterling Insurance - 38.10%

Rightsure - 34%

Acorn - 33%

City Insurance said: "We have been reviewing our premium finance arrangements and the APR charged to customers, particularly following the recent market review of premium finance.

‌



“As part of that review, we have agreed new terms which will reduce the representative APR from the 53.03% rate as identified by Which? to approximately 36%, based on a flat-rate charge of 13.25%. The new terms will be introduced shortly once the revised contractual arrangements have been completed."

RightSure said: "As an insurance broker, we do not control all of the factors that contribute to the total price payable by a customer. However, APR alone does not necessarily demonstrate the value provided to a customer.

Sterling Insurance said: “We are a specialist non-standard insurance provider, providing insurance cover to customers and risks that are often difficult to place within the standard insurance market, while seeking to maintain competitive and affordable premiums."

Article continues below

The Mirror contacted UDrive Cover and Acorn for comment.

News.title: Donald Trump shares tiger attack video of British man killed at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
News.content:
Donald Trump shares tiger attack video of British man killed at Yorkshire Wildlife Park

Donald Trump has shared video footage of a British man being fatally attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster to 13 million followers on his social media platform

View 2 Images Donald Trump told a crowd in Ohio to vote for a Senate candidate in Minnesota (Image: AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar)

Donald Trump has posted insensitive footage of a young man being fatally mauled by a tiger at a British wildlife park.

‌



‌



The US President shared the brief clip on his Truth Social platform, writing: "Don't ever mess with nature!". The Mirror - and other publications - have not shared the video due to the nature of it but Mr Trump blithely used it as fodder tonight for his 13 million followers.

‌



It depicts the animal biting and clawing the victim, since named as William Chapman, as he sat within the enclosure, though not the actual killing, at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, which is near Doncaster.

‌



William Chapman: Tiger attack victim was former child actor who appeared on BBC and ITV READ MORE :

View 2 Images William Chapman pictured in Rome (Image: instagram.com@williamchapman2024)

Mr Trump subsequently followed this with another post containing a video compilation that appeared to feature multiple individuals being attacked by lions, set to an upbeat soundtrack.

‌



A health and safety inquiry has been initiated into the incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, where Mr Chapman lost his life after entering the tiger enclosure on Saturday, reports the Daily Record.

The park will stay shut on Wednesday for a fifth consecutive day following the attack. Emergency services were alerted shortly after 1.30pm on October 10 when Mr Chapman, who police confirmed was visiting the park by himself, entered the enclosure. He was declared dead at the scene.

Family trapped in zoo after it closed with them inside use Facebook to get help READ MORE :

It emerged tonight Mr Chapman was a former child actor. The man, described as in his 20s, jumped into the tiger enclosure at the zoo as terrified onlookers urged him to "play dead".

Article continues below

The Amur tiger, named Altai, then viciously attacked Mr Chapman and he was later pronounced dead at the scene. He had filmed chilling footage of himself approaching the tiger breathing heavily in the moments before the mauling.

Witnesses said Mr Chapman had seemed "so happy" before he climbed into the enclosure with police confirming he was not accompanied by anyone at the time of the attack .

The park confirmed that the tiger will not be euthanised following the incident.

News.title: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer as surgery to remove right lung lobe proves successful
News.content:
Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer as surgery to remove right lung lobe proves successful

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing major surgery, which saw part of his right lung removed, the Vatican has said today

View 2 Images Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer (Image: Getty Images)

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing major surgery which saw doctors remove part of his right lung, the Vatican said.

‌



‌



Tests confirmed the 71-year-old has lung adenocarcinoma, which had been suspected by pre-operative tests and was confirmed during the 90-minute long procedure on Tuesday.

‌



The Vatican said there were currently no plans for the Pope to begin chemotherapy or other therapies, adding that the surgery was "successful" with "no complications".

‌



The Pope was in the operating room for around three hours, with the procedure itself lasting roughly 90 minutes, the statement added.

Pope risks reigniting Trump feud and slams death penalty after botched execution READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Pope's surgery was 'successful,' the Vatican said (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

He woke up normally after the surgery, and after a brief period of observation, returned to his room on the 10th floor of Rome's Gemelli Hospital to recover.

‌



According to the medical report, the Pope's operation involved the "radical" removal of the lower lobe of his right lung in a bid to eliminate the cancer.

"In order to make the procedure curative, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique," lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, said after the surgery.

"A rapid intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as had been suspected from the pre-operative tests."

‌



Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, developing in cells that produce mucus, usually in the outer parts of the lungs.

It is a form of non-small cell lung cancer, and treatment depends on factors including how far the cancer has spread.

All of the Pope's audiences up to October 20 have been cancelled to allow him time to recover.

Article continues below

During his Sunday noon prayer, Leo revealed doctors had discovered a small nodule on his lung, adding that he would have it removed.

Oncologists previously said that even if the growth proved to be cancerous, Leo's prognosis was "excellent" as the nodule would be removed at an early stage.

News.title: Family pays tribute to 'warm and engaging' man killed in tiger attack
News.content:
The family of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park has paid tribute, describing him as "bright, warm and engaging".

William Chapman, 23, visited Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday and was attacked after going into the animal's pen. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

In a statement, his family said that he had suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and had been prescribed "strong medication".

It said it was for the coroner to decide whether his mental illness played a part in his death, asking that the public respect that process.

City of Doncaster Council has launched a health and safety investigation into Chapman's death and the park remains closed.

"William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back," a statement released on Tuesday evening said.

The family also asked for privacy, saying "the publication and circulation of deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress at an exceptionally vulnerable time".

"The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened," the statement continued.

"The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did."

A spokesperson for the South Yorkshire Police said Chapman's family are being supported by specialist officers.

The incident, which took place shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday, led to the evacuation and ongoing closure of the park.

An eyewitness described seeing Chapman wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in.

Mobile phone footage, believed to be from Chapman, appears to show the inside of the enclosure as he approaches the tiger across a patch of grass.

Chapman was a former pupil of the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe.

"We loved watching William grow, both as a person and as a performer, during his time with us," the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe said in a tribute on Tuesday.

"It was a privilege to be part of his journey, and he will be remembered with great fondness by everyone who had the pleasure of knowing him."

"Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with William's family and friends during this incredibly difficult time," the statement continued.

As a child, Chapman appeared in the ITV production May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson - who is best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films - and Darren Boyd.

He also portrayed Edward Jenner in the BBC series True Stories.

Staff at Yorkshire Wildlife Park have separately said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" are with Chapman's family and confirmed the rare Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

Dan Swaine, the local authority's executive director of place, said the council was "deeply saddened" by the incident and sent its "deepest sympathies" to Chapman's family and those who were at the scene.

News.title: Zelensky and Burnham to meet in Downing Street
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street on Wednesday, as the UK announces it will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv.

Burnham is also expected to set out how his government will draw up further sanctions against Russia.

Speaking ahead of the meeting, Burnham said the UK was with Ukraine "for as long as it takes", adding: "Russian aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent."

The UK will also urge allies to step up pressure on Russia, with Chancellor John Healey using International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings to call for a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG).

This will be Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister. His first was in late July, days after Burnham entered No 10, when the pair met troops and led a news conference at a naval base in Portsmouth.

Burnham said: "Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia.

"My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe.

"It is not just the right thing to do, but it's the necessary thing to do."

Among the measures being announced is the quicker delivery of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMMs), with the UK having already committed to send more than 5,000 worth Â£1.6bn over the next four years.

The UK will also reaffirm its plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports.

The meeting between Zelensky and Burnham follows what Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described as a "very difficult few days" for UK-US relations due to President Donald Trump's decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.

Zelensky criticised the US deal with Russia, calling it a "gift" to President Vladimir Putin. Trump, in response, called for new leadership in Ukraine and criticised Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries.

Meanwhile, Healey will ask partners at the IMF to step up support for Kyiv and ensure Russia heeds the US' call for a full energy ceasefire.

Trump claimed on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire - but hours later, Zelensky said Russian attacks on energy facilities had continued.

On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine did not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

News.title: Royal Mail losing 400 postal workers a week, says union
News.content:
About 400 postmen and women are leaving Royal Mail per week, according to the Communication Workers Union (CWU), who claims this number has gone up since the company introduced a new delivery system earlier this year.

The CWU says the firm had been losing about 330 postal staff a week from a workforce of 83,000 before it rolled out DM26, which reorganised routes to improve delivery performance.

The union claims the new system is not working in hundreds of offices, and BBC Your Voice has heard from staff warning of a "nightmare" Christmas ahead as the number of parcels increases.

Royal Mail says the reforms are part of its plan to deliver a more "efficient and financially sustainable" service.

Over the last year we've been in touch with more than 30 postal staff in all four nations of the UK, as they have switched over to DM26.

It allows for second class post to only be delivered every other weekday, and is supposed to guarantee first class mail and parcels are delivered every day, by putting workers into groups of three and changing the walking pattern of rounds.

But posties speaking to us anonymously say parcels are still being prioritised, letters left behind, and time wasted in sorting and dividing mail into first and second class.

"I didn't take any first class mail out on my last shift because I was on a road that's been behind for weeks," a worker in the West Midlands told me. "But I'm sure a manager would have ticked a box to say all first class mail went out."

A Royal Mail spokesperson said the company always worked to ensure all mail - both letters and parcels - were delivered on time.

News.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
News.content:
"It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action," he added.

Fraternities have existed at university campuses across the US for decades and function as all-male social clubs where the students live, study and socialise. Over the years, the groups have become notorious for binge-drinking, partying and dangerous hazing rituals.

In a statement, a lawyer representing Doe said she filed a civil lawsuit "to achieve her aim of improving Cornell and its response to abuse claims".

"While the steps announced today are helpful to achieve this goal, they are too late to protect Ms. Doe," said lawyer Thomas Giuffra.

Cornell's president said anyone who violated the new fraternity party policy at the New York university would be suspended.

The school also said it planned to improve support for survivors of sexual assault, including more staff to help people report sexual misconduct and navigate other support systems as well.

Through Title IX, the federal law that governs how universities handle sexual assault claims, schools are required to provide measures of support to help survivors stay in school after assaults. Doe's lawyer has said she dropped out after the alleged assault.

The president said the school will allow New York State Police's trauma-informed officers to investigate allegations of sexual assault on its campus.

These officers will interview survivors who want to pursue criminal charges and prepare "comprehensive investigative summaries for the appropriate law enforcement agency", Kotlikoff said.

Cornell has faced criticism over the information shared with the local district attorney's office about Jane Doe's allegations.

Out of hundreds of documents that US media outlets have obtained from Cornell's investigation into the assault, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said that in 2024, his office received only a six-page statement signed by the victim as well as Snapchat messages in which the men at the fraternity party advertised a free sexual encounter with Doe.

State officials have also criticised Van Houten's decision not to bring charges or interview victims and witnesses himself. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed the state's attorney general, Letitia James, to investigate the case.

Kotlikoff said Cornell would be bringing in national sexual violence prevention experts to examine "the factors leading to campus sexual violence and strategies to promote responsible sexual citizenship".

He said the steps were the first toward "systematic change" on campus.

News.title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
News.content:
Students protests in France have entered their fourth week and with a renewed impetus, according to the BBC's James Waterhouse.

The nationwide demonstrations against poor classroom conditions, including old buildings, teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, have caused disruption to education across France as hundreds of lycÃ©es (15-18 year-olds colleges) had to be closed.

Students on the streets of Paris told the BBC that they had not achieved anything yet and that stopping now would be a "defeat".

More on this story.

News.title: Actress Selma Blair faces charges for kicking nurse and officer after plane incident
News.content:
US actress Selma Blair has been charged with two additional assault counts over allegedly kicking an officer and a nurse after being removed from a flight.

Blair was arrested late Sunday in New York after she allegedly attacked flight attendants on a Delta plane travelling from Los Angeles to New York. The FBI issued her a federal summons accusing her of assault on board.

While appearing in court over the additional charges, the Legally Blonde star's attorney asked the judge to consider the actress's "body of work", and called Blair the "gold standard." The judge said she should not "get special treatment".

Blair has pleaded not guilty. She has since been released on bail.

She was taken to hospital after the incident on the flight. Her representatives have told the BBC that she had "experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct".

As the flight landed in New York on Sunday evening, airport officials responded to a call about "a physically abusive passenger" on the flight. Two flight attendants were hurt and one was taken to hospital, the New York Port Authority said.

Audio recorded on air traffic control details a pilot asking for medical help, describing "a bloody nose" and "some bite marks", according to CBS News, BBC's US News partner.

Blair, 54, who also starred in Cruel Intentions and Hellboy, was arrested and taken to hospital. She was issued a federal summons for a charge of assault within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the US.

The two additional charges of assault, filed in state court, came after she was taken off the plane.

One of the alleged assaults happened when she was being transported in an ambulance, where she allegedly kicked a police officer. Once at hospital, prosecutors allege that she also assaulted a nurse.

News.title: Gales and heavy rain to impact UK as yellow wind warning issued
News.content:
A weather system containing the remnants of Hurricane Isaias is forecast to send gales, heavy rain and a surge of warm air to parts of the UK this week.

The centre of the low, and its most significant impacts, will stay hundreds of miles from UK shores but north-west Scotland will see a spell of gales.

A Met Office yellow warning has been issued for parts of the Highlands and Western Isles with the risk of gusts touching 70mph (113km/h) in places.

Heavy rain will also affect parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland but much of England and Wales will remain largely dry with spells of sunshine.

The area of low pressure will also send a renewed surge of warm air across the country bringing above-average temperatures for many.

News.title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026
News.content:
An emotional scene of an elephant carrying a deceased calf has earned Italian photographer Federico Veronesi the title of Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026.

While tracking elephants in Namibia's Huab River Valley, Veronesi spotted an unusual trail of drag marks across the sand of a dry riverbed.

Following the tracks, he came across a female elephant carrying a dead calf, its leg wedged between her tusk and trunk.

Initially, Veronesi assumed the elephant was the calf's mother. But after sharing his photographs with an elephant research project working in the area, he learned that this wasn't certain.

Researchers recognised the elephant as a female who had lost a calf several years earlier and said she had previously picked up dead calves belonging to other females.

For Veronesi, the encounter was deeply significant. "Of all the 20 years I've done photographing animals, this is the most heart-wrecking and fascinating and dramatic," he said, describing it as "revealing of the depth and complexity of the emotions, the feelings of the animals."

He hopes the image will encourage people to look beyond animals' physical appearance and recognise them as individuals with their own relationships, memories and emotions. "It's a small window that opens just a crack into the complexity of their world," he said.

The competition's annual exhibition, external opens at the Natural History Museum on Friday 16 October 2026. Keep scrolling to see more award-winning images.

News.title: Football regulator says he would quit over any political interference in Man City case
News.content:
The head of English football's independent regulator says he will resign if he encounters any political interference over the future of Manchester City.

As chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives.

If an independent commission's findings that the club broke Premier League financial rules are upheld, the watchdog could even force a sale.

Last month, the Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owners selling the club.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is," he added.

When asked about Burnham's comments, Kogan told BBC Sport: "The Prime Minister is entirely entitled to make his own observations on anything.

"We are independent. That is in the name. I am the chairman of the Independent Football Regulator and independence absolutely runs through everything we're doing.

"And no politician has tried to influence and would try to influence anything we do on that."

When asked what he would do if he did come under political pressure over the case, Kogan replied: "I would resign."

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy prime minister Sheikh Mansour - are said to have topped up the value of commercial deals as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to the scale of Â£830m.

City insist they are innocent and have appealed.

News.title: Argentina targets UK in legal claim over Falklands oil exploration
News.content:
