The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles (209 km) from the Falkland Islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.

The Falkland Islands government extended exploration licences last month and the field is expected to start pumping in 2028, potentially generating huge revenues for the roughly 3,500 inhabitants of the islands.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â have insisted they have valid licences issued by Britain.

The Argentinian government claims the marine environment of disputed maritime areas is protected by international law.

Its application "seeks to preserve Argentina's sovereign rights over its continental shelf and prevent activities authorised unilaterally and illegally by the United Kingdom".

In a post on X, Argentinian Foreign Affairs Minister Pablo Quirno said the government was requesting the tribunal make a number of orders against the UK, including halting new exploration permits.

But the UK government insists Sea Lion is lawful, located on the Falkland Islands shelf and regulated by the islands' government.

While the Falkland Islands government grants exploration licences, they must be signed off by the UK Foreign Secretary.

Kumaran said the tribunal application "does not invalidate licenses issued by the Falkland Islands government, alter the islands' regulatory authority, or require lawful hydrocarbon development activities to cease".

The tribunal that will consider the dispute is an independent judicial body based in Hamburg which is responsible for the fair application of the United Nations' Convention on the Law of the Sea.

FCDO officials have made clear the UK will engage with the tribunal but resist Argentina's claim firmly.

They said the aim was not to escalate the dispute but respond firmly to Argentina's latest move, and defend what the UK sees as legitimate economic activity.

They also hope to provide reassurance to businesses fearful of Argentine retribution. That is why they are introducing measures under the Protection of Trading Interests Act that would protect firms from any extra-territorial impact of Argentine laws following Milei's sanctions threats.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Argentina's attempts to intimidate businesses and individuals engaged in legitimate commercial activity are unacceptable. Companies should be free to make lawful commercial decisions without the threat of political coercion."

The latest move comes after Milei roundly criticised the UN in his speech at the General Assembly late last month for failing to act over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.

He said the UN had become "a useless organisation" which only serves "arrogant parasites dressed up as well-intentioned bureaucrats".

On Tuesday Kumaran described Milei's remarks at New York as "inflammatory".

Despite its defeat in 1982, Argentina has always maintained its right to the Falkland Islands. But over the years successive governments have pressed their claim with varying degrees of aggression and diplomacy.

UK officials believes the current Argentine leadership is deliberately picking a fight ahead of elections next year.

News.title: MI5 chief warns against overstating Russian interference in Brexit vote
News.content:
MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has said there was Russian interference in the the Brexit referendum, but warned against overstating its impact on the result.

It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham provoked a backlash from some Brexit campaigners by saying it was "clear" there had been interference by Moscow in the 2016 vote.

Sir Ken said it was "a matter of public record" that there was interference in the referendum by online trolls and bots.

However, he suggested Russian trolls would be "delighted" to be front page news again, "despite the comparative unimpressiveness" of their efforts.

He added: "There is a really important difference between interference attempted and outcome swayed.

"I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall."

Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart branded Sir Ken's comments "an extraordinary slap down to the prime minister".

In an interview released on Monday, Burnham told The Rest is Politics podcast, external that upon arriving in Downing Street, he had asked if there had been Russian interference in the 2016 vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was."

He did not provide details about the extent or nature of Russian activities during the interview, and when pressed on the subject in the House of Commons on Monday afternoon appeared to be less definitive.

The PM denied claims from Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch that he was implying the referendum result was illegitimate because of Russian interference.

He said it was a "matter of record" that Russia sought to interfere in the 2019 general election, adding: "We think it is inconceivable that this was the first time".

A No 10 spokesperson also clarified that while the prime minister believed it was highly likely Russia tried to influence the referendum result, he did not believe those efforts were successful.

The Conservatives accused Burnham of making an "embarrassing retreat" after "being caught out trying question the legitimacy of the referendum result".

News.title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal
News.content:
A former deputy church warden could not have have legally caused a university lecturer's death by giving him potentially sedated whisky, the Supreme Court has been told.

Benjamin Field, 35, was jailed for at least 36 years in 2019 after being found guilty of murdering 69-year-old Peter Farquhar in Maids Moreton, Buckinghamshire.

In April, appeal judges quashed Field's conviction and ordered a retrial, but said the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) could take the case to the Supreme Court first.

And on Tuesday, five justices at the UK's highest court were asked to consider whether Field could have made Mr Farquhar cause his own death without Field legally being responsible.

During his murder trial prosecutors said Field drove Farquhar to believe he was losing his mind, secretly drugging him and spiking his whisky so his death would appear to be suicide or an accident, allowing Field to inherit his home and money.

The case has previously been adapted into Bafta winning BBC drama The Sixth Commandment, starring Timothy Spall and Anne Reid.

Before his murder trial, Field admitted burglary and fraud offences connected with relationships he had formed with Farquhar and his neighbour, fellow pensioner Ann Moore-Martin, to persuade them to change their wills.

He received a concurrent 16-year sentence for those offences. He was cleared of conspiring or attempting to murder Moore-Martin and of possessing an article for use in fraud.

The hearing was due to conclude on Tuesday, with a decision expected at a later date.

News.title: Majority of English football clubs on the edge of financial disaster, report says
News.content:
English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark report by the independent football regulator.

Research by the watchdog found 94% of clubs are loss-making, and more than 60% of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent.

The regulator (IFR) warns of "a dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".

The 'State of the Game' report also suggests that despite the economic success of the Premier League, the financial 'cliff-edges' between and within leagues have grown significantly.

The report says:

94% of clubs in the top five English leagues made losses in 2025-26

17 clubs across the EFL and National League would be loss-making even if their players played for free

66% of clubs could not survive for more than 90 days without new owner funding

29% of clubs reported they could not survive more than 30 days without such funding

68% of clubs have no contingency plan if their owner walks away

The IFR claims "the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform", and its report "should serve as a wake-up call" for English football.

"Seventeen clubs are now trading in such a way that if their players played for free, their non-playing costs would mean they would go bust," IFR chair David Kogan told BBC Sport.

"Thirty-two clubs are operating on only 30 days' cash. If the owner chooses not to pay cash at the end of the month, those clubs go bust.

"That is a very, very risky scenario. This is the moment of addressing these problems before money starts to dry up.

"We can actually fix the house while the sun is still shining and that's essentially what our role is going to be in this."

News.title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash
News.content:
The court heard Dowling, from Caerphilly, was driving with his wife and their lifelong friend, who they were taking to a hospital appointment, when the collision happened.

Despite wet and windy conditions, heavy rain and high levels of surface water, he was travelling at 76mph (122 km/h) just three seconds before the crash.

After aquaplaning, the defendant crashed into a stationary black Audi A3 driven by Sharon, who had pulled over because of the weather conditions.

She suffered catastrophic injuries and spent three months in hospital before her death in January 2024.

In a victim impact statement, her son Luke Berry, who is expecting a child, described the family's loss as immeasurable, saying his mother would never get the chance to meet her grandchild.

He said: "She was loving, caring and would do anything to make sure I was OK.

"My family will never be the same without her."

The court was also told Jane Beedell suffered multiple injuries in the crash, including chest and elbow injuries, bruising, wounds to her fingers, bleeding on the brain and multiple fractures to her ribs.

She was placed in an induced coma for weeks, and told the court the crash had left her struggling with "fear, anxiety and depression".

"I used to be confident, strong and an outgoing individual," she said, explaining how she now relies on family and friends for daily support and struggles with everyday tasks, finding it difficult to go out alone.

After 48 years working in the civil service, Jane said she had lost her job and now relied on benefits.

She said she was devastated by the changes to her life, adding: "I sometimes feel guilty I survived".

The court heard how Kim Dowling was left paralysed with a broken back and neck and unable to speak after her voice box was removed following the crash.

Mitigating, Dowling's barrister said the defendant felt "deep regret and remorse for the loss of life", along with "strong feelings of guilt and emotional distress".

The court heard that every time Dowling looked at his wife, he was reminded of what he had done.

The case was initially brought as dangerous driving, but the charges were later changed to careless driving, to which he pleaded guilty.

Dowling had previously been disqualified from driving for six months about 15 years ago after reaching 12 penalty points, the court heard.

However, he had no previous convictions despite years of long-distance driving for work and was described as a man of "good character" who was a full-time carer for his wife.

During the sentencing, Judge Hughes said Sharon Berry had suffered a "senseless death", adding that "no amount of sentence given to Dowling would bring her back".

Dowling was sentenced to 27 months in prison for causing death by careless driving and two counts of causing serious injury by careless driving, suspended for two years.

He was also disqualified from driving for four years, ordered to complete 250 hours of unpaid community work and pay Â£1,630 in prosecution costs.

News.title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show
News.content:
Raye has hit back at ticket touts who she says "overwhelmed" the sign-up process for an upcoming live show by using artificial intelligence (AI) bots to create "hundreds of thousands of fake registrations".

The Where Is My Husband! singer revealed there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her one-off 5,000-seat performance at the Royal Albert Hall on 23 October.

To avoid a pre-sale which she felt scalpers could exploit, Raye said the sign-up list had been manually reviewed to identify a shortlist of people believed to be "real fans".

A spokesperson for the Royal Albert Hall said they "invest heavily" in protecting their ticketing systems from "automated attacks" but the "law needs to catch up".

The award-winning artist said she had "never witnessed bots on this scale" and was changing the process as it is "so important" to her that fans can buy tickets at the face value price.

"I'm not sure what the future holds for ticketing, I do know this experience has really opened my eyes," she said in a statement shared on her social media accounts, external.

"Me and my team are going to think really hard about what we can do in the future."

Raye said the fans manually selected would receive a pre-sale link and code by email at 11:45 BST on Tuesday, and pre-sale opened shortly afterwards.

She added that the remaining tickets would be available to all on general sale.

This Symphony May Contain Hope show will showcase songs from her recent chart-topping second album, This Music May Contain Hope, that fuses old-school jazz with orchestral sound, blues, big band and soul.

The 17-track record is a concept album which explores overcoming heartbreak, self-doubt and internet trolling.

News.title: Katie Price denies 'any venom' against ex at his rape trial
News.content:
Katie Price has denied having "any venom" against her ex-husband at his rape trial.

Kieran Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one of sexual assault against a then-13-year-old girl in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.

When challenged by defence lawyer Arlette Piercy on her view of her ex-husband, Price said: "I don't have any venom against Kieran, it was amicable when we split."

Reality star Price also denied being "angry and vengeful" towards Hayler.

During her evidence to Lewes Crown Court, Price was asked by Piercy if she "loved revenge or is it just TV?".

"It's TV, it's what I say. It's what drives me in my work," Price said.

Piercy told Price: "You are angry and vengeful towards the defendant Kieran Hayler, you have evidenced a vendetta against him over a number of years."

Price responded: "That is not true."

Price also said she was using "a figure of speech" when she messaged the teenage girl allegedly raped by her then-husband.

Jurors had previously seen messages sent between Price and the girl, then aged 14, in which the media personality said she had heard Hayler and the girl kissed and he had "tried it on" with her, adding: "I'm only asking as this is a serious allegation."

The teenager replied that it was "just a flirt thing" and "nothing happened".

News.title: Paralympian on OnlyFans to make ends meet until 2028 Games is getting huge offers. But she’s not that type of girl
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A U.S. Paralympic athlete facing medical and living expenses while training for the 2028 Los Angeles Games has taken on an unconventional sponsorship deal: posting strictly safe-for-work content on OnlyFans while turning down five-figure offers to post adult content.

Catarina Guimaraes, a 22-year-old from Cranford, New Jersey, signed a $25,000 annual deal with the subscription platform best known for hosting adult entertainment, as reported by NJ.com.

Although her presence on the site has attracted substantial offers for adult content — including a $15,000 request for a single private video call — Guimaraes has drawn a firm line, refusing to post anything explicit.

“All my teammates were like, ‘You should totally take him up on [the call],’” Guimaraes said. “I was like, ‘Nooooo, that is not what I’m about.’ But it was crazy. I did not realize people would offer that much money for that stuff.”

Instead, the U.S. track and field athlete publishes behind-the-scenes workout videos, gym routines, personal updates and clips of herself singing Broadway songs to help promote the platform’s non-explicit sports tier, OnlyFans Sports.

open image in gallery Catarina Guimaraes, a US Paralympic athlete managing medical and living expenses while training for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, has accepted an unconventional sponsorship deal to post strictly non-explicit content on OnlyFans ( Getty Images )

Despite the platform’s reputation, Guimaraes maintains strict boundaries regarding her profile, which charges subscribers $10 per month.

“They basically offered to compensate me for posts on their platform and on my platform about them to bring a more wholesome view of their page,” Guimaraes said. “It isn’t anything racy, unless you want to count a video of me doing power cleans in a sports bra and shorts as racy.”

An OnlyFans spokesperson said in an email to NJ.com that the company “loves working with athlete creators who are excited about using the platform to connect with their audience while building a new revenue stream through their content.”

The financial support allows Guimaraes to manage the costs associated with her cerebral palsy while pursuing world-class training. The neurological condition affects muscle tone, posture and body movement, which Guimaraes describes as “having bad WiFi in your brain.”

“It’s like this constant fight to keep everything in sync,” she said.

open image in gallery Despite turning down a single $15,000 proposal for a private video call, the Team USA athlete says her $10-a-month profile features only gym workouts ( Getty Images )

Her father, John Guimaraes, emphasized that the financial backing allowed her to concentrate on her athletic performance.

“The idea behind this is to reduce her financial strain,” John Guimaraes told the publication. “When she wakes up, she shouldn’t be thinking, ‘Do I have enough gas money to get to the training center?’ It should be her training.”

Guimaraes’ path to international competition began early. Diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 3 after a neurologist in Portugal identified the condition, she pushed to join track events in elementary school.

“I’ve never met a 9-year-old who trained for a school race before,” Guimaraes said. “But I was at the track every other day, practicing and busting my butt, running sprints, ladders, just to get into this race.”

She lost her first race — “And I got my a** kicked,” she said. “I got smoked, like, completely” — but continued competing.

She eventually earned a second-degree black belt in taekwondo, joined an adaptive track club and went on to become the first NCAA Division I athlete with cerebral palsy after signing with High Point University.

Guimaraes represented Team USA at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, placing eighth in the long jump at Stade de France.

open image in gallery Guimaraes (right) represented Team USA at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, placing eighth in the long jump at Stade de France ( Getty Images for USOPC )

“It was like, ‘Oh my God, I’m at the Paralympics,” she said.

Currently based in Chula Vista, California, Guimaraes is balancing her training for the International Federation of Cerebral Palsy Football World Cup and the 2028 Los Angeles Games with coursework for a master’s degree in kinesiology from Louisiana State University.

Beyond athletics, Guimaraes built a social media following around female empowerment in sports, though her association with OnlyFans has brought drawbacks, including reach restrictions on Instagram. Still, she remains committed to presenting a balanced image on her platform.

“I really love the idea that you can be feminine and powerful and strong at the same time,” Guimaraes said. “I feel like people forget that. And that’s what my page has been about.”

The Independent has contacted OnlyFans for further comment.

News.title: Polymarket is already taking bets on when Trump’s pick Katie Zacharia will be out as press secretary
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A prediction market is already taking bets on when President Donald Trump’s pick for White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, will be out — and it’s not looking good for the conservative communications specialist.

Polymarket dropped a new question for traders shortly after Zacharia’s disastrous first press briefing Tuesday morning: When will she be canned?

As of Tuesday evening, the odds of her being ousted by the end of the month remain low at 8 percent. More money is being placed on her not making it into the new year. Zacharia had a 29 percent chance of leaving the White House by December 31.

Zacharia was visibly nervous behind the lectern Tuesday, compared to her predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, who often sparred with journalists. After stumbling through prepared remarks boasting about Trump’s perceived wins, Zacharia took questions from three conservative outlets and then wrapped up the quick 14-minute briefing.

Her job performance was ripped apart online, with some wondering if she will even last as long as ex-White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci, who held the position for a record-short stint of 10 days in 2017 during Trump’s first term.

open image in gallery A prediction market is already taking bets on when President Donald Trump’s pick for White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, will be out — and it’s not looking good for the conservative communications specialist ( Getty Images )

“What's the over/under that she doesn't last a Scaramucci?” criminal defense lawyer Scott Greenfield wrote on X.

Scaramucci also chimed in after independent journalist George Sisca suggested that Scaramucci would be happy about Zacharia’s performance “because his record might get broken.”

“Not me. I hope she makes it,” he wrote on X.

One former Trump official who remains close to people serving in the administration told The Independent’s Andrew Feinberg that Zacharia’s debut was “a train wreck” after previously describing her as a “joke hire” who’d likely be “gone in six months.”

open image in gallery Zacharia had a 29 percent chance of leaving the White House by December 31 on Polymarket Tuesday evening ( AFP via Getty Images )

White House Communications Director Steven Cheung commended Zacharia’s job, calling the briefing a “tremendous start.”

“She commanded the room and effectively reminded the American people of all the great work President Trump and his Administration has done thus far,” he wrote on X.

Zacharia served as senior communications advisor for Trump’s Truth Social platform before joining the White House press team, according to her LinkedIn profile.

She also previously worked as a commentator for Fox News and Newsmax and worked on the Department of Homeland Security press team from February to March.

open image in gallery Zacharia was visibly nervous behind the lectern Tuesday, compared to her predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, who often sparred with journalists ( AFP via Getty Images )

The White House went without a press secretary for more than a month after Leavitt left her post in late August to spend more time with her young family.

In that time, other members of the administration filled in for press briefings, including Vice President JD Vance and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

Trump told reporters before boarding Air Force One in late August that he was “going to miss” Leavitt.

“I have never had so many job applications in my life. They all want that job. They love that job. She’s made that job very glamorous,” Trump said, pointing to Leavitt next to him.

News.title: Fixer in lucrative NCAA basketball betting scheme sentenced to 6 years in prison
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A man charged with rigging college basketball games as part of an elaborate point-fixing scheme that raked in millions was sentenced to six years in federal prison, prosecutors in Pennsylvania announced on Tuesday.

It was the first penalty handed down as part of an investigation that revealed a sprawling network of professional gamblers and college basketball players who, prosecutors say, profited off fixed games.

Prosecutors said Jalen Smith, 30, played a “central role” in helping fix games in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 NCAA Division I basketball seasons, placing bets and recruiting players with the promise of a big payment for purposefully underperforming during a game, U.S. Attorney David Metcalf said on Tuesday. Bettors would then wager against the players’ teams in those games, defrauding sportsbooks and other gamblers, authorities said. Smith pleaded guilty earlier this year to bribery and wire fraud charges.

The sentencing comes at the start of the 2026-27 NCAA basketball season, when bettors will wager billions of dollars both legally and illegally on games nationwide. In the meantime, law enforcement, regulators and sports leagues have struggled to keep up with gambling's growing popularity in collegiate and professional sports alike.

“Today’s sentencing sends a clear message: Those who exploit professional and collegiate athletes for personal gain will be held accountable,” said Wayne A. Jacobs, special agent in charge of the FBI's Philadelphia office. “This conduct does more than harm individual athletes. It undermines the integrity of sports and the trust placed in fair competition.”

The point-shaving scheme Smith was involved in is said to have involved nearly 30 NCAA basketball games, and included schools like DePaul University, State University of New York at Buffalo and Tulane University, among others.

Prosecutors accused Smith and at least 26 other named defendants of wagering millions of dollars and paying hundreds of thousands of dollars to players in bribes. Payments to players typically ranged from $10,000 to $30,000 per game, according to an indictment.

Smith and others strategically targeted players considered “underdogs” in games, encouraging them to underperform in order to guarantee certain spreads. Those players were prime targets, prosecutors said, because they were offered money that exceeded potential income from legitimate sponsorships.

Smith, of Charlotte, North Carolina, trained and developed local basketball players for professional scouting combines and used those connections with players when he became part of the scheme, according to prosecutors.

The point-shaving scheme resulted in more than $3 million in fraudulent wagers. Smith, who also pleaded guilty to a separate felony gun possession charge, will have to pay $1.1 million in restitution, which prosecutors said is the cost incurred by gambling platforms as a result of the scheme.

Besides the fixers who recruited players and placed bets, the charges targeted over a dozen former college basketball players and four other players who were active with their college teams last season.

News.title: Even MAGA stalwart Lauren Boebert is speaking out against the Iran war
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rep. Lauren Boebert, an ally of President Donald Trump, has spoken out against the ongoing Iran war, describing it as “detrimental on many levels.”

The Colorado Republican made the remarks during a debate with Democrat challenger Eileen Laubacher on Monday, just three weeks out from Election Day.

She joins a small minority of GOP lawmakers who have openly criticized the Middle East conflict, which polls indicate is broadly unpopular and could dampen Republican prospects in the midterms.

“I never wanted us to be in war, at war in Iran,” Boebert said when asked whether the conflict has been worth the cost. “I do agree that this is expensive, and I hear from Republicans, unaffiliated and Democrats that they want this to come to an end, and so do I.”

“We are having conversations with the Department of War and with the president and his administration on a regular basis about how to come to an end with this,” she added.

Rep. Lauren Boebert, a Colorado Republican, has spoken out against the ongoing Iran war, describing it as ‘detrimental on many levels’ during a debate on Monday night ( Getty )

Still, Boebert said she supports Trump as the commander-in-chief, noting that “he is not the first president to use force.”

Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, portrayed Boebert’s vocal opposition to the war as insufficient, pointing out that she refused to vote for war powers resolutions that sought to curb Trump’s authority in Iran.

“Your job is to vote whether or not you think the war should continue, and Ms. Boebert has voted now, I believe, five times to keep this war going,” Laubacher said. “And so, you can say all day long that you don’t want there to be war and you want it to draw to a close, but you’re not using your voice to raise the voices of the people you describe in Congressional District 4 who are opposed to this war.”

Boebert previously voiced opposition to supplemental war funding in March. “I have folks in Colorado who can't afford to live. We need America First policies right now,” she said at the time.

The war, which began in late February when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, has now stretched on for seven months with no clear end in sight. Trump has repeatedly suggested it could come to a close soon.

The conflict has led to the deaths of at least 18 U.S. service members, cost taxpayers upwards of $30 billion, and spiked fuel prices across the country.

A recent poll indicates Boebert holds a narrow lead over Laubacher — 45 percent to 40 percent — in Colorado’s 4th congressional district.

News.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer after surgery to remove lower lobe of lung
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with cancer and has had the lower lobe of his right lung removed during surgery on Tuesday, according to the Vatican.

Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, the Vatican said. The diagnosis had been suspected during preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.

The 71-year-old pontiff spent around three hours in the operating room, and the surgery itself took around 90 minutes.

“In order to make the procedure curative, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique,” wrote lead surgeon Professor Stefano Margaritora.

"A rapid intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as had been suspected from the pre-operative tests.”

open image in gallery Pope Leo has been diagnosed with cancer after lung surgery on Tuesday ( Getty )

The Vatican said the surgery was successful and there were no complications. Afterwards, Pope Leo was awake and resting in his hospital room.

Dozens of well-wishers greeted him at the hospital before the procedure.

In a rare level of transparency, the Pope revealed the discovery of a small nodule on his lung during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.

A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3cm (1.2ins) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. The scans are often done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening.

A nodule may be benign or malignant, and surgical removal is often recommended to establish whether it is cancer, and to treat a malignancy while it is still localised.

Before the procedure, oncologists said that even if the growth proved to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis was “excellent” because it would be removed at an early stage.

open image in gallery Pope Leo XIV arriving at the Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic in Rome ( AP Photo/Alessandra Tarantino )

The Vatican has cancelled all of Leo’s audiences for a week while he recovers.

The Pope is known to be sporty and in good shape, playing tennis weekly and swimming. The lung surgery is believed to be his second spell in hospital.

He came down with typhoid fever as a young missionary priest in 1985, soon after arriving in Chulucanas, Peru. The illness and hospital stay were a cathartic moment for him to decide to stay in the poverty and discomfort of Peru after living in relative comfort in Rome — a decision that ultimately paved the way to his papacy, according to an interview he gave to Elise Ann Allen last year for Pope Leo XIV: The Biography.

According to the book, Leo said he prayed to God to let him die rather than suffer the “horrible” pain of the fever. “I was hooked up to an IV, and I said, ‘If this is your sense of humour, Lord, I think you could do a little better’.

“Obviously, I survived; I recovered, but it turned out to be a very significant moment for me, because it was like, ‘Well, you’ve already dealt with the illness; you already see what the needs are here — the order, the Augustinians, the church are telling you, ‘We need you here; go for it.’ I never looked back.”

News.title: Dolly Parton's nephew denies threatening to harm her estate, pushes back against restraining order
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Dolly Parton’s nephew and longtime head of security said in a Tennessee court filing Tuesday that he was a close friend and ally of Parton's longtime manager Danny Nozell before Nozell took out a restraining order accusing him of threatening to do violence and destroy Parton’s legacy and business empire.

In an affidavit opposing the temporary order becoming permanent, Bryan Seaver said text messages Nozell cited as evidence against him were a “private conversation between two friends who were both frustrated, grieving and discussing strategy." The text messages were sent shortly before and after Parton's Aug. 25 death.

Seaver said he never sent threatening messages to any of Parton’s businesses or business partners or their employees.

The filings represent Seaver’s first public defense of himself since a serious rift opened up in the country music legend’s circle and spilled into public view shortly after her death, with Nozell and Seaver on opposing sides.

Seaver's court filing says Nozell did not react with alarm to his text messages at the time and that he agreed with or reacted positively to some of them. Seaver says Nozell encouraged him to publicly tout the military and arms aspect of his security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, as a smart business-promotion move, then turned around and used them as evidence of Seaver's capacity for dangerous violence.

She's Alive, an entity run by Nozell and founded to manage and protect Parton’s estate, terminated Seaver and SAPS in early September, and the following week petitioned for the restraining order against him, arguing that his“terrorizing conduct made their continued retention untenable.”

In granting the temporary restraining order, Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles, cited Seaver's “claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate.”

The two sides will make their cases to Myles at a hearing on Oct. 20. Emails seeking comment were sent to lawyers for She's Alive and Nozell.

Seaver said he was blindsided by the order, which was granted while he was doing contract security work in Haiti.

Seaver and SAPS must refrain from entering any She’s Alive property or talking with or being within 1,000 feet (about 300 meters) of She’s Alive employees and business partners. The order is also meant to keep Seaver from interfering with its business relationships.

Seaver argued in his response that the order is so broad, and Parton's business reach so great, that much of Nashville and even his own relatives are off limits to him.

In one message written Sept. 1 that was cited by She's Alive, Seaver said: “I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f——— pay me.”

Seaver said his anger and the demand were only over more than $250,000 that his company was owed for completed work by Herschend Family Entertainment, which operates Parton’s amusement park Dollywood and her Songteller Hotel, which opened after her death.

Seaver acknowledged being overly crude and profane in his messages to Nozell. He said allegations that he had “menaced and intimidated” HFE employees were simply false.

He included as an exhibit a 2024 letter from Parton praising him and his company. Parton had handpicked Seaver to announce her death once she succumbed to cancer.

Parton was a widely beloved country music giant, philanthropist and cultural icon who wrote hundreds of songs, including classics such as “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors” and “I Will Always Love You.” Her music earned a total of more than 100 million worldwide sales and more than 1 billion online streams.

News.title: A Wyoming grad student who allegedly poisoned a colleague has been arrested fleeing to China
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Wyoming microbiology graduate student from China has been arrested on accusations she poisoned the tea of a fellow student who had pending patents and with whom she didn’t get along, then tried to flee the country after police questioned her.

Aili Wang, 32, was arrested the next day at Los Angeles International Airport, where prosecutors allege she sought to return to China. With her were laptops, electronic storage devices and documents now in the possession of police, who allege Wang was seen on surveillance video rummaging through the desk of the victim who specialized in research similar to what she once did in China.

Wang remained jailed without bail Tuesday in Los Angeles. She allegedly bought a chemical, acrylamide, over eBay, and it was first detected when the alleged victim’s wife and others tested water from the coffee maker he used to brew tea.

U.S. officials for years have accused China of stealing intellectual property from American universities.

News.title: Trump rails against ‘disgusting’ nemesis Letitia James handling Cornell rape investigation
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump on Tuesday demanded that New York Attorney General Letitia James be removed from an investigation into an alleged rape at Cornell University, calling the state’s top prosecutor a “disgusting cop” with “zero credibility.”

He posted to Truth Social that James’s involvement in the case would lead to automatic appeals and urged New York Gov. Kathy Hochul to replace her.

“How can ‘New York State Attorney General,’ Letitia James, be allowed to investigate the Cornell rape scandal, when she is a DIRTY AND DISGUSTING COP herself, and has ZERO credibility?” Trump posted. “Any decision will be appealed by her mere presence on this case. The stench of Letitia James will greatly add to the anguish that everybody feels in viewing how this case is being handled.

“The Governor should take James off this case, IMMEDIATELY, and replace her with somebody who is not a Third Rate, Crooked Politician!”

Earlier this month, Trump said he felt “badly” for the seven men accused of gang-raping a young woman at Cornell, as well as for the Ivy League school, the local district attorney and university police after Hochul appointed James to oversee investigations into the allegations and their handling.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump demanded on Truth Social that New York Attorney General Letitia James be removed from an investigation into an alleged rape at Cornell University — in his post, he called the state’s top prosecutor a ‘disgusting cop’ ( AFP/Getty )

James previously secured a civil fraud judgment against Trump and his business empire. Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg prosecuted the criminal case that led to Trump’s 2024 conviction on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records.

Speaking to reporters before departing the White House for Mobile, Alabama, Trump was asked by Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy about the case being assigned to James.

“Well, Letitia James is a corrupt person,” Trump said. “She’s totally corrupt, and I can’t imagine it. I feel badly for whoever she's looking at because they won't get a fair shake.”

The case gained national attention following a lawsuit filed by Jane Doe, the unnamed accuser, against the university over its response to her October 2024 rape complaint. The 101-page civil complaint, filed September 14, alleges she was sexually assaulted over several hours at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house in Ithaca, New York. According to the filing and disclosed text exchanges, fraternity members later discussed the incident in a group chat.

Trump had previously said that he was unfamiliar with the details of the case but trusted the administration, telling reporters: “Cornell's a fine school, and I'm sure they’ll do what's right.”

open image in gallery New York Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Attorney General Letitia James’s appointment on October 2, stating she had lost confidence in local police and the district attorney ( Getty )

Hochul announced James's appointment on October 2, stating she had lost confidence in local police and the district attorney.

“Newly released information continues to raise serious questions about the investigation conducted by the Cornell Police Department and the decision by the Tompkins County District Attorney not to prosecute an alleged sexual assault on Cornell University’s campus in October 2024,” Hochul said. “This has, in turn, undercut my faith, and the public’s faith, in the District Attorney’s ability to effectively investigate and prosecute the case at this time.”

Cornell officials have denied wrongdoing and rejected claims that the university mishandled the complaint. However, public outrage over the response of the school and local authorities has reignited debate surrounding campus sexual assault and legal definitions of consent.

Later on October 2, Trump reiterated his criticism in a post on Truth Social: “Why would the Governor of New York, Kathy Hochul, appoint a Corrupt Prosecutor, Letitia ‘Peekaboo’ James, to represent the State in the highly controversial Cornell University rape case?”

The president then traveled to Alabama for a campaign rally — part of a broader effort to boost Republican candidates ahead of next month’s midterm elections, following stops in Texas and Oklahoma.

News.title: Beaten Man Utd in crisis as Martinez launches lacerating attack on board
News.content:
And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of his dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s powerbrokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decision must now be called into question.

News.title: Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop
News.content:
The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: Donkey prices in Gaza skyrocket from $1,000 to $30,000
News.content:
The price of a donkey in Gaza has jumped from about $1,000 before the war to $30,000 today, according to one of the embattled enclave’s most senior vets.

The surge in the value of the pack animals is due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport in the strip and the emergence of a small group of black marketeers who have become hugely rich trading in intercepted aid.

The donkeys, whose number has been halved in the past three years, are also now in comparatively short supply.

“It’s a little bit crazy and people keep asking me ‘are you sure about that number?’”, Dr Ahmed Thabet, a Gazan veterinary surgeon told the Telegraph.

“They say ‘do you mean $3,000?’ but I tell them ‘no’. The average price of a donkey before the war was between $1,000 and $1,200. Recently it was $20,000 and last week I witnessed one that was sold for $30,000”.

News.title: The secret to the perfect holiday in Somerset
News.content:
Somerset’s landscapes are steeped in legend, from the lush fields of “Avalon” to Cheddar Gorge and the wilds of Exmoor. Its winding, country lanes lead to secrets and natural splendour. The local food scene is flourishing, too, involving everyone from Michelin-starred chefs to foragers on the Mendip Hills and farmers selling cheddar and cider from the barn door.

Glastonbury Festival shines as the centre of the musical universe in June – but the region is becoming known for much more than this. Quiet, agrarian villages are now fashionable places to spend time – I’m often found dawdling over a lazy brunch, browsing designer ceramics and paddleboarding down river. Bruton has an internationally renowned art gallery and the county’s hip, country house hotels – from Soho House-owned Babington House to The Newt – are some of the UK’s most desirable.

What makes Somerset so exciting is that it preserves a bucolic way of life while keeping its finger firmly on the pulse.

News.title: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle
News.content:
You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

News.title: AI cuts diagnosis for eye disease from 23 days to just 30 seconds
News.content:
Patients whose eye scans were read by an AI programme got results in 30 seconds, compared to facing an average waiting time of 23 days for results from a doctor, a study in Tanzania has shown.

Millions of people around the world have diabetic retinopathy, a condition where high blood sugar levels damage the tiny blood vessels in the retina.

It can lead to irreversible blindness if left untreated. Around a third of the 23 million people with diabetes in Africa have the complication.

In its early stages, diabetic retinopathy can have no symptoms, and the World Health Organization recommends that people living with diabetes undergo regular screening to check their eye health, so that they can be treated if necessary.

For the new study, published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers randomly assigned over 2,000 patients with diabetes visiting clinics in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions to either receive usual screening care, or to have a new type of AI-assisted screening.

Two fifths of the participants had changes in their eyes that needed referral to specialist care. In the half screened using AI, 36 per cent attended the central ophthalmology clinic within eight weeks, compared to 18 per cent in the standard care group.

Most of the people working in the regions where the study was based are farmers, said Dr Justus Rwiza of the Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, co-author on the paper. “They depend on vision.”

The economic effects of blindness are felt by the whole family, he said, recalling how the daughter of one patient “had to stop schooling to help the mother”.

News.title: WHO probes ‘unanswered questions’ over Russian plague worker
News.content:
The World Health Organization has said it still does not have enough information to rule out a lab accident after the death of a worker in a Russian plague lab.

Last week reports emerged that Darya Shipilova, a lab worker in Irkutsk, Siberia, had died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube containing samples of the pathogen Yersinia pestis, which causes the disease.

Some 200 people were quarantined and there were reports of a further case. Shipilova was working at the Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk.

Russian authorities have insisted that there was no lab accident and Shipilova’s mother, Svetlana, has also disputed that her daughter dropped a test tube.

“It’s impossible to break a test tube like that,” she said. “Even if you fling it at the wall. Only an amateur could say something like that,” she said.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez savages Man Utd owners and says club weren't ready for Champions League
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez savages Man Utd owners and says club weren't ready for Champions League

Manchester United slipped to their fourth defeat of the season against Atletico Madrid with defender Lisandro Martinez issuing a withering assessment of the goings on at Old Trafford

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez speaks after Man Utd's loss at Atletico Madrid

Lisandro Martinez tore into Manchester United's hierarchy in the aftermath of their defeat to Atletico Madrid.

‌



‌



The Red Devils slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign in Spain on Tuesday night. They had a woeful start with Pablo Barrios giving Atletico the lead within the opening minute.

‌



Ademola Lookman doubled the lead shortly after Leny Yoro's red card. The defeat leaves United with just two wins in all competitions this season.

‌



But Martinez has suggested that the fault is not with the players and instead took aim at those running the club.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking to Amazon Prime Video, he said: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

"I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

‌



View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was furious after Man United's defeat against Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Asked which areas could have been strengthened, the Argentine defender said: "In general. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

"It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here."

‌



Asked if any of the fault could be with boss Michael Carrick: "I don't think so. He does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can't say more. Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

United spent around £150m strengthening their side in the summer ahead of Carrick's first full season at the helm, albeit all of their investment came in midfield. Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos were signed from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively, while Carlos Baleba completed a big-money move from Brighton.

‌



View 3 Images Jason Wilcox was the target of Martinez's furious rant (Image: Getty Images)

Tielemans was asked about Martinez's comments after the full-time whistle but simply replied: “I’ve got no comment on that.”

United boss Carrick was also probed about Martinez's comments. He said:"I haven't seen it. After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time to comment.

‌



"We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through."

United icon Wayne Rooney also spoke out on Martinez's comments and criticised the former Ajax man for his rant, particularly with United in such a difficult spot. He said: "It's disrespectful to his team-mates, he's saying his team-mates aren't good enough.

"I think Bruno is the only one who has the right to say this. That interview is not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick’s dream is turning into a nightmare as Man Utd left with Atletico regrets
Sports.content:
Manchester United's tricky start to the season continued against Atletico Madrid as they slipped to defeat at the Metropolitano.

Diego Simeone's side took the lead after mere seconds through Pablo Barrios. The Spanish side thought they had doubled their lead moments before the break as Johnny Cardoso swept home, only to see the goal ruled out following a VAR review.

United's evening then got even more difficult in the second-half as VAR intervened again to see Leny Yoro sent off for a last-man challenge on Jonathan David, with Ademola Lookman then scoring to extend the Spanish side's lead.

The defeat leaves Carrick under real pressure heading into what could potentially be a decisive Premier League showdown with Leeds this weekend.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

DREAM TURNING INTO A NIGHTMARE

Michael Carrick will have been desperate for a fast start in Madrid in an effort to lift the gloom. He got exactly the opposite, with the home side opening the scoring after less than a minute.

Alex Baena was released behind the Red Devils defence and instead of going on his own, he elected to wait for support before rolling the ball across for Barrios. In acres of space, he rolled home via a touch off of Ayden Heaven.

‌



And while United did eventually manage to find a foothold in the game, their efforts were then all-but ruined midway through the second half as Yoro took down Jonathan David as the last man. Lookman then tucked home from close range to make it 2-0.

After Nicky Butt's claims that Carrick did not want to go into management unless it was United, the current boss might feel that he maybe should have stuck to that claim regardless of employer.

View 3 Images Pablo Barrios celebrates his early opener for Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

UNITED GIVEN VAR REPRIEVE

United had a number of lucky breaks in Madrid and given their fortune so far this season, they might have felt they were due a bit of luck. Their first escape saw defender Alex Grimaldo hit the post from a brilliant free kick.

‌



But it was the VAR review on the stroke of half-time that saw them breathe the biggest sigh of relief. Atletico thought they had doubled their lead through Cardoso, who swept home a brilliant effort.

But United instantly appealed for a handball by Marcos Llorente earlier in the move, with Ayden Heaven and Bruno Fernandes in particular leading the appeals.

The game was incidently stopped and the referee chalked the strike off. It looked to be a harsh call, with the ball bouncing off of Llorente's thigh and onto his arm before it hit Heaven's hand. Cardoso still had plenty to do to find the net.

Either way, the decision went in United's favour. As did Julian Alvarez's spectacular second-half attempt that hit the post.

‌



View 3 Images Leny Yoro was sent off for a last-man challenge on Jonathan David (Image: Getty Images)

WASTEFUL RED DEVILS

While United have fallen to another defeat, that was not due to a lack of effort or creativity in Madrid - quite the opposite. Carrick's men actually created an array of presentable chances but were unable to take them.

Bryan Mbeumo twice went close in the first-half as he at first rolled an effort wide, while he also saw an drive parried away by Jan Oblak.

Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes also went close, the latter lifting an chipped effort just wide. The Portuguese playmaker then struck the woodwork. Matheus Cunha should also have at least found the net in stoppage time but saw his effort saved.

‌



But in the end, if you don't put the ball in the net, you're not going to get many wins.

Sports.title: Luis Enrique delivers clear Man City punishment wish ahead of Champions League clash
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique delivers clear Man City punishment wish ahead of Champions League clash

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules during 2009 and 2018

View 2 Images Luis Enrique has spoken out about Man City's financial charges case (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique hopes Manchester City can avoid punishment for breaking rules, insisting that the club deserve credit for their trophy-winning success in recent years. City remain at the centre of an unprecedented financial charges case after being found guilty by an independent commission of 114 Premier League charges.

‌



‌



The Premier League alleged that the club used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their revenues by £900million. However, City continue to deny any wrongdoing, maintaining their innocence and citing 'irrefutable evidence' to support their defence.

‌



An independent commission will oversee the case, with an outcome expected before the end of the year. A key part of City's defence is understood to be that the sponsorship deals were legitimate and funded by the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

‌



Football regulator David Kogan says he will QUIT if Andy Burnham interferes in Man City case READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca's side returned to Premier League action for the first time since the verdict, securing a 3-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday. As expected, the Cityzens were met with boos and jeers as they stepped onto the pitch at Anfield following the international break.

Their attention has since turned to their Champions League clash against the reigning European champions, PSG. The French champions' boss, Enrique, was quizzed about the ongoing charges against the club.

Enrique and former City boss Guardiola, who played alongside each other at Barcelona, have both established themselves as two of the most successful managers in modern football. Guardiola has won numerous trophies during his time at the Etihad, and Enrique was full of praise for the 'incredible' work done by his compatriot, suggesting he'd like to see City avoid sanctions.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"There is a lot of noise around Manchester City and there is often noise around big clubs," Enrique said.

"We have just have to wait and see what the final decision will be. I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win on the pitch all the trophies they have won.

‌



"Now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say."

View 2 Images Guardiola and Enrique

He added: "The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction.

‌



"But we have to wait. The things I will say to Pep I will do in private."

There have been calls for City to face severe punishment should their appeal fail, including expulsion from the Premier League.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta's massive gamble pays off but struggling Arsenal star fluffs his chance
Sports.content:
This was some turnaround and proof there is no substitute for proven quality.

Arsenal blitzed Lille with a three-goal second half salvo from Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka as the Gunners maintained their winning start in the Champions League.

But it needed Mikel Arteta to bring on the big guns to really seal the win after a frustrating hour in which a much-changed line-up struggled before it eventually became very comfortable.

It now sets up Arsenal for their heavyweight clash at Bayern Munich next week but it also showed they are on a mission in Europe this season.

‌



There is a sense of unfinished business in the Champions League for Mikel Arteta after losing last season’s final to Paris Saint Germain.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arteta almost left his last sentence hanging before the match as he talked about regrets, falling below their usual standards in Budapest last May and trying to go one better this time.

‌



They certainly delivered a statement of intent as they won their first Champions League tie at Napoli and this felt like a big opportunity to keep the momentum going against French club Lille.

But Arteta gambled by changing half of his outfield starting line-up - and, for much of the match, it looked like it was in serious danger of backfiring.

They looked like strangers against what was, quite frankly, a very average looking Lille side as the fresh faces struggled to seize their opportunities.

In came Timber, Bruno Guimaraes, Eze, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres from the team which beat Leeds on Saturday. You might have thought Gyokeres would be chomping at the bit after his frustrating start to the season but he looked miles off it.

‌



View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres failed to deliver on a rare start for Arsenal

They missed chances in a very dull first half and you could sense the frustration beginning to build inside the Emirates.

It took Arsenal 20 minutes to even have a shot. Gyokeres fed Timber and his pull back set up Guimaraes who, despite his goalscoring supersub heroics on Saturday, had mislaid his shooting boots this time and fired wide.

Two minutes later, Timber was at it again as his cross found Merino but his header was straight at Lille keeper Berke Ozer. Merino normally eats up those sort of headed chances.

‌



Merino was having an off night and the frustration got to him as he was booked for a blatant trip on Lille forward Ayase Ueda.

That was the story of Arsenal’s night. They were lacking in rhythm and momentum. Then it all changed with three goals in the space of seven minutes.

The first came after 64 minutes. Madueke’s short pass found Timber who turned neatly and then fired a cross shot into the far corner to break the deadlock.

View 3 Images Eberechi Eze made it two for Arsenal

‌



Suddenly the mood inside the Emirates changed. Arteta also brought on the big guns as Saka came on and his low cross was swept home by Eze who scored his first of the season.

Then it got even better after 71 minutes. Arsenal substitutes Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard combined beautifully to set up Saka whose low shot flew into the far corner to make it 3-0.

When he needed them most, the big guns stepped up from the bench to maintain Arteta’s perfect start to the Champions League campaign.

There was a late cameo for Lille’s former Arsenal striker Olivier Giroud who came on to a mixed reception after his defection to Chelsea.

‌

Sports.title: Liverpool and Chelsea alerted as Alex Scott January transfer gets green light
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Chelsea alerted as Alex Scott January transfer gets green light

Alex Scott was linked with a move away from Bournemouth in the summer but it appears that a switch could potentially be on the cards in the upcoming winter window

View 2 Images Alex Scott is out of contract in 2028 (Image: Getty Images)

Bournemouth are ‘open’ to selling Alex Scott in January, with Premier League rivals now circling. The former Bristol City midfielder was linked with a move away from the South Coast in the summer after rejecting two new contract offers.

‌



‌



But the Cherries remained firm in their intent to keep Scott at the Vitality Stadium despite an attempt from Chelsea. It appears that a fresh switch could now be on the cards.

‌



According to BBC Sport, Bournemouth are now open to selling Scott if an offer in the region of £100m is lodged for his services. Chelsea remain interested, while Liverpool are keeping an eye on developments.

‌



Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham were all thought to be interested in the summer but have shifted their focus elsewhere. Liverpool could be among the frontrunners for Scott’s services given the presence of former boss Andoni Iraola at Anfield.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But there remains one potential stumbling block in any potential deal and that is Bournemouth’s place in the Premier League. It is suggested that if the Cherries are struggling towards the end of the table then they may look to keep Scott to ensure their survival and then re-evaluate their position in the summer.

Scott, 23, joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023 and he has gone on to score seven goals in 95 appearances in all competitions. He is currently sidelined with a thigh injury he picked up on international duty with England.

“It's an injury from a muscle, and we'll do pictures [scans] in some days again,” boss Marco Rose said at the time.

‌



“But we're going to miss him, for sure, for four or five weeks. I'm very disappointed and it's a big loss. We miss a very important player, but I don't want to blame anyone.

View 2 Images Scott made his debut for England during the most recent international break (Image: Getty Images)

“We are very happy that he made his debut for the English national team. He did well and we just hope that he is getting fit again quite soon.”

Article continues below

Scott’s current deal with Bournemouth is set to run until the summer of 2028. Should he leave, he would become the latest high-profile player to depart Bournemouth over recent seasons.

Antoine Semenyo, Ilya Zabarnyi, Dean Huijsen, Milos Kerkez and Dango Outarra all chose to depart last season, while Dominic Solanke left for Spurs 12 months before. That has seen Bournemouth turn a huge profit when it comes to transfers over the past few seasons.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid star pulls out of Man Utd Champions League match after mum's death
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid star pulls out of Man Utd Champions League match after mum's death

Atletico Madrid will be without their captain when they play Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday, following the death of his mother

View 3 Images Koke's mother died ahead of the game (Image: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid captain Koke has pulled out of his side's Champions League clash with Manchester United following the death of his mother. Ana Merodio Borja died early on Tuesday in Madrid, Atletico said.

‌



‌



The Spanish side will wear black armbands for the clash against Premier League opposition, and a moment of silence will take place at the Metropolitano Stadium ahead of kick-off.

‌



Koke, full name Jorge Resurrección, is joined by his brother, Borja, at Atletico. The latter is the assistant coach of the La Liga giants' under-19 side.

‌



A moment of silence was observed ahead of their side's UEFA Youth League match against United, with Atletico coming away 3-0 victors.

View 3 Images Koke's mother passed away on Tuesday (Image: @koke6/Instagram)

‌



Manchester United paid their respects on social media: "Manchester United is saddened by the passing of Ana Merodio Borja, beloved mother of Atletico de Madrid captain Koke and U19s assistant coach Borja Resurrección.

"We offer our condolences to the family at this difficult time and invite supporters to join the two teams in a minute’s silence ahead of kick-off tonight."

View 3 Images Manchester United line up on the touchline for a minute's silence in a tribute to the mother of Koke (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

United will hope to be victorious in Champions League action, having recorded their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years under Michael Carrick. The Red Devils have picked up just six points from as many matches in the Premier League.

Carrick led his team to victory in their first European match of the season when his side defeated Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford. The Premier League side overcame their Spanish rivals in pre-season, claiming a 2-1 victory as Bryan Mbeumo scored a brace after the team had gone 1-0 down.

‌



United are without Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo for the clash after picking up issues against Tottenham. They have not made the trip to Spain, but Dutch defender Matthijs de Ligt has after almost a year out of action.

"We're not light on numbers, no," said Carrick. "Of course, we've got a couple of issues with some players missing out but we're definitely not light on numbers. It's good for Dan [Armer] to be part of it and for younger players to sample it, the build-up to the game, and get a sense of it.

"It's good to have Matta in and around it. We've had a little bit of patience with him, working through that and working hard to get to this stage. He's had a long journey so we're delighted to have him back."
