Sports.title: Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester United
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick had seen it in his players, he said, but no one else can. Not so far in the Premier League, where they have suffered their worst start in 40 years, and not here in Madrid, where Manchester United’s head coach insisted they would embrace the challenge. The reaction was coming, he promised; he had looked at them and was sure of it. Instead, they were a goal down after just 53 seconds and all that came was the old familiar sting, that early opener from Pablo Barrios and a second from Ademola Lookman condemning them to another defeat.

So much for a reaction, a rebellion: in their place a kind of resignation, a sense that maybe this is just United’s reality: a game that began badly, did not get very much better, and finished even worse. True, the result could have been different, Bryan Mbeumo unable to convert two first-half chances while Bruno Fernandes struck the bar and put an opportunity wide, but that did not diminish the feeling that something is really wrong. It may even have deepened it.

Even the late, harsh red card for Leny Yoro which can be offered in mitigation did not change a simple fact: at the end of another insipid night, United lost. United are lost, perhaps.

“Sometimes when it’s not quite going for you, you see who’s really there,” United’s manager said the night before, a message that perhaps hinted at something rotten beneath the surface, but on the opening goal no one was really there. They weren’t there on the left, where Lee Kang-in’s pass sent Álex Baena into a wide-open space; they weren’t there to close him down as he cut into the area; and they weren’t there on the right either, where Barrios was running through alone. Baena laid across and Barrios’s shot went off Ayden Heaven and into the net.

Barrios held up six fingers, the number of the club captain, Koke, whose mother had died in the hours before kick-off. From the bench Koke’s shirt was raised. All around the Metropolitano, supporters roared. This was set, it seemed.

Although another effort from Baena soon hit Lisandro Martínez, United did find a foothold and could have found a way back. Mbeumo had two clear chances in quick succession: the first, after nice footwork on the right, went wide; the second, following a neat exchange with Youri Tielemans, was stopped by Jan Oblak on the other side. From the corner, Carlos Baleba headed straight at the keeper.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes reacts after Manchester United concede a second goal, scored by Ademola Lookman. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

That was short-lived, though, Atlético soon asserting themselves, moving the ball with a pace and conviction United couldn’t match. Barrios and Baena couldn’t be controlled, and the spaces they opened were vast. The pressure United applied tended to arrive late or not at all. On the touchline too the contrast was stark: Diego Simeone prowled, Carrick stood motionless in the corner of his technical area, chin in his hand. The Argentinian was booked for waving an imaginary card. Maybe United’s manager could try that. Something, anyway.

By half-time, Atlético had enjoyed 66% of possession. They could also have had a greater lead. Álex Grimaldo rattled a superb free‑kick off the bar and just before the break Johnny Cardoso’s sweeping finish was ruled out when the video assistant referee revealed a Marcos Llorente handball in the buildup. The second half then began with a neatly floated ball from Barrios setting up Julián Álvarez to volley against a post. Again, the space, time and the ease with which the move played out was just too big.

At the other end, Bruno Fernandes then had a wonderful opportunity to level it. Tielemans did superbly to find him, the ball sitting up and Oblak coming off his line to meet him – the kind of opportunity, in short, that is supposed to end only one way but that this time ended another.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United’s captain lifted the ball past the keeper and wide. Soon, Atlético were back again, Baena bending a shot wide, although Atlético appeared to have settled, the game drifting. That perhaps suited United: with Atlético’s threat no longer so present, the ball was theirs for the first time and the lead was still only one, opportunity there. Fernandes, increasingly involved, swung a shot against the bar.

View image in fullscreen Leny Yoro trudges off after being shown a red card. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Which was when it finally, definitively and far too easily fell apart. Suddenly, on 74 minutes, Jonathan David was running through the middle on to a Morten Hjulmand ball. Yoro went with him, grappling as they ran, and the pair fell. Although Glenn Nyberg didn’t give a foul, allowing the move to play out with David scrambling the ball to Lookman, a voice in his ear called him to the screen to watch the challenge again. When he returned, he had a red in his hand.

The decision felt harsh. It was also the end. Three minutes later, Atlético were running through United again. Grimaldo slotted a pass into David, inside the area and, although his shot was saved by Senne Lammens, Lookman was there to score. Heaven and Fernandes were removed; this was done, nothing left to fight for, not that they had fought much in the first place, the reaction postponed for some other day.

Sports.title: James and Russo lead rout of Greece as ruthless England set up Ukraine playoff
Sports.content:
A mercurial Lauren James scored two and provided an assist in a thrilling four-goal first 45 minutes against Greece, as England put themselves two games away from securing their place at the World Cup.

James’s double was matched by Alessia Russo, who scored either side of the break, and her Arsenal ­teammate Georgia Stanway was also on the scoresheet, with the Lionesses setting up a playoff final against Ukraine in November and December. It was a clinical and slick statement from England, albeit against a team they should bypass with ease.

Any Greek hopes of arriving in Leicester and launching a Trojan horse-style smash and grab, after a hugely impressive performance in their 3-1 defeat by an ­unconvincing Lionesses team in Crete, were quickly dashed.

Sarina Wiegman had said on the eve of the game that she wanted to see improvement in the final third. In the King Power Stadium, which had a club vibe to it before kick-off as dance remix after dance remix blared out, the Lionesses responded to their manager’s call, Russo producing the first goal from the first shot and first attack in the third minute.

James was the architect, the ­Chelsea player driving forward and picking out the No 9, who shrugged clear of Eleni Markou’s challenge before firing a low shot in.

View image in fullscreen Alessia Russo gets England up and running with a third-minute goal. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

It was Russo’s fourth goal in four games for club and country, with the Arsenal forward having gone five Women’s Super League games without a goal before this run, and it was a sign of things to come from a team keen to shake off criticism of their lack of ruthlessness.

James was in majestic form, her injury worries behind her this season, and England fans were treated to a glimpse of what they missed at the Euros in Switzerland in 2025, when a less than half-fit James struggled and looked frustrated as her body failed to meet her demands on it.

James has said that the best is yet to come from her and Wiegman agreed. “I think so,” said the manager. “She was really enjoying herself, scored some great goals, but also picked up some great positions. I thought she looked really fresh and played well.”

On the Chelsea forward’s use more centrally, having previously been preferred in a wider role, Wiegman said: “As a winger or inverted winger she does similar things. She can play any position up front, right or left, because she’s right- and left-footed. When she plays on the outside she also gets the opportunity to come inside, and I think she can do both things then, and that’s when she comes to life.”

James delivered England’s ­second and fourth in Leicester, her two first-half goals sandwiching ­Stanway’s header into the far corner from ­Lauren Hemp’s chipped cross.

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway heads in England’s third goal as they swiftly put the result beyond doubt. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

For her first, the 25-year-old ­cushioned Maya Le Tissier’s pass before sending a rising drive goalwards with her left foot. Her second was far simpler, the unmarked forward turning in Hemp’s ball from close range.

Job well and truly done, James was withdrawn at half-time in favour of Beth Mead, Wiegman’s jewel safely nestled back in a velvet pouch after shining so brightly.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wiegman leapt on the opportunity presented by the 7-1 aggregate scoreline to rotate ­further at the hour mark, with Niamh Charles, Jess Park and Freya Godfrey given a chance to demonstrate why they should be on the plane to Brazil should England overcome Ukraine.

Whether the changes took the sting out of the game or England just eased back on the intensity given the margin did not really matter because the home team remained in complete control of the ball. Their more than 50-place superiority in the Fifa world rankings was far more ­evident in Leicester than it had been in Heraklion.

Russo was the beneficiary of ­England’s patience as the clock ticked down, collecting Keira Walsh’s angled pass before she raced clear, stepped around Styliani ­Katergiannaki in the Greece goal and rolled the ball into the empty net.

“I think today we played a lot better,” said Wiegman. “We totally dominated the game … As soon as we got in behind and we scored that goal that helped and I think after that we were really, really good in the final third.”

Ultimately, despite the performance put on there is very little to be learned from a game against a team so far below England’s level. Any slip-up would only ever have been of England’s own making, as the poor defending for Greece’s goal in Crete demonstrated. However, perhaps that sluggishness could be ­attributed to a rustiness after a four-month break from international football.

Ukraine are up next, the homeless team preparing to face the European champions after a 4-1 aggregate defeat of Slovakia.

England met Ukraine in their World Cup qualifying group earlier in the year and secured a 9-1 margin across the two matches, so it would take the most almighty of collapses for the Lionesses to fail to book their place in Brazil now.

Sports.title: Timber’s touch of class and supersub Saka secure Arsenal win against Lille
Sports.content:
Twelve wins in a row and counting. On a night when Arsenal remembered Ken Friar – the club’s life president who was instrumental in their move from Highbury to the Emirates in 2006 – it was fitting that Mikel Arteta’s side should rack up yet another Champions League milestone at their home that has become a fortress.

Such has Arsenal’s dominance been here in recent seasons that when Bukayo Saka slotted home their third against a dogged Lille side, it was the 36th goal they have scored at the Emirates in the league or group stage since returning to Europe’s top table under Arteta three years ago. In those 12 wins, they have remarkably conceded only three times.

Arsenal have also now racked up 14 successive league-stage victories in this competition – three short of Bayern Munich’s record – even if Arteta’s side were made to work for this one and had to wait until the 64th minute to find the breakthrough. That came from the unlikely source of Jurriën Timber after Arsenal’s second-string attack – and Viktor Gyökeres in particular – had looked laboured. But while Arteta may be concerned that it needed the introduction of Saka from the bench along with Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz to put this game to bed as Eberechi Eze added a second before Saka rounded off the scoring with a third in the space of seven minutes, they never looked in any danger of losing their proud record as Olivier Giroud received a standing ovation on his return to north London.

“I’m sure he is very happy to see how the boys played. But not only that, because I know how proud he felt about what we built,” said Arteta of Friar. “It’s a really sad day for everyone who loves football. The legacy that Ken is going to leave for this club is going to be for ever.”

Arsenal had earlier paid tribute to Friar, who worked his way up from the box office to club secretary before becoming managing director in the 1980s, when his death at the age of 92 was confirmed. The players wore black armbands as a mark of respect. Friar would have been especially proud of their formidable record here under Arteta in this competition that stretches back to the 2023-24 season, when they returned to the tournament after an absence of six years. It is little wonder that Arteta was so reluctant for redevelopment plans to go ahead given the disruption any temporary move away to Wembley or elsewhere would have caused.

Despite the absence of Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi after they were both injured during the warm-down after the victory over Leeds on Saturday, the Arsenal manager was still able to make five changes. Lille’s manager, Davide Ancelotti, who worked under his father, Carlo, at Everton and Real Madrid among others before being appointed during the summer in only his second senior role, resisted the temptation to start with 40-year-old Giroud against his former club.

View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka slots home Arsenal’s third goal from close range. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Restored to his favoured right flank after excelling on the left against Leeds, it had not been saying much that Noni Madueke had once again been Arsenal’s most dangerous outlet in a first half in which they struggled to create much against a deep-lying defence.

Bruno Guimarães and then Mikel Merino spurned decent chances, while Ayase Ueda had the ball in David Raya’s net after Nabil Bentaleb’s shot deflected off Timber and hit Hákon Haraldsson on the way through, with the video assistant referee confirming the Japan striker was marginally offside.

But Arsenal lacked creativity without Ødegaard and Gyökeres showing plenty of hustle and bustle yet making little real impact.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It summed Arsenal’s first half up when he could not get out of the way after Eze forced Berke Ozer into his first proper save and was promptly flagged offside. Ozer then had to scramble the ball away from the feet of the Sweden striker after spilling a shot from Guimarães on the stroke of half-time.

The referee, Felix Zwayer, waved away appeals at the start of the second half when Guimarães went down in the area under pressure from Alexsandro but the Arsenal midfielder seemed to be looking for the contact. A wayward effort that almost made it into the upper tier from Madueke was the signal for Arteta to summon Ødegaard, Saka and Havertz to get ready.

Before they had time to be introduced, Arsenal finally found the breakthrough when Madueke picked out Timber to apply a deft finish with his right foot after a brilliant first touch. Saka made an immediate impact by setting up Eze to dispatch the second with his left foot – possibly with the help of a deflection – less than three minutes later, before adding a third after combining with Havertz and Ødegaard. Lille must have wondered what had hit them.

As well as the chance to pay their respects to Giroud, the Arsenal fans were treated to a late cameo from the dazzling Max Dowman to round off another very satisfying evening that has become the norm.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: racist chanting mars Swansea’s win at Millwall
Sports.content:
Substitute Ronald scored a last-minute winner to keep Swansea top of the Championship after their match at Millwall was held up for almost seven minutes due to a complaint about racist chanting at the Den.

The referee, Edward Duckworth, halted the match in the 65th minute and walked to the dugouts to speak with Lions manager, Alex Neil, Swans counterpart Vítor Matos and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo.

A security guard was also on the scene, with the referee seeming to point to an area in the stands behind the Swansea dugout. When play eventually resumed it was announced in the stadium that there had been a report of racist chanting, adding that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.

But the unsavoury incident could not take the gloss off a dramatic last-gasp 1-0 victory for the table-toppers.

The Brazilian defender Neto Borges bagged a dramatic injury-time winner after earlier scoring an own goal as high-flyers Middlesbrough secured a thrilling 3-2 victory over battling Stoke.

The 30-year-old netted his first league goal for 18 months as Boro stay second in the table after stretching their current unbeaten run to five games.

Callum Brittain had fired the visitors ahead three minutes into the second half before Junior Tchamadeu’s shot deflected in off Borges for an unfortunate own goal soon afterwards.

The England Under-21 hitman Will Lankshear restored the visitors’ lead with his eighth league goal in 10 games after Stoke keeper Viktor Johansson inexplicably spilled Brighton loanee Amario Cozier-Duberry’s left-foot strike from the edge of the area. It took the striker to the top of the Championship scoring charts.

Substitute Robert Bozenik looked to have earned the home side a point, slotting home after Boro skipper Luke Ayling’s poor clearance with five minutes left, but Borges scored from close range in the first of four minutes of stoppage time.

View image in fullscreen Neto Borges fires in Middlesbrough’s winner. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Watford’s woeful season took another turn for the worse as they conceded four first-half goals in a 5-1 defeat at Cardiff to drop into the relegation zone.

Rising Republic of Ireland star Jack Moylan scored twice in the first half, winning and converting an 11th-minute penalty and then picking his spot to beat Federico Ravaglia in a one-on one in the 35th.

Hornets skipper Mattie Pollock had brought down Moylan for the penalty and then headed into his own net from a corner in the 41st minute before Ollie Tanner added the fourth in the fifth minute of first-half added time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Birmingham underlined their growing promotion credentials with a commanding 4-0 victory over 10-man Preston at St Andrew’s. Two goals from August Priske and one each for Liam Millar and Demarai Gray gave Chris Davies’ men a third win in four games – and their first at home. Preston, who played most of the second half with 10 men, remain rooted to the bottom of the table.

Ivan Mesik scored a dramatic last-gasp leveller for Charlton to clinch a 2-2 draw at Burnley, extending the hosts’ 360-day wait for a home league win. Largie Ramazani’s 57th-minute goal put Burnley into a 2-1 lead at Turf Moor, but substitute Mesik denied equalised with virtually the last kick of an absorbing contest.

West Brom staged a dramatic late revival to beat Wrexham 2-1 at Stok Cae Ras. Kieffer Moore’s stunning second-half strike gave Wrexham hope that they could claim back-to-back home wins for the first time since February. But West Brom scored twice in five minutes through Isaac Price and Aune Heggebo to stop the rot after derby defeats to Wolves and Birmingham.

Wolves suffered their first home league defeat of the season as Bolton won 3-1 at Molineux. Atsuki Ito gave Steven Schumacher’s visitors a deserved 28th-minute lead and although Jean-Ricner Bellegarde equalised five minutes after the break, substitute Sam Dalby and Josh Sheehan struck in the last 20 minutes to seal victory.

A magnificent goalkeeping display from Balazs Toth inspired Blackburn to a 1-0 victory over Bristol City at Ashton Gate. Toth was simply unbeatable on the night, making a string of outstanding saves, particularly in the first half. Oladapo Afolayan rifled home the only goal in the 38th minute.

Sports.title: Football regulator chair insists he will resign if politically pressured over Manchester City
Sports.content:
The chair of the Independent ­Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan, has said he will resign if he faces any political pressure on how to respond to Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, insisting “my independence is absolute”.

Kogan could remove City’s Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) should the damning verdict of an independent commission be upheld at the end of an ongoing appeal process. ­Concern had been raised, however, that the proximity of City’s ­ownership to Abu Dhabi’s rulers could trigger a political intervention by the UK ­government and an immediate test of the new regulator’s powers.

Those concerns have been rebuffed by Kogan. “Our independence is absolute and my independence personally is absolute,” he said. “I [have] made it very clear … any form of political interference on the way we operate is going to result in my resigning from this role, and I stand by that completely. And, just to be crystal clear, we’ve come under absolutely no political pressure whatsoever on this or any other topic.”

Kogan was speaking on Tuesday at the launch of the long-awaited State of the Game report, a document that lays out the financial challenges facing the English football pyramid. The City case has cast a huge shadow as the regulator prepares to introduce a new licensing regime for clubs later this season. “We have powers within the legislation that allow us to review not only owners and directors and senior executives, but also whether those owners are fit and proper ­people to run clubs going forward,” said Kogan, describing the process by which the regulator might intervene.

“That process is reliant on us ­having very detailed knowledge and information, which requires a ­certain amount of investigation. Then we would take judgments based on the legal advice that we then receive.”

Should a club owner ultimately be found to have failed a “fitness” test related to “integrity, honesty and financial soundness”, the regulator could force the club to be sold. “We deal with issues of this type much more frequently than you might realise because we are constantly looking at clubs,” Kogan said, stating if any decision by the regulator became the subject of legal action then clubs would be asked to foot the bill through a funding levy.

View image in fullscreen David Kogan reiterated that the regulator had powers to determine whether owners such as Manchester City’s were ‘fit and proper’. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

The acceleration of revenues among the Premier League’s biggest clubs is one of the key findings in the State of the Game report. The highest earning top-flight club currently earns 605 times the revenue of the lowest earning National League club. At the same time, spending has increased at all levels of the game, with 94% of the 116 clubs under the regulator’s regime posting a financial loss in 2025-26. In one particularly eye-catching statistic, the report found 11 Football League clubs recorded costs that exceeded their income even once player wages had been stripped out.

Kogan argued that a number of external factors that fall outside the regulator’s purview are affecting the game, including the expansion of the club calendar, the regulation of ­players’ agents and the recent rise in interest rates. However, he argued that one key measure – the agreement of a redistribution deal between the Premier League and EFL – could unlock change immediately.

While Kogan accepts the Premier League’s argument regarding the need for parachute payments due to “colossal” drops in revenue caused by relegation, he believes they have had a “distortive effect that’s grown over the years”. Kogan said that if a deal was done that reduced parachute payments but increased the amount going to all clubs then “that will go some way towards looking at the ­distorted effect”. Once that money was distributed, he said, “you’re going to see a softening effect going through down the 116 clubs”.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s owner, Sheikh Mansour, and chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, are under scrutiny. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The Premier League welcomed the publication of the report, arguing: “It recognises what English football has built – the world’s most popular league, the leading second tier, and a pyramid of unmatched depth.”

The league argued that a recent offer of financial redistribution to the EFL – understood to amount to £320m per season – “meets the ­objectives the IFR has set out in its report” and said it “remains ­committed to concluding a long-term partnership with the EFL that is fair, generous and ­balances the interests of all clubs”.

The EFL said the report’s findings “reinforce the EFL’s longstanding position that English football generates sufficient revenue to sustain both a successful Premier League and a thriving pyramid” and it remained “committed to working constructively with the Premier League and the regulator to secure a financial settlement in the interests of the whole game”.

Meanwhile, the secretary of state for digital, culture, media and sport, Lisa Nandy, said the stark figures covered in the report had “blown the doors off the game”. She urged football authorities to “consider these findings for the good of the game, for the fans, and for the communities of which they are so often the bedrock”.

Sports.title: Champions League roundup: Tresoldi treble stuns Inter in Club Brugge win
Sports.content:
Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side.

A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go.

Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time.

Having lost 2-1 to Real Madrid at the Bernabéu in their opener, Inter remain on zero points and will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk. Brugge, who lost at home to Aston Villa on matchday one, will next host the French club Lens.

Bayern Munich were held 3-3 at Viking, with the Norwegian champions equalising late through Herman Haugen after Michael Olise was sent off. Bayern trailed 2-0 at half-time thanks to goals from Gianni Stensness and Peter Christiansen. Harry Kane seemed to have dragged Bayern to victory as he scored twice and set up another for a 3-2 lead, but Olise picked up two yellow cards in the space of a minute.

View image in fullscreen Viking’s Herman Haugen (second right) celebrates after scoring his side’s third goal against Bayern Munich. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB/AP

Viking made the most of their advantage with Haugen scoring in the final minute to snatch a shock draw for the Norwegian champions against the German giants. Olise’s red means he will miss next week’s blockbuster clash with Arsenal in Munich.

Barcelona and Lamine Yamal rediscovered their sparkle after a rocky first-half spell in the cauldron of Istanbul’s Ali Sami Yen stadium to win 4-1 against Galatasaray.

The Turkish club took the lead after 27 minutes. After Anthony Gordon went tumbling in the penalty area, the hosts launched a rapid counterattack through Rafael Leão on the left. He pulled the ball back to the edge of the area to the Russian Aleksey Batrakov, whose drive deflected off João Cancelo and into the net.

That ignited a spell of furious home pressure which culminated with Victor Osimhen rising to head a corner past Joan García. Baris Yilmaz toed the ball over the line but was ruled offside. Barcelona reasserted control, and when Lamine Yamal went down on the edge of the box, the ball broke to Davinson Sánchez, who gave it away immediately. It fell to Dani Olmo, who threaded a pass for Cancelo to score.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal was on sparkling form as Barcelona won 4-1 in Istanbul. Photograph: EPA

At the start of the second half, Lamine Yamal took over. After setting up Gordon, who spurned the chance, he helped put Barça ahead in the 50th minute, placing a gentle curled cross on the forehead of Fermin López, who nodded home.

Three minutes later, Lamine Yamal beat Eren Elmali three times, and in three different ways, in a tiny space before rolling a pass to Gordon in front of goal. This time the England attacker made no mistake. After 65 minutes, Lamine Yamal cut in from his wing and fired a pass to Gabriel Jesus. The former Arsenal man, on as a substitute, could not control the ball but it deflected to Karim Adeyemi who drilled the ball home.

Villarreal recovered to beat Napoli 3-1 at home with goals from Georges Mikautadze, Santiago Mouriño and Tani Oluwaseyi. Brajan Gruda’s 75th-minute strike gave RB Leipzig a 1-0 win over PSV Eindhoven after Maarten Vandevoordt had saved Ivan Perisic’s early penalty with a boot.

The Azerbaijani outsiders Sabah claimed a historic first win in the league phase, beating Slavia Prague 2-0. Second-half goals from Kaheem Parris and Joy-Lance Mickels secured the historic win in Baku for a club that was founded only nine years ago.

In the other early kick-off, Sporting also sealed a 2-0 win, prevailing at Lens thanks to goals in either half from Luis Suárez and Issa Doumbia.

Sports.title: Iraola has ‘100% trust’ in Wirtz and Barcola but tells others to step up
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has said he trusts Liverpool’s big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola “100%” but needs players to step up in the absence of his three leading goalscorers.

Liverpool will again be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai when visiting the Austrian side Lask in the Champions League on Wednesday. Iraola said he did not know when any of the trio, all of whom are carrying minor injuries sustained on international duty, would be available.

Their absence heightened the responsibility on Wirtz and Barcola against Manchester City on Sunday but both struggled as Liverpool suffered their first defeat under Iraola. Barcola is yet to produce a goal or an assist in six appearances since his £123m arrival from Paris Saint-Germain, or even win possession in the final third, while Wirtz has one assist this season and continues to underwhelm in a Liverpool shirt.

“Cody, Alex and Dom are our top scorers this season and now we don’t have them. We need other players to give us those numbers,” said Iraola. “We trust the players we have now to play in those positions. With Bradley and Flo, they have had good games and bad games this season like everyone else. We know their level and we know they will give us good performances.

“The other day, if [Lewis] Koumas scores the goal that he connects with really well, then it is one assist for Bradley Barcola. His performance would be exactly the same but we will all say: ‘Oh, he played really well with an assist.’ Sometimes we focus only on the numbers. With Bradley, the other day he had good situations and we did not finish them. Bradley and Flo are players that I trust 100%.”

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola (left) has not won possession in the final third this season. Photograph: Jon Super/AP

The Liverpool head coach confirmed he was likely to make changes in Linz, with several players knocks against City.

Iraola insisted he was happy with the team’s spirit, attitude and work rate in Sunday’s defeat, “including from the offensive players”, but not with the collective response to Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh dismissal. “A lot of what happened after we went down to 10 men was because we conceded straight away,” Iraola said. “We were making adjustments and then you go 1-0 down and it’s different, because then you have to go [for it] and you get caught in-between.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The goal we conceded straight away hurt us. If we had made the adjustments earlier and been more compact at 0-0, it becomes a lot easier. But once you concede it’s not enough to just be compact. You need to go a little bit more and then spaces open.”

Virgil van Dijk is in line to captain Liverpool for a 200th time in all competitions on Wednesdaytonight.

Sports.title: Maresca says he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he were a United fan
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has admitted he would describe Manchester City as “cheats” if he were a Manchester United or Arsenal fan. The manager’s ­comments came as he suggested it had been harder for City’s supporters to deal with the scandal surrounding the club than it had been for him or the players.

Maresca guided City to an ­impressive 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. He was asked whether the performance was down to the team being brought closer together by the guilty verdict.

“It probably has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me as it’s more complicated,” he said, “because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan and you are a City fan, I can tell you: ‘Hey, my friend, you cheat’ – or this kind of thing. But we were happy at the end of the game and inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield.”

City, who have appealed against the independent commission’s ­ruling and continue to protest their innocence, have drawn criticism for the exuberant manner of Sunday’s celebration. Maresca defended the revelry but is conscious of the need to focus on Wednesday’s visit of Paris Saint-Germain in their second Champions League game of the season, following their 2-0 victory at Porto.

“We won 0-3 at Anfield,” Maresca said. “Even if it was 0-1 it would be exactly the same. We are here today to win tomorrow’s game and we work every day to win games. It’s the only thing that we can think; we can be focused. The rest is just things from outside that we need to deal with but we were so happy inside the pitch and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca (right) talks with Enzo Fernández during a training session on the eve of the clash against PSG. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

“I promise you that I stress a lot about the gameplan and how we can train every day but I don’t stress about things I don’t [control]. The message to the players will be the same. We know how serious the situation is but at the same time it’s not something that we can do [anything about].”

Rúben Dias, City’s captain, echoed his manager. “When you build yourself as a player, you build yourself against any noise,” the defender said. “Personally, and I feel like I speak for the whole group, we’re very calm. We trust the club, and we’re very focused on enjoying football. People don’t love us winning and we love to win.”

Pep Guardiola is expected to be at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday in a show of support for City’s owners. “In case he’s coming, it’s a nice feeling,” Maresca said of his predecessor. “Especially for him, because this has been his house for 10 years. It’s exciting for everyone.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Luis Enrique, PSG’s head coach, said City should keep all the ­trophies won from 2009-18, the timeframe of the guilty charges. “The first time that you hear [about the verdict], is it is a surprise,” he said. “But we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision. The authorities are responsible for making these decisions. But speaking only about football, they deserved those trophies. I love their football. Beyond that, we have to wait for the judges’ decision.”

Luis Enrique played with ­Guardiola at Barcelona. The 56-year-old was asked what he would say to his ­former teammate. “Nothing ­serious,” he said. “The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. But we have to wait. The things I will say to Pep I will do in private.”

City claimed three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, and three League Cups in the nine-year span.

Sports.title: Harry Kane overtakes Lionel Messi in stunning Champions League feat as he chases Cristiano Ronaldo streak
Sports.content:
Harry Kane overtakes Lionel Messi in stunning Champions League feat as he chases Cristiano Ronaldo streak

Harry Kane has impressively overtaken Lionel Messi for Champions League goals scored over the age of 30 in fewer games.

The striker netted twice in Bayern Munich’s entertaining 3-3 draw at Norwegian side Viking on Tuesday evening.

4 Harry Kane fired scored twice for Bayern in a 3-3 draw against Viking and moved past Messi's tally for Champions League goals after 30 Credit: Getty

4 Kane has now surpassed Messi's tally and is also chasing Cristiano Ronaldo's record

Trailing 2-0 at the interval, Kane inspired Bayern to a comeback, scoring twice while playing a key role in his side’s third before they unfortunately conceded late on.

Kane’s first came from the penalty spot in the 54th minute and the England captain only had to wait a further six minutes to grab his second of the evening.

And it was that goal that took his tally to 36 goals in 40 games after the age of 30.

Kane, now 33, has bolstered his account since arriving in Bavaria in 2023, so much so that he has now eclipsed Messi’s total.

The Argentine netted 35 goals in 48 games beyond his 30th birthday.

That shows the magnitude of Kane’s prowess in recent years while providing a ringing endorsement for his recent Ballon d’Or nomination.

Kane’s double means he has now scored for nine successive games to equal Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy's record.

And now Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of 11 goals in succession is firmly in his sights ahead of the visit of Arsenal to the Allianz Arena next week, live on talkSPORT.

Should get on the scoresheet against the Gunners, Kane’s opportunity to equal Ronaldo will come in the trip to Atletico Madrid next month.

Kane’s season at a glance

The striker is now up to eight goals for the season while registering four assists in his nine appearances.

4 Kane is now eyeing Ronaldo's record of 11 consecutive goals after scoring in his ninth straight European game Credit: Getty

Kane kicked off the season in style with three goals and three assists in five first five Bundesliga outings.

His brilliance has spilled onto the international scene with Kane having achieved his 125th cap for England, matching Peter Shilton's all-time national appearance record.

He scored six times in England’s four matches during the recent international break, taking his tally to 91 goals for the Three Lions.

Kane’s contract with Bayern expires next summer but negotiations are on going over a two-year extension.

Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund said on Friday that he is ‘very positive’ about discussions with Kane who himself has expressed his desire to remain at the club.

"There are always scenarios as long as it's not signed," Freund said. "There's no new development.

4 Kane's goals fired Bayern to a league and cup double as he scored 61 times for the club last season Credit: Getty

"The talks are going well. We're very positive, everyone knows we're determined to extend his contract and Harry feels very comfortable here."

Since his arrival from Tottenham, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 154 appearances.

He has scooped the Bundesliga Golden Boot in each of his three seasons, whilst firing Bayern to two Bundesliga titles.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney slams ‘disrespectful’ Lisandro Martinez as Man United star calls out board in furious outburst
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez slammed the Manchester United board after defeat to Atletico Madrid - but it didn't sit well with Wayne Rooney.

United conceded inside minute one of their 2-0 Champions League loss and Leny Yoro was later shown a straight red for a last man foul.



3 Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United as he called out the board for their transfer business Credit: Getty

Ademola Lookman made it game, set and match for Atletico with 11 minutes to play as they won their first match of the league phase.

It meant United have won just two of nine matches this season in all competitions, adding further pressure on head coach Michael Carrick.

But Martinez believes their shortcomings are down to the club board and their transfer business in the summer.



What did Martinez say in his outburst?

"It was really poor, really poor," he told Amazon Prime minutes after the full-time whistle.

"I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.



"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."



Martinez added: "Last season we created a base to build an amazing team. It's annoying and disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team get an amazing result here."

On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he replied. "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more. It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Rooney responds to Martinez rant

United legend Rooney, who won the Champions League at the club, was a pundit for Amazon and gave an instant response to Martinez.



"I actually disagree, because I think the performance was okay. I think the performance was better, there were some positive signs in there.

"It's a difficult one because I always used to feel I was outspoken as a player, you want to have your opinion.

"I think he's maybe gone a bit too far. That's down to the manager, and that should really stay internal.

"The fans want to hear the players speak, they want to hear the players care, so you can clearly see that he cares and he wants the club to invest more money in more players.



"I think if they do that, he'll probably be one of the players who's out the door, if we're being honest, his performances haven't been good enough.

3 Rooney acknowledged Martinez's frustrations, but claims he was disrespectful to his teammates during the rant Credit: Getty

"I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch, in defence as well. But it looks like that was a bit of an agenda he's wanted to say, because that doesn't mirror the performance, I thought it was better.

Rooney added: "I think it's a bit disrespectful to his teammate as well, because he's disrespecting his teammates, he's saying the team aren't good enough...



"I think Bruno (Fernandes) is probably the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that, if we're being honest, as captain.

"Even then, it should be behind closed doors if there's issues, which does happen - players have conversations with the manager, the manager has conversations with the board.

"But I think that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute. That's going to bring greater noise around it, players are not happy, they're not settled, they don't trust their own teammates, that's not going to help at all."

What has Michael Carrick said?

Man United manager Carrick was asked about Martinez's comments, but said: "I haven't seen it.



3 United are now winless in five matches across all competitions, with defeats coming in three of those Credit: Getty

"After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time.

"We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through."

Sports.title: Kate Scott jokes Micah Richards will be stripped of titles in brutal Man City charges dig
Sports.content:
Kate Scott jokes Micah Richards will be stripped of titles in brutal Man City charges dig

Kate Scott wasted little time in poking fun at Micah Richards about Manchester City and their guilty verdict on financial charges.

As we have extensively covered here on talkSPORT, an independent commission found them guilty on all charges related to financial rule breaches in the Premier League from 2009 to 2018.

3 City are front and centre of the biggest story in football after being found guilty on all their Premier League financial rule breaches Credit: Getty

City have lodged an appeal and claim to have a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' supporting them, but face serious sanctions including points deductions and relegation.

Stripped titles is another possible outcome which means Richards, who won the 2011/12 Premier League and 2010/11 FA Cup with City, could have his winners' medals invalidated.

The former defender made an emotional plea to his old club to disclose the evidence that they say supports their innocence.

Richards acknowledged that his success could now be in question amid the verdict.

But, when Scott opened the CBS Sports coverage of the Champions League on Tuesday night, she poked fun at her colleague.

Scott delivers brutal dig at Richards

"I'm Kate Scott. I'm joined by a man who has won it all - the World Cup, the Euros, the Champions League, the Premier League, LaLiga, Thierry Henry.

"Next to him, a Champions League winner, he also won what was the UEFA Cup, now the Europa League, he won the FA Cup and the League Cup too, Jamie Carragher.

"And then... well, this is awkward. He already has less accolades than anybody else on set.

"For now, he is still a Premier League winner and FA Cup winner, until he has to mail those winners' medals back to somebody at Stoke or Manchester United. What will he tell women then, everybody? Big Meeks, Micah Richards!"

Richards cut a downcast figure in response, whilst Carragher laughed and Henry simply repeated: "Wow!"

3 Richards gave an emotional assessment of his former club as they face serious sanctions despite an appeal Credit: Getty

3 But Scott joked that he could lose his Premier League and FA Cup winners' medals, leaving him lost for words Credit: @CBSSportsGolazo X

City played their first match since the announcement of their guilty verdict on Sunday afternoon.

They were 3-0 winners against ten-man Liverpool with goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

Liverpool fans greeted them at Anfield with boos and banners that read 'Cheats' amid the ongoing saga.

However, City have won all six of their Premier League matches this season and sit top of the table.

They return to Champions League action on Wednesday night to host reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, live on talkSPORT.

Former boss Pep Guardiola is set to be in attendance after publicly backing the club.

Sports.title: Sporting in staggering 51-year Champions League first that Arsenal failed to achieve twice
Sports.content:
Sporting in staggering 51-year Champions League first that Arsenal failed to achieve twice

Sporting CP became the first team to win and keep a clean sheet in a European tie away at Lens in 51 years.

The Portuguese giants produced a solid display to see off the Ligue 1 side 2-0 at the atmospheric Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

2 Luis Suarez fired Sporting in front at Lens Credit: AFP

Goals from Luis Suarez and Issa Doumbia ensured Sporting continued their 100 per cent start to their Champions League campaign.

But there was further cheer for Rui Borges side who inflicted a first European home win on Lens with a clean sheet in a whopping 51 years and 48 games.

It is a feat that even Arsenal failed to achieve in their match against the French outfit in October 2023.

Gabriel Jesus fired the Gunners in front that night only for Lens to come from behind to win 2-1.

An Arsene Wenger-led Arsenal were thwarted back in 1998 when a Marc Overmars strike was cancelled out by a last-gasp equaliser.

Lens have made their home stadium a fortress in Europe over the years with Bayern Munich and AC Milan among the big names to have failed to come away with a victory.

Manchester City will hope to follow Sporting’s lead when they head to northern France in a League Phase clash in January.

The defeat brings an end to Lens’ unbeaten European home run stretching back to November 2006.

In that time, Lens clocked up ten consecutive matches without defeat – winning seven and drawing three.

How are Lens faring this season?

Lens, who finished as Ligue 1 runners-up last season, have had an eventful start to the season.

2 Arsenal were left shell shocked by Lens in 2023 Credit: Getty

They toppled European Champions Paris Saint-Germain in the Trophee des Champions in August – the curtain raiser to the Ligue 1 season.

Since then it has been underwhelming in the league having picked up just two wins from their opening six matches.

Lens sit 10th in the table with seven points while picking up three points from the opening two Champions league fixtures.

Following Pierre Sage’s exit and subsequent arrival as Crystal Palace boss, Lens hired German tactician Dino Topmoller as head coach.

But his stay at the club was a brief one as he departed the club by mutual consent after just six competitive games.

His exit stemmed from a disagreement over a decision by club chiefs to restructure the coaching staff.

He was replaced by assistant coach Yannick Cahuzac.

Sports.title: Watford set to sack manager Alessio Dionisi and move on to fifth new boss of 2026
Sports.content:
Watford set to sack manager Alessio Dionisi and move on to fifth new boss of 2026

Watford are set to sack Alessio Dionisi, talkSPORT understands.

The Italian only joined the Championship club as head coach in June but is already heading for the exit after a poor start to the season.

2 Watford are set to make another managerial change with Dionisi on course to be sacked four months after joining Credit: Getty



After a 2-1 victory over Southampton on the opening weekend, they won just one match in the following eight.

talkSPORT understands that their Tuesday night trip to Cardiff City was critical for Dionisi's future.

However, they were 4-0 down at half-time during their 5-1 loss, and the 46-year-old is set to be dismissed at Vicarage Road.

More change at Watford

Watford are now due to have a fifth manager in the dugout in 2026 after Javi Gracia, Charlie Daniels, Ed Still and Dionisi.



The next appointment will be the club's 25th since the Pozzo family took over in 2012.

Dionisi will leave Watford with three wins from 12 in all competitions.



Championship victories have come against Southampton and Preston North End, with another being at home Crawley Town in the Carabao Cup first round.

Watford are the first non-Italian club of his managerial career that featured a spell in Serie A with Sassuolo.



It remains to be seen who is in contention to replace him at the club.

However, whoever the successor is will be tasked with tasked with avoiding relegation to League One, five years after they lasted played in the Premier League, as they sit in 22nd.

2 Watford are in their fifth consecutive season in the Championship and already at risk of the drop to League One Credit: Getty

Watford fans booed and chanted 'Sacked in the morning' to Dionisi during their 4-0 defeat to Burnley at the weekend.



"It's difficult to speak about it after a 4-0 loss, because I'm not happy about the first half, and I'm not happy about the second half," he said after. "In the first half, we played with 11 players.

"In the second half, we played with five different players, and I'm not happy with either half. The problem now is the attitude, the team, the coach, everyone. Not one player or one striker.

"(You could say) it's better to play this player than someone else, but no, there is balance in this team. I listen to a lot of words said about my players, but now it is probably better we say nothing, because I don't see one best player inside the team.

"To provide a good result, it's better to play with mentality, to play together, not to play for one player, because in this team, there isn’t [one standout player].



"Probably in other teams, there is, but in this team, there isn't one. Unless I don't remember well, but I remember well... very well."

Sports.title: Aston Villa star hints that £100m stadium renovation has had negative impact on form
Sports.content:
Aston Villa star hints that £100m stadium renovation has had negative impact on form

Matty Cash has suggested that redevelopment of the North Stand at Villa Park has affected Aston Villa's form this season.

Cash and Villa have lost to Arsenal and Nottingham Forest in their three-match winless home run in the Premier League.

3 Villa still play their home matches at Villa Park, but the North Stand is shut for fans due to renovation work Credit: Getty

They led Brentford 2-1 in the 77th minute on Saturday but conceded moments later and settled for a 2-2 draw.

Fans inside Villa Park and those watching from afar have noticed that there is a stand full of supporters behind one of the goals.

Villa announced in April that the North Stand would be shut for the entire season due to ongoing works, including 12,000 new seats.

This will see the overall stadium capacity increase to over 50,000 as it prepares to host matches at Euro 2028.

But Villa defender Cash believes its rebuild, which will cost a reported £100million, has affected their home form.

No excuses, but Villa Park is 'different'

Speaking ahead of their Champions League clash against Fenerbahce at home on Wednesday night, live on talkSPORT, he was asked about how he has found playing with a missing stand.

"Our home form has not been what we want it to be," he admitted. "Without sounding like we're making excuses, because we have to deal with the circumstances.

"Obviously for the club and the platform, it's really good to make the stand bigger, and the stadium bigger for capacity.

"But it's obviously different, I'm not going to sit here and lie and say it's not, it is different.

"But as I said, the circumstances, you have to deal with it as a player, you can't make excuses, you have to play with what's in front of you.

3 Cash has hinted that the lack of fans in the North Stand has impacted Villa's home form during the season so far Credit: Getty

"When it's done, it will be amazing but obviously at the minute, it is a bit different without making excuses."

What does Emery think about the missing stand?

Villa boss Unai Emery also weighed on the North Stand's absence at their stadium, and acknowledged as a 'handicap' for his side.

"Tomorrow we will be (at) Villa Park again with the energy we need. We have one handicap, it's less supporters for this situation," he said.

"But at the beginning of the season, the club decided it, and it’s something to improve for the future – not now, but for the future.

"It's not excuses. We must try to be together, and without 7,000 supporters like (there) normally are in Villa Park, we must push everybody, and play football.

"One improvement in Villa Park is (to) play football, better football than we played.

3 Villa are aiming to complete the work on the North Stand in 2027 and ahead of Euro 2028, with Villa Park being a host venue Credit: Getty

"Compete better than we compete, to be focused more than we did, to be demanding more than we did.

"Those improvements are very important, more than the stand, and giving us lack of some supporters (who) normally were helping us.”

Sports.title: Alex Scott valuation revealed with Bournemouth open to selling Liverpool and Chelsea target in January
Sports.content:
Alex Scott valuation revealed with Bournemouth open to selling Liverpool and Chelsea target in January

Bournemouth are open to selling Alex Scott in January – but have slapped a price tag of over £100million on the midfielder.

The England international has caught the attention of some Premier League’s big hitters after delivering a string of impressive performances for the Cherries.



2 Alex Scott could leave in January if the right offer arrives, with two Premier League giants eyeing a move Credit: Getty

Whilst the possibility of a mid-season exit stands, Bournemouth will only sell if their £100m+ valuation is met by interested parties.

Chelsea and Liverpool have long been linked with the star with both clubs understood to be in the race for his signature.

The Blues tabled unsuccessful offers for Scott over the summer, while the Reds are understood to be in a strong position giving a pre-existing relationship with the player.



Any January deal for Scott will also hinge on whether Bournemouth are well positioned to retain their Premier League status.

Marco Rose’s side are currently 18th in the table and without a win from their opening six matches.



Scott is on the sidelines for the next month with a thigh injury picked up in England's 7-0 win over Croatia in the Nations League.

Why has Bournemouth's stance changed?

Bournemouth were orginally staunch in their stance of Scott not being for sale when dealing with interest over the summer.



However, after talks across the last few days, the door has now been opened for a potential exit.

Real Madrid have also scouted Scott, who is yet to sign a new contract at the Vitality Stadium.

His current deal at the club expires in 2028.

2 Chelsea and Liverpool are understood to be leading the race for Scott, who Bournemouth would accept bids of over £100m for

Despite their shortcomings in the summer, Chelsea retain an interest in Scott.



So do Liverpool, though they have two other options on their radar if a move does not materialise.

AS Monaco star Lamine Camara is one alternative after a deadline day move to Chelsea fell through.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs reported that Liverpool asked Camara to wait over a transfer, suggested they could make one next summer.

However, it's understood that Liverpool did not directly interfere with negotiations that took place between Chelsea and Monaco.



Manu Kone is another potential target, having had a move to Chelsea blocked by AS Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini.

Sports.title: The next three Ballon d’Or winners predicted and next English winner will not be Harry Kane
Sports.content:
The next three Ballon d’Or winners predicted and next English winner will not be Harry Kane

Lamine Yamal has been tipped to win this year's Ballon d'Or ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

That is the verdict of talkSPORT's Rory Jennings ahead of the awards ceremony later this month.



5 The winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or will be announced on October 26, with Kane predicted to just miss out on the award by Jennings Credit: Getty

The 2026 recipient will be announced at the London Palladium on Monday, October 26.

Yamal, Kane and Mbappe are seen to be amongst the frontrunners for the prestigious awards after impressive 2025/26 seasons for their respective clubs and countries.

Kane won a third successive Bundesliga golden boot as he fired Bayern Munich to a domestic double in Germany.



The England captain ended the season with 61 goals in 51 matches for his club across all competitions.

He then went on to score six goals for the Three Lions on their way to a third place finish at the World Cup.



Kane failed to score past the round of 16 stage in North America, though, while Yamal went on to lift the trophy.

Can Kane win the Ballon d'Or?

Jennings believes this will hinder his hopes of winning the Ballon d'Or as he revealed his top three for this year's ceremony.



Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he was asked whether Kane can win it, explaining: "Listen, I love Harry Kane and you know what, for about a decade I’ve been arguing that Kane deserves a Ballon d’Or almost for cumulative achievements.

"He has been at some point in the last 10 years the best footballer in the world and perhaps in the way that Leonardo DiCaprio got the Oscar for The Revenant when it wasn’t his best film, maybe Harry Kane deserves it as a lifetime achievement award, a contribution to football like when Ryan Giggs got Premier League Player of the Year.

"I think on some level he deserves it for that Kane, but I don’t think he’s the best footballer in the world at the moment.

5 Kane enjoyed a stellar 2025/26 season for Bayern and England and is one of the leading contenders to win this year's Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty



"I think he failed for England. The two goals against DR Congo are doing a lot of heavy lifting in his contribution during the World Cup. Where was he against Norway? Where was he against Argentina when we needed him most?

"Didn’t really turn it on in the Champions League for Bayern Munich. I know he scored a last-minute goal, but it really felt like a consolation goal in that semi-final.

"I don’t see how you cannot give it to Yamal, to be honest. Mbappe’s form during the World Cup blew my mind, but Yamal has won the World Cup and he has won LaLiga. It’s very difficult to look beyond him.

"I think Rodri has an outside shout as well. Rodri is one of the most important footballers to any team in the world.



"If I were voting, as much as I love Kane, I don’t think you can give it to him. I think he didn’t deliver when England needed him most. I’d be inclined to give it to Yamal."

Still only 19, Yamal finished as runner-up for last year's Ballon d'Or behind Ousmane Dembele.

5 Yamal's World Cup triumph puts him ahead of Kane, according to Jennings Credit: Getty

The teenager scored 24 goals as well as providing 18 assists in all competitions for Barcelona last season.



His LaLiga title triumph was followed by a World Cup victory with Spain as Yamal scored once and added an assist across eight appearances at the tournament.

Who will be the next three Ballon d'Or winners?

With Yamal his favourite to win this year's Ballon d'Or, Jennings has also predicted the next two recipients through to 2028.

Asked who will be next to claim the award, he added: "I think Barcelona win the European Cup this year and therefore I think it will be Rodri. I think Rodri will win it again. I think he’s unstoppable.

"It’s not a coincidence that everywhere he goes, he’s just so linked to the success both internationally and at club level.



"Then I think it will be Jude Bellingham. I think Jude Bellingham will win it, but the next English winner of the Ballon d’Or will be Jude Bellingham.

5 Jennings expects Bellingham to win the Ballon d'Or in 2028 and has also tipped Rodri to win the award for a second time Credit: Getty

"What Jude Bellingham did for England at the World Cup, it blew my mind. I went to Mexico, I witnessed it firsthand, I witnessed his desperation to win, I witnessed his leadership qualities.

"I witnessed the way that he was the conduit between the fans in the stadium and the players on the pitch.



"Bellingham is everything that you want from a footballer. He has that will to win, that desperation, that silk, that skill, that end product.

"Jude Bellingham will win a Ballon d’Or and I think it will be in the next two years. I’m going to say it will be in two years after Rodri."

Bellingham will still only be 25-years-old come the 2028 Ballon d'Or ceremony.

The midfielder is already into his fourth season with Real Madrid after joining the Spanish giants from Borussia Dortmund in 2024.



5 Bellingham scored seven goals for England at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

He has since won both a LaLiga title and the Champions League.

Bellingham has also scored 14 goals in 60 caps for England at 23, including seven goals at the World Cup to take home the Bronze Boot.

Alongside Kane, he is one of three England players nominated for this year's award, with Declan Rice completing the trio.

It is Bellingham who has previously finished on the podium, though, coming third behind Rodri and Vinicius Jr two years ago.



He also won the Kopa Trophy in 2023, which is awarded to the best Under-21 player in the world.

Bellingham had previously finished as runner-up behind Pedri back in 2021.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi misses Villarreal's Champions League win after he and his family are held at gunpoint in armed robbery at home
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi and his family have been the target of an armed robbery at their home in Puzol, Spain.

The now Villarreal shot-stopper and his wife, Diana Vigh, are reported to have been held at gunpoint just hours before the 36-year-old was due to play his club's Champions League clash with Napoli.

However, the Hungarian was ruled out of the fixture after a group of four masked intruders, armed with pistols, broke into their luxury home, which is located on an estate north of Valencia.

Gulacsi is believed to have been held at gunpoint and ordered by the group to hand over valuables from a locked safe during the terrifying ordeal, while one of his two children is believed to have been inside the property.

No one is believed to have been injured during the incident, which went on for around an hour on Tuesday morning, while it is not yet clear what possessions were taken from the property, or their worth.

The intruders are alleged to have fled the scene in two luxury cars and a police investigation into the incident is now underway. No arrests have been made at the present time.

Peter Gulacsi missed Villarreal's win over Napoli on Tuesday after being the subject of an armed robbery

The shot-stopper and his wife, Diana Vigh, are reported to have been held at gunpoint by four intruders

Gulacsi is reported to have been shaken by the incident, which led to him pulling out of Villarreal's squad to face Napoli later that day. The Spanish side went on to win 3-1 at Estadio de la Ceramica (formerly known as El Madrigal).

Daily Mail Sport have appraoched Villarreal for comment.

The Hungarian joined the club back in August following an 11-year stint as the No1 goalkeeper at German side RB Leipzig, where he made over 350 appearances.

Gulacsi began his senior career on Merseyside with Liverpool, having left his boyhood club MTK Budapest initially on loan in 2007, before making the move permanent.

However, he never made a competitive appearance between the sticks in red during his six years at Anfield, spending four of those on loan at the likes of Hereford United, Tranmere Rovers and Hull City.

The goalkeeper has made 58 appearances for his country, Hungary, before retiring from international duty in the summer of 2025.

Sports.title: Man United will 'NEVER' win the Premier League with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre-back, insists Paul Scholes
Sports.content:
Man United legend Paul Scholes believes the club needs to overhaul its defence after claiming they cannot compete for the Premier League title with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre-back. The Red Devils have endured a slow start to the Premier League season, winning one of their opening six matches of the campaign. Michael Carrick's side are 13th in the league following Saturday's 1-1 draw against Tottenham, leaving them 12 points adrift of leaders Man City. Man United had looked poised for a second victory of the season after leading 10-man Tottenham 1-0 but the visitors, who began the day bottom of the table, levelled in stoppage time through a Dominic Solanke header. Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Scholes highlighted Lisandro Martinez's role in Tottenham's equaliser by stressing that the centre-back had been 'bullied' by Solanke in a physical duel. Scholes expressed concerns that Man United's defence has been overlooked in recent years regarding recruitment, with Martinez and Harry Maguire still lining up for the Red Devils. Man United legend Paul Scholes has called for Man United's defence to be overhauled, as he insisted they cannot win the league with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre back Scholes claimed Martinez being 'bullied' by Dominic Solanke for Tottenham's equaliser on Saturday was 'criminal' and 'beyond belief' ‘Tottenham were bottom of the league ahead of the game on Saturday and they absolutely run all over Manchester United,' Scholes said. ‘We talk a lot about recruitment, don’t we? The idea is to make your team better and someone like Elliot Anderson would make them better, but I’m not sure the players they brought in make them better. ‘I actually think they’re alright in the forward areas but look at the centre-halves, that’s an area of the pitch that hasn’t been addressed for a few years. ‘We’ve had the same centre-halves now for two or three years and we know you’re not going to be successful with them. You’re never, ever going to win the Premier League with them. ‘The goal on Saturday was a prime example – we know Lisandro Martinez is a good footballer but for your centre-half to be bullied like that, that was purely physical. 'Martinez, it is criminal, how he let them score that goal is beyond belief. ‘Manchester United need a new back-four, they need a new back-four.’ The Red Devils' backline will be put to the test on Tuesday when they face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Atletico are currently second in La Liga after winning six of their opening eight matches of the campaign. Man United will be without left back Luke Shaw and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo. Shaw’s second injury already this season is particularly painful given that United neglected to sign cover at left back in the summer. The two players who replaced him for three games in September – Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui – are also out of action at the moment so right back Diogo Dalot and young Harry Amass are Carrick’s options.
