World.title: Champions League: Lookman scores as Atletico down Carrick’s struggling Man United
World.content:
Atletico Madrid’s Nigerian forward #11 Ademola Lookman celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 2, football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and Manchester United at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP)

Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick.

Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone’s side and after Leny Yoro’s 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid.

Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions.

Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side.

Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer.

“Defend what we love,” Atletico fans ordered their supporters with a banner display before kick-off and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds.

Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick applauds at the end of the UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 2, football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and Manchester United at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid on October 13, 2026. Atletico Madrid won 2-0. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Alex Baena found a way in behind United’s defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder’s shot from crossing the line.

Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero’s legs but firing just wide.

Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico’s lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar.

The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente’s hand during the build-up.

Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half.

United rallied and Fernandes’s lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine.

However the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man.

It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes.

Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed.

Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United.

Simeone’s side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool.

World.title: Court overrules El-Rufai’s objection to DSS forensic witness
World.content:
Former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai

A Kaduna State High Court on Tuesday has overruled an objection by former Governor Nasir El-Rufai’s defence team to the testimony of the Department of State Services (DSS) digital forensic expert.

The presiding Judge, Justice Darius Khobo ruled that the prosecution could call the witness, who was subpoenaed by the court, despite his name and evidence summary being absent from the prosecution’s witness list.

The judge held that the defence’s right to fair hearing could be protected by allowing it to cross-examine the witness.

The ruling followed objections by El-Rufai’s senior counsel, Paul Erokoro, who argued that the defence had not received the witness’s evidence summary or the subpoena.

Erokoro submitted that the omission denied the defence adequate notice to prepare for cross-examination and understand the case it was required to answer.

The ICPC prosecution counsel, Ayodele Adedipe, however, argued that failure to include a subpoenaed witness in the proof of evidence did not automatically render the testimony inadmissible.

In its ruling, the court confirmed that the witness had been subpoenaed through an order signed by the court on June 30, 2026.

Khobo said the prosecution’s position reflected the applicable law, citing previous cases in support of the ruling.

The judge held that the witness’s absence from the prosecution’s witness list and evidence summary did not prevent him from testifying because he had been subpoenaed.

He added that the defence’s fair-hearing concerns could be addressed by allowing it to cross-examine the witness.

Earlier, the DSS digital forensic examiner, Shegun Kayode, testified about a forensic examination of communication records and audio recordings allegedly linked to the defendant.

Kayode told the court that specialised software revealed two-way communications involving El-Rufai and suspected associates, including Bashir El-Rufai and another person, between October. 25 and 28, 2025.

He said the findings prompted further analysis of audio recordings received from a communication intelligence server.

The witness explained that he immediately created a forensic image of the original audio file, sealed it and secured it to preserve its technical integrity.

Kayode said subsequent software examination showed that the audio was authentic and had not been artificially generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that El-Rufai arrived at the court amid heavy security, accompanied by his wife, Asiya El-Rufai, and Isa Ashiru Kudan, the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kaduna State.

El-Rufai was brought to court for the continuation of his trial over alleged corruption in a suit filed against him by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC).

During the proceedings, an audio recording of his interrogation by the DSS concerning the alleged importation of about 10 kilogrammes of thallium sulphate, a highly toxic and strictly regulated substance, into Nigeria was played.

The recording, which lasted about one hour and 30 minutes, contained the interrogation and other exchanges.

The case was adjourned until November. 30 and December 1 for continuation of the cross-examination of the DSS witness by the defence counsel.

Speaking with journalists after the court proceedings, Adedipe said the prosecution had opened its case by calling its first witness, a forensic expert.

He said the witness testified and tendered a forensic investigation report before cross-examination commenced.

Adedipe explained that the proceedings took considerable time because of objections and legal arguments but said the prosecution was able to conclude its presentation with the witness for the day.

He confirmed that the case had been adjourned until November 30 and December 1 for continuation of cross-examination.

Erokoro, counsel to El-Rufai, said the prosecution had opened its case and called its first witness, adding that the lengthy proceedings showed the parties’ commitment to ensuring the trial progressed.

He expressed confidence that his client would be discharged and acquitted of all the charges.

Erokoro said the defence had begun examining the witness’s testimony and would continue to scrutinise the evidence when the court reconvened.

He maintained that the next hearing would provide the defence with an opportunity to test the accuracy and credibility of the prosecution’s evidence.

World.title: ECOWAS Defence Chiefs seek sustained Nigerian support for regional security
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The outgoing and incoming Chairmen of the ECOWAS Committee of Chiefs of Defence Staff (CCDS) have called for sustained Nigerian support to strengthen regional security cooperation and address growing threats across West Africa.

The two military chiefs made the appeal on Tuesday during a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters in Abuja.

The outgoing Chairman, Lieutenant General Amara Idara Bangura, who is Sierra Leone’s Chief of Defence Staff, expressed appreciation to Nigeria for its continued support for the ECOWAS defence framework and regional security initiatives throughout his tenure.

Bangura disclosed that he and his successor had spent the previous two days conducting formal handover activities ahead of the transition in the leadership of the ECOWAS defence committee.

He commended Nigeria’s longstanding contributions to peace and stability in West Africa, particularly its support for Sierra Leone during the country’s civil war and subsequent peacebuilding efforts.

He also highlighted Nigeria’s contributions to regional peacekeeping operations, counter-terrorism cooperation and logistical support, describing the country’s role as critical to the security of the sub-region.

The outgoing chairman urged Oluyede to extend the same level of cooperation and goodwill to his successor to ensure continuity in regional security efforts.

In his remarks, the incoming Chairman of the ECOWAS Committee of Chiefs of Defence Staff and Senegal’s Chief of Defence Staff, Vice Admiral Oumar Wade, thanked the Nigerian military leadership for the warm reception accorded the delegation.

Wade identified terrorism, violent extremism, transnational organised crime and maritime insecurity as some of the complex and evolving threats confronting ECOWAS member states.

He described Nigeria as a key regional power and an anchor of security in West Africa, stressing that its continued guidance, participation and support would be essential to the committee’s ability to fulfil its mandate.

Responding, Oluyede thanked the two defence chiefs for their commendation of Nigeria and its Armed Forces, describing their visit as a demonstration of solidarity and a shared commitment to regional peace and security.

The CDS called for stronger unity, cooperation and mutual understanding among ECOWAS member states, urging countries to set aside political differences, divergent interests and bilateral disputes to confront common security threats.

He emphasised that security was indivisible, noting that no country could effectively guarantee its own safety in isolation from its neighbours.

Oluyede reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to supporting ECOWAS security initiatives, citing the country’s determination to promote regional peace, integration and development.

He also assured Wade of Nigeria’s full support during his tenure as chairman, expressing confidence that sustained cooperation among member states would strengthen the region’s collective security architecture.

World.title: Ex-gang leader sentenced to minimum 40 years for Tupac murder
World.content:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday.

The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere.

Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s.

He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur.

“For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement… in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,'” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom.

“I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.”

“You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said.

Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.

A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino.

The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding.

Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later.

The name of that person has not been definitively revealed and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive.

The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded.

– ‘Born an icon’ –

The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, was one of America’s most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why.

Known for hits including “All Eyez on Me,” Shakur — the son of a Black Panther activist — was raised in Harlem and Baltimore, but quickly became the epitome of California hip hop when he signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records.

His sister Sekyiwa Shakur paid emotional tribute on Tuesday to her brother, a man whom she said “was born an icon.”

She said their mother “consciously raised him to be a human rights activist, someone to stand up for those weaker and smaller than he was, and that’s who he was to me and all the family. He was the person that you go to for protection.

“He dedicated his career to the advancement of his people. He was gentle and kind to women and children. He fed anyone he knew that didn’t have. He was truly my shining star, my shining prince. He was who God trusted to take care of me.”

Davis offered no words of contrition ahead of the sentence being handed down, vowing only to appeal the guilty finding.

World.title: BIC Recognised for Decade-long Brand Legacy
World.content:
BIC Nigeria has received two major honors at the 2026 Edge Awards, winning the Edge Outstanding Legacy Brand Award of the Decade (Corporate) and the Edge Outstanding Legacy Brand Award (Shaving Razor).

The awards, presented at Marketing Edge’s Edge Awards Night on Friday, September 25, in Lagos, recognize the brand’s sustained equity and performance in Nigeria’s fast-moving consumer goods sector over the past decade, alongside the continued relevance of its shaving razor brand to Nigerian consumers.

The double recognition reflects the longevity of BIC in Nigeria and the trust its brands have earned across generations of consumers. It also highlights the company’s focus on delivering products that meet everyday needs while evolving with changing consumer expectations.

“We are proud of these awards and thankful to Marketing Edge,” said Anthony Amahwe, General Manager, BIC Nigeria. “For us, a legacy is built through the trust people place in our products, day after day. These awards are a reflection of the work of our teams and partners, as well as the loyalty of consumers who have made BIC part of their everyday lives. They encourage us to keep building brands that remain relevant to consumers and the changing needs of the market.”

World.title: Stakeholders Urge Insurance, Pension Operators to Prioritise Customer Value
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

Stakeholders in the insurance and pension sectors have urged operators of the two sectors to deploy funds raised through recapitalisation to improve services, develop innovative products and strengthen customer confidence.

Speaking on the insurance sector, Managing Director, SanlamAllianz General Insurance, Mrs Jacqueline Agweh, said the post-recapitalisation era had given insurers an opportunity to develop products that would address customers’ specific needs.

She said that insurers must work closely with customers to understand those needs and provide tailor-made products and services.

Also speaking, Executive Director, NLPC Pensions, Mr Babalola Rufus urged operators to ensure that policyholders and Retirement Savings Account (RSA) holders had their funds secured, properly invested and paid when due.

Rufus noted that shareholders and contributors had committed funds to the insurance and pension sectors expecting value from their investments and contributions.

He said the success of recapitalisation in both sectors should ultimately be judged by the benefits delivered to customers.

On his part, Managing Director, Zenith Pensions Custodian Ltd., Mr Peters Elendu, advised pension operators to invest in technology, artificial intelligence, data analytics and innovation to make pension services easier and more accessible.

Earlier, Mrs Ebere Nwoji, Chairman of NAIPE said the conference was organised to bring together regulators, industry operators and investment experts to examine how the capital raised by insurance and pension institutions could be deployed prudently.

Nwoji said this was because effective investment of the funds would help generate sustainable returns for investors, strengthen the economy and improve the long-term financial security of Nigerians.

World.title: Lasaco Assurance Secures Approval to Underwrite Agric Insurance Business
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

Lasaco Assurance Plc, has secured approval of the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) to underwrite agricultural insurance for farmers, marking a pivotal advancement in the company’s strategic expansion and its commitment to Nigeria’s agricultural sector.

Speaking on the development, Lasaco Assurance Managing Director, Mr Ademoye Shobo, said as part of its agricultural insurance offerings, Lasaco Assurance would provide a comprehensive range of products designed to support farmers and stakeholders across the sector.

According to him, agriculture continues to be a vital driver of Nigeria’s economic development, sustaining livelihoods, contributing significantly to food production, and creating business opportunities nationwide.

He said the availability of tailored agricultural insurance products through reputable financial institutions plays a crucial role in meeting the risk management needs of farmers, agribusinesses, and other sector participants.

She expressed confidence that this approval would substantially boost the company’s revenue going forward. She emphasised that it presented a valuable opportunity for Lasaco Assurance to contribute meaningfully to the protection and growth of this niche market.

Also speaking, Head of Strategy at Lasaco Assurance, Mr. Adedayo Adetokun, noted that the development aligned perfectly with Lasaco Assurance’s long-term vision to deepen sectoral diversification and strengthen its competitive positioning. He noted that leveraging strategic partnerships and innovative approaches would be key to maximising the potential of the agricultural insurance portfolio.

“This milestone signals a new phase in Lasaco Assurance Plc’s business trajectory, enhancing its engagement within Nigeria’s agricultural market and setting the stage for continued expansion and value creation”, he said.

World.title: ICSAN: Sound Corporate Governance Strengthens Investor Confidence
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

The Institute of Chartered Secretaries and Administrators of Nigeria (ICSAN) has stressed the critical role of sound corporate governance in strengthening investor confidence, attracting investment and supporting Nigeria’s economic development.

The Institute said this at the Closing Gong Ceremony of an event to mark its 60th anniversary.

Speaking at the event,President and Chairman of the Governing Council of ICSAN, Mrs. Uto Ukpanah traced the Institute’s origins to the public sector. She noted that its founding principles of integrity, transparency and professionalism.

She described the milestone as an opportunity to celebrate the Institute’s legacy while preparing the next generation of governance professionals for emerging challenges.

“60 years is not just a milestone to celebrate; it is a call to prepare for the future. We must continue to strengthen a community of governance professionals who can promote accountability, reinforce investor confidence and support Nigeria’s development,” Ukpanah said.

In his welcome remarks,Chief Executive Officer of NGX, Jude Chiemeka underscored the link between sound corporate governance and investor confidence, noting that effective governance is fundamental to the credibility and integrity of market institutions.

“Corporate governance is fundamental to building and sustaining investor confidence. For the capital market to fulfil its role in mobilising long-term capital and supporting economic growth, investors must have confidence in the institutions and businesses in which they invest. This makes the work of governance professionals increasingly important,” Chiemeka said.

World.title: Expert Warns Pension Fund Managers of Post Recapitalisation Pitfalls
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

As pension sector operators continue to race towards meeting the regulator’s recapitalisation requirements with June 30th, 2027 as deadline, their attention has been drawn to issues that lie ahead after recapitalisation.

These issues have been summarised in an acronym titled SCOPE, which the expert described as scale, compliance and regulatory awareness; organisational adoption of technology, people strategy and culture, external engagement and differentiation.

Former Chief Executive officer of Pension Operators Association of Nigeria (PenOp), Mr Oguche Aguda, stated this while delivering a paper titled, “Post Recapitalisation and Market Dynamics in Nigerian Pension Industry,” at the 11th Annual National conference of Nigerian Association of Insurance and Pension Editors( NAIPE).

He said the need for scale manifested in business combination witnessed in pension sector some of which are the combination between Trust- fund Pensions and Premium Pension and the combination between Leadway and Pal pension.

He highlighted the advantages of these as gaining economics of scale by the various firms involved, increasing complexity of operations , streamlining costs and competing effectively in the market place.

On compliance and regulatory awareness, Aguda noted that pension was the most rejected sector and this has made the regulator to be at the centre of the industry ensuring that operators have sound compliance and culture.

On adoption of technology, he said operators must ask themselves the question on how to leverage technology to make their operations quicker, simble and help them to scale.

According to him, they should also meditate on how to use Artificial Intelligence to compete as well as how to manage cyber security threat.

Aguda who featured as keynote speaker on pension matters at the conference highlighted fact about the on going recapitalisation exercise in pension sector as pension sector regulator PenCom having mandated all licensed pension fund administrators to raise their minimum capital from N5 billion to N20 billion, and one percent more if their Asset Under Management is above N500 billion by June 2027.

Aguda said second fact about recapitalisation in the pension sector is PenCom mandating all licensed pension fund custodians ( PFCs) to raise their minimum capital to N25 billion by June 2027.

World.title: Financial Trust Accuses NDIC of Withholding Liquidation Surpluses for 30 Years
World.content:
.Demands release of audited accounts

.Says funds owed to estate of late founder

Sunday Ehigiator

Financial Trust Group has accused the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) of withholding liquidation surpluses and dividends due to the estate of its late founder, William Olufemi Olateju Ajayi, for more than 30 years following the liquidation of Financial Merchant Bank Limited and Republic Bank Limited in 1994 and 1995, respectively.

The group, in a statement yesterday, condemned what it described as the NDIC’s “prolonged and unwarranted refusal” to account for and release the funds, demanding an immediate settlement of all outstanding entitlements due to the late founder’s estate.

It said the corporation had continued to withhold the funds despite statutory provisions requiring the distribution of residual assets to shareholders and contributories after depositors and creditors had been fully paid.

“For over three decades, the NDIC has withheld funds rightfully belonging to the Ajayi family and associated legacy entities, despite statutory mandates requiring the distribution of residual assets to shareholders and contributories once depositors and creditors have been fully settled,” the statement said.

Financial Trust Group further alleged that the corporation had failed to provide a transparent, audited account of the assets realised from the liquidation of the two banks, despite reports indicating that depositors and creditors had long been settled.

“Despite NDIC annual reports confirming that depositors and creditors of the defunct banks have long been fully satisfied, the NDIC has maintained a posture of opacity, refusing to provide a transparent, audited accounting of the asset realizations or to distribute the resulting liquidation surpluses,” it said.

The group traced the dispute to the military era, alleging that the business interests of its late founder were severely affected under the administrations of Generals Ibrahim Babangida and Sani Abacha.

It described Ajayi as a prominent pro-democracy advocate and publisher of The Republic, a newspaper that supported the presidential ambition of the late Chief Moshood Abiola under the Hope ’93 mandate.

According to the group, the military regimes repeatedly proscribed Ajayi’s publications, targeted his businesses and eventually revoked the operating licences of the two banks.

“The Babangida and Abacha regimes repeatedly proscribed his publications, hunted his enterprises, and ultimately engineered the revocation of the banks’ operating licences in January 1994 and June 1995, even as orderly rescue and acquisition offers were underway,” the statement added.

Financial Trust Group said the prolonged dispute had continued to impose a burden on the family and the institutional legacy of its late founder, despite the contributions of the company to Nigeria’s financial markets.

The group’s parent company, Financial Trust Company Nigeria Limited, marked its 50th anniversary in May 2026.

Founded in 1976, the company said it holds the distinction of being the first indigenous stockbroking firm admitted as a dealing member of the Lagos Stock Exchange.

While acknowledging recent developments in Nigeria’s capital market and the Federal Government’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy, the group said the unresolved dispute remained a concern for accountability in the country’s financial system.

It called on the NDIC management to act in line with the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope agenda by providing a full account of the liquidation proceeds and releasing the outstanding funds.

It added, “Financial Trust Group calls upon the management of the NDIC, under the Renewed Hope agenda of the Federal Government, to immediately uphold transparency, adhere to statutory obligations, and disburse all accumulated liquidation surpluses and dividends owed to the Estate of Late Otunba W.O.O. Ajayi without further delay. Justice deferred for 30 years is accountability denied. The financial regulatory framework must honor the integrity of indigenous pioneers who built Nigeria’s financial architecture.”

The NDIC could not be reached for comments as at the time of filing this report.

World.title: Nine Banks Report N2.99tn Operating Expenses on Inflation, Regulatory Charges
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

On the bank of sustained inflation, Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI), Zenith Bank Plc and seven other financial institutions operating in Nigeria and other Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) countries declared N2.99 trillion operating expenses (OPEX) in the half year ended June 30, 2026.

Analysis of the banks audited/unaudited H1 2026 result and accounts showed that the N2.99 trillion OPEX is about 7.8 per cent increase over N2.78 trillion reported in H1 2025.

Despite the increase in OPEX, the banks posted N3.2 trillion profit before tax in H1 2026, about 19.2 per cent increase over N2.69 trillion reported in H 2025.

Inflation across SSA remained relatively contained during H1 2026 despite renewed global price pressures, supported by prudent monetary policy, easing food prices, and improving exchange rate stability in several economies.

While inflation accelerated in Ghana to 5.2 per cent and edged higher in Nigeria to 15.91per cent, reflecting lingering domestic cost pressures, Côte d’Ivoire maintained low inflation at 1.8 per cent, while Kenya (4.5 per cent) and Tanzania (4.0 per cent) continued to record moderate price growth.

Nigeria’s inflation remained on a broad disinflation path during H1 2026 despite a temporary uptick

driven by higher global energy prices following geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Headline

inflation eased early in the year before rising to 15.93per cent in May and moderating slightly to 15.91per cent in June 2026.

In response, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), adopted a cautious monetary policy stance, reducing the MPR from 26.50 per cent in February to 23 per cent at the last Monetary Policy Committee meeting (MPC) to contain inflationary pressures, preserve exchange rate stability, and anchor inflation expectations.

Further analysis of the banks’ results and accounts, showed that ETI, Zenith Bank and First HoldCo Plc declared the highest OPEX by value, while Jaiz Bank posted the highest by percentage difference.

As of H1 2026, ETI reported N856.5 billion OPEX, a 0.34 per cent increase from N853.65 billion reported in H1 2025.

Zenith Bank declared N633.76 billion OPEX, up by 9 per cent from N581.43 billion in H1 2025. On its part, First Holdco posted N608.09 billion OPEX, representing an increase of nearly 10 per cent from N552.83billion in H1 2025.

This was closely followed by GTCO that announced N277.39 billion OPEX in H1 2026, a growth of 7.3 per cent from N258.5billion in H1 2025.

GTCO in a presentation stated that its OPEX’s 7.3 per cent increase is with non-controllable costs accounting for 26.6% of total OPEX.

“The increase was driven largely by higher regulatory charges, depreciation and infrastructure-related costs, as well as continued investment in people and customer service. These pressures were partly mitigated by reductions across technology, marketing and other discretionary expense lines, reflecting continued focus on cost efficiency,” GTCO said in a presentation to analysts and investors

According to the lender, the key OPEX growth drivers was regulatory and statutory charges remained a significant component of the cost base, with AMCON expenses increasing 9.9% to N55.9billion and Deposit Insurance Premium rising 15per cent to N18.0billion.

“The increase reflects the scale of the group’s balance sheet and deposit franchise, with these costs largely determined by regulatory and statutory requirements. The group continued to absorb higher infrastructure-related costs, with Depreciation and Amortisation increasing 41.8per cent to N54.3billion, while Occupancy Costs and Repairs & Maintenance rose 10.2 per cent to N19.8billion. The movements reflect the continued build-out and maintenance of the Group’s physical and operating infrastructure.

“Investment in human capital and service delivery remained a priority, with Personnel Expenses rising 4.7per cent to N57.0billion and Customer Service Related Expenses increasing 98.3 per cent to N2.4billion. The increase in customer service costs reflects continued efforts to strengthen service capacity and customer experience.

“4.7per cent growth in Personnel expenses (N57.0 billion vs N54.4billion) resulted from the full weight impact of staff promotion and increases in salaries of Core and non-Core employees done to cushion the impact of rising cost of living for employees across the Group’s Banking and non-Banking entities,” GTCO added.

However, Jaiz Bank’s OPEX grew by 44.5 per cent to N26.6 billion in H1 2026 from N18.44 billion in H11 2025 to record the highest growth by proportion.

Analysts believe the hike in inflation rate, among others, contributed to the companies’ cost of sales and OPEX, stressing that its impact affected not only their robust profit generation, but dividend payout at the end of the year.

They predicted further hike in OPEX in 2026, stressing that its impact may cut down on earnings and dividend payout to shareholders.

Speaking, Vice President, Highcap Securities Limited, Mr. David Adnori said the hike in cost of sales and operating expenses is a reflection of global economic unrest, stressing that financial institutions operating in Nigeria and in Africa do not operate in isolation.

He expressed that the growth in cost of sales and operating expenses reported by listed companies would definitely have an impact on profit and dividend payout to shareholders.

He said, “The world is currently facing a high inflation rate and Nigeria, Africa at large are not exempted from this experience, with countries on the continent witnessing record high inflation rate. The surge in inflation rate is following the rally in crude oil prices, amidst the face-off between Russia-IUkraine and USA-Israel/ Iran, among other nations.”

“Reacting to the surging inflation rate, regulators of several countries where Nigerian companies operate have also raised their interest rates to curb the rising cost of goods and services. However, this is yet to yield any significant positive as the inflation rate above 30 per cent. With cost impacted, Nigerian companies may suffer slow profitability this year and it might impact on dividend payout,” he added.

World.title: ‘Betray his whole family’: Angelique Gerber shades Jacques Potgieter?
World.content:
Did Angelique Gerber shade her ex, Jacques Potgieter? Images via IG

Angelique Gerber has shared a cryptic post alluding to her ex, Jacques Potgieter. This comes after the actress and the former Springbok fuelled rumours that they had reconciled following a four-year separation.

During that time, Jacques dated another woman, whom he split from in June.

Jacques and Angelique married in 2016 and have three children together: son Jacques Jnr and twin daughters Annabella and Olivia.



ANGELIQUE GERBER THROWS SHADE AT EX, JACQUES POTGIETER?

On her Instagram Stories, Angelique posted several cryptic quotes about “exes”.

One read: “Your ex is running someone else’s life. You are safe”.

Another stated: “If you ever feel stupid….just remember a woman saw a man betray his whole family and still thought, ‘that’s my soulmate”

Angelique Gerber’s IG Stories.

The former 7de Laan actress appeared to be shading her ex, Jacqus Potgieter, and implying that he had moved on to another relationship.

It comes as Jacques has deleted pictures of himself and Angelique, which followers believed alluded to their short-lived reconciliation.

In several since-deleted posts, the former couple are seen embracing each other. In one pic, Jacques carried Angelique in the air, whilst in a third, she sat on his lap.



“I hit the bullseye”, he captioned the post. Referring to his ex, he posted in another: “You make my heart beat fast again”.

Jacques Potgieter deleted pictures of him with his ex.

Images via IG

WHAT WENT WRONG?

Jacques Potgieter and Angelique Gerber wed a decade ago on a wine farm in the Western Cape.

The couple began dating in 2014, when Angelique played the popular character “Clara” on the now-defunct SABC soapie 7de Laan.

In mid 2022, Jacques allegedly admitted to being unfaithful to his Springbok wife, Angelique Gerber in a series of Instagram Stories.

At the same time, Angeliqe posted a cryptic post on her IG Stories that read: “The truth always comes out”.

Jacques later claimed his account was “hacked” and assured the public the accusations about his marriage and alleged affairs were false.

Angelique then posted an apology on her account, implying the same.

By Christmas, it was clear the couple had officially split after removing all romantic posts featuring each other. To further fuel the fire, Jacques began posting pictures with his new girlfriend, Lizane Wagner.

Fast forward to 2023, and Angelique put Jacques Potgieter on blast for failing to financially support their three children.

In June, the retired rugby player – now a head coach for Centurion Rugby Club – split from Lizane.

This followed a four-year relationship with the woman many have accused of being behind his marriage breakdown.

Speaking to an Afrikaans publication, Lizane confirmed their break-up, adding that she was not the “other woman” in her ex’s marriage.

World.title: Pensioner feeding several dependants on one SASSA grant shares his biggest fear
World.content:
A Mpumalanga pensioner says his biggest concern is not his own survival but his children’s future. The Older Person’s Grant recipient, who asked to remain anonymous, shared his story in The South African’s SASSA grant survey.

He has received the grant for three years. Five people depend on that single grant at home, and he says it simply does not stretch far enough.

Children’s future weighs on the pensioner

When asked about his biggest financial concern, the pensioner pointed to his children’s future.



That worry is rooted in a hard reality. Someone in his household has gone without food in the past month. He regularly struggles to make ends meet and runs out of money before the month ends.

He spends his grant on a mix of essentials, from food to everyday household costs. With several people relying on one income, every rand is already accounted for long before the next payment arrives.

Owning his home gives the family a roof over their heads, but it does not guarantee food on the table.

Still searching for work

The pensioner is unemployed and actively looking for work. He has experience in construction and general labour and says he is willing to relocate for the right opportunity.

He believes a job would give his family the security the grant alone cannot provide.

Long queues and waiting times at SASSA offices remain his biggest challenge with the grant system, although he says his payments have been straightforward. He rates SASSA’s communication with recipients as poor and has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available.



His call for a bigger grant

The pensioner acknowledges that the grant helps his household.

“The grants does help a little bit,” he said.

However, he wants to see the amount rise.

“If it can be increased it will be better,” he added.

He suggested R5 000 a month would make a real difference for families like his. If he could change one thing about SASSA, he would increase the grant amount.

For now, he continues to stretch one grant across an entire household while hoping for a better future for his children.

World.title: KZN’s Thami Ntuli defends call for SANDF deployment in Durban
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal Premier Thami Ntuli has defended his decision to request the deployment of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) in Durban following violent protests.

The request came after violent protests erupted in Durban’s central business district (CBD), during which buildings, houses and vehicles belonging to foreign nationals were set alight by mobs protesting against a Department of Home Affairs directive concerning asylum seeker applications.

Meanwhile, Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) deputy mayoral candidate in eThekwini, Sizwe ‘Mavava’ Skhakhane, publicly criticised Ntuli for calling for the army to be deployed to quell the unrest. Skhakhane argued that the decision could negatively affect the IFP’s prospects in the 4 November local government elections.



Mavava Skhakhane has criticised Premier Thami Ntuli for calling in the military during protests, saying he never did the same over crimes allegedly committed by foreign nationals. He claims Ntuli appears to prioritise foreign nationals over South Africans. pic.twitter.com/OFuBIjv5ji — Durban Network (@Durbannetwork) October 12, 2026

THAMI NTULI DEFENDS SANDF DEPLOYMENT REQUEST

Responding to the backlash, including criticism from members of his own party, Ntuli said his critics failed to understand that there was an alleged plan to destabilise KwaZulu-Natal.

“These protests started in Durban and would have spread throughout the province as they had already started in Pietermaritzburg with burning tyres. No one would vote for the IFP because shops were torched, some are now lying and saying because the army has been deployed people will not vote for the IFP. Does that mean they should vote for the IFP because shops are being torched, there’s looting and other criminal activities?” Ntuli said.



Ntuli maintained that he did not regret his decision, citing the looting and vandalism of businesses and vehicles belonging to both foreign nationals and South Africans during the protests.

“We will protect KwaZulu-Natal, whoever has planned to destroy job opportunities because they have a selfish agenda to destroy businesses, they will not succeed,” he added.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs legend reveals how Pirates tried to block his debut
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs defender Fabian McCarthy has revealed how Orlando Pirates protested against him as he prepared to make his debut for Bloemfontein Celtic in September 1997.

The retired defender played for Celtic before joining Mamelodi Sundowns in 2000, but it was at Chiefs where he enjoyed some of the best moments of his career.

Speaking to Izinja ze Game podcast, McCarthy recalled how the Buccaneers challenged his eligibility to play during a match at the old FNB Stadium.



“It was September, but I can’t recall the date. I think it was a midweek game at the old FNB Stadium, and I was in the team but on the bench. As I was about to enter the match, Pirates protested,” he said.

McCarthy spent five years with Kaizer Chiefs

McCarthy explained that Pirates believed he had not obtained the necessary clearance after previously attending trials with the club and having links to Jomo Cosmos.

“They protested because I was at Pirates for trials and the Cosmos story. Obviously, they thought I was a defaulter, that I didn’t get my clearance. The late John Moeti went to the referee to protest.

“I said, ‘Why?’ because John didn’t know me. Somebody on the team said something,” McCarthy recalled.

Despite the protest, the former Kaizer Chiefs star was allowed to enter the field and make his Chiefs debut.

“I still went into the field and made my debut. Fortunately, we lost 1-0, but I made my debut. I think it was 1996 or 97, but it was 1997 in September,” he added.



McCarthy, now 49, went on to establish himself at Kaizer Chiefs, winning two league titles during his five-year stay with the Soweto giants.

World.title: From Ginimbi to Chivayo: The late Zimbabwean business moguls who had ties to South Africa
World.content:
The late Ginimbi and Wicknell Chivayo. Images: Facebook/Orina Makori Vincent/Sir Wicknell Chivayo

South Africa has long featured in the business journeys of prominent Zimbabwean entrepreneurs, from those who expanded their companies across borders to wealthy figures who established themselves in Johannesburg.

The careers of the late Genius “Ginimbi” Kadungure, Wicknell Chivayo and Mutumwa Mawere illustrate different connections between Zimbabwe’s business community and South Africa.

Ginimbi expanded his business into South Africa

Genius Kadungure, popularly known as Ginimbi, built his public profile through gas trading, entertainment and a flamboyant lifestyle.



According to The Herald, his Pioneer Gases business operated across Zimbabwe, South Africa and Botswana.

His wider business interests were associated with Piko Trading Group, which also included Rivonia Gases in South Africa.

Ginimbi’s South African connections extended beyond business.



Sowetan reported that he was a familiar figure in Johannesburg’s northern suburbs’ social scene, where he became known for extravagant parties.

He died in a car crash in Harare in November 2020, aged 36.

Wicknell Chivayo’s South African business connections

The late Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo has also attracted attention for his connections to South Africa.



Investigative organisation Open Secrets reported that Chivayo had nine businesses in South Africa and acted as an agent for Ren-Form, a Johannesburg-based commercial printing company.

The company’s dealings with Zimbabwe’s electoral commission featured in a wider investigation into a controversial contract worth hundreds of millions of rand.

Chivayo died on 30 September 2026 in a helicopter crash in Zimbabwe’s Marondera.



Mutumwa Mawere built a business empire across borders

The late Mutumwa Mawere was another Zimbabwean businessman whose career became closely linked to South Africa.

Mawere built an extensive business portfolio through Africa Resources Limited, with interests spanning mining, manufacturing, financial services, telecommunications and other sectors.

He acquired Shabanie Mashaba Mines in 1996, establishing himself as a major figure in Zimbabwe’s industrial sector.



According to The Herald, Mawere had been living in South Africa, where he died at Mediclinic Sandton Hospital on 15 January 2026, aged 66.

His life reflected the intersection of Zimbabwean enterprise, cross-border investment and disputes over business ownership.

These three businessmen demonstrate how Zimbabwean entrepreneurs have developed connections with South Africa through commercial operations, investment and residence.



However, their experiences differ. Ginimbi expanded into regional gas markets, Chivayo developed business links involving South African companies, while Mawere established a long-term base in South Africa after building an industrial empire.

Their stories offer a glimpse into the business relationships connecting the two neighbouring countries.

In the recording, the unidentified speaker discusses knowing Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala but denies receiving money from him to pass on to Sibiya.

Another recording introduced alleged personal connections involving a senior judicial figure.

World.title: Three arrested in KuGompo City after cops recover copper valued at R60k
World.content:
* Editor's note: This article has been updated with new information.

KUGOMPO CITY - Police in the Eastern Cape have confirmed the arrest of three men aged between 24 and 37 for the possession of stolen property.

The arrest happened on Tuesday.

Reports had indicated that inmates had escaped custody.

However, a recent statement by police spokesperson Nobuntu Gantana clarified the matter.

She said on Tuesday at around 6am members of the SAPS noticed a stationary vehicle on the roadside along the N2 with a heavy load.

“The members stopped to assist after observing that the vehicle had a puncture. Upon seeing the members approaching, five occupants fled on foot in different directions," Gantana detailed.

She said two of the suspects were arrested, with cops recovering copper valued at approximately R60,000 inside the said vehicle, which has since been impounded.

According to Gantana, later in the day, while travelling to Cambridge, SAPS officials spotted two other suspects near the bridge.

“A chase ensued, and with assistance from local private security personnel, one suspect was apprehended.”

This brings the total number of suspects arrested to three.

Police are continuing with investigations and tracing the remaining two suspects, Gantana said.

The three men are expected to appear before the KuGompo Magistrate’s Court on 14 October 2026.

ALPA argues that the committee’s reasons for reversing an earlier decision were not based on new and material facts, making the decision irrational.

READ | EFF argues Madonsela appointment reversal was unlawful

The committee’s chairperson Makashule Gana has defended its decisions, insisting they were consistent with National Assembly rules and procedures.

Gana said its legal team is ready to respond to the Economic Freedom Fighters and ALPA’s arguments in court.

“Having listened to both the EFF and ALPA, I say that as a committee, we've got a strong case and that every decision that we've taken was within the practice and the rules of the National Assembly. I'm very much confident that the legal team that will present,” he added.

The High Court in Cape Town has heard heads of argument from the EFF and the ALFP in the legal challenge linked to Parliament’s Section 89 Impeachment Committee.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
