World.title: Africa: Rwanda Set to Welcome Formula One Back to Africa, 30 Years Later
World.content:
Frenchman Alain Prost claimed the last of his four Formula One world championships at the Kyalami Circuit near Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1993, the last time the continent hosted a Grand Prix. The event's subsequent collapse brought Formula One's presence in Africa to an abrupt end.

More than three decades later, Africa is preparing for a likely return to the sport's calendar, with Rwanda securing a 10-year partnership to host a Grand Prix, with the inaugural race projected for the early 2030s.

South Africa and Morocco have also been linked to efforts to bring Formula One back to the continent, but Rwanda's agreement marks a significant step towards making that ambition a reality.



For Rwanda, however, the proposed Grand Prix is beyond motor racing. The government sees it as an opportunity to attract investment, boost tourism, create jobs and develop technical skills, while positioning the country as a regional hub for business and international sporting events.

During an exclusive interview with The New Times, Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire said Rwanda viewed the agreement as a responsibility to the wider continent, with the potential to open new opportunities for African talent and businesses.

"The excitement of F1 had been for so long left out of Africa, and Africans are known to be good fans," she said, describing the partnership as a long-term commitment whose benefits should be felt beyond Rwanda.

With Africa's population estimated at around 1.3 billion, much of it young, Mukazayire said bringing Formula One back would offer opportunities to expand participation in a sport that has largely been absent from the continent for decades.

The announcement follows President Paul Kagame's declaration at the FIA Awards in Kigali in 2024 that Rwanda was bidding to host a Formula One Grand Prix.

ALSO READ: Kagame says Rwanda's bid to host Formula 1 Grand Prix 'progressing well'

Why Rwanda secured the deal

According to Rwanda Development Board (RDB) Chief Executive Officer Jean-Guy Afrika, the country's experience in hosting major international sporting events was among the factors that strengthened its bid.

Rwanda has hosted several high-profile competitions and gatherings, including the Basketball Africa League (BAL), the 2025 UCI Road World Championships, the FIFA Congress and the FIA Awards.

Afrika said the country had demonstrated its ability to organise large-scale events while presenting a broader vision that links the proposed Grand Prix to tourism, infrastructure and economic development.

"I think there are several reasons why F1 ended up choosing Rwanda. It's not the first time that we organise a large-scale sporting event. We've already shown an ability to execute and deliver large-scale events here in Rwanda," he said.

"The second one was probably vision, and it was very clear when we started bidding for the event to happen here that it was bigger than just F1 itself and was part of a larger project that ties with the airport and driving tourism," he added.

The government is pursuing the project through a consortium involving public institutions, private-sector partners and technical specialists, working alongside Formula One and the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA).

Afrika also emphasised that Rwanda's selection should not prevent other African countries from pursuing opportunities to host the sport in the future.

"We very much welcome other countries joining and placing bids and competing for Formula One," he said.

A huge boost for tourism

The planned Grand Prix will be presented by Visit Rwanda, extending the country's strategy of using international sports partnerships to raise its profile and attract visitors.

The tourism brand has partnered with prominent sporting organisations, including English football clubs Arsenal and Bayern Munich, French side Paris Saint-Germain, Spanish club Atlético de Madrid, the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers and the NFL's Los Angeles Rams. Rwanda has also been involved in the Basketball Africa League.

ALSO READ: Hamilton, Verstappen welcome Africa's potential return to F1 calendar

Afrika described Formula One as a natural extension of the strategy, offering access to a global audience while creating opportunities to attract more international and African tourists.

"It's a continuation of the strategy to use sports to increase the country's visibility and drive inbound tourism. The strategy has been very successful," he said.

According to Afrika, Rwanda recorded $685 million in tourism receipts in 2025 and is targeting $1.9 billion in 2026.

He said the Grand Prix would support efforts to grow tourism by attracting visitors beyond the race itself, with opportunities to promote Rwanda as a destination for leisure, business and other sporting activities.

More than 100 million Africans follow Formula One, according to figures cited by Afrika, with approximately 60 per cent of the audience aged below 35.

"The idea is to continue to use Visit Rwanda, which is presenting the F1 race, to drive tourism to the country and, in this particular case, not only global tourism but also African tourism," he said.

The size and age profile of the audience, he added, make the continent an important market for Formula One as it seeks to expand its reach.

Bugesera airport city at the centre of investment plans

Rwanda expects the Grand Prix to stimulate economic activity across hospitality, construction, transport, logistics, retail, financial services and real estate.

Afrika said the event should be viewed as a long-term investment rather than expenditure on a single race, with potential returns extending across the wider economy.

"It's an investment. It's not an expenditure for a single event. And it's a long-term investment with several ways in which we expect returns to come back to the economy," he said.

A key part of the plan is the development of Bugesera International Airport and an airport city around the facility. The proposed commercial hub is expected to accommodate logistics operations, hotels, apartments, restaurants and other businesses serving travellers and investors.

According to Afrika, the new airport is expected to increase passenger-handling capacity from about one million to more than five million, creating additional opportunities for businesses serving international arrivals.

He said the Grand Prix could amplify the economic potential of these developments by generating demand for accommodation, transport, food services, retail and other activities.

"Hotels, restaurants, retail outlets, but also logistics, because when tourists visit, they have to be able to move. Financial services, because there will be a lot of transactions happening," he said.

Construction is also expected to benefit as Rwanda develops the infrastructure needed for the race, including access roads and facilities for teams, officials, spectators and other visitors.

Beyond existing businesses, the government hopes the event will encourage new investors to establish operations around the airport city.

"We also expect it to drive new investments, not just for existing investments and hotels and hospitality to benefit, but for new investments to come in," Afrika said.

He added that new businesses could create jobs, expand the tax base and increase government revenue available for infrastructure and social and economic development.

However, the scale of those benefits will depend on how effectively Rwanda attracts investors and converts the expected increase in demand into sustainable business activity.

Preparing for a decade of racing

Under the agreement, Rwanda expects to host a Grand Prix annually for 10 years, with the first race projected for the early 2030s.

Mukazayire said preparations would extend well beyond the construction of a racing circuit, requiring investment in transport, accommodation, restaurants, entertainment, operational systems and the workforce needed to deliver the event.

She acknowledged that hosting Formula One would be a major undertaking but said Rwanda would draw on its experience in organising international competitions and seek expertise from across Africa and beyond.

"Our target is to make sure that we run an African Grand Prix that represents long-term value for Rwandans and for Africa," she said.

The government's ambition is to integrate the race into a wider ecosystem of infrastructure and services, ensuring that investments made ahead of the inaugural event continue to support economic activity throughout the partnership.

Afrika said the new infrastructures in Bugesera including the airport and other amenities that are part of the Airport City supporting will be important elements of that broader vision, with Formula One expected to help increase demand for the facilities and services being developed.

Close 

Creating opportunities for young Rwandans

Beyond tourism and investment, the government wants the Grand Prix to support local talent development and create career opportunities in motorsport.

Mukazayire said the initiative aligns with Rwanda's sports strategy, which prioritises talent development, increased participation and employment.

She noted that motorsport encompasses much more than professional driving, offering opportunities in engineering, mechanics, vehicle technology, technical support and event management.

ALSO READ: F1 in Rwanda: A gateway to opportunities for African youth

The government also envisages establishing a motorsport academy to help young Rwandans develop the skills needed to participate in the industry.

"We're being intentional in giving an opportunity to an African or a young Rwandan to also enter into that sport," she said.

"There is a place for a young Rwandan in this motorsport, whether it's behind the wheel, whether it's crafting the wheel or even running the event," she added.

The expected economic activity could also create employment in hospitality, construction, transport, retail and financial services, opening opportunities for people whose skills are not directly related to racing.

For Africa more broadly, the return of Formula One could provide a platform to develop technical expertise, strengthen participation in motorsport and connect local talent with the global industry.

Rwanda's challenge will be to translate the agreement into tangible benefits through infrastructure development, investment, training and job creation.

As preparations move forward, the government is betting that the Grand Prix can become more than a sporting spectacle, serving as a catalyst for tourism, business expansion and the development of motorsport in Rwanda and across Africa.

World.title: Rwanda: Kagame Announces 10-Year Formula One Grand Prix Deal
World.content:
President Paul Kagame has announced a 10-year agreement for Rwanda to host a Formula One Grand Prix, with the inaugural race expected in the early 2030s.

President Paul Kagame has announced a 10-year agreement for Rwanda to host a Formula One Grand Prix, marking a major step towards the championship's return to Africa after nearly four decades.

The inaugural race is expected to take place in the early 2030s, bringing Formula One back to the continent for the first time since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.

The agreement follows years of discussions between Rwanda, Formula One and motorsport authorities over the conditions required to bring the championship back to Africa.

ALSO READ: Hamilton, Verstappen welcome Africa's potential return to F1 calendar

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The race will be staged on a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, about 40 kilometres south of Kigali and near the new Kigali International Airport.

The circuit will be developed to FIA Grade 1 standards as part of a wider sports, tourism and commercial development led by the Rwanda Development Board (RDB).

Designed around Bugesera's natural landscape and elevation changes, the track is expected to provide a challenging racing experience for drivers while offering strong viewing opportunities for spectators.

Beyond Formula One race weekends, the facility is expected to host other motorsport competitions, conferences, major events and entertainment activities.

Kagame said the agreement would give African motorsport fans greater access to Formula One while opening opportunities for young people to pursue careers in motorsport and related industries.

He added that the development of the circuit, alongside the new international airport, would support employment, tourism, investment and business growth in Rwanda and the wider region.

Formula One's return to Africa is also expected to open the championship to a growing audience on the continent. More than 100 million fans across Africa follow the sport, with nearly 60 per cent of fans in key Sub-Saharan African markets aged below 35.

Rwanda has in recent years expanded its profile as a host of major international sporting events.

The country has hosted the UCI Road World Championships, the Basketball Africa League, the 2023 FIFA Congress, the 2024 FIA General Assemblies and the FIA Awards Ceremony.

The Formula One Grand Prix, presented by Visit Rwanda, is expected to further support the country's efforts to attract tourists, investors and international businesses.

Beyond hosting the race, the project is expected to create jobs, develop local skills, support businesses and attract investment, with Rwanda and Formula One aiming to deliver long-term economic and social benefits.

Close 

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, president of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), said Formula One's return to Africa would expand motorsport's reach and help develop talent across the continent.

He said the FIA would work with Formula One and its partners to ensure the new circuit meets the required international safety and technical standards.

ALSO READ: F1 in Rwanda: A gateway to opportunities for African youth

Stefano Domenicali, president and chief executive of Formula One, said Rwanda's addition to the calendar would bring the championship to every inhabited continent from the next decade.

He said the partnership would seek to deliver lasting benefits through tourism, investment, skills development and opportunities for local businesses.

Further details, including the inaugural race date, construction milestones and race-weekend plans, will be announced later.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Ex-DR Congo President Kabila to Lead New 'Politico-Military' Alliance With M23 Rebels
World.content:
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila signing the documents formalising the creation of the Front for the Rebuilding of the Nation (FRN), a political and military movement, on 12 October 2026 in Goma, in the east of the DRC.

Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila has joined forces with the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group to lead a new political and military alliance, marking his most direct intervention yet in the conflict that has gripped the country's east.

The alliance was unveiled on Monday at a joint press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma - the main city in eastern DRC which has been under M23 control since January 2025.

The new organisation, known as the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation, or FRN, was presented as a "politico-military" movement that would bring together the resources and forces of Kabila's supporters and the rebels.

Its stated objective is to "put an end to tyranny by any means, including force".

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Kabila will head the movement, with senior rebel figures serving as his deputies.

The announcement represents a significant escalation in the former president's confrontation with the government of his successor, Félix Tshisekedi, and brings together one of the country's most prominent political figures with an armed movement that controls large areas of eastern DRC.

Kabila, 55, ruled the country from 2001 until 2019 and has largely stayed out of public view since leaving office.

He was sentenced to death in absentia in 2025 after being convicted of "complicity" with the M23.

Congolese authorities have also accused him of being one of the driving forces behind the Congo River Alliance - known by its French acronym AFC - which previously served as the political wing of the M23 before being dissolved.

Kabila has denied those allegations.

Kabila death sentence deepens political and regional divides in DR Congo

Political tensions ahead of 2028

The alliance comes as political attention increasingly turns to 2028, when Tshisekedi is due to complete his second and final five-year term under the constitution.

Figures within the presidential majority have in recent months raised the prospect of constitutional changes, prompting opposition concerns over whether the rules on presidential mandates could be revised.

Kabila first came to power in 2001 after the assassination of his father, Laurent-Désiré Kabila. He was elected president in 2006 and re-elected in 2011, before eventually stepping down following the 2018 election that brought Tshisekedi to power.

DRC opposition postpones protest after Tshisekedi announces national dialogue

Conflict and stalled peace efforts

Close 

M23, whose leadership is drawn largely from the Congolese Tutsi community, first launched an insurgency in eastern DRC in 2012 and returned to arms in late 2021.

The group has since captured extensive territory in North and South Kivu, including Goma.

The United Nations and Western governments accuse Rwanda of supporting the rebels, a charge Kigali denies.

Eastern DRC has been affected by armed conflict for more than three decades, displacing millions of people despite repeated diplomatic efforts.

A Washington-backed agreement between Kinshasa and Kigali signed in December has so far produced little change on the ground, while a separate ceasefire process agreed between the Congolese government and M23 under Qatari mediation in July 2025 has also failed to halt the fighting.

Kabila's new role now ties the eastern rebellion more directly to the political struggle over Congo's future leadership.

(with newswires)

World.title: Nigeria: You Have Nothing to Fear If Tinubu Wins Second Term - Shettima to North
World.content:
The Arewa for Asiwaju group storms Aso Rock and declares full support for the president's reelection.

The Vice President, Kashim Shettima, has issued a rallying cry to the North for President Bola Tinubu's reelection in the 2027 presidential election, declaring that the region has absolutely nothing to fear from a second term for the president.

With urgent intensity, he implored northern leaders and citizens to unite behind the president's re-election bid, framing the administration's second-term agenda as a secure, bulletproof guarantee for the region's future prosperity and stability.

Mr Shettima made the call on Monday when he received, on a courtesy visit, a delegation from the Arewa for Tinubu (A4A) - a northern-based think tank -working for the re-election of President Tinubu.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He called on leaders across the region to unite into a single front and work for the progress of the area and the well-being of its people, which are top priorities for the Tinubu administration.

According to the VP, the North has no reason to be scared of the re-election of Mr Tinubu, as it has benefitted immensely in terms of appointments and game-changing projects and programmes.

His words: "Let's unite as a people and work for the development of our region and the progress of our people through the re-election of this administration. We are benefiting, and we stand to benefit more from this government in many ways.

"The Bank of Agriculture has disbursed N450 billion to 700,000 smallholder farmers in Nigeria, and about 70 per cent of the beneficiaries are from the north.

"The present administration is working towards completing landmark and groundbreaking projects in parts of the country. I can assure you that the president loves the north and the president will work for the north."

The vice president thanked the group for their steadfast support for President Bola Tinubu at all times and appealed to them to work harder and galvanise across wards, communities and local governments in the northern region for the president's re-election.

Earlier, the Director General of the Area for Asiwaju and former Jigawa State Governor, Abubakar Badaru, said the organisation will not rest on its laurels until they make the North proud by reelecting President Tinubu.

He said the group plans to meet with religious leaders, including Muslim and Christian clerics, as well as other prominent Nigerians to explain to them the need to support the Tinubu/Shettima ticket in 2027.

"On discussions with the high profile, we have gone far. We have met them several times, and the BoT is meeting them again to consolidate our gains and to tell them why there is need to support this ticket.

"We are also supporting the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) with whatever they want us to do that is micro in nature because they are so big and we really don't want to lose sight of the bigger arrangement that is there. We want to focus very well on the contacts at the grassroots - the local government areas and the wards."

Close 

Also, Chairman of the organisation's Board of Trustees (BoT) and former Kano State Governor, Ibrahim Shekarau, said the think tank which worked for President Tinubu's election in the 2023 general election will repeat the same feat in 2027.

He said the organisation had been meeting with northern governors and other stakeholders to compare notes and collaborate on areas of working together to achieve the President's reelection.

He noted that the organisation has concluded plans to have a full-fledged secretariat for purposes of coordination, where there will be offices for directors and state coordinators to compare reports, analyse them, and give out instructions to its members.

The BoT chairman formally invited the vice president to officially commission the A4A office complex on Saturday, October 17, 2027.

Also present at the meeting were former Governors of Plateau, Joshua Dariye and Simon Lalong; Taraba, Jolly Nyame; Kogi, Yahaya Bello; Katsina, Ibrahim Shema; Bauchi, Isa Yuguda; Special Adviser to the President on Policy and Coordination, Hadiza Bala Usman; Chairman of NDLEA, Buba Marwa, some top officials of government, and other members of the A4A BOT and Secretariat.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice)

12th October, 2026

World.title: Liberia: Sen. Konneh Asks U.S. to Sanction Mining Enablers, Warns Liberia At 'Most Dangerous Point'
World.content:
Monrovia - Gbarpolu County Sen. Amara M. Konneh has asked the United States to impose Global Magnitsky sanctions on people who enable mining licensing deals in Liberia and move the proceeds into US real estate, telling a Washington policy audience that the country faces its gravest threat since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic.

By Lennart Dodoo

Sen. Konneh made the request Oct. 7 at a private roundtable convened by the National Endowment for Democracy in Washington, according to a statement his office released Oct. 12. He also asked Washington to support court monitoring in Liberia, resume mentoring of law enforcement officers vetted by the US Drug Enforcement Administration "with appropriate oversight," and engage the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network on active financial intelligence cases.



"Liberia is not yet a captured state. But we are at the most dangerous point since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic," Konneh said. "My request is straightforward: help us establish transparent regulations before agreements are finalized, and support impartial enforcement of the law after confiscation, whether the suspect is an airport baggage handler, a police crimes director, a former Vice President, or a multinational corporation."

Sen. Konneh, an independent who chairs the Senate Public Accounts and Audit Committee and previously served as minister of finance and development planning, described two threats he said are unfolding at the same time: corporate capture of the mining sector and the infiltration of state institutions by drug traffickers.

On mining, he said broad executive discretion in negotiating 25-year Mineral Development Agreements has created conditions for companies to capture the country's regulatory and fiscal institutions. Mining accounts for 12% of gross domestic product and 65% of export earnings, he said, yet affected communities receive less than 3% of direct revenue. The statement does not give a source for those figures.

On narcotics, Konneh said transnational trafficking networks have shown they can penetrate Liberia's law enforcement, judicial and financial systems. He pointed to two seizures this year: 237 kilograms intercepted at Roberts International Airport in June, valued at $19.2 million, and 3.9 metric tons seized in Duazon in July, valued at $317 million. He said the seizures had links to trafficking networks in Spain, Colombia, Serbia, Croatia and Ukraine.

He also described the spread of kush, a cheap synthetic drug now present in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Gambia, Guinea and Senegal, as both a public health and a governance emergency. Citing the UN Office on Drugs and Crime's World Drug Report 2025, he said opioid use in West and Central Africa stands at 2.35%, above the global average, and that Africa accounted for 57% of pharmaceutical opioids seized worldwide between 2019 and 2023.

Close 

Sen. Konneh said he is advancing a set of reforms in the Senate. They would require publishing all Mineral Development Agreements before ratification, create independent oversight of transfer pricing in iron ore concessions, mandate preserving evidence in drug cases, make financial investigations compulsory in all first-degree drug felonies, and introduce unexplained wealth legislation that allows assets to be forfeited without a criminal conviction.

World.title: Reparations official demands compensation beyond a 'single check' as advocates makes progress in California
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Advocates for racial reparations celebrated a legislative victory in California after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 2599 — the Truth in Disclosure Act — into law. But key figures behind the effort say corporate transparency is only a starting point, maintaining that direct cash compensation remains essential.

Kristin Nimmers, policy and campaign manager for the California Black Power Network (CBPN) and the Alliance for Reparations, Reconciliation, and Truth, told Fox News Digital that financial reparations must go far beyond a "single check."

"We really focus on a harm-based approach, so whoever was harmed should be entitled to that repair," Nimmers said. "Compensation for slavery, unpaid labor, for the 40 acres and a mule that were promised after the end of slavery — that should go to folks who have lineage and are descendants of people who were enslaved, because that is the harm that is being repaired."

REPARATIONS ADVOCATES SLAM CASH COMPENSATION ‘HANDOUT’ LABEL, POINT TO PAST GOVERNMENT REMEDIES

However, Nimmers emphasized that racial inequities persisted long after the end of chattel slavery.

"Black Americans were denied wages. We were denied property. We were denied access to capital. We were denied access to equal education — all of that over hundreds of years," Nimmers added. "And so a single check is not going to holistically repair our communities."

AB 2599 requires qualifying corporations doing business in California with more than $100 million in gross revenue to search their historical records and publicly disclose any financial ties to chattel slavery. Lawmakers and advocacy groups are now attempting to leverage the bill's passage as momentum to turn broader recommendations from the California Reparations Task Force into law.

During the multi-year tenure of the California Task Force to Study and Develop Reparation Proposals for African Americans (established under AB 3121), CBPN served as an official state community anchor. The coalition facilitated grassroots civic engagement across California, hosting listening sessions to gather public testimony that directly informed the task force’s landmark 1,100-page final report issued in 2023.

CALIFORNIA COUNTY APPROVES REPARATIONS PLAN AS NEIGHBORING SCHOOL DISTRICT 'BLACK THRIVING' EFFORT STALLS

However, the path forward for direct cash payouts remains difficult. While Newsom signed AB 2599, the governor has consistently taken a cautious stance on direct financial restitution, resisting high-cost payout proposals and vetoing related financial measures backed by progressive lawmakers.

Newsom's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment regarding CBPN's support for cash payments.

Progressive coalitions also face internal ideological divisions within the broader movement. Grassroots organizations like the U.S. Freedmen Project — comprised of self-identified "Foundational Black Americans" — strongly disagree with broader, harm-based eligibility frameworks. The group aims to educate the public on the legal and historical distinctions between African Americans who directly descend from enslaved people in the U.S. and those who voluntarily immigrated to the country in recent decades.

The U.S. Freedmen Project told Fox News Digital that recent immigrants and Black Americans who do not meet its ancestry criteria should not be included in government reparations programs, arguing that left-leaning advocates are using the legacy of slavery to fund a far broader social platform.

Nimmers pushed back on lineage-only requirements, arguing that systemic discrimination in the 20th century affected a wider range of Black residents.

NEWSOM SIGNS FIRST-IN-NATION LAW FORCING MAJOR COMPANIES TO REVEAL SLAVERY-ERA TIES: 'MAKE IT PUBLIC'

"If you are a Black person — maybe a Black immigrant who came here in the 1950s before the Civil Rights Act was passed — then you also experienced segregated schools," Nimmers said. "If you experienced segregated schools, if you experienced redlining, and we are coming up with some sort of policy or some sort of form of repair for those things, then you should also be included in the group that is repaired. It isn’t really a lineage-based outlook, but more of a harm-based approach."

While state-level cash proposals remain stalled, localized initiatives have moved forward. Earlier this year, the Reparations Committee in Evanston, Illinois, approved $25,000 housing grants to 44 Black residents. City officials focused on housing, calling historical redlining and discriminatory zoning "the strongest case for reparations."

For California advocates, the long-term goal remains a comprehensive package encompassing both financial compensation and systemic policy reform.

"Reparations is not a handout. It is about acknowledging, addressing, and repairing harm," Nimmers told Fox News Digital. "What is the repair for that harm, and who fits within the group that was harmed? It's necessary because we are owed that compensation for unpaid labor and historical harms."

World.title: NBA announcer Mike Tirico addresses the truth behind Michael Jordan's, limited NBC role
World.content:
NBC’s return to NBA coverage last season offered longtime basketball fans a dose of nostalgia. The venerable broadcast network regained the league’s rights as part of an 11-year media deal, reviving the iconic theme song that accompanied NBA broadcasts from 1990 to 2002.

Disney-owned ESPN and Amazon Prime Video also joined the deal, which marked the NBA’s move away from longtime broadcast partner TNT. As NBC prepared to launch its 2025-26 NBA coverage, the network announced that former Chicago Bulls superstar and six-time NBA champion Michael Jordan had been named a "special contributor."

Some interpreted the announcement as a signal that Jordan would become a regular presence on the studio desk. Instead, his role amounted to a single sit-down interview with lead play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico, which NBC split into several segments and aired throughout the season.

MICHAEL WILBON REVEALS JORDAN'S TRUE FEELINGS ABOUT LEBRON

MIKE BREEN SAYS FANS 'DESERVE TO BE THROWN A BONE' AS NBA CUTS ALL LOCAL BROADCASTS FROM THE PLAYOFFS

I think he is above the daily discourse of, ‘Hey, who is the best point guard in the NBA right now?’ and ‘who’s the best this or the best that?’"

World.title: Man who lived as woman for eight years warns surprising teen sexuality data may not tell full story
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A man who spent eight years identifying as a woman is casting doubt on reports of a dramatic decline in teenagers identifying as gay or bisexual, warning that social media and peer pressure may be influencing how young Americans describe their sexual orientation.

Walt Heyer, who detransitioned roughly 40 years ago and now serves as a senior fellow at the Family Research Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive video interview he remains skeptical of the apparent shift, suggesting some teenagers may be reluctant to openly identify as gay or bisexual because of social pressures.

"I don't really believe that there's a big dramatic free fall," Heyer said, referring to recent reports about declining rates of gay and bisexual identification among some teenagers.

LOG CABIN REPUBLICANS REMOVES 'T' FROM LGBT ADVOCACY, SAYS 'RADICAL' TRANS ACTIVISTS ARE ERODING GAY SUPPORT

"I think what's happening is that, because of social media, there's a lot more influence on people who may not want to fall into that classification on a social media level and will withhold the fact that they are gay or bisexual but really don't want to openly admit it," Heyer said.

The comments come after The Washington Post highlighted CDC data showing that the percentage of ninth grade girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual fell from 30% in 2021 to 17% in 2025. The share identifying as bisexual alone dropped from 26% to 13% over the same period.

PRISHA MOSELY: AS A DETRANSITIONER AND MOM, I KNOW WHAT GENDER IDEOLOGY STOLE FROM ME

The percentage of boys identifying as gay or bisexual has remained largely unchanged over the past decade, while the share of high school girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual surged after the COVID-19 pandemic before beginning to decline, the Post reported.

Heyer, an author and co-author of multiple books, including "Trans Life Survivors" and "Paper Genders," and has spent years working with people questioning their gender identities, argued that social dynamics among young people could complicate attempts to interpret the findings.

"I've had actual people in school saying that they're bullied into identifying one way, or they're bullying and bullied to not identify that way," he said.

BLUE STATE SCHOOL DISTRICT ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT, HIDING GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

Heyer also said he believes peer and societal pressures are significant factors in kids choosing to identify with something else that is not their biological sex.

"What's interesting about that is that many kids are sort of coerced by their peers to say things one way or the other, so I've been very skeptical about what the kids are saying, whether they're gay or bisexual," Heyer said.

"I don't really believe that there's a big dramatic free fall. That was, I think, quoted as a free fall in the people identifying as gay or bisexual," he added. "I think what's happening is that, because of social media, there's a lot more influence on people who may not want to fall into that classification on a social media level and will withhold the fact that they are gay or bisexual but really don't want to openly admit it."

A DETRANSITIONER CONFRONTED A CALIFORNIA LAWMAKER ON THE HARMS OF GENDER TRANSITION. HERE'S WHY HE SPOKE OUT

Simply but perhaps most importantly, Heyer said he thinks adults should do a better job of only affirming what is true.

"I think that what I've really discovered is that we know now and have evidence, factual evidence, that nobody has ever changed their gender," Heyer said. "I went through the hormones, had all the surgeries, identified that way. So far in all world history, nobody has actually biologically changed their gender. This is a cosmetic social appearance. It is not a biological change.

"And when you come to that conclusion, you realize that really the procedures and these terminologies and labels, what I refer to as God rejecting labels, God rejecting procedures in every aspect. This is the way young people and adults reject God and say God doesn't exist by taking these labels on," he added.

DETRANSITIONERS REVEAL HOW DOCTORS PUSHED THEM TOWARD LIFE-ALTERING TREATMENT AS TEENS

Heyer also urged researchers to conduct additional studies before concluding that the numbers reflect a lasting shift in sexual identity.

"I just think it's important for us to be much more thorough and go to other areas before we come to some conclusion that there's a giant, giant drop in these identities," he said. "I don't think we're there yet."

World.title: Former Chicago police detective linked by DNA to 8-year-old girl's cold-case murder, police say
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A former Chicago homicide detective has been identified as the killer of an 8-year-old girl who disappeared while walking to church in 1960, with authorities now examining other cases that may have involved the officer.

Thomas F. McInerney Jr. joined the Chicago Police Department in 1959, just one year before Gloria Kowalewicz was abducted and murdered. He later became a detective investigating violent crimes and remained with the department until retiring in 1987.

More than 65 years after the killing, Chicago police confirmed to Fox News Digital that advances in DNA technology and a preserved fingerprint helped investigators identify McInerney, who died in 2006 at age 70.

COLD CASE BREAKTHROUGH SOLVES TEEN KILLING AFTER SUSPECT LIVED FREE FOR DECADES: 'BETTER BE AFRAID'

Gloria disappeared Nov. 12, 1960, after leaving her home shortly before 8 a.m. to attend morning Mass at St. Mary of Mt. Carmel Church, just a few blocks away. Her body was discovered roughly four hours later in a ditch at a forest preserve southwest of Chicago. She had been shot and killed.

The murder prompted an extensive investigation, with police interviewing more than 1,300 people and knocking on hundreds of doors. Despite those efforts, the case remained unsolved for decades.

Investigators preserved evidence from the crime scene and surrounding area, including a bullet, Gloria's coat and shoes, and a white communion purse containing her prayer book. A fingerprint was also recovered from the purse's strap.

DISCARDED TRASH UNCAPS 41-YEAR-OLD MURDER CASE IN RITZY SEASIDE RESORT TOWN, AUTHORITIES SAY

Working with the FBI and Illinois State Police, investigators used modern forensic technology to link DNA and the preserved fingerprint to McInerney, according to the department.

"McInerney should never have worn the CPD star, and it is devastating to accept that he was never identified and held accountable while he was alive," Chicago police said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

The Cook County State's Attorney's Office is working to identify other cases that may have involved McInerney, according to The Associated Press.

KILLER EX-COP EXECUTED FOR CHILD'S SLAYING AS SHERIFF SAYS HE’S SURE SAME MONSTER MURDERED ANOTHER GIRL

Police said Gloria's parents died before learning who killed their daughter, but expressed hope that identifying McInerney would bring some closure to those who knew her.

McInerney later worked for the Federal Public Defender's Office in Nevada before retiring in 2004, according to the AP. He died two years later without facing charges in Gloria's murder.

World.title: Joe Manganiello's secret seven-year health battle that nearly killed him

Joe Manganiello is opening up about the secret health battle that nearly "took his life" over seven years.

Manganiello sat down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss his health and his newly released memoir, "Bloodlines."

During his appearance, the actor told Gayle King he was offered the role as the main villain, Deathstroke, in Ben Affleck's canceled "Batman" movie.

He wrote in his memoir that, at the same time as the job offer, he was "dying." Manganiello received the call to appear in the movie in 2016.

"I got the call about a month out of the hospital after I collapsed on another set," Manganiello told King. "After about a year of feeling these mystery symptoms, I went into the hospital for two months straight and, at the end of my stay, they wound up having to remove my entire large intestine to save my life.

JOE MANGANIELLO DENIES SOFIA VERGARA’S CLAIM MARRIAGE ENDED BECAUSE HE WANTED A BABY: ‘SIMPLY NOT TRUE’

"They had split me open. My entire large intestine had turned to pus, and it was about to explode," he continued. "They took it out, and the surgery left me with an ostomy bag. And in the wake of that, I lost 60 pounds in two weeks. I couldn't walk. My eye went cross-eyed. I lost my voice. I had five catheters."

"I went into the hospital for two months straight and, at the end of my stay, they wound up having to remove my entire large intestine to save my life." — Joe Manganiello

Manganiello explained that, after he was released from the hospital, he was in the process of trying to gain the weight back when he got the call to meet Affleck and appear in the "Batman" movie.

The actor told King he was still married to Sofia Vergara at the time, and she was the one who ultimately made the decision for the doctors to save his life and remove his large intestine.

"They had to call her as my next of kin and give her options of what she thought I would want done to me while I was unconscious. She chose the right one, and it bought me time," Manganiello said. "It didn't solve the problem. The doctors still had no idea what was causing this, how to treat it. But it bought me enough time."

"But we do have to credit her for saving your life. For making that decision," King replied.

"Absolutely," Manganiello said.

"That kind of pain was like a flood in my life. You can't predict how that's going to affect people. It affected me a certain way, it affected her," he said. "It was seven years long. People didn't know about it. I was living in secret with this. Only the closest people around me knew."

King mentioned that Vergara's son, Manolo Gonzalez Vergara, 35, shared a post about a "narcissistic" man on Monday.

World.title: Trump rally protester attacked in act of ‘senseless’ political violence, Ohio mayor says
World.content:
At least two men attending President Donald Trump’s rally in Ohio attacked a female protester in a “senseless” confrontation decried by the mayor of Youngstown on Tuesday.

A pair of males, one in an adjustable baseball cap and a bald man in a dark t-shirt, put hands on a woman Monday during the GOP event inside Covelli Centre in Youngstown, multiple videos of the incident showed.

The man in a blue baseball cap pawed at the woman, wearing a shirt reading “Release the Epstein Files,” and pushed her down before the balding man jumped on her.

He appeared to throw multiple punches at the woman’s face, pull her hair and put the victim in a headlock before uniformed law enforcement arrived to take the protester away.

Mike Cardew / USA Today via Reuters

A protester is removed as President Donald Trump speaks in Youngstown, Ohio, on Monday. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty

“It must be emphatically stated that senseless (political) violence has absolutely NO place in our community or in our democratic process,” Youngstown Mayor Derrick McDowell said in a statement on Tuesday afternoon.

“Regardless of someone’s political affiliation or their point of view, every person attending a public event has the right to do so without fear of being assaulted or threatened,” he wrote. “I condemn this senseless conduct unequivocally.”

Youngstown police were not at this event, as security was provided by the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office and the United States Secret Service, according to the mayor.

It wasn’t immediately clear if anyone was arrested or charged in connection to the incident. Representatives for the sheriff and the Mahoning County Prosecutor’s Office could not be immediately reached for comment by NBC News on Tuesday.

The violence briefly delayed Trump’s speech as he watched the assault unfold.

He mocked the protester’s weight and said, without evidence, that the woman must have been paid to be there.

“You know they’re paid protesters,” Trump said. “That’s a very low class protester.”

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The president as in Ohio seeking to boost GOP hopes in what has been a reliably red state. Sen. Jon Husted has been trailing in polls against Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown and one-time Trump rival Vivek Ramaswamy is also locked in a close battle for the governor’s office against Democrat Amy Acton.

World.title: Trump attacks Rep. Ilhan Omar and Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed at Ohio rally
World.content:
Chants of “deport” rang out Monday night as President Donald Trump criticized Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, at a rally for Republican candidates in Youngstown, Ohio.

“I don’t know what they’re doing with it, but I can tell you this: She’s a disaster,” Trump said of Omar, whose home in Washington, D.C., was searched hours earlier by federal agents, two people familiar with the investigation told NBC News.

A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations “executed a judicially authorized search warrant” as “part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.” The statement did not specify that the investigation was related to Omar, nor did it provide more information about the search.

“She comes in from a country without laws, without police, without military, where all they do is shoot each other, and she comes into our country and she says, ‘I have a constitutional right,’” Trump said. “She’s telling us about the Constitution, and she comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet.”

Trump then spoke of Somali gang activity in Minnesota and what the FBI has described as a recently thwarted shooting at the state’s Mall of America, alleged to have been plotted by an American-born U.S. citizen of Somali descent, The Associated Press reported. That’s when the first wave of “deport” chants began.

Omar, who was born in the war-torn country of Somalia, immigrated to the U.S. as a child decades ago. El-Sayed was born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrants.

“For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” Omar wrote earlier Monday on X. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”

Speaking to reporters Monday afternoon, Trump said he had “nothing to do” with the search of Omar’s home.

At the rally, he segued from his attack on Omar and people of Somali descent in Minnesota to an attack on El-Sayed.

“These people are crazy,” Trump said. “You look at the guy running in Michigan. He’s a jihadist.”

Trump went on to praise El-Sayed’s Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, before he again referred to El-Sayed as a “jihadist” and proclaimed that “Somalia bandits, Third World gangsters, jihadist sympathizers do not belong in Ohio.”

He added: “They don’t belong in America. Better get them the hell out of here.”

More chants of “deport” then erupted from the audience at Youngstown’s Covelli Centre.

A spokesperson for El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment Monday night. Last week, after Trump referred to him on social media by his middle name, Mohamed, El-Sayed condemned it as a tactic meant to raise fears about his religion.

“They point to my name and they point to my faith, trying to distract us from the challenges that we have,” El-Sayed, who is Muslim, told supporters at an event Thursday in Grand Rapids, Michigan. “My name did not raise your gas prices. My faith is not the reason you can’t afford your groceries.”

Trump’s remarks Monday continued his leading role in ratcheting up rhetoric around Muslims and immigrants. Days after El-Sayed won Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary, Trump warned that the U.S. could become a “jihadist-run country.” And Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., accused El-Sayed of sympathizing with Osama bin Laden as he was campaigning with Rogers last week in Michigan.

Trump was in Ohio’s Mahoning Valley — a once reliably Democratic region that has become increasingly Republican since his rise in politics — to campaign for Sen. Jon Husted and Vivek Ramaswamy, the state’s GOP nominee for governor.

It was his second visit to Ohio in less than 10 days. His last trip, to the Dayton area, included remarks about nearby Springfield. During a 2024 presidential debate, Trump repeated the unsubstantiated and racially charged claim that Haitian immigrants in the city were eating pets.

Trump mentioned Springfield again Monday in Youngstown, immediately after his attacks on Omar and El-Sayed.

“All of a sudden, they dropped 35,000 people in from Haiti, and it didn’t work out too well,” he said before he defiantly repeated his past falsehoods. “Remember during the debate I said some of the things they were doing? I was right.”

World.title: Texas DA says ICE intentionally hit immigrant with a car and may have withheld evidence
World.content:
HOUSTON — Videos collected by local investigators make it “pretty obvious” that an ICE officer intentionally ran over Miguel Parra Hernandez during an immigration stop Saturday, which could lead to assault charges, the district attorney said Tuesday.

“This was an intentional striking and running over of the person by the vehicle, and in that case, that is an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in Texas,” Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare told NBC News.

Teare said the federal government is not cooperating with the investigation conducted by his office and the Harris County Sheriff’s Office. He also said ICE may have allowed the erasure of critical data in the vehicle involved in striking Parra, who was on foot.

Teare said that in his seven years as a Harris County vehicular crimes division chief, he has reviewed video from a number of other auto-pedestrian collision cases. He said the video his investigators have gathered in Parra’s case “goes above” the video that was posted online and obtained by NBC affiliate KPRC of Houston.

“My viewing of it, and many other investigators that have viewed it, as well, it’s pretty obvious that this was an intentional striking and running over of the person by the vehicle, and in that case, that is an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in Texas,” he said.

Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare. Raquel Natalicchio / Houston Chronicle via Getty

Parra, 48, was left with multiple breaks and fractures in his body, according to his attorney and an advocate who has been speaking on his behalf. He had surgery on one leg and faces multiple additional operations, said Cesar Espinosa, co-founder and executive director of FIEL, an immigrant civil rights group.

Video obtained by KPRC shows a white truck headed in the opposite direction of traffic on a busy roadway. It shows a vehicle jumping a yellow median and heading in the direction that Parra is running.

It then appears to show the vehicle, which is not marked, swerving left toward Parra’s path, in front of a truck stopped in a shopping center. The parked truck leaves, and a man can be seen on the pavement behind the ICE vehicle, the video shows.

An ICE spokesman said over the weekend that officers were pursuing the fleeing men and that “Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck.”

Teare, a Democrat, announced late Monday that his office had launched an independent investigation.

On Tuesday, an ICE spokesperson who was not identified said in a statement that “allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE. The men and women of ICE are entrusted with upholding the rule of law and are held to the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct.”

ICE said the allegations are “disgusting smears” that are “peddled by the media,” leading to more than a 1,600% increase in assaults and a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks against its law enforcement officers. It did not offer data behind those numbers.

ICE has said that Parra was not the target of the attempted stop but that he was in the country illegally. Parra’s attorney and family have said he has no criminal record and was on his way to work applying stucco.

Teare said his office and the sheriff’s office determined that the vehicle that struck Parra was a Jeep Cherokee and that it potentially had evidence, including a data crash recorder. He said his office wanted to know whether the vehicle locked in information at the time of the collision that could be downloaded, such as speed, steering and braking. Teare said the way to preserve data from the car would have been to “put it on a flatbed trailer and you take it to forensically download it.”

But he said he believes any data on the recorder related to the incident could have been erased when ICE drove the car away.

He and the sheriff’s investigators told ICE the information needed to be downloaded, but ICE refused, Teare said.

ICE did not respond to questions about a data crash recorder, the erasing of any potential data or any refusal to download it.

“Our office began drafting a search warrant that we were in the process of drafting when the ICE agent in question, the one that had been driving, we believed, at the time of the collision, jumped back into the car and drove it away from the scene,” Teare said. “In my 20-year career, I’ve never heard of anything like that.”

Teare also said two people from “an entirely different operation” were in the back seat of the ICE vehicle when it struck Parra. Those two people are also in ICE custody, along with Parra. Teare said his office is working to ensure all three remain in the country as material witnesses.

“I’ve taught for years at the Houston Police Department Academy, Harris County Department Academy. I’ve worked with law enforcement for 20 years. There is not a single agency in the United States that would teach that once you put people in custody in your car, you then begin to pursue other people,” he said.

Doing so puts “every single person out there in danger again,” he said.

According to Teare, the ICE vehicle should have activated its emergency equipment, such as its lights and siren, as it jumped a median and crossed into oncoming traffic.

A senior official at the Department of Homeland Security told NBC News on Tuesday that multiple ICE officers on the scene at the time were wearing body cameras. ICE is reviewing video of the scene as part of an internal investigation, the official said.

Espinosa said Parra told him that he fled because it was unclear whether there were officials in the vehicles, which he said were unmarked, did not use sirens and had dark, tinted windows.

ICE has said it was targeting another man, Jose Mendoza Cervantes, who was in the country illegally and had committed several crimes. Espinoza and Parra’s attorney Kim Bruno said neither Parra nor the man who was with him when ICE stopped their vehicle has any association with Mendoza.

Miguel Parra Hernandez. Noticias Telemundo

In previous encounters between ICE and targets of its arrests in vehicle stops, including some who have been killed, such as Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, ICE has alleged the people it tried to arrest weaponized their vehicles.

Parra was struck less than two weeks after the Trump administration issued guidance setting tighter rules for vehicle stops.

The guidance says only agents who have completed specific training should make vehicle stops. The memo also says that vehicles used for traffic stops must have lights and sirens and that all officers on the scenes of vehicle stops must wear and activate their body cameras.

The Harris County District Attorney’s Office has been asking witnesses and people who may have photos or video of the incident to contact it. Teare said that there is a secure portal that goes directly to the district attorney’s office and that no one is asked about citizenship or immigration status.

“All we are interested in is getting the truth, and any shred of cellphone footage, anyone that saw something and really can point us in the right direction, it would be wonderful,” he said.

World.title: Diesel futures jump, signaling higher prices to come despite Trump’s Russia deal
World.content:
Diesel futures traded sharply higher Tuesday, as doubts mounted about the likely impacts of the Trump administration’s latest efforts to push prices down.

U.S. diesel futures were up 5% by midday to their highest level in weeks.

In Europe, diesel futures rose by about 3.8%, while gas futures spiked to levels not seen all year.

A move higher in futures markets typically signals that prices will climb in the coming days.

Already, the average nationwide price of diesel is up 70% since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. The cost of unleaded gas has risen by more than 45% over that period.

Crude oil prices, meanwhile, were mixed. Brent traded around $106 per barrel, while U.S. crude oil neared $95 per barrel. Both of those key energy benchmarks have risen around 70% since the start of the year.

Gas and diesel prices are rising especially fast in parts of the country where President Donald Trump and Republicans can least afford to anger voters ahead of November’s midterm elections.

“Absolutely stunning price spikes in wholesale diesel today,” Gulf Oil adviser Tom Kloza wrote Tuesday on X. “US retail diesel price record of $6.53/gal could be topped by the midterms.”

“Up 18cts/gal Gulf Coast and East Coast; but up 28cts/gal in Southern California and 25-30cts/gal in Great Plains and Great Lakes,” he wrote.

Patrick De Haan, the head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, wrote on X that “$6/gal diesel may be here to stay for now.”

“Truckers and farmers not going to see any relief anytime soon,” he wrote.

The broad spike higher in diesel futures came just days after Trump announced a controversial deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase diesel supplies in the United States by buying previously sanctioned Russian reserves.

When Trump announced the deal, he said it would result in millions of metric tons of additional diesel for the world.

While that may sound like a lot, analysts have since crunched the numbers and determined that, at best, the diesel in question would amount to less than two weeks’ worth of U.S. demand.

Tuesday’s higher diesel futures are evidence of the market “clearly not believing that Russian oil is on the way,” Kloza said.

The deal with Putin also required that the Trump administration suspend long-standing sanctions on Russian energy purchases.

The sanctions were put in place after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and the decision to lift them until April has drawn widespread backlash both at home and abroad.

Trump has also applied pressure to European allies in an effort to get them to release more of their diesel reserves.

The president’s Oct. 2 announcement that Europe had bowed to the pressure and would release fuel temporarily cooled prices for a few days. But a lack of additional details about that release gradually erased any price relief.

A subsequent statement from the International Energy Agency confirmed what traders had suspected: Europe would not be releasing any new diesel reserves, merely continuing to fulfill a pledge it made in March as part of a multinational effort to cap rising fuel prices.

Trump also signed an executive order this month that sought to ease restrictions on an off-road formulation of diesel that is dyed red and not subject to federal gas taxes.

But industry groups quickly warned truckers to avoid using “red dye” diesel without more information about how the taxes would work.

As of Tuesday, it was unclear whether Trump’s red dye diesel order had any impact on domestic prices or supply.

World.title: What’s fueling inflation? Fuel.
World.content:
Inflation in America is being powered by diesel.

The price of the fuel, used by farmers and truckers, is up more than 75% since the start of the Iran war in late winter. Diesel costs have become a particular concern for economists, who say that higher diesel fuel costs trickle down into “just about everything.”

And the final government inflation report before November’s pivotal midterm elections will likely reflect how much of a headache it’s become for businesses and consumers.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics is set to release its September consumer price index report at 8:30 a.m. Wednesday. It’s expected to show the annual rate of inflation rose to 3.7% from 3.4%, according to a survey of economists from Dow Jones. From August to September, prices are expected to have risen by 0.6%. The monthly jump, if confirmed, would also be one of the largest in years.

Since August, oil prices have risen to more than $105 per barrel from about $80. The price of regular gas, which most consumers buy, also remains elevated by more than 45% since late February, when the Iran war was launched.

As early voting kicks off this week, a higher inflation reading would come at a precarious moment for Republicans defending majorities in the House and Senate. Polls consistently find that inflation and the high cost of living are top issues this year for voters in both parties.

Higher diesel prices this summer and fall have hit agricultural states like Kansas, Iowa and Texas especially hard. Long viewed as Republican strongholds, all three states have Democrats outperforming in Senate races with campaigns focused on the high cost of living.

In response to the outcry over the high cost of gas and diesel, President Donald Trump has pulled several policy levers in recent weeks aimed at pushing down prices. But so far, none of them has made much of a dent.

The Trump administration has pressured G7 allies to release more diesel stocks, issued an order to allow more widespread use of tax-free diesel, and announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin that Russia release some diesel supplies and drop some of its export restrictions.

The latest action has drawn global backlash after Trump also eased some sanctions on Russia in order to facilitate the Russian diesel deal.

Core concerns

Consumers’ wages are still lagging behind the rate of inflation. As of September, wage growth was 3% and has not grown faster than inflation since March.

Still, despite the pressure on prices and wages, consumers continue to spend. The CEOs of the nation’s largest banks on Tuesday reported that consumers remain spending at a steady pace.

“While various headwinds, most recently higher energy prices, and tighter monetary policies have been challenging, the global economy has held up remarkably well in the U.S.,” said Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser. “While much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much” of the economy’s momentum, she added.

“Our data shows that our consumer and business customers are doing well,” said Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said the economy “continued to be fueled by strong business investment and ongoing consumer spending” over the last three months.

Core inflation, which is more closely watched by the Federal Reserve and which strips out food and energy prices, is expected to rise as well, to 2.5%. If confirmed, that would be its highest level since June.

One key sector fueling higher core inflation is airfare. “Airfares remain the core category most directly affected by higher oil prices,” said economists at Morgan Stanley. “Airfare CPI is already up 23% y/y, which raises the question of how much further prices can increase.”

They noted that jet fuel prices have risen 90% since this time last year, “and typically account for roughly 20-30% of airline operating costs.” As a result, “Airlines may already be approaching full pass-through of the increase in fuel costs to consumers.”

iPhones and interest rates

Another major consumer item that could impact September’s inflation rate: pricier iPhones.

Apple’s latest iPhone began selling on Sept. 12, and Morgan Stanley’s economists said “price increases were generally in the 10%-14% range across models.”

“Given Apple’s roughly 50% share of the U.S. smartphone market,” this could translate into what they said could be a small upside impact on overall inflation.

But while these higher iPhone prices are likely contributing to September’s inflation, they are also the product of inflation earlier his year — inflation that traces back to the ever-expanding buildout of AI data centers.

The race to build data centers and chips for AI has triggered a scramble for memory, in particular. Given that the supply of memory chips is limited, prices have soared at an unprecedented pace.

In June, Apple told NBC News that it has “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly.”

Economists at Goldman Sachs also expect to see a jump in September in other key consumer categories.

“We expect a pickup in autos inflation, reflecting a 0.5% increase in used car prices, a 0.2% increase in new car prices, and a 0.2% increase in the car insurance category,” they wrote in a note.

Wednesday’s data could also “determine whether the Fed’s next hike is imminent, or simply still ahead,” said economists at UBS. Already, the central bank has interest raised rates once this year to try to slow inflation. A number of top Fed officials have also spoken about the need to raise rates even higher.

“If the economic data continue to come in as expected, I anticipate additional hikes to support a timelier return of inflation to our two percent goal,” said Federal Reserve governor Christoper Waller on Thursday. “But there is some flexibility about when those hikes will occur.”

The Fed is expected to raise rates one more time this year, most likely in December. But an inflation reading on Wednesday that comes in hotter than expected could increase that urgency and lead to a pre-Election Day rate hike at the central bank’s Oc. 27-28 meeting.

World.title: Cornell bans fraternity parties for the rest of the academic year amid investigation into alleged sexual assault
World.content:
Cornell University said Tuesday it is suspending all “parties and social events” at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year amid an uproar over a former student’s allegation that she was sexually assaulted by members of the campus Chi Phi chapter nearly two years ago.

00:24 Cornell suspends fraternity events through end of year 00:00 00:00

Michael I. Kotlikoff, Cornell’s president, also announced that the Ivy League institution would bring on “experienced, trauma-informed criminal investigators” to review allegations of sexual assault on campus.

“These are first steps toward systemic change on our campus,” Kotlikoff said in a statement posted on Cornell’s website. “We will take all necessary steps to address the conditions that led to Jane Doe’s experiences, and those of other survivors.”

The former student, identified in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe, alleges she was sexually assaulted and plied with drugs Oct. 19-20, 2024. She filed a civil lawsuit last month against multiple parties, including the university, the fraternity, her sorority, Tri Delta, and seven former Chi Phi members.

Attorneys for four of the men have said their clients deny sexually assaulting Jane Doe or coercing her with drugs. The three other men have not responded to requests for comment. None of the seven has been criminally charged. The fraternity and the sorority previously declined to discuss the pending litigation.

Jane Doe’s lawsuit put renewed scrutiny on the Cornell University Police Department’s handling of the 2024 probe and the local district attorney office’s decision not to bring criminal charges. Cornell and Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten have defended their investigations, with the prosecutor saying his office was not provided with all the materials from the campus police investigation.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has appointed state Attorney General Letitia James to oversee the case going forward. Cornell separately tasked former acting U.S. Attorney General Sally Yates with an independent review of how the school responds to sexual harassment, assault and misconduct on campus.

“I am deeply sorry for the harm Jane Doe suffered in 2024, and appalled that this act of sexual violence occurred within our Cornell community,” Kotlikoff said in Tuesday’s announcement. “It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action.”

Tuesday’s announcement outlined other changes in response to the Jane Doe case, including additional staff members at the Cornell Office of Civil Rights.

In response to a request for comment, Jane Doe’s lawyer said his client’s “goal in filing her lawsuit was not solely for herself.”

“She wanted to achieve her aim of improving Cornell and its response to abuse claims. While the steps announced today are helpful to achieve this goal, they are too late to protect Ms. Doe,” said the lawyer, Thomas Giuffra. “However, these steps will hopefully go a long way to help ensure that there are no more Jane Does.”

The Cornell investigation

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to take over the case — a decision several of the former fraternity members are challenging in court.

World.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as ambassador over corruption allegations
World.content:
Washington — Kimberly Guilfoyle said Tuesday she would step aside as U.S. ambassador to Greece after the White House asked her to resign, days after reports that she offered access to administration officials in exchange for help paying off her debt.

"We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said during her first press briefing Tuesday, breaking the news. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well."

The president, who said he hasn't spoken with Guilfoyle, soon confirmed she is leaving her post.

"She will not be there. I didn't like what I read," he told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House on his way to campaign in Alaska.

The move came days after an associate shared text messages indicating she had asked him for $100,000 to pay her American Express bill before her Senate confirmation hearing last year. The Wall Street Journal first reported the messages last week.

In recent days, Guilfoyle had expressed reluctance to step down, but the White House briefing on Tuesday left her with little choice, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

Guilfoyle confirmed her plans to resign in a post on X less than two hours after Zacharia's comments.

"While my time as ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote.

But she also denied the allegations against her and said she intends to "rigorously defend" her name.

"Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime," she wrote. "I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of the world."

There were no names circulating Tuesday in the White House for a new ambassador to Greece.

Guilfoyle has few remaining allies in the Trump administration. Her former fiancé, Donald Trump Jr., has been polite to her but no longer has much contact with her, sources said.

The move to oust Guilfoyle comes after the president told reporters Monday he was "looking at" firing her, explaining he was "not happy."

Businessman Eric Deters said in an interview with CBS News last week that Guilfoyle asked him in July 2025 to wire $100,000 to her American Express account so her credit card debt wouldn't show up on her financial disclosures as she awaited Senate confirmation.

Deters characterized her request as "pay to play," and said he had sought help from Guilfoyle with access to Trump administration officials, including the attorney general and IRS commissioner. White House officials were told that the text messages between Guilfoyle and Deters were authentic, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News last week.

Deters told CBS News that "at that moment in time, I didn't have $100,000 to spare to give to Kimberly Guilfoyle, or I actually would have been a dumbass enough to do it." He said he made up an "excuse" that his wife wouldn't go along with it.

Guilfoyle appeared at her confirmation hearing in mid-July 2025 and was confirmed that September.

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle had boasted in January about Greek tycoons who were footing the bill for her luxury travel and expressed outrage about being blocked from a dinner for Eric Trump during the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.
