She added that the notification is not a judgment, does not invalidate licences issued by the archipelago’s government and does not require activity to stop.

With the two-week deadline set by President Javier Milei expired, the Argentine government said on Tuesday it had asked the Hamburg-based tribunal for provisional measures to “preserve Argentina’s sovereign rights over its continental shelf” and prevent activities it considers “unilaterally and illegally” authorised by the United Kingdom.

In a joint statement, Britain’s Department for Business and Trade and the Foreign Office said they are preparing measures under the Protection of Trading Interests legislation, which allows the government to prevent UK companies and individuals from being compelled to comply with extraterritorial foreign rules. The statement made clear it does not seek to restrict British trade with Argentina. “This makes it clear in no uncertain terms that this Government will act where Argentina seeks to impede lawful UK commercial activity,” said Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds. “Argentina’s attempts to intimidate businesses and individuals engaged in legitimate commercial activity are unacceptable,” added Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.

According to The Guardian, the United Kingdom has also asked Interpol to reject Argentine requests for red notices against individuals linked to Sea Lion, calling them “politically motivated”. Interpol’s constitution prohibits it from intervening in matters of a political character.

Argentina argues that unilateral exploitation contravenes UN General Assembly resolutions 2065 and 31/49. In previous cases, tribunals under the Convention have declined to rule on territorial sovereignty disputes; Kumaran confirmed London will challenge any attempt to use the procedure for that purpose. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Lubetkin warns Flávio Bolsonaro that “it is not easy to leave Mercosur”
World.content:
Lubetkin warns Flávio Bolsonaro that “it is not easy to leave Mercosur”

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 14:52 UTC Full article

“It is not easy to leave Mercosur. There are too many interrelated agreements in the business sphere, and that would cause major losses for the Brazilian economy,” Lubetkin said

Uruguay’s Foreign Minister Mario Lubetkin has warned Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro that “it is not easy to leave Mercosur”, in response to his criticism of the bloc during the campaign for the October 25 runoff. In the same interview, with the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, he said Uruguay would not restore diplomatic relations with Venezuela while Delcy Rodríguez governs.

“It is not easy to leave Mercosur. There are too many interrelated agreements in the business sphere, and that would cause major losses for the Brazilian economy. And there are too many mechanisms that prevent such a quick exit,” Lubetkin said. “I hope that, if that gentleman ends up presiding over Brazil, when he starts governing he will realise that many statements made during the election campaign are impracticable once in government.”

The government programme Bolsonaro registered with the Superior Electoral Court does not mention Mercosur. On the campaign trail, the senator has spoken of “freeing Brazil from the shackles of Mercosur”, referring to the constraints the common external tariff places on negotiating its own trade agreements, a phrase some media have interpreted as raising the possibility of leaving the bloc. Uruguay has held the Mercosur pro tempore presidency since July 1.

Lubetkin said Uruguay would work with whoever is elected: “First, let the elections be clean, transparent, democratic and calm. Then, naturally, the Brazilian people will choose whoever they consider best, and we will work with whoever wins, as state policy.”

On Venezuela, the minister ruled out resuming relations: “In no way, and we are not going to resume them.” He argued that from elections Uruguay had questioned “came a president who is now, on top of everything, imprisoned in the United States, and from that president comes a president as illegitimate as he was”. Uruguay will restore ties, he said, when “an independent court confirms” the winner of a democratic election. Caracas withdrew its diplomatic staff from Uruguay and six other Latin American countries in July 2024 after they questioned Nicolás Maduro’s re-election; Maduro has been detained in the United States since January. Rodríguez announced at the UN in September that elections would be held, without setting a date.

World.title: “Falkland Islanders will is to remain British, and we will uphold it”, PM Burnham told Trump
World.content:
“Falkland Islanders will is to remain British, and we will uphold it”, PM Burnham told Trump

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:13 UTC Full article

The Prime Minister believes a UK/EU summit will enhance chances for an open discussion “about our relationship with the EU in the longer term”.

“In my meeting with President Trump I raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the Islanders to remain British”, revealed United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham in an oral statement to the House of Commons this Monday.

PM Burnham also emphasized that the point was made very clear in his speech to the UN General Assembly, “we will also always do whatever it takes to uphold Islanders’s will”.

The oral statement on his 22 September intervention before the UN General Assembly Burnham also reiterated support for Ukraine rejecting Russian aggresion, UK’s commitment with NATO and the proposal for a new National Centre for Information Defense, deepeniong collaboration with Germany, Italy and Japan.

On the Middle East situation he confirmed support for the US and Saudi Arabia, and protective security for shared bases.

“I want to thank our police and military personnel for their swift response. to the incidents at RAF Fairford and RAF Molesworth”, which he said is highly likely to have been coordinated and certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.

As to relations with the European Union, the PM anticipated a UK/EU summit in Brussels on 20th November, with the purpose of boosting UK growth and controlling illegal immigration. And this includes cutting costs and bureaucracy for sectors like farming and its food trade with EU.

On immigration, “we could link up our law enforcement efforts once again, sharing more data and criminal records of foreign nationals as well as faster electronic evidence from the phones of those behind the gangs”.

And “I believe our chances of doing so will be enhanced by being open to a discussion about our relationship with the EU in the longer term”.

Beyond Europe, a confident Britain is ready to play our part on the global stage as we take up the presidency of the G20 in 2027. “I confirmed in New York that we will place AI centre stage in our presidency, capturing the incredible opportunities it presents while guarding against the risks”.

Finally, the message at the UN and to the world is clear, after a decade of turbulence, Britain is back and can be relied upon as a consistent and stable partner in an uncertain world, always upholding the shared values set out in the UN Charter.

World.title: Brazil blames human action for the fires sweeping the Amazon
World.content:
Brazil blames human action for the fires sweeping the Amazon

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 06:29 UTC Full article

The fires coincide with an El Niño episode that forecasts place among the most intense in recent decades and that is usually associated with drought in the Amazon

The Brazilian government has blamed deliberate human action for the wave of fires in Amazonas state, where 540 new hotspots were recorded in 48 hours, more than half of those detected in the whole of October 2025, according to the National Institute for Space Research. The situation has led to a state of emergency in 36 municipalities.

Environment and Climate Change Minister João Paulo Capobianco flew over the region on Sunday with Integration and Regional Development Minister Waldez Góes and observed fire in hard-to-reach forest areas. Since fires do not occur spontaneously in the Amazon biome, the minister argues the outbreaks are the result of deliberate action, possibly to degrade the forest and prepare the ground for future clearing. “It is essential that those acting criminally see that they will be punished,” he said.

According to the institute’s data, 494 fires started in the state on Saturday 10, the highest figure of the month; on the same day in 2025, none were recorded. There were 874 hotspots in the whole of October 2025.

The smoke led civil defence authorities in Manaus, the state capital, to issue a health warning on Friday over air pollution. A joint municipal, state and federal operation is fighting the fires. The federal environment agency, Ibama, sent four water-bombing aircraft, two helicopters and 290 firefighters, and the air force added two KC-390 aircraft on Sunday. “It is one thing to deploy all the forces we can to put out the fire. It is another to assist people who need humanitarian aid and medical care because of the fires,” Góes said.

The fires coincide with an El Niño episode that forecasts place among the most intense in recent decades and that is usually associated with drought in the Amazon, while it brings extreme rainfall and flooding to the south of the continent.

World.title: San Luis Potosí auto cluster sees potential for Chinese manufacturing investment
World.content:
Could a Chinese automaker open a plant in the state of San Luis Potosí?

The president of the San Luis Potosí Automotive Cluster, an industry group, believes it’s possible.

Alberto Rosales Reyna, the cluster’s president, told the San Luis Potosí-based newspaper Plano Informativo that Asian automakers, including Chinese ones, have considered investing in the state, where BMW and General Motors have plants.

He acknowledged that no new automotive plant projects have been confirmed for San Luis Potosí, but suggested that could soon change.

“A very significant [possible] investment in the production of Chinese vehicles [in Mexico] has been spoken about as part of an effort to increase local content and have Chinese production in our state,” Rosales said.

He didn’t mention the names of any Chinese automakers that could open a plant in San Luis Potosí. However, Rosales asserted that the state has the capacity to welcome an automaker from China or any other country.

The geographical location of San Luis Potosí, the “technical ability” of its workforce, proximity to supply chains and “support that the local government could provide” all make the state an attractive place for automotive investment, he said.

Those things give San Luis Potosí “a great advantage,” Rosales said.

BYD is among the Chinese automakers that have expressed interest in opening a plant in Mexico. But neither that company — the world’s largest electric vehicle manufacturer — nor any other Chinese automaker has opened a plant in the country to date.

(However, a Mexican company, Giant Motors Latinoamérica, does assemble vehicles for Chinese automaker JAC at a plant in Ciudad Sahagún, Hidalgo.)

SLP automotive industry event could generate ‘business opportunities’ worth more than US $100 million

Rosales’ remarks about the possibility of a Chinese automaker investing in San Luis Potosí came ahead of Automotive Connection Potosí 2026, a business-to-business (B2B) networking event that will be held in San Luis Potosí city on Nov. 11 and 12.

The San Luis Potosí Automotive Cluster and the state Ministry of Economic Development are collaborating on the event.

According to the event website and media reports, Automotive Connection Potosí 2026 is projected to generate over US $100 million in “business opportunities” through meetings between automotive sector buyers and suppliers. Thirty buyers are listed on the event website, including BMW and Stellantis.

More than 500 suppliers are slated to attend the event, at which more than 1,500 B2B meetings will take place, according to the organizers.

According to a report by the news outlet Quadratín, San Luis Potosí Economic Development Minister Mario García Valde said that the event “seeks to facilitate local companies’ access to automotive sector buyers and open up opportunities for their incorporation in new productive projects.”

With reports from Plano Informativo and Quadratín San Luis Potosí

World.title: Viva-Volaris airlines merger likely to proceed, Reuters reports
World.content:
Mexico’s antitrust commission is expected to approve the unification of Volaris and Viva airlines before the end of the year, creating Mexico’s largest aviation conglomerate.

Citing six sources familiar with the case, Reuters said the National Antimonopoly Commission (CNA) will approve the planned merger between the popular low-cost carriers and the formation of a new company to be called Grupo Más Vuelos.

Executives from Volaris and Viva (formerly Viva Aerobus) say the self-styled “merger of equals” will respect brand identities and “strive to ensure consumers recognize the individual service models with which they have become familiar.”

The CNA will reportedly require Grupo Más Vuelos to meet specific benchmarks and consumer protection criteria — such as keeping fares low and avoiding widespread layoffs — according to three of the sources cited by Reuters.

Critics have raised regulatory concerns, such as route eliminations — the two companies currently operate 55 identical routes — and diminished market competition. They also point out that the transaction would concentrate 73% of domestic air traffic in a single company.

CNA approval is likely to come with requirements that the conglomerate maintain existing route networks and comply with a low-cost mandate that is aligned with regional budget operators.

Yucatán Magazine reported that the federal government has apparently sought to influence the vetting process, since both airlines “serve as redirection points and primary operators at the state-run Felipe Angeles International Airport on the periphery of Mexico City.”

While the merger, first announced last December and approved by international regulatory authorities last month, aims to increase low-cost air travel and connectivity, media reports suggest it is also a “defensive decision.”

Both carriers have experienced financial troubles since the COVID-19 pandemic. Volaris recorded a net loss of US $103.8 million in 2025 and reported a loss of US $127 million in this year’s second quarter. Viva accumulated US $133 million in losses during the first half of 2026).

According to the business consultancy Antitrust Intelligence, the merger aims to build a competitive advantage centered on cost reductions, fleet efficiencies and balance sheet recovery.

Despite the economic challenges the two airlines have been facing, market analysts and investors are said to view future operational synergies favorably.

With reports from Reuters, Yucatán Magazine and Mexico Business News

World.title: Morelos authorities free alleged criminal leader to secure release of 3 kidnapped police
World.content:
Authorities in Morelos freed an alleged criminal leader just hours after he was captured on Monday to secure the release of three kidnapped police officers.

José David Vergara, an alleged leader of the Pueblos Unidos criminal group, was detained on Monday afternoon on drug possession charges in Totolapan, a municipality in northeastern Morelos on the border with México state.

#Estados | Quema de vehículos y bloqueos carreteros se registran la tarde de este lunes en Totoloapan, Morelos, luego de un enfrentamiento armado entre elementos de seguridad e integrantes de un grupo del crimen organizado. De acuerdo con información preliminar, los hechos de violencia son resultado del despliegue de un operativo para capturar a un líder criminal considerado generador de violencia en la región. Información en desarrollo. 📹 Especial — La Silla Rota (@lasillarota) October 13, 2026

The Morelos Attorney General’s Office (FGE) said in a statement that police detained Vergara, known as “El Güero Gym,” during an anti-extortion operation. It said that “cells” of the Pueblos Unidos criminal group retaliated by detaining “three collaborators of the Eastern Region Prosecutor’s Office” — i.e., state police officers. Those officers were conducting homicide investigations and were not involved in the operation during which Vergara was captured.

After the police were kidnapped, “the protocol for handling kidnapping cases was activated to prioritize the lives of the victims being held against their will,” the FGE said before disclosing that the officers were freed at about 7:35 p.m. Monday after “the person detained hours earlier” was handed over.

“One of our colleagues was hospitalized due to a gunshot wound,” the FGE said, adding that he was in “stable” condition.

“The Attorney General’s Office of the State of Morelos stresses that the lives of our personnel are a priority for the institution and for that reason the necessary actions to protect their physical safety were carried out,” the FGE said, adding that “these criminal acts won’t go unpunished.” The newspaper Reforma reported that criminals threatened to kill the state police officers if “El Güero Gym” wasn’t released. On Tuesday, Morelos Attorney General Fernando Blumenkron Escobar said that the events in Totolapan on Monday “can’t be analyzed in an isolated way or reduced to the assertion that [organized] crime forced authorities to give in.” He said that Vergara was under investigation prior to his arrest, but was not subject to an arrest warrant. Blumenkron said the suspect was arrested for drug possession — not for high-impact crimes (such as murder) for which he is under investigation. Blumenkron also said that “at least 10 people” would be investigated in connection with the kidnapping of the three state police officers.

The capture and subsequent release of Vergara was reminiscent of the capture and release of Ovidio Guzmán López in Culiacán, Sinaloa, in 2019. The capture of Guzmán López, a drug trafficker and son of convicted drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán Loera, triggered a hostile response from the Sinaloa Cartel, leading authorities to decide to release him in an attempt to quell the violence in the Sinaloa capital. García Harfuch: Decision to release suspect was to ‘save lives’ At President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference, Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said that the Morelos government’s decision to release Vergara was aimed at “avoiding a greater confrontation” with criminals. “In effect, it was to save lives,” he said. “There were a lot of civilian people in the streets,” García Harfuch said. Citing “preliminary information” from the Morelos government, the security minister said that the state police operation in Morelos on Monday wasn’t specifically aimed at capturing Vergara. However, when officers saw “this individual in flagrante,” they detained him, García Harfuch said. “It wasn’t an operation specifically to detain this person,” he said. As a result, state police officers had “insufficient” force and backup from federal officers to effectively respond to the violence that ensued, García Harfuch said. He said that the decision to release Vergara doesn’t mean that he will go unpunished. “We’re going to arrest him,” García Harfuch said. Vergara’s arrest triggers narcobloqueos in Morelos

In addition to kidnapping three police officers, the Pueblos Unidos criminal group responded to Vergara’s arrest by setting vehicles and tires on fire to create so-called narcobloqueos (narco-blockades).

Reforma reported that narcobloqueos were set up in four municipalities in Morelos: Yecapixtla, Atlatlahucan, Tlayacapan and Oaxtepec.

Criminals also exchanged gunfire with police officers after the arrest of Vergara. Citing “unofficial information,” the El Universal newspaper reported that at least two police officers suffered gunshot wounds.

Morelos, which borders Mexico City, México state, Puebla and Guerrero, is one of Mexico’s most violent states. It recorded 673 homicides in the first nine months of 2026, according to data presented at Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference.

4 police officers killed in crash while responding to unrest

A police vehicle in which several officers were traveling crashed on the La Pera–Cuautla highway on Monday as they headed to assist colleagues responding to the unrest that followed Vergara’s arrest.

Two officers were killed at the scene of the crash, while two of three injured officers died while being transported to hospital, according to the Morelos Security Ministry.

With reports from EFE, El Universal, Reforma and El Financiero

World.title: In a first, 2 longtime searchers for missing relatives — mother and daughter — earn official certification
World.content:
After years of searching for missing loved ones, Ceci Flores and her daughter have obtained government certification recognizing their skills, a first for relatives confronting Mexico’s disappearance crisis.

Flores announced last week that she and her daughter, Milagros de Jesús Valenzuela Flores, had received the credentials, issued by Mexico’s National Council for Standardization and Certification of Labor Competencies, an agency affiliated with the Education Ministry.

The certification recognizes expertise developed by families who search for missing relatives while pressing authorities to investigate their disappearances.

Flores, 53, has become a leading voice for Mexico’s searching families since her son Alejandro disappeared in 2015. She later founded Madres Buscadoras de Sonora (Searching Mothers of Sonora) and was named to the BBC’s list of 100 inspiring and influential women in 2022.

Alejandro remains missing, but in March, searchers recovered the remains of another son, Marco Antonio, who disappeared in 2019. DNA testing confirmed his identity earlier this year.

Flores’ daughter, Milagros, leads Jóvenes Buscadores de Sonora, a youth search collective she helped establish with about 15 other young people. She is in her mid-20s.

Mexico had 130,381 people still missing or unlocated as of Oct. 12, according to National Registry of Missing and Unlocated Persons figures reported this week by Conexión Migrante. The total excludes people already located alive or dead by that date.

The credentials fall under Competency Standard EC1542, which evaluates information gathering, preparation of case files, interviews, field and remote searches, and reporting.

Flores credited Guanajuato’s State Training Institute and the forensic and legal consulting firm Forensic and Legal with supporting the training, evaluation and certification, El País reported.

“We want to have more tools to do what no mother should have to learn to do: search for her children,” Flores wrote in an Oct. 7 post on X.

Eight women searching in Guanajuato will also receive certification after meeting the same standard, UnoTV reported last week. The women, who will receive their certificates within two months, UnoTV said, completed nine five-hour training sessions, with state scholarships covering certification costs.

In her post, Flores stressed that certification does not transfer the authorities’ search responsibilities to families or search collectives.

Mexico has about 200 such groups — who look for missing relatives while pressing authorities to investigate their disappearances — according to an Amnesty International estimate cited by ADN40 in March.

Meanwhile, Mexico City’s Cuauhtémoc borough has named its council chamber Madres Buscadoras, or Searching Mothers, according to an agreement published Tuesday in the Official Gazette.

The designation honors mothers and other searching relatives without endorsing any specific organization or political position.

With reports from El País, Aristegui Noticias, Vanguardia and Excélsior

World.title: 4 Mexican bars are among this year’s World’s 50 Best
World.content:
Mexico is home to four of the best bars in the world, according to the 2026 edition of The World’s 50 Best Bars, with two of them ranking in the top 10.

Here are the Mexican bars that made the list.

h

Handshake Speakeasy – Mexico City (No. 6)

Crowned The World’s Best Bar in 2024, Handshake Speakeasy has maintained its high global ranking thanks to its culinary approach to mixology.

Located in the heart of Mexico City’s Zona Rosa, the establishment was founded by Rodrigo Urraca, Marcos Di Battista, and Dutch bartender Eric van Beek, who is responsible for its creative cocktail program.

“Hands down, the legend of Handshake Speakeasy speaks for itself,” The 50 Best Bars said, highlighting the bar’s special take on the classic piña colada.

Bar Mauro – Mexico City (No. 10)

Located in the Roma Norte neighborhood, Bar Mauro secured 10th place and won the Disaronno Highest New Entry Award 2026, which honors the highest-ranking of the bars that enter the top 50 for the first time.

The project belongs to brothers Ricardo and Eduardo Nava and opened its doors in November 2024. Ranking even higher (No. 2) on The 50 Best Bars in North America list, Bar Mauro marks one of the standout venues in Mexico.

The 50 Best Bars highlights the Negroni (named after an Italian count), the basilico (a basil-based cocktail) and the Maurito (a diminutive of the bar’s name) as some of the bar’s most recommended cocktails.

El Gallo Altanero – Guadalajara (No. 28)

The only Mexican bar outside Mexico City to make the top 50, El Gallo Altanero is located in the city’s hip Colonia Americana neighborhood. It was opened in 2018 by Swedish bartender Freddy Andreasson and Alejandra Aguinaga.

Its cocktail menu prioritizes Mexico’s seasonal ingredients, and The 50 Best highlights the Jalisco Old Fashioned and the tuna negra (that’s the Spanish word tuna, by the way, as in the fruit of the nopal cactus).

Tlecan – Mexico City (No. 47)

This mezcalería opened in 2019, founded by Bernardo Serna, Eduardo Panchur and Eli Martínez Bello. Like Bar Mauro, it’s located in the bar-rich Roma Norte neighborhood.

Tlecan’s cocktail menu is a nod to Mexico’s agave culture and lesser-known spirits like bacanora, pox and raicilla. The 50 Best highlights the paloma blanca, made with clarified grapefruit juice, and a piña colada variation using pulque.

Beyond the 50 Best

Mexico’s presence doesn’t end with those four names. The extended list features Form + Matter (No. 59) and Licorería Limantour (No. 63) in Mexico City; and Arca in Tulum (No. 67).

Mexico News Daily

World.title: MND Local BCS: Historic ‘Cabo to Cabo’ running of the Baja 1000 announced for November
World.content:
Before the recent announcement by SCORE (Southern California Off-Road Enthusiasts) International, the sanctioning and governing body of the world’s longest-running and most legendary off-road race, that the Baja 1000 would feature a unique “Cabo to Cabo” routing for its 59th edition this November, Cabo — shorthand for either the municipality of Los Cabos or its most populous city, Cabo San Lucas — had been included on the course map on only two previous occasions: in 2000 and 2007, when the race started in Ensenada and concluded in Cabo San Lucas.

That makes this year’s race — scheduled for Nov. 9 to 15 — a historic one, and not just because the race will start for the first time in Los Cabos; specifically, on Avenida Centenario in San José del Cabo, where the 964.66-mile competition sponsored by BF Goodrich Tires will both start and finish. This will also mark the first time the Baja 1000 has been run entirely within the state of Baja California Sur.

The course map for 2026

An estimated 250 teams representing 15 countries are expected to participate in the 2026 Baja 1000. Teams (generally two drivers or a driver and navigator, along with support crew) compete across several classes determined by age and vehicle type — from trucks, cars and buggies to motorcycles, quads and UTVs — vying not only for cash prizes, but also coveted points in the SCORE World Desert Championship, for which the Baja 1000 is the season’s finale.

The Baja 1000 has no set route. Ensenada has hosted the starting line for 49 of the 58 previous races, and the finish line for 31; hence, the city’s nickname as the “Desert Racing Capital of the World.” La Paz, Baja California Sur’s capital, has also been a popular terminus, serving as the finish line 22 times.

However, new and “innovative” routes are regularly included in the course rotation.

Going ‘Transpeninsular’

“Every three years, we aim to hold a ‘Transpeninsular’ version,” notes Juan Tintos Funcke, General Manager of Score International, per El Imparcial. “The most recent one was in 2023 and ran from south to north. Normally, the route goes from Ensenada to La Paz, but that year it went from La Paz to Ensenada. That is how we constantly seek innovation and offer different challenges in our races — we adjust the logistics to keep the events appealing.”

The “Cabo to Cabo” route in 2026 will certainly be that, winding its way up the East Cape from San José del Cabo, passing La Paz and then Loreto before making a turn to head back down the Pacific Coast, skirting Todos Santos and El Pescadero on the return loop to San José del Cabo.

In total, four of the five municipalities in Baja California Sur will see action along the race route (Comondú, La Paz, Loreto and Los Cabos are included; Mulegé is not).

The birth of the Baja 1000 and its enduring popularity

Southern California hot rod pioneer Don Francisco and race vehicle builder Bill Stroppe were key links between Mexico’s legendary Carrera Panamericana — the world’s longest and most dangerous race held lengthwise across Mexico between 1950 and 1954 — and the Baja 1000. Francisco had helped Stroppe and Clay Smith prepare Lincolns for the Carrera Panamericana, experience with epic-scale routing that no doubt came in handy when he aerially surveyed the inaugural route for the Baja 1000, which was run under the auspices of NORRA (National Off-Road Racing Association), founded by Ed Pearlman, Francisco and others in 1966. NORRA organized the first six Baja 1000 races between 1967 and 1972.

Although the Carrera Panamericana supplied the precedent for an internationally promoted, grand-scale Mexican endurance race, the Baja 1000 grew directly from the timed record runs of the 1960s … inspired by the 1962 durability demonstration of Honda CL72 Scrambler motorcycles, which Dave Ekins and Bill Robertson Jr. drove from Tijuana to La Paz, navigating a network of dirt tracks, washes and trails in just under 40 hours. The 950 miles they traversed were very close to the total later covered by the Baja 1000, and 40 hours is still the time limit for teams to complete the race.

Baja’s timeless off-road allure

The challenges of the Baja California peninsula’s rugged terrain have been attracting those thirsty for adventure ever since, first from those seeking to beat Ekins and Robertson’s time, and later, during the six-decade heyday of the Baja 1000, from everyone from professional drivers to rock stars (Ted Nugent) and Hollywood movie stars like Steve McQueen, James Garner and Paul Newman (who also became a professional race car driver and completed his last Baja 1000 just before he turned 80).

Parnelli Jones, who famously described the Baja 1000 as a “24-hour plane crash,” was among the first of the crossover auto racing stars to embrace the event. After winning the Indianapolis 500 in 1963, he claimed overall Baja 1000 titles in 1971 and 1972 in his famed Dick Russell and Stroppe-built Ford Bronco, “Big Oly.” A host of Formula 1, NASCAR and IndyCar champions followed, including Robby Gordon, Jimmie Johnson, Rick Mears and Alexander Rossi.

However, following the OPEC Oil Crisis in 1973, NORRA’s permits were revoked, and the Baja Sports Committee organized that year’s race before the 1974 event was canceled, and the Mickey Thompson-founded SCORE took over in 1975 — an association that to date has lasted more than 50 years.

What’s at stake this year?

The Baja 1000 brings with it tangible economic benefits: about US $35 million is expected to flow to municipalities statewide. Additionally, the race and its run-up — pre-running begins Oct. 24 — bring excitement as high season ramps up in Los Cabos during what has been a disappointing year for tourism. International arrivals, for example, have thus far been down 8.4% in 2026, and tourism as a whole down 5.6%.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by SCORE International (@scoreinternational)

There’s a lot on the line for racers, too. San Diego’s Luke “The Luke” McMillin, for example, is attempting to complete a rare full-season sweep of the 2026 SCORE calendar, having already logged Trophy Truck class wins in the San Felipe 250, Baja 500 and Baja 400. Tyler Lynn, Carter Klein and their SLR (Slam Life Racing) Honda team, meanwhile, are attempting to go that feat one step better, aiming at a second consecutive Motorcycle class season sweep.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📉 Homicides fall 30.6% year over year in September : National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 42.2 homicides per day last month, down from 60.8 per day in September 2025.

: National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 42.2 homicides per day last month, down from 60.8 per day in September 2025. 📊 Homicides down 51.4% from September 2024 : Figueroa said the decline was “more than 52%” compared to López Obrador’s final month in office, but her data showed a 51.4% reduction.

: Figueroa said the decline was “more than 52%” compared to López Obrador’s final month in office, but her data showed a 51.4% reduction. 📍 Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state : Baja California recorded 1,092 homicides from January to September (8.5% of the national total of 12,854), narrowly ahead of Guanajuato with 1,089.

: Baja California recorded 1,092 homicides from January to September (8.5% of the national total of 12,854), narrowly ahead of Guanajuato with 1,089. ✅ Homicides decline in all 32 states in first nine months of 2026 : San Luis Potosí recorded the steepest year-over-year drop (78.6%). Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur, Nuevo León and Zacatecas also saw declines of more than 50%.

: San Luis Potosí recorded the steepest year-over-year drop (78.6%). Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur, Nuevo León and Zacatecas also saw declines of more than 50%. 🔫 Over 14,000 weapons handed in since Sheinbaum took office : Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” turned in under the Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz program between Oct. 1, 2024 and Oct. 12, 2026.

: Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” turned in under the Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz program between Oct. 1, 2024 and Oct. 12, 2026. 🚨 70,571 arrests for high-impact crimes in two years : Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug labs, between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026.

: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug labs, between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026. 🏥 Sheinbaum rejects claims of “crisis” in public healthcare as IMSS workers protest: Asked about the protests scheduled for Tuesday, the president acknowledged the need to hire more specialists, promised higher resident doctor scholarships in 2027 and admitted medicine distribution problems remain. She said healthcare workers’ legitimate demands would be addressed and urged them to protest peacefully.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Federal officials presented the government’s monthly security report at President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference.

Data showed that homicides declined significantly in September, continuing a downward trend seen throughout 2026.

Sheinbaum and other officials assert that the reduction in homicides and other crimes is evidence that the government’s security strategy is working. However, there is skepticism about the accuracy of the government’s homicide numbers, which are based on data provided by Attorney General’s Offices in each of Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

While security was the main focus of today’s mañanera, Sheinbaum also fielded a question about the national protests scheduled for Tuesday, at which Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) healthcare workers will demand higher pay and better working conditions, and denounce a lack of medications and medical supplies at IMSS hospitals. In Mexico City, a large protest march (megamarcha) is scheduled to set off from the Siglo XXI National Medical Center on Tuesday afternoon.

Homicides fall 30% year over year in September

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported that there was an average of 42.2 homicides per day in September, a decline of 30.6% compared to the same month of 2026.

Compared to August, the daily homicide rate rose 3.2%.

Homicides declined 51% in September compared to 2 years earlier

Figueroa said that homicides declined “more than 52%” last month compared to September 2024, the final month of Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s presidency.

However, the data she presented showed a slightly lower reduction of 51.4%. There was an average of 86.9 homicides per day in September 2024, compared to an average of 42.2 per day last month.

Figueroa presented data that showed that last month was the least violent September of any year since 2015.

Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state

Figueroa reported that Baja California recorded the highest number of homicides among Mexico’s 32 federal entities in the first nine months of 2026. There were 1,092 homicides in the northern border state between January and September, representing 8.5% of the national total (12,854).

The murder count in Baja California was slightly higher than that in Guanajuato, which has been Mexico’s most violent state in terms of homicides in recent years. Until the end of August, Guanajuato was the most violent state in 2026 as well.

However, in the nine months to the end of September, Guanajuato ranked as the second most violent state, recording 1,089 homicides or 8.5% of the national total.

The five states that recorded the next highest homicide counts in the first nine months of 2026 were:

Chihuahua: 1,009 (7.8% of the national total)

Sinaloa: 987 (7.7%)

México state: 818 (6.4%)

Guerrero: 731 (5.7%)

Morelos: 673 (5.2%)

The seven states with the highest murder counts between January and September accounted for almost half (49.8%) of all homicides perpetrated in Mexico in the period.

Oaxaca, Jalisco and Michoacán ranked eighth, ninth and tenth, respectively, for total homicides in the first nine months of 2026. Mexico City ranked 12th with 585 homicides.

Yucatán recorded the lowest number of homicides among Mexico’s 32 federal entities, with just 21 between January and September.

Homicides declined in every state in the first 9 months of 2026

Figueroa reported that homicides declined in every federal entity in the first nine months of the year. Compared to the January-September period of last year, homicides fell 78.6% in San Luis Potosí, the largest reduction of any state.

Five other states recorded year-over-year declines in homicides of more than 50%. They were:

Nayarit: 69.5%

Quintana Roo: 59.7%

Baja California Sur: 54.6%

Nuevo León: 51.5%

Zacatecas: 50.4%

Mexicans have handed in more than 14,000 firearms and explosive devices since Sheinbaum took office

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez reported that 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” handed over to authorities between Oct. 1, 2024 — the date Sheinbaum was sworn in as president — and Oct. 12, 2026. The weapons were turned in under the government program Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz (Yes to Disarmament, Yes to Peace).

Rodríguez noted that people who handed over weapons received cash from authorities. She also said that children have exchanged more than 15,000 “war toys” for “educational toys” since Sheinbaum took office.

Over 70,000 arrests since Sheinbaum took office

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch reported that 70,571 people were arrested for allegedly committing high-impact crimes between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026. Among the offenses classified as high-impact crimes are murder, kidnapping, violent robbery, rape and extortion.

According to the information presented by García Harfuch, authorities seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs between Oct. 1, 2024, and Sept. 30, 2026.

In addition, authorities dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug laboratories in the same period.

Sheinbaum pledges to address the concerns of protesting healthcare workers

A reporter asked the president what message she would send to IMSS workers planning to protest on Thursday.

Sheinbaum first pointed to her government’s healthcare achievements.

“It’s important that what we’ve done in two years is known,” she said before reporting a range of achievements, including the construction of 34 new public hospitals and the opening or modernization of 650 operating rooms.

“We haven’t had our arms crossed. We’ve been working intensely for two years to support the country’s healthcare system,” Sheinbaum said.

She acknowledged that there is more to do, specifically noting that authorities need to hire more specialist doctors for the public health system. Sheinbaum also said that resident doctors’ “scholarships” need to be increased, and pledged that would happen in 2027.

“They earn less than the minimum wage,” she said.

“And a lot of the time the work of specialists falls on them. … The operation of [public] hospitals is supported by them in many cases,” Sheinbaum said.

She also said that the government has work to do to resolve problems related to the distribution of medications, although she indicated that the Rutas de la Salud (Health Routes) program — which delivers medicines and medical supplies to public healthcare facilities — is functioning well.

Sheinbaum said her government would address legitimate demands of public healthcare workers, but rejected claims that there is a “crisis” in Mexico’s health system. She said that healthcare workers have the “freedom” to protest, but urged them to do so peacefully.

“The objective is to have the best healthcare system and make progress on [addressing] some deficiencies we’ve had for some time,” Sheinbaum said.

World.title: Army rescues 32 in Ensenada as floods and landslides endanger lives on Mexico’s Pacific coast
World.content:
Air search and rescue operations are ramping up as twin storm systems batter Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing the deaths of at least five people.

In response to Hurricanes Rachel and Simon, the Defense Ministry (Sedena) has activated Plan DN-III-E, its operational emergency management plan that places thousands of soldiers, sailors and national guardsmen on alert to protect and aid civilians during natural disasters. Some 14,000 federal and state agents were deployed across Baja California to respond to the emergency.

Soldiers and guardsmen on Monday rescued 32 people stranded outside Ensenada, Baja California, after a mudslide caused by Tropical Storm Rachel cut off their only escape route.

The Air Force employed a “UH-60” Black Hawk helicopter to carry out three air operations, rescuing 22 foreign nationals, 10 Mexicans and three dogs.

The evacuees were members of the Genesis religious community, a Christian ministry that operates orphan care, camps and community outreach programs just outside the port city in the northwestern part of the peninsula.

Rachel, now wreaking havoc in southern California and places as far inland as Las Vegas, has already claimed the lives of four people — including two children — in Mexico.

Ejército Mexicano, Fuerza Aérea y Guardia Nacional rescata a 32 personas y tres caninos en Ensenada, Baja California. Este 12 de octubre del presente año, personal del Ejército, Fuerza Aérea y Guardia Nacional como parte de la aplicación del Plan DN-III-E realizaron una operación aérea de búsqueda y rescate, con el fin de evacuar a integrantes de una congregación religiosa que quedaron aislados en el rancho “Genesis”, Ensenada, B.C., debido a un deslizamiento de tierra que dificultó el acceso terrestre a la zona el cual fue provocado por las fuertes lluvias de la tormenta tropical “Rachel”. Ante las condiciones adversas del terreno, clima y las dificultades para acceder por vía terrestre, la Fuerza Aérea Mexicana empleó un helicóptero UH-60, cuya tripulación ejecutó tres operaciones aéreas que permitieron rescatar exitosamente a 22 personas extranjeras, 10 de nacionalidad mexicana y 3 caninos que se encontraban imposibilitados para trasladarse a un lugar seguro, a quienes se les proporcionó atención médica oportuna. Con estas acciones, el Ejército Mexicano, la Fuerza Aérea y la Guardia Nacional, refrendan su compromiso de brindar el auxilio necesario en situaciones de emergencia, poniendo todas sus capacidades operativas, preparación y recursos al servicio de la población, con el objetivo prioritario de salvaguardar la vida y la integridad de las personas. #EjércitoMexicano #FuerzaAéreaMx #GuardiaNacional — @Defensamx (@Defensamx1) October 13, 2026

Baja authorities say at least five others remain missing as floodwaters swept away vehicles, damaged homes and knocked out electricity in Ensenada, while landslides and overflowing rivers were causing problems across the state.

In addition to Sedena’s efforts, Tijuana’s mayor ordered specialized personnel from the municipality’s Security Ministry to support operations in Ensenada, about 80 kilometers (50 miles) to the south.

The Tijuana delegation includes specialists from the Fire Department trained in rescue maneuvers in rugged terrain and hydrometeorological contingency situations, members of the Canine Unit and agents from its Search Cell division.

Farther south, Hurricane Simon is following in Rachel’s path.

Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man in Chilpancingo, Guerrero, while also downing trees and electricity poles, making roads impassable and flooding homes in coastal towns.

Though Simon has weakened to a Category 1 hurricane, it is expected to maintain hurricane strength through Wednesday, though its short-term direction and intensity track has defied forecasters’ expectations.

About 127 to 255 millimeters (5 to 10 inches) of rain are expected from Simon across coastal west-central Mexico, with as much as 380 mm (15 inches) in the state of Sinaloa by Thursday.

Flooding and landslides have also been reported in the states of Michoacán and Colima.

With reports from Reporte Índigo, The Guardian, CBS News and La Jornada

World.title: Guyana Opposition Leader Arrested After Shooting
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Central Georgetown and the Demerara River waterfront, seen from the air in February 2015. (Photo: amanderson2, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

POLITICS · GUYANA

Key Facts — The country Guyana is an English-speaking South American country whose offshore oil output is led by US company ExxonMobil.

— Why it matters The arrested man is Guyana’s Opposition Leader, under US Treasury sanctions since June 2024 and facing a US extradition request.

— Why now The shooting came hours before Mohamed was due at the Court of Appeal to challenge parts of Guyana’s extradition law.

— What happened Police say the Special Branch chief fired at Mohamed’s car at about 11:45 p.m. on Monday 12 October after hearing an apparent gunshot.

— The numbers Police report one .32 pistol without a serial number, three live rounds, one spent .32 shell and four spent 9mm shells.

— What it means for US readers The man Washington wants extradited is now also the subject of a separate Guyanese firearm investigation.

— Still open Whether charges follow, what ballistic tests and CCTV footage show, and whether any shot came from the car.

Guyana opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed was arrested in Georgetown late on Monday 12 October, the Guyana Police Force said. Police said the head of the Special Branch intelligence unit fired at his car after hearing what appeared to be a gunshot.

Mohamed, 39, is under US Treasury sanctions and faces a US extradition request, so the case reaches well beyond Guyanese politics. He says police tried to kill him and planted a pistol in the car, and none of the claims on either side has been tested in court.

Mohamed leads We Invest in Nationhood (WIN), the main opposition party in the National Assembly, according to Demerara Waves. He was formally declared Opposition Leader in January 2026, after the 2025 general election.

What Police Say Happened in Kitty

According to the Guyana Police Force statement, the incident happened at about 11:45 p.m. on Barr Street in Kitty, a district of Georgetown. Senior Superintendent Prem Narine, the head of Special Branch, said he saw a black Toyota Allion moving slowly past his home.

The car passed his residence and returned a short while later, police said. As it approached a second time, Narine heard what appeared to be a gunshot, took cover and fired several rounds from his service weapon.

The car drove away and was later stopped at the junction of Vlissengen Road and Sandy Babb Street, also in Kitty. Inside were Mohamed and two men from Timehri, on the East Bank of Demerara, aged 25 and 35.

Police said a search of the car, carried out in front of the three men, found a .32 Taurus pistol with no serial number. Officers also found three live .32 rounds, and the three men were arrested for possessing a firearm and ammunition without a licence.

Investigators recovered one spent .32 shell on the southern side of Barr Street, roughly opposite Narine’s home, and four spent 9mm shells. Police said the weapon, ammunition and shells were sent for ballistic testing and that CCTV footage from the area will be reviewed.

Police are also investigating an alleged discharge of a loaded firearm with intent, News Source Guyana reported. The state-owned Guyana Chronicle said Narine told police he had previously seen the same car watching his home.

The three men remained in police custody on Tuesday as the investigation continued, police said. The statements published by Tuesday afternoon did not say whether any charge would follow.

Mohamed Says the Gun Was Planted

Speaking on a Facebook Live from the Kitty police station early on Tuesday, Mohamed said officers fired at the vehicle intending to kill him. He said shots were fired on Barr Street and again at the car on Vlissengen Road, Demerara Waves reported.

Mohamed and his lawyer, Siand Dhurjon, said an earlier search of the car found nothing and that the pistol was planted. Dhurjon said the gun, found under the accelerator pedal after a sniffer dog was brought in, had not been there seconds before.

According to News Source Guyana, Mohamed said he and his workers were in the area to document what he called an abuse of state resources. He pointed to a large police presence outside the Special Branch chief’s home, and the outlet reported visible gunshot damage on the car.

These are allegations by one side, and the police account is also an early version of events. Mohamed and the two other men are presumed innocent, and no court has yet examined any of the evidence.

The Extradition Case Behind the Clash

Narine is a witness in the hearing on the US request to extradite Mohamed, held before Chief Magistrate Judy Latchman. On the stand he has called Mohamed a threat to national security, citing alleged killings for which Mohamed has never been charged.

On Tuesday the Court of Appeal heard Mohamed’s challenge to Guyana’s extradition law, the Fugitive Offenders Act, in his absence. Acting Chancellor Roxane George reserved the ruling, noting the court has up to one month to decide, News Room reported.

It is the latest police action involving the Guyana opposition leader this year. Earlier detentions this year were covered in Guyana Opposition Leader Arrested Twice, Then Released.

His Facebook posts have also drawn scrutiny, with a lawyer for President Irfaan Ali reporting one of them to Meta, as covered in Guyana Lawyer Flags Opposition Post to Meta. On Monday night Mohamed again used a live social media broadcast to put his side of the confrontation.

What It Means for US Readers

On Tuesday 11 June 2024, the US Treasury sanctioned Mohamed, his father Nazar Mohamed and their gold company, Mohamed’s Enterprise, for public corruption. It acted under Executive Order 13818, which implements the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act.

Treasury said the company left more than 10,000 kilograms of gold out of import and export declarations between 2019 and 2023. It said this avoided more than US$50 million in duty taxes owed to the government of Guyana.

For US companies and investors active in Guyana’s oil-driven economy, the sanctions mean dealings with him or his listed companies are off limits. A Guyanese firearm investigation now runs alongside the US extradition effort against the same man.

Guyana keeps the same clock as US Eastern time in October, so the shooting took place at about 11:45 p.m. New York time too. The police statements describe one encounter across two streets and mention no wider risk to the public.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the apparent gunshot Narine reported came from the car, or who fired the .32 shell found on Barr Street. Ballistic tests and CCTV footage should help answer those questions, but no results had been published by Tuesday afternoon.

It is unclear how custody affects the Guyana opposition leader’s extradition hearing, and the appeal ruling may take up to a month. Police had not said by Tuesday afternoon whether charges or bail would follow for any of the three men.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was arrested in Kitty, Georgetown?

Police identified the three occupants of the car as Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed and two men from Timehri aged 25 and 35. They were arrested on suspicion of possessing a firearm and ammunition without a licence.

Why did the police officer fire at the car?

Senior Superintendent Prem Narine, head of Special Branch, said he heard what appeared to be a gunshot as the car passed his home a second time. He took cover and fired several rounds from his service weapon, police said.

What does Azruddin Mohamed say happened?

He says police tried to kill him and planted the pistol, which his lawyer says was found under the accelerator pedal. None of these claims has been tested in court.

Why is the Guyana opposition leader under US sanctions?

The US Treasury sanctioned him on 11 June 2024 for public corruption linked to gold exports. Treasury said his family company avoided more than US$50 million in duty taxes owed to Guyana.

Has anyone been charged?

Police statements published by Tuesday afternoon did not announce any charge. All three men are presumed innocent.

Sources: Guyana Chronicle (Guyana Police Force statement); News Source Guyana; News Room Guyana; Demerara Waves; Demerara Waves (Mohamed’s account); News Room Guyana (Court of Appeal); US Department of the Treasury, 11 June 2024.

World.title: Who Is Nyesom Wike, Tinubu’s Opposition Ally
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

PROFILE · NIGERIA

Key Facts — The country Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, holds a presidential election in 2027. President Bola Tinubu of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is seeking a second term.

— Why it matters Nyesom Wike, a former Rivers State governor and now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), brings opposition votes to Tinubu while staying in the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

— Why now On Monday 12 October in Abuja, Wike said he helped the APC defeat his own party’s candidate in the 2024 Edo State governorship election.

— What happened Wike said he was “behind” the alliance and has “no regrets”. On Tuesday 13 October the APC named him Tinubu’s campaign coordinator for Rivers State and the FCT.

— The numbers The electoral commission (INEC) declared the APC’s Monday Okpebholo the Edo winner with 291,667 votes. The PDP’s Asue Ighodalo polled 247,274.

— What it means for US readers A broad cross-party coalition improves Tinubu’s re-election odds, pointing to policy continuity in a major oil exporter. It also deepens doubts about the strength of Nigeria’s opposition.

— Still open Whether either PDP faction disciplines Wike, and whether his Rainbow Coalition can deliver votes in Rivers and Abuja.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Bola Tinubu a 74% chance of winning the 2027 presidential election (13 October, 2:49 p.m. ET).

Nyesom Wike, the minister who runs Nigeria’s capital territory, admitted on Monday 12 October that he helped the ruling party beat his own. He told a cross-party meeting in Abuja that he was “behind” the 2024 Edo alliance and has “no regrets”.

The admission matters beyond Nigeria because Wike now openly works to re-elect President Bola Tinubu while keeping his opposition party card. For US investors, a smoother path for Tinubu points to continuity in Africa’s most populous country and a major oil exporter.

Wike, a member of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), spoke at a meeting of the Rainbow Coalition, according to Premium Times. That is a cross-party platform mobilising support for Tinubu, the leader of the governing All Progressives Congress (APC), in 2027.

From Rivers Governor to Abuja Minister

Wike was sworn in as governor of Rivers State on Friday 29 May 2015 and served two four-year terms. Rivers, whose capital is Port Harcourt, sits at the centre of Nigeria’s oil-producing Niger Delta.

Tinubu swore him in as FCT minister on Monday 21 August 2023, Daily Post reported. The post puts him in charge of administering Abuja, the federal capital, including land titles and city planning.

On the day he was sworn in, Wike vowed to do the job without fear or favour. He said that included the national secretariat of his own party if it lacked a valid certificate of occupancy.

The PDP governed Nigeria from 1999 until 2015 and remains the best-known opposition brand. Premium Times reports that Wike is still a PDP member despite serving in Tinubu’s APC-led government.

The party is now split into rival camps, one of them backed by Wike. INEC, the electoral commission, has been dealing with a National Working Committee led by Abdulrahman Mohammed, Daily Post reported in August.

A rival faction, linked to Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, is led by Tanimu Turaki. Atiku Abubakar, the PDP’s 2023 nominee, is now the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

What Wike Said About Edo

The Edo governorship election was held on Saturday 21 September 2024. INEC declared the APC’s Monday Okpebholo the winner with 291,667 votes, against 247,274 for the PDP’s Asue Ighodalo.

Labour Party candidate Olumide Akpata received 22,763 votes, according to INEC’s announced results. The Supreme Court upheld Okpebholo’s victory in July 2025, Daily Post reported.

Wike said his aim was to stop the outgoing PDP governor, Godwin Obaseki, from installing a successor. Obaseki governed Edo from 2016 to 2024 and backed Ighodalo, whom Wike described as a former bank chairman.

Wike said Ighodalo came to see him “more than three times” to ask for support. “Returning you would be like bringing him back, so I am sorry, you have to fail,” Wike recalled telling him.

He said Adams Oshiomhole, a former APC national chairman, could attest to the alliance. Wike also argued that coalitions across party lines have long been a normal part of Nigerian elections.

A Record of Crossing Party Lines

Edo was not the first time Wike worked against his own party’s candidate. Before the 2023 election he led the G-5, five PDP governors who refused to back the party’s presidential nominee, Atiku Abubakar.

The group demanded the resignation of then party chairman Iyorchia Ayu, arguing that the nominee and chairman should not both come from the north. Tinubu won that election, with Atiku second and the Labour Party’s Peter Obi third.

In Rivers, INEC declared Tinubu the winner with 231,591 votes, ahead of Obi with 175,071 and Atiku with 88,468. A later Premium Times review of uploaded polling-unit results found substantial discrepancies in Obio/Akpor, Wike’s political stronghold.

In March 2025, Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers and installed an administrator, retired Vice Admiral Ibok Ibas. Daily Post reported that the president announced it in a nationwide broadcast on the night of Tuesday 18 March.

Tinubu’s Opposition Ally for 2027

At Monday’s meeting, Wike declared himself coordinator of Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the FCT and Rivers State. Participants from the PDP and APC reportedly agreed to back APC candidates for the FCT’s Senate and House seats.

Daily Trust reported on Tuesday that the APC’s revised presidential campaign council formally named him coordinator for both (see APC Campaign Council Adds Wike, Adeleke, Soludo). The same list made Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke the campaign coordinator in Osun.

Senator Abdulaziz Yari remains director-general of the re-election campaign, Daily Trust said. Oshiomhole, the former Edo governor Wike cited as a witness to the Edo deal, is deputy director-general for mobilisation.

The arrangement puts Wike in the position of campaigning against candidates of the party he formally belongs to. For a wider map of who holds power, see Nigeria Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026.

What It Means for US Readers

For US investors and policymakers, the main signal is that Tinubu is assembling support from inside the opposition well before the vote. A broad coalition could lower the odds of an abrupt reversal of his economic programme, covered in Nigeria’s Tinubu Cites World Bank Report on 4.2% Growth.

Rivers State is home to Port Harcourt, a hub of the Niger Delta oil and gas industry that drives Nigeria’s exports. Political calm there matters to energy companies, shipping firms and anyone watching global oil supply.

The risk is that deal-making across party lines weakens the opposition and feeds distrust in elections. At least 25 observer groups said the 2024 Edo vote fell short of expectations, criticising how results were collated, Daily Post reported.

Americans who visit or work in Abuja deal with a city whose land and planning decisions run through Nyesom Wike’s office. Any shift in his political standing could therefore reach well beyond party politics.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the PDP will discipline Nyesom Wike, or which faction would have the authority to do so. No formal response from either faction to Monday’s remarks could be confirmed by Tuesday evening.

It is also unclear how many PDP voters in Rivers and the FCT will follow him to Tinubu. The Rainbow Coalition has not yet been tested at the ballot box as a platform.

Wike’s account of how the 2024 Edo result was won has not been independently confirmed. The PDP disputed that result at the time, but the Supreme Court later upheld Okpebholo’s win.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based betting platform, gives Tinubu a 74% chance of winning the 2027 presidential election as of 2:49 p.m. ET on 13 October. Peter Obi is next at 21%, and these prices reflect bets, not polls.

About US$130,000 has been traded on the overall election market, including about US$82,000 on the Tinubu contract. Tinubu’s price has risen about 2.5 percentage points over the past week.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Nyesom Wike?

Nyesom Wike is Nigeria’s Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, the official who administers Abuja. He was governor of Rivers State from 2015 to 2023 and remains a member of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party.

What did Wike admit about the 2024 Edo election?

On Monday 12 October he said he worked with the ruling APC to defeat his own party’s candidate, Asue Ighodalo. He said he wanted to stop former governor Godwin Obaseki from installing a successor and has no regrets.

What role does Wike have in Tinubu’s 2027 campaign?

The APC’s revised presidential campaign council names him campaign coordinator for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory, Daily Trust reported on 13 October.

Is Wike still in the PDP?

Yes. Premium Times reports he remains a PDP member, even though he serves in Tinubu’s APC-led government and campaigns for the president’s re-election.

Why does this matter to US readers?

Wike’s cross-party support strengthens Tinubu’s re-election chances in a major oil exporter, which points to policy continuity. It also raises questions about the health of Nigeria’s opposition and trust in elections.

Sources: Premium Times, 13 October 2026; Daily Post, 13 October 2026; Daily Trust, 13 October 2026; Daily Post, 21 August 2023; Daily Post, 11 July 2025; Daily Post, 19 March 2025; Daily Post, 11 August 2026; Daily Post, 25 September 2024.

World.title: Colombia Summons Eva Ferrer in Alcocer Probe
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Central Bogotá seen from Monserrate hill. Colombia's oversight bodies, including the Procuraduría, are based in the capital. (Photo: Javier Benítez, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

POLITICS · COLOMBIA

Key Facts — The country Colombia, a close US security partner, swapped Gustavo Petro’s leftist government for conservative President Abelardo De La Espriella in August.

— Why it matters Former first lady Verónica Alcocer faces allegations of flying drugs to Venezuela and returning with cash. The US Treasury already sanctioned her and Petro in October 2025.

— Why now On Tuesday 13 October the Procuraduría, the watchdog that disciplines public officials, summoned Eva Ferrer and five others to testify under oath.

— What happened The watchdog also opened a preliminary inquiry into unnamed Air Force and presidency officials over the use of official aircraft between 2023 and 2026.

— What it means for US readers These are allegations, not charges. Any finding could feed US scrutiny of a sanctioned former first family and of flights to Venezuela.

— Still open Whether Ferrer shows evidence, whether she attends a prosecutors’ summons on Wednesday 14 October, and whether Alcocer answers the new claims.

Colombia’s Inspector General’s Office, the Procuraduría, on Tuesday summoned Eva Ferrer and five other people to testify under oath. Ferrer is a former adviser who accuses ex-first lady Verónica Alcocer of flying drugs and cash between Venezuela and Colombia.

The case matters abroad because Washington already treats Alcocer as a sanctions target. The US Treasury designated her and her then husband, former President Gustavo Petro, on Friday 24 October 2025.

Nothing has been proven, and nobody has been charged over the new claims. Alcocer, Petro and everyone named are entitled to the presumption of innocence.

Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Procuraduría Ordered

The Procuraduría General de la Nación announced the summons on Tuesday 13 October in a statement from Bogotá. It said the testimony relates to alleged acts of corruption by several public servants, as reported by Semana magazine on Saturday.

Besides Ferrer, the order names Carmen Caballero, Angie Rodríguez, Concepción Baracaldo, Guillermo Reyes and Ingrid Carolina Plata Navas. Each must testify under oath in the same case.

Semana describes Rodríguez as a former head of the Administrative Department of the Presidency, known as Dapre. It lists Baracaldo as an ex-head of the ICBF welfare agency, Caballero of ProColombia and Reyes as ex-ambassador to Sweden.

The order tells the watchdog’s National Directorate of Special Investigations to gather evidence on the published claims. The Procuraduría said the step extends an inquiry it had already opened after earlier Semana reports quoting Ferrer.

Later on Tuesday, the Procuraduría issued a second order over aircraft of the Colombian Aerospace Force, known as FAC. It opened a preliminary inquiry into officials of the FAC and Dapre who have not yet been identified.

The aim, the watchdog said, is to identify any alleged offenders and establish whether the facts existed and have disciplinary relevance. A preliminary inquiry is the earliest stage of a disciplinary case and is not an accusation.

According to the order seen by El Tiempo and Semana, investigators will inspect Dapre and the military air transport command, Catam. They want records of Alcocer’s trips to Venezuela from 2023 to 2026, including passengers, crews and flight orders.

The Procuraduría disciplines public officials and can suspend or dismiss them, but it does not bring criminal charges. Criminal cases belong to the Attorney General’s Office, the Fiscalía, which runs its own inquiry.

What Ferrer Alleges and How Petro’s Camp Responded

Ferrer, who was born in Barcelona, ran Alcocer’s communications during Petro’s 2022 campaign and later served as a presidential adviser. El Tiempo and El Heraldo both describe that background, and she later fell out with Alcocer.

In an interview published by Semana on Saturday 10 October, Ferrer alleged that Alcocer flew drugs to Venezuela on an official aircraft. She also claimed Alcocer returned from one trip in January 2023 with US$2.5 million.

Ferrer said she learned of the cash from a man named Manel Grau, not first hand. She said photos of drug-filled suitcases seem to exist but has not published them.

Petro rejected the claims on X on Monday 12 October and announced legal action. He challenged Semana’s owner, Gabriel Gilinski, to prove that Alcocer used an Air Force plane to traffic drugs or weapons.

Petro also asked his daughters and their mother to sue Gilinski for aggravated slander, according to El Heraldo. He also said the claims could hurt Air Force officers who only followed their superiors’ orders.

Alcocer had not answered the Saturday interview publicly by Tuesday evening, as far as Colombian media reported. When Ferrer’s first recordings surfaced in August, Alcocer said the claims lacked any basis and did not correspond to reality.

Senator Agmeth Escaf, whom Ferrer also accuses, told Caracol Radio the claims are a smear campaign against Petro’s progressive movement. He said Ferrer’s account has changed over time and that he is preparing legal action for slander.

Separately, the Fiscalía has summoned Ferrer for a third time to give a statement at 9:00 a.m. on Wednesday 14 October, Caracol Radio reported. She did not appear at earlier dates in August and on 29 September.

That criminal inquiry stems from recordings Semana released on 1 August, in which Ferrer first raised claims about Alcocer’s circle. An earlier report, Colombia Probes Alcocer Flights Over US$2.5M Claim, covered the Air Force inquiry ordered on Saturday.

What It Means for US Readers

The US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control designated Petro, Alcocer, Petro’s son Nicolás and Armando Benedetti in October 2025. It acted under counternarcotics authorities, accusing Petro of allowing drug cartels to flourish.

New claims that link Alcocer to Venezuela land in a sensitive place for Washington. President De La Espriella has asked US authorities, along with Colombian courts and prosecutors, to examine the allegations within their powers.

For investors, the case is political noise rather than a market event. De La Espriella‘s government moved quickly on the claims, while Petro’s camp calls them a campaign against the opposition.

Travellers and businesses face no direct effect from a disciplinary inquiry. The calmer reading is that the claims now move into formal channels, where testimony and flight records can confirm or dismiss them.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Ferrer holds documents, photos or witnesses that support her account. Her main cash claim rests on what she says Grau told her, and he has not publicly confirmed it.

It is unclear whether Ferrer will attend either summons, given that she missed two earlier dates set by prosecutors. The Procuraduría has not published dates for the six testimonies.

Nobody yet knows which Air Force or presidency officials, if any, will face disciplinary charges. Alcocer’s own response to the new interview, and any US reaction, also remain open.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Eva Ferrer?

Eva Ferrer is a Barcelona-born communications strategist who ran Verónica Alcocer’s image during Petro’s 2022 campaign. She later served as a presidential adviser before falling out with Alcocer.

What did the Procuraduría decide on 13 October?

It summoned Ferrer and five others to testify under oath about alleged corruption reported by Semana. It also opened a preliminary inquiry into unnamed Air Force and presidency officials over official flights.

Has Verónica Alcocer been charged?

No. The allegations have not been proven, and the Procuraduría inquiry targets public officials rather than Alcocer herself.

What do Petro and Alcocer say?

Petro called the claims false, challenged Semana’s owner to show proof and announced lawsuits. In August, Alcocer said earlier claims lacked any basis and did not correspond to reality.

Why does this matter to the United States?

The US Treasury sanctioned Petro and Alcocer in October 2025 over alleged drug links. President De La Espriella has asked US authorities to examine the new allegations too.

World.title: Mercado Libre Founder Attacks Argentina Loan-Cost Rule
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

A Mercado Libre office building in the Saavedra district of Buenos Aires. The company runs the Mercado Pago lending app. (Photo: Fernando Martello, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

MARKETS · ARGENTINA

Key Facts — The country Argentina, where the central bank (BCRA) sets disclosure rules for banks and registered non-bank lenders, including fintech apps such as Mercado Pago.

— Why it matters Mercado Libre, listed on Nasdaq as MELI, offers consumer loans in Argentina through its Mercado Pago app, so the rule shapes how its prices look.

— Why now On Monday 12 October founder Marcos Galperin called the cost figure the BCRA makes lenders publish “false” and “inflated”.

— What happened He was replying to a screenshot of a Mercado Pago loan showing a 60% nominal rate and a 102.36% total annual cost.

— The numbers In that example a borrower receives 10,000 pesos (about US$6.61) and repays 14,496.24 pesos (about US$9.58) over 12 months.

— What it means for US readers How regulators let Mercado Pago present its loan prices affects demand, reputation and regulatory risk for a Nasdaq-listed company.

— Still open No public reply from the BCRA had been reported by Tuesday evening, and no change to the rule has been announced.

Marcos Galperin, founder of Mercado Libre, has opened a Mercado Libre loan cost row with Argentina’s central bank. On Monday 12 October he wrote on X that the official annual loan cost figure lenders must display is false and inflated.

The row matters to US investors because Mercado Libre trades on Nasdaq and its Mercado Pago app lends to consumers across Argentina. It also shows how hard it is for borrowers in a high-inflation economy to compare what credit really costs.

What Galperin Said and Why

The dispute began on Sunday 11 October, when Argentine economist Agustín Etchebarne posted a Mercado Pago loan simulation on X. Under the heading “basic financial education”, he advised people to check the total financial cost before borrowing.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Galperin, who founded Mercado Libre in 1999 and became executive chairman on 1 January 2026, replied the next day. “The ‘Total Effective Annual Financial Cost’ that the BCRA requires to be published is FALSE, INCORRECT,” he wrote, Infobae reported.

He argued that the measure assumes compound interest and a loan rolled over again and again for a full year. “In tens of millions of loans granted, that NEVER happens,” he added.

Etchebarne answered on Tuesday 13 October that the indicator is exactly what borrowers need to compare annual costs. “In no way is it false,” he wrote, according to Perfil.

The economist also called for scrapping the taxes charged on credit, which he said make borrowers pay twice. The Buenos Aires financial daily Ámbito reported that Galperin had distanced himself from the government with the post.

One Mercado Pago loan simulation, four numbers: 60% nominal, 79.59% effective, 102.36% total annual cost, but about 45% more repaid over 12 instalments. (Chart: The Rio Times; data from the loan screen shared on X on 11 October, as reported by Infobae and iProfesional) RT Ask Rio Times Latin American markets, currencies and companies. What the Central Bank Rule Requires

BCRA rules require every loan contract and receipt to state the nominal rate, the effective annual rate and the total financial cost. The total cost must be “expressed as an effective annual rate” that adds commissions and charges to interest.

Advertising faces a stricter test. In s, the total financial cost must appear in a highlighted colour, in type five times larger than the nominal rate.

The requirement is not new, since the current definition dates from a BCRA communication that took effect in July 2018. The separate consumer-protection rulebook, last updated on 6 May 2026, extends these duties to non-bank credit providers.

In guidance quoted by Infobae, the central bank says the total cost “shows how much a loan really costs”. It includes interest, fees, insurance and tax, and the bank advises borrowers to compare it rather than the instalment alone.
