What MercadoLibre does. MercadoLibre, Inc. operates online commerce platforms in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, and internationally. The company operates Mercado Libre Marketplace, an online commerce platform that can be accessed through mobile app or website; and Mercado Pago, a financial technology solution platform, which offers comprehensive set of financial technology services to users and other users…

How One Loan Shows Four Prices

In the simulation, a borrower receives 10,000 pesos (about US$6.61) and pays 12 fixed instalments of 1,208.02 pesos (about US$0.80). The total repaid is 14,496.24 pesos (about US$9.58), at the BCRA reference rate of 1,512.50 pesos per US dollar on Tuesday 13 October.

The screen shows a nominal rate of 60%, which is 5% a month. Compounded over 12 months, that becomes the 79.59% effective annual rate, and taxes and charges lift the total annual cost to 102.36%.

Yet the borrower in this example repays about 45% more than they received, not 102%. That gap exists because each instalment repays part of the principal, so the balance shrinks through the year.

Mercado Pago made the same point in August, after reports that some of its loans showed annual costs of up to 1,375%. The company said then that only about 2% of its loans carried that top rate, according to Infobae.

Etchebarne’s reply is that an annualised figure lets borrowers compare loans of different lengths on one scale. That is the logic of the BCRA rule, and Galperin’s reported posts did not propose a replacement measure.

For background, see Mercado Libre’s Founder Faces a Criminal Usury Complaint Over Loans Costing Up to 1,375% a Year. For the company’s recent debt sale, read MercadoLibre Raises US$1 Billion in Ten-Year Notes.

What It Means for US Readers

For MELI shareholders, the Mercado Libre loan cost dispute shows that lending in Argentina is regulated and politically sensitive. A headline cost above 100% invites scrutiny from courts, consumer groups and lawmakers, even when the cash cost is far lower.

The stabiliser is that the rule has applied since at least 2018, so lenders already work within it. No BCRA communication announcing a change had been published by Tuesday.

For Americans living in Argentina or using local apps, the lesson is practical. Compare the total amount repaid in pesos as well as the annual percentage, because the two numbers answer different questions.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Mercado Libre will formally ask the BCRA to change the method or will challenge it in court. The company had issued no statement beyond Galperin’s posts by Tuesday evening.

It is also unclear how the government of President Javier Milei, a libertarian economist, will respond to the criticism. The BCRA had not commented publicly on Galperin’s claims at the time of writing.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Marcos Galperin say about the BCRA rule?

On Monday 12 October he called the annual cost figure the central bank makes lenders publish false and inflated. He said it wrongly assumes compounding and repeated renewal over a year.

What is the CFTEA in Argentina?

It is the total financial cost of a loan expressed as an effective annual rate. Under BCRA rules it adds commissions, charges and certain taxes to the interest rate so borrowers can compare offers.

Is the rule new?

No. The current definition dates from a BCRA communication that took effect in July 2018. It applies to banks and registered non-bank lenders.

Does a 102% annual cost mean a borrower pays back double?

No. In the example shared on X, the borrower received 10,000 pesos (about US$6.61) and repaid about 45% more over 12 instalments.

Why does this matter to US investors?

The Mercado Libre loan cost row involves a Nasdaq-listed company, ticker MELI, that lends in Argentina through Mercado Pago. Rules on how loan prices are shown can affect demand and regulatory risk.

World.title: Costa Rica Arrests 2 in Liberia Journalist Killing
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

A street in central Liberia, the capital of Guanacaste province in northwest Costa Rica (Photo: Ll1324, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CRIME · COSTA RICA

Key Facts — The country Costa Rica, a Central American democracy where the OIJ (Organismo de Investigación Judicial, the judicial police) investigates homicides and other serious crime.

— Why it matters A well-known local news presenter was shot dead near Liberia, the Guanacaste city whose airport lists 20 destinations in the United States.

— Why now After about 11 weeks of investigation, OIJ agents raided three homes in Liberia before dawn on Tuesday 13 October.

— What happened Two men, aged 27 and 23, were detained over the killing of Wilfredo Pizarro Bermúdez on Thursday 30 July. A third suspect is at large.

— The numbers Three suspects, three raids, two arrests and seven shots, according to the OIJ. Pizarro was 51.

— What it means for US readers The OIJ describes a ride requested by someone who knew the victim, not a random attack. Visitors should still use official taxis or registered ride apps.

— Still open The motive, the role of each suspect, the third man’s whereabouts and whether a court orders pretrial detention.

Costa Rica’s judicial police arrested two men on Tuesday 13 October over the Liberia journalist killing that shook the province of Guanacaste. Wilfredo Pizarro Bermúdez, a 51-year-old regional news presenter, was shot dead near Liberia on Thursday 30 July.

Liberia is the gateway city for many US visitors, because its Guanacaste Airport lists 20 destinations in the United States. The arrests show investigators moving on a high-profile violent case in the country’s main Pacific beach region.

What Happened in Liberia on Tuesday

The Organismo de Investigación Judicial (OIJ), Costa Rica’s judicial police, began three simultaneous raids at 4 a.m. local time. Agents searched two homes in barrio Corazón de Jesús, in central Liberia, and one in the Martina Bustos neighbourhood.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 with 36.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (75); weakest: military means (0). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Two men, aged 27 and 23, were detained and handed to the Ministerio Público, the public prosecutor’s office. Teletica reported that a hearing on precautionary measures, such as pretrial detention, would follow.

A third suspect is still on the run, and on Tuesday the OIJ published his name and photograph to ask the public for help. Agents also seized mobile phones in the raids, which the OIJ press office described as evidence in the case.

The OIJ has released only the surnames and ages of the two detained men. Neither man has been convicted of any crime, and both are presumed innocent under Costa Rican law.

How the OIJ Says the Killing Happened

Vladimir Muñoz, the OIJ’s acting deputy director, said one suspect apparently knew Pizarro and asked him for a ride. Pizarro, who also worked as an informal driver, picked up three men in barrio Corazón de Jesús, according to Muñoz.

The group then travelled to Calle Coyote in Cañas Dulces, a rural district of the Liberia canton, the OIJ said. “For reasons we do not yet know, an argument broke out,” Muñoz said, adding that Pizarro was shot seven times.

The suspects then took Pizarro’s car and other belongings, according to the OIJ. The car was found abandoned in Liberia days later, and La Nación reported, citing his family, that its dashboard camera was missing.

Pizarro’s sister told Telenoticias that his wallet and cash were found beside his body. Local outlets differ on the likely motive, with Teletica citing theft of the car and La Nación a possible personal dispute.

Who Wilfredo Pizarro Was

Pizarro was well known in Liberia as a presenter of news and local stories for Guananoticias, a regional outlet in Guanacaste. La Nación reported that he had also appeared on Telenoticias, the national newscast of Channel 7.

In an earlier municipal race, Guananoticias reported, the Frente Amplio, a left-wing party, chose him as its candidate for mayor of Liberia. The outlet said he was then also vice-president of a community development association in Las Brisas.

On the day he died, Pizarro went to the beach with his mother and then went back to driving passengers, Teletica reported. His family told La Nación on Tuesday that those responsible “have to pay” for what they did to him.

What It Means for US Readers

Guanacaste Airport in Liberia lists 20 US destinations on its website, including Atlanta, Houston, Dallas, Denver and New York. For many Americans heading to the Pacific beaches of Guanacaste, the city is the point of arrival.

The OIJ account describes a ride requested by someone who apparently knew the victim, not a random attack on strangers. Visitors are still wise to use official red taxis, airport shuttles or registered ride apps rather than informal drivers.

For frequent visitors and property owners, the arrests show the OIJ reaching suspects in a high-profile case within about 11 weeks. The risk is that the case stalls if the third suspect stays at large or the motive stays unclear.

The wider crime picture is set out in Costa Rica Retiree Safety: What the Numbers Show. Recent OIJ work elsewhere is covered in Costa Rica Police Raid 80 Sites in Cargo Theft Probe.

Press Safety and the Liberia Journalist Killing

The OIJ has not said whether Pizarro’s work as a presenter played any part in his death. Its public account so far centres on a requested ride, an argument and the theft of his car.

Regional outlets have followed the case closely since July, and La Teja published tributes from his friends in September. The arrests offer some reassurance to local reporters, although investigators have not publicly ruled out any motive.

What Is Not Known

The OIJ has not said who fired the shots or what role each suspect is alleged to have played. The reason for the argument is also unknown, by the OIJ’s own account.

It is not known where the third suspect is, or whether a court will order the two men held before trial. Formal charges against the detained men have not been made public.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was Wilfredo Pizarro?

Wilfredo Pizarro Bermúdez, 51, was a news presenter for the regional outlet Guananoticias in Liberia, Guanacaste. He also worked as an informal driver and was shot dead on 30 July 2026.

How many people were arrested in the Liberia journalist killing?

The OIJ detained two men, aged 27 and 23, in raids on Tuesday 13 October. A third suspect is still being sought, and all three are presumed innocent.

Was the killing linked to his journalism?

The OIJ has not said so. Its account centres on a requested ride, an argument for reasons still unknown and the theft of his car.

Is Liberia, Costa Rica, safe for US visitors?

The OIJ describes a crime involving someone who apparently knew the victim, not a random attack. Visitors should use official taxis, airport shuttles or registered ride apps.

What happens next in the case?

The two men were handed to the public prosecutor’s office, and a hearing on precautionary measures such as pretrial detention is expected. The search for the third suspect continues.

World.title: Puerto Rico Bird Flu Quarantine: What It Means
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The salt flats at Cabo Rojo National Wildlife Refuge in southwest Puerto Rico, an area that draws migratory birds. (Photo: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

HEALTH · PUERTO RICO

Key Facts — The country Puerto Rico, a US territory in the Caribbean whose residents are US citizens. The cases are in Cabo Rojo and Lajas, in the island’s southwest.

— Why it matters Bird flu can wipe out poultry flocks and occasionally infects people who handle sick birds. The CDC rates the current public health risk as low.

— Why now Laboratory tests confirming avian influenza on two private properties were announced on Tuesday, 13 October. Officials outlined health monitoring and possible hunting limits the same day.

— What happened The Department of Agriculture quarantined both properties for 120 days after about 20 ducks and 30 guinea fowl died.

— The numbers 27 people under health monitoring, none with symptoms so far. Duck-hunting season opens on Sunday, 1 November.

— What it means for US readers No travel restrictions have been announced. Avoid touching sick or dead birds, and cook poultry and eggs properly, as the CDC advises.

— Still open The source of the virus, whether duck hunting will be restricted, and whether any other property is affected.

Puerto Rico’s Department of Agriculture has placed two bird flu sites in Cabo Rojo and Lajas under a 120-day quarantine. The Puerto Rico bird flu quarantine follows tests, announced on Tuesday, 13 October, confirming avian influenza on two private, non-commercial properties.

For US readers, the island is American soil, and local officials say they are working with federal authorities on the case. Health officials say the risk to the general public is low, and none of the people being monitored has symptoms.

What the Quarantine Does

Agriculture Secretary Irving Rodríguez Torres, who heads the island government’s farm department, announced the test results on Tuesday. He said the quarantine covers the properties where the birds died, with limits on moving birds and strict cleaning and disinfection.

On the Cabo Rojo property about 20 Creole ducks died, according to the department. On the Lajas property several species died, including about 30 guinea fowl.

El Nuevo Día, a San Juan daily, reported that the department identified highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) as the cause. Rodríguez Torres said both sites are private farms, not commercial poultry operations.

The department’s main aim is to stop the virus reaching commercial farms or backyard flocks. If it reached a large farm, the secretary said, every bird there would have to be destroyed.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

He spoke at En Récord, the regular government press conference at La Fortaleza, the governor’s office in San Juan. Protecting the egg and poultry meat sector and avoiding economic losses is the priority, he said.

Officials suspect migratory birds, although the origin has not been established. Ducks were the species found at one site, and the secretary called migratory birds “the usual suspect.”

The department is discussing precautions with the Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DRNA), which regulates hunting. Duck-hunting season opens on Sunday, 1 November, and Rodríguez Torres said restrictions would be his suggestion.

He is concerned that hunters could carry infected birds home and spread the virus to other towns. The final decision rests with the natural resources secretary, he said.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Risk to People

Health Secretary Víctor Ramos Otero, head of the island’s Department of Health, said 27 people from the two farms are under surveillance. “So far, nobody has had symptoms,” he said on Tuesday.

Metro Puerto Rico reported that these contacts are being followed for 14 days. Ramos Otero described the chance of infection as very low and said treatment is the same as for any other influenza.

Symptoms resemble seasonal flu, he said, including fever, breathing difficulty, body aches and sometimes vomiting or diarrhoea. He added that anyone with symptoms would most likely have ordinary human flu, but tests are available.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) rates the current public health risk from A(H5) bird flu as low. Its situation page lists 71 reported US human cases since February 2024, with sporadic cases among dairy and poultry workers.

According to the CDC, people catch the virus mainly through close, prolonged and unprotected contact with infected birds or contaminated surfaces. Anyone who falls ill within 10 days of such contact should stay home and contact the health department.

What It Means for US Readers

Puerto Rico is a US territory, and its residents are US citizens. The case sits inside the US animal-health system, so the US Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) takes reports alongside local officials.

None of Tuesday’s official statements mentions any restriction on travel, beaches or hotels. The measures announced apply to the quarantined properties and to moving birds, not to visitors.

Visitors and residents should not touch, pick up or move sick or dead birds, officials say. Keeping pet or farm birds away from wild birds is the other main advice.

The secretary said there is no suspicion, for now, that any commercial poultry operation is affected. The CDC says cooking poultry and eggs to the proper internal temperature kills bacteria and viruses, including avian influenza.

The CDC also advises against eating raw or undercooked poultry and recommends washing hands after touching it. That is general food-safety guidance, not a measure specific to this outbreak.

To report sick birds or unusual deaths, call USDA-APHIS on 1-866-536-7593. The Puerto Rico Department of Agriculture takes calls on 787-721-2120.

The first laboratory results are covered in Puerto Rico Confirms Bird Flu in Two Towns. Bird flu has also prompted precautions elsewhere in the region, as in Barbados Steps Up Port Checks Over Suriname Bird Flu.

What Is Not Known

The source of the infection has not been confirmed, and migratory birds remain a working hypothesis. The virus subtype was not named in Tuesday’s official statements.

It is not known whether the DRNA will restrict the duck-hunting season before it opens. The final count of dead birds at the Lajas property has also not been published.

The 27 contacts remain under 14-day monitoring, and no human case has been reported. Officials have not said whether more properties will be tested beyond the two under quarantine.

The Puerto Rico bird flu quarantine runs for 120 days, so the limits on the two sites could last into February. Officials have not said whether it could end earlier or be extended.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Puerto Rico announce on 13 October?

The Department of Agriculture confirmed avian influenza in birds on two private properties in Cabo Rojo and Lajas. It imposed a 120-day quarantine with limits on moving birds and strict disinfection.

How long does the Puerto Rico bird flu quarantine last?

It runs for 120 days on the two affected properties. Officials have not said whether it could be shortened or extended.

Is it safe to visit Puerto Rico?

Officials have announced no travel restrictions, and the measures apply to the quarantined properties. Visitors should simply avoid touching sick or dead birds.

Can people catch bird flu from eggs or chicken?

The CDC says cooking poultry and eggs to the proper internal temperature kills avian influenza viruses. It advises against eating raw or undercooked poultry.

Has anyone in Puerto Rico been infected?

No human case has been reported. The Department of Health is monitoring 27 people who were at the two farms, and none had symptoms as of Tuesday.

World.title: Argentina Asks Sea Tribunal to Halt Falklands Oil Work
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The waterfront of Stanley, capital of the Falkland Islands, with Christ Church Cathedral (Photo: amanderson2, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

LAW OF THE SEA · ARGENTINA

Key Facts — The country Argentina claims the British-run Falkland Islands, which it calls the Malvinas. Britain has governed the islands since 1833 and fought Argentina over them in 1982.

— Why it matters Sea Lion, a Falklands oil project north of the islands, is preparing for development drilling. Argentina wants a treaty court to stop it before production starts.

— Why now A two-week deadline Argentina gave Britain to halt Sea Lion work has run out. Argentina opened arbitration under the UN Law of the Sea convention on Monday 28 September.

— What happened On Tuesday 13 October Argentina asked the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in Hamburg for four provisional measures against Britain, the tribunal confirmed.

— What it means for US readers The case tests whether a treaty court can freeze oil work in disputed waters. It adds legal risk for Falklands oil investors, but nothing has been halted yet.

— Still open The hearing date, whether the tribunal accepts it has jurisdiction, and how Britain argues its case. The tribunal said it will announce the hearing date shortly.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a UK announcement transferring the Falklands to Argentina in 2026 about a 2% chance (13 October, 2:37 p.m. ET), on about US$25,000 in total bets.

Argentina has asked a sea tribunal in Hamburg to halt Sea Lion, a Falklands oil project majority-owned by Navitas Petroleum. The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) confirmed on Tuesday 13 October that it had received the request.

The case matters beyond the South Atlantic because it tests whether a treaty court can freeze oil work in disputed waters. Britain is a NATO ally of the United States, and Argentina has been a major non-NATO ally of Washington since 1998.

The request followed the expiry of Argentina’s two-week deadline for Britain to stop Sea Lion work, the Tucumán daily La Gaceta reported. The deadline dates from 28 September, as set out in Falklands Oil: Argentina Gives the UK Two Weeks, Then Plans a Law of the Sea Case.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Argentina Asked the Tribunal to Do

According to the tribunal’s press release, Argentina invoked article 290, paragraph 5, of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. That rule lets a party seek urgent measures in Hamburg while a separate arbitral tribunal is still being formed.

Argentina opened that arbitration under Annex VII of the convention by notifying Britain on 28 September. ITLOS can act only if the future arbitral panel would, prima facie, have jurisdiction and the urgency of the situation requires it.

Argentina asked for four measures in total. First, Britain should prevent the start or continuation of hydrocarbon exploitation by Sea Lion in the North Malvinas Basin.

Second, Britain should not use data from exploring the disputed waters against Argentine rights. Third, it should stop preventing Argentina from protecting the marine environment there, as articles 192 and 194 of the convention require.

Fourth, Britain should take no step that could aggravate the dispute, especially new permits on the disputed continental shelf. The tribunal said the date of the oral hearings will be announced shortly in a further press release.

The Office of the President said the aim is to preserve Argentina’s sovereign rights over its continental shelf, Radio Nacional reported. It said Britain authorised the activities “unilaterally and illegally” and that they aggravate a dispute recognised by the United Nations.

The Foreign Ministry under Pablo Quirno runs the case with the Treasury Attorney’s Office and international legal advisers, La Gaceta reported. The newspaper stressed that the request does not ask the tribunal to rule on sovereignty over the islands themselves.

Why Sea Lion Matters and Who Owns It

Rockhopper Exploration discovered the Sea Lion field in 2010 in licence PL032, according to the British company’s website. Rockhopper holds 35% of that licence, and La Gaceta reported that Israel’s Navitas Petroleum holds the remaining 65%.

La Gaceta put the field about 220 kilometres (137 miles) north of the islands. Company plans call for development drilling in 2027 and first commercial production in the first quarter of 2028, the paper said.

For Argentina, the project tests its claim to the seabed around the islands, which it treats as its own continental shelf. For Britain, Sea Lion is a lawful project, and it says the islanders have the right to develop their natural resources.

The British government’s statement on Tuesday put it plainly. “Decisions on economic development in the Falkland Islands are matters for the Falkland Islands Government and the companies involved,” it said.

How Britain Responded

A British government statement published at 15:07 London time on Tuesday did not mention the tribunal filing. Instead it announced protective measures under the Protection of Trading Interests legislation against Argentine rules targeting Falklands business.

The measures are meant to stop UK companies from being forced to comply with Argentine rules applied outside Argentina. London aims to bring the secondary legislation into force before the end of the year, the statement said.

Business and Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the government “will act where Argentina seeks to impede lawful UK commercial activity.” Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called Argentine attempts to intimidate businesses “unacceptable” and said UK support for the islands is “steadfast.”

Argentina’s domestic Malvinas rules have been tightening for weeks, as set out in Argentina’s Falklands Bill Carries Sweeping Powers Over Money and Trade. Neither government’s step stops work at sea today, because the tribunal has not ruled and London’s new rules still need legislation.

What It Means for US Readers

For investors, the filing adds legal risk to Falklands oil but does not halt it, since no order exists yet. Any provisional measures the tribunal prescribes would be binding, and the convention requires the parties to comply promptly.

The United States has never ratified the Law of the Sea convention, so it is not a party to this procedure. Still, a ruling could shape how courts treat resource work in disputed seas, an issue that also touches US interests elsewhere.

The request concerns oil work, exploration data and permits. It does not ask for limits on shipping, flights or travel to the islands, so visitors face no change from the filing.

For President Javier Milei, a close US partner, the case moves the islands dispute into a courtroom rather than onto the sea. That keeps tension with Britain high, but it is a legal process with clear rules and a neutral bench.

What Is Not Known

The tribunal has not yet set a hearing date or said when it would rule. It also has not said whether it sees prima facie jurisdiction, the first hurdle any such request must clear.

Britain’s formal legal answer to the request is not yet public. The reaction of the Falkland Islands Government to the filing could not be confirmed.

It is not known whether Rockhopper and Navitas will change their 2027 drilling plan. Neither company’s response to the filing could be confirmed from their own statements.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket gives a UK announcement transferring the Falklands to Argentina in 2026 about a 2% chance (13 October, 2:37 p.m. ET). Trading volume on the question is about US$25,000, and its price slipped about one percentage point over the past week.

These are bets on a political outcome, not polls, and trading on this question is thin. A single large bet can therefore move the price sharply.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea?

It is an independent court set up under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea and based in Hamburg, Germany. It hears disputes about the convention, including urgent requests for provisional measures.

What did Argentina ask the tribunal to do?

Argentina asked for four provisional measures: that Britain prevent hydrocarbon exploitation by Sea Lion, not use exploration data against Argentine rights, stop blocking Argentina’s marine-environment duties, and avoid new permits or other steps that aggravate the dispute.

Does the filing stop the Sea Lion project?

No. The request does not suspend the project automatically. The judges must first decide whether the future arbitral tribunal would have jurisdiction and whether the situation is urgent.

Will the tribunal decide who owns the Falkland Islands?

No. According to La Gaceta, Argentina is not asking the tribunal to settle sovereignty over the islands, only to act on maritime obligations it says Britain has breached.

How has Britain responded?

On 13 October the British government announced measures under its Protection of Trading Interests legislation to shield UK businesses from Argentine rules targeting Falklands activity. Its statement did not mention the tribunal filing.

Sources: ITLOS press release 401 (13 October 2026); Radio Nacional (Office of the President statement); La Gaceta; UK government statement; Rockhopper Exploration.

World.title: Argentina Inflation Rises to 1.9% in September
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

ARGENTINA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Argentina’s consumer prices rose 1.9% in September from August, the national statistics office INDEC reported on Tuesday, 13 October, matching the forecast but faster than August’s 1.7%.

— Why it matters The figure tests whether President Javier Milei can keep prices slowing before the 2027 election, since bringing monthly price rises down is the central goal of his economic programme.

— The numbers INDEC puts annual inflation at 33.4%, down from 33.5% in August, with prices up 23.6% since December; the central bank’s official rate averaged 1,513.89 pesos per US$ in September, up 8.1% in a year.

— Who is who INDEC is Argentina’s National Institute of Statistics and Census, the government agency that publishes official inflation data; Javier Milei, a libertarian economist, took office as president in December 2023 promising to end decades of high inflation.

— What to watch INDEC will publish October consumer prices on Thursday, 12 November, showing whether the September pickup carried into October; the release did not say how the Economy Ministry or the central bank will respond.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Milei a 55.0% chance of winning the 2027 presidential election (13 October, 3:04 p.m. ET).

— What it means for you Argentina is more expensive in dollar terms for American travelers, with restaurant and hotel prices up 34.6% in a year against 8.1% for the official dollar, while US holders of Argentine bonds and YPF shares should watch interest rates and the peso.

Argentina’s consumer prices rose 1.9% in September, the national statistics office INDEC reported on Tuesday, 13 October. The monthly rate matched the 1.9% forecast but was faster than August’s 1.7%.

Argentina inflation came in at 1.9% for September, according to the National Institute of Statistics and Census (INDEC). For US investors in Argentine bonds and shares, it tests whether President Javier Milei can keep prices slowing before the 2027 election.

Annual inflation stood at 33.4%, compared with 33.5% in August, and prices have risen 23.6% since December. INDEC scheduled the release for 4 p.m. in Buenos Aires, or 3 p.m. on the US East Coast.

Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Happened

INDEC, the government agency that measures prices, jobs and growth, published its September consumer price index on Tuesday afternoon. The index tracks what households across the country pay for food, rent, utilities, transport and other goods and services.

The 1.9% monthly rise was exactly what analysts had forecast. The annual rate eased to 33.4% from 33.5% in August, just above the 33.3% forecast.

Monthly inflation had eased to 1.7% in August from 2.1% in July, the lowest reading of 2026 until then. September’s 1.9% was faster than August but slower than July’s 2.1%.

The forecasts were set out in the preview Argentina Inflation Due Tuesday After 1.7% in August. That preview also flagged August’s 33.5% annual rate as the benchmark.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Argentina economy Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Numbers

Core inflation, which leaves out seasonal and regulated prices, was 1.7%, driven by meals out and medicines. Regulated prices rose 2.3%, led by gas, electricity and private health plans, while seasonal items rose 2.9%, led by vegetables.

The largest increase was in housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels, at 3.1%, followed by education at 3.0%. The smallest changes were in restaurants and hotels (1.1%) and clothing and footwear (1.4%).

Goods prices rose 1.7% and services prices 2.4% from August. In Greater Buenos Aires, the capital and its suburbs, prices rose 2.0%, while Patagonia had the lowest regional rate, at 1.4%.

A monthly rate of 1.9% would add up to about 25% over a year if it held steady. In September 2025, a year earlier, monthly inflation had been 2.1%.

What It Means for Milei and the Peso

Javier Milei, a libertarian economist, took office in December 2023 promising to end decades of high inflation. Bringing monthly price rises down remains the central goal of his economic programme.

The peso has moved far less than prices over the past year. The central bank’s official reference rate averaged 1,513.89 pesos per US$ in September, up 8.1% from 1,399.90 a year earlier.

That gap has made Argentina more expensive in dollar terms. Based on INDEC and central bank data, a peso-priced basket cost roughly 23% more in US dollars than a year earlier.

The reference rate, known as Comunicación A 3500, stood at 1,515.88 pesos per US$ on Friday, 9 October, its latest published value. A steady peso helps slow price rises, but it can also squeeze exporters and the tourism industry.

What It Means for US Readers

US funds hold Argentine dollar bonds and shares of Argentine companies listed in New York, such as the energy firm YPF. Inflation data shape expectations for local interest rates and the peso, which drive returns on those assets.

For American travelers, Argentina is no longer the bargain it was when the peso was weaker. Restaurant and hotel prices rose 34.6% in a year, while the official dollar rate rose only 8.1%.

Expats paid in dollars lose purchasing power when local prices outrun the exchange rate. Those paid in pesos face rising rent, utility and school costs, which INDEC tracks in separate groups.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bettors gave Milei a 55.0% chance of winning the 2027 presidential election on 13 October at 3:04 p.m. ET. Axel Kicillof, the Peronist governor of Buenos Aires province, stood at 32.5%, in a market with about US$840,000 traded.

Before the release, a separate Polymarket contract on September inflation priced a 1.9% to 2.1% reading at 60.5%, with about US$33,000 traded. The official 1.9% landed in that favoured range, while 1.6% to 1.8% had stood at 33.5%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The INDEC report does not say how the Economy Ministry or the central bank will respond to the figure. No official reaction was part of the release.

It is not known whether the September pace will hold in October. INDEC publishes measured prices only, not forecasts.

The dollar-terms comparison is an estimate based on monthly averages of the official rate. Prices in Argentina’s parallel dollar market and individual household costs can differ.

What Comes Next

INDEC will publish October consumer prices on Thursday, 12 November, according to its website. That report will show whether the September pickup carried into October.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Was Argentina’s Inflation Rate in September?

Consumer prices rose 1.9% from August, INDEC said on Tuesday, 13 October. The annual rate eased to 33.4% from 33.5% in August.

Was the Figure Higher or Lower Than Expected?

Analysts had forecast 1.9% for the month and 33.3% for the year. The monthly figure matched that forecast, while the annual rate came in slightly higher.

What Is INDEC?

INDEC is Argentina’s National Institute of Statistics and Census, the government agency that publishes official inflation, jobs and growth data. It releases the consumer price index once a month.

Is Argentina Getting More Expensive for US Visitors?

Yes, in dollar terms prices have risen faster than the official exchange rate over the past year. A peso-priced basket cost roughly 23% more in US dollars than in September 2025.

Why Does the Figure Matter for Milei?

Lowering inflation is the central goal of President Javier Milei’s economic programme ahead of the 2027 election. Polymarket bettors gave him a 55.0% chance of winning on 13 October.

Sources: INDEC, Índice de precios al consumidor, September 2026; INDEC, Índice de precios al consumidor, August 2026; INDEC consumer price index page; Banco Central de la República Argentina, Comunicación A 3500 reference rate (all accessed 13 October 2026).

World.title: Thief caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle in Santa Elena
World.content:
Thief caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle in Santa Elena

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police in Santa Elena are investigating the theft of a motorcycle valued at $2,000 after surveillance footage reportedly captured a helmeted individual making off with the vehicle late Sunday night.

The cycle’s owner reported that he parked his black Lifan 125-5 motorcycle outside his rented residence on Peter August Street around midday on October 11.

The man told police he fell asleep later that night and forgot to move the motorcycle into his fenced yard. When he woke around 6:30 a.m. Monday, the vehicle was missing.

After reviewing surveillance footage with his landlord, the owner reportedly discovered that an individual dressed entirely in white and wearing a helmet had taken the motorcycle around 11:45 p.m.

The suspect was seen heading toward Orchid Street before turning in the direction of the Santa Elena Cemetery.

The motorcycle bears licence plate SIM-05698. Police are investigating.

World.title: Teen motorcyclist charged after allegedly riding into police officer during pursuit in Cayo
World.content:
Teen motorcyclist charged after allegedly riding into police officer during pursuit in Cayo

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 17-year-old student from the Cayo District has been charged with aggravated assault and several traffic-related offences following a motorcycle pursuit that reportedly ended with a police officer being struck.

According to police, officers conducting patrols in Bullet Tree Village around 10:15 p.m. on October 3 attempted to stop a red and white dirt bike carrying two individuals. The driver allegedly ignored police signals and sped away.

The pursuit continued through several streets before the motorcycle encountered a roadway obstructed by an ongoing wake. Police allege that the teenager turned the motorcycle around and rode toward the pursuing officers, striking one officer on the arm.

The motorcycle subsequently fell, and the teenager allegedly resisted attempts to detain him.

Police later confirmed that the motorcycle’s documents were up to date. The student was formally charged on October 4 with aggravated assault, wilfully refusing to stop when directed, reckless driving and resisting arrest.

The teenager’s identity is being withheld because he is a minor.

World.title: Five new US gateways to Belize with BermudAir
World.content:
Five new US gateways to Belize with BermudAir

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Fort Lauderdale is just the beginning.

BermudAir says its new Fort Lauderdale route, launching October 26, is the first of five new gateways connecting the United States to Belize.

Nonstop service from Boston, Massachusetts; Raleigh Durham, North Carolina; and Orlando Sanford and St. Petersburg/Tampa Bay in Florida is scheduled to start in December 2026.

The new routes will open easier access to Belize for travellers across the eastern United States.

The expansion comes at an important time for Belize’s tourism industry. Minister of Tourism Anthony Mahler recently confirmed that overnight arrivals declined from June through August, but said new flights would help the industry bounce back in the final quarter. BermudAir was among the airlines he highlighted.

With the high season approaching, tourism operators from San Pedro to Cayo will be hoping the new connections bring more visitors through the door.

To celebrate the launch, BermudAir is offering one way fares from US$99 between Fort Lauderdale and Belize City for bookings made through October 19.

Book at www.flybermudair.com.

World.title: Belize City baker, 23, charged after homeowner catches alleged burglar trying to pry open window
World.content:
Belize City baker, 23, charged after homeowner catches alleged burglar trying to pry open window

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 23-year-old Belize City baker has been arrested and charged with attempted burglary after allegedly trying to break into a home on Albert Street early Sunday morning.

Police reports indicate that a 29-year-old man was awakened by a loud noise coming from his bedroom window around 6:00 a.m. on October 11. When he investigated, he reportedly saw a man attempting to pry open the burglar bars on the window.

Pitts told police he observed the individual for approximately five minutes before calling 911. Responding officers apprehended the suspect, and the homeowner subsequently discovered damage to his burglar bars valued at $350.

Police identified the accused as Camron August, 23, of Peter Street, Belize City. He was formally arrested and charged with attempted burglary on Tuesday, October 13.

World.title: Krismar Espinosa sentenced to life imprisonment for murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.; Must serve 32 years before parole eligibility
World.content:
Krismar Espinosa sentenced to life imprisonment for murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.; Must serve 32 years before parole eligibility

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Convicted murderer Krismar Espinosa, 37, was sentenced to life imprisonment on Tuesday for the execution-style killing of Wilbert “Yellow” Banks Jr., a well-known member of Belize’s cycling community who was lured to his death in April 2024.

High Court Justice Nigel Pilgrim ordered that Espinosa serve a minimum of 32 years before becoming eligible for parole, with the sentence taking effect from April 9, 2024.

In determining the minimum term, Justice Pilgrim began with 30 years but added five years after considering aggravating factors, particularly Espinosa’s previous manslaughter conviction. The judge noted that his criminal history demonstrated a danger to the public and raised concerns about his rehabilitation.

However, three years were deducted for mitigating factors, including his good conduct while on remand, participation in prison rehabilitation programmes, family support and positive character references.

Espinosa was found guilty on July 31, 2026, following a trial without a jury. The court heard that Banks, 38, was shot seven times on April 5, 2024, in the Lake Garden area near Ladyville after being lured there by his former girlfriend, who was in a relationship with Espinosa.

The woman testified that Espinosa threatened to kill her and her young son unless she brought Banks to the location. Banks attempted to escape after being shot but crashed his vehicle. Espinosa denied involvement, claiming he was home at the time.

The sentencing followed emotional victim impact statements from Banks’ employer, Andrew Ordonez, his father, Wilbert Banks Sr., and his 14-year-old daughter.

Ordonez remembered Banks as a hardworking and peaceful employee who was like a son to him. His father spoke of the devastating loss of both his sons, including Kadeem Banks, who died in a traffic accident while covering a cycling race in 2022.

Banks’ daughter recalled Sunday barbecues, Valentine’s Day gifts and the comfort she felt around her father. She told the court that Father’s Day would never be the same and that she would always feel his absence.

Espinosa had previously served approximately 16 years in prison in connection with another killing, having been convicted of manslaughter. He was released in July 2023, less than a year before Banks was murdered.

The Crown had sought a life sentence, arguing that the calculated nature of the killing, the use of a firearm and Espinosa’s criminal history warranted severe punishment.

Espinosa will be eligible to apply for parole only after serving the minimum 32-year term. His release at that point is not guaranteed.

World.title: Five in a row: San Ignacio Resort Hotel named Belize’s Leading Hotel again
World.content:
Five in a row: San Ignacio Resort Hotel named Belize’s Leading Hotel again

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP):

What a way to celebrate 50 years.

San Ignacio Resort Hotel, which marks its 50th anniversary this year, has been named Belize’s Leading Hotel 2026 at the World Travel Awards. It is the hotel’s fifth consecutive win in the category, following titles every year from 2022 through 2025.

This year’s Caribbean and The Americas winners were celebrated at a gala at the Princess Grand Jamaica, the flagship event of World Travel Week Jamaica.

For half a century, San Ignacio Resort Hotel has welcomed guests from around the world to Cayo. Among its most famous guests was Queen Elizabeth II, a proud part of the hotel’s long history.

Known today as “the only jungle in town,” the hotel blends comfort, adventure and authentic Belizean charm in San Ignacio Town. Guests enjoy elegant rooms with sweeping views, fine dining at the award winning Running W Restaurant, and the signature Green Iguana Conservation Project.

The hotel credits its success to its loyal guests and its dedicated staff, who make every visitor feel like family.

The win comes just days after San Ignacio Resort Hotel hosted the 2026 Wildlife Ambassador Conference and Wildlife Hero Awards.

Congratulations to the entire San Ignacio Resort Hotel family on 50 remarkable years.

World.title: The Accountability Test for Belize Conservation Finance
World.content:
The Accountability Test for Belize Conservation Finance

By Gustavo Pessoa – Professor of Economics and Finance at Fundação Getulio Vargas in Brazil: The financial achievement of a debt transaction can be recorded on the day it closes. Conservation takes longer. Belize’s blue bonds should therefore be assessed across two timelines: the restructuring of public obligations and the sustained use of the resources committed to marine protection.

The 2021 transaction combined debt refinancing with conservation finance. An IMF working paper published in 2025 describes the commitment to annual payments into a conservation fund and an endowment intended to support funding after the initial period. These components have different purposes. An amount invested for future use is not the same as money available to finance conservation today.

The distinction matters when progress is reported. A payment received by a fund, a grant awarded to an organisation and expenditure on an activity are separate events. Each has value, but adding them together could count the same resources several times. An account that follows money through the stages would help readers understand both the financing secured and the work it has supported.

Belize already has a foundation for that scrutiny. The Belize Fund published its 2025 impact report in July, with financial audit reports also available through its reporting portal. In a February account of its next phase, it described work on a programme impact strategy. The opportunity is to connect financial reporting and conservation assessment so that they answer a shared set of questions.

One useful presentation would reconcile opening resources, conservation payments received, investment income, grants disbursed, administrative expenditure and closing resources. Commitments to future grants should appear separately from cash already paid. The endowment would require its own account of investment value, costs and the rules governing future distributions. This would make changes in available finance easier to interpret.

Financial audits and environmental evidence serve different purposes. An audit can establish whether financial statements present the fund’s position appropriately under the relevant standards. It cannot, by itself, establish that a marine ecosystem improved because a grant was made. Conservation reporting needs an account of the action funded, the result sought and the evidence used to assess it.

That assessment should be proportionate to the activity. Equipment delivered, staff trained and an area brought under a management arrangement can be important intermediate achievements. The report should explain how they are expected to affect conservation and what remains to be tested. A final ecological outcome may take years to observe and may also be influenced by conditions outside the funded project’s control.

A credible programme can acknowledge those limits without losing direction. It should define a baseline where feasible, explain how changes will be monitored and record why an intervention is continued or altered. Independent review can help distinguish a promising approach from one that requires correction. A disappointing result can inform the next decision if it is described honestly.

Communities affected by conservation decisions also need a way to follow the resources. Reporting could connect grants with their intended local benefits and the commitments made to participants. An activity that seeks to change how marine resources are used must consider the practical costs borne by those asked to change. That information belongs beside the ecological objective, even where it is difficult to express as a single indicator.

The analysis should keep the sovereign transaction and the grant programme connected without assuming that success in one proves success in the other. Lower debt obligations can improve public finances. Reliable conservation funding can support work that would otherwise be difficult to sustain. The value of that work still depends on allocation, implementation and evidence.

Belize can make its experience more useful by showing how a long term financial commitment becomes a series of accountable conservation decisions. The most persuasive record will allow a reader to trace resources from their agreed source to verified activity, and then to an assessment of the result. That is how the financing mechanism earns confidence beyond the transaction that created it.

Gustavo Pessoa is a professor of Economics and Finance at Fundação Getulio Vargas in Brazil. The views expressed in this are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial views of Breaking Belize News.

World.title: Minister of Culture and Battle of the Drums Committee discuss opportunities for strengthening the preservation of Garifuna culture
World.content:
Minister of Culture and Battle of the Drums Committee discuss opportunities for strengthening the preservation of Garifuna culture

By Zoila Palma: Today, Francis Fonseca, Minister of Culture, met with Darius Avila, President, and the Executive of the Battle of the Drums Committee to discuss opportunities for strengthening the preservation, promotion and development of Garifuna culture in Belize.

The Battle of the Drums Secretariat has played an important role in advancing cultural retrieval and preservation.

“Today’s engagement reflects the importance of continued collaboration between Government and cultural organisations in safeguarding Belize’s rich cultural heritage for generations to come,” NICH said.

World.title: Seprod shareholders approve stock split, share issuance
World.content:
The Seprod corporate offices in Kingston.

Seprod Limited is set to split its shares in the coming weeks, preceding a potential new equity offer to raise fresh capital to reduce its debt balances.

All three resolutions at the company’s virtual extraordinary general meeting (EGM) were approved by shareholders on Monday. As a result, the company’s authorised share capital will be adjusted from one billion ordinary shares to 1.9 billion ordinary shares, effectively lifting the ceiling of how many shares can exist.

Subsequently, the company’s directors will set a date for its ordinary shares to be split five-to-one. This will result in the authorised share capital rising to 9.50 billion ordinary shares while the existing share count will move from 910,945,538 ordinary shares to 4,554,727,690 ordinary shares.

If an investor holds 12,500 ordinary shares of Seprod at Tuesday’s closing price of $79.82, those shares are worth $997,750. A five-to-one stock split would increase the number of shares held to 62,500 ordinary shares with each share valued at $15.96. As a result, an investor holds more shares at a lower nominal price while retaining the same value of shares.

This reduced share price will benefit the company which has hinted at re-entering the markets for fresh capital. The third resolution empowered the directors to allot and issue new ordinary shares for an additional public offer (APO), rights issue or private placement at price(s) deemed fit. The resolution spoke to the net proceeds being applied as the directors see fit, including the repayment of debt by the company and its subsidiaries.

Chairman Paul B Scott reiterated the debt reduction strategy at Monday’s EGM, a point which Seprod has emphasised during 2026. At the company’s July 29 annual general meeting, Scott explained that the group aims to cut its consolidated debt load from $51.21 billion to $47 billion by year end.

The focus on debt reduction was recently rewarded by CARICRIS (Caribbean Information & Credit Rating Services Limited) which revised its outlook on the manufacturing and distribution conglomerate from negative to stable. The ratings agency reported a negative outlook in October 2025 based on the group’s financial flexibility being constrained due to the growing debt levels to fuel the acquisition-led growth. At the time, CARICRIS expected Seprod’s debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) to remain challenged over the next 12 to 15 months.

“The stable outlook is premised on the high likelihood that Seprod’s financial flexibility will continue to improve over the next 12-15 months. This is underpinned by the refinancing of short-term debt into a longer-tenor bond, stronger cash balances, improved capitalisation and an increased focus on deleveraging,” CARICRIS noted as it expects the group’s effective DSCR to remain above 1.0 times.

Seprod’s standalone debt has moved from $13.92 billion in 2022 to $15.88 billion in 2025, with $8.45 billion of this debt in the form of bonds maturing between December 2027 to July 2031. Seprod’s core Jamaican operations and subsidiaries have seen their aggregate debt balances move from $17.13 billion to $19.46 billion.

Meanwhile, subsidiary Musson International Dairies Limited refinanced an $854.35 million bond in December 2025 through the issuance of a new $3 billion bond in November 2025. This included a $1.53 billion tranche with a 9.75 per cent interest rate and a $1.47 billion tranche with a 10.25 per cent interest rate.

However, Seprod’s consolidated debt balance has moved from $33.01 billion in 2022 to $51.21 billion in 2025. The higher debt load is due to its subsidiary A S Bryden & Sons Holdings Limited (ASBH) which has been the vehicle used to expand Seprod’s presence across the English-speaking Caribbean over the last four years.

Aside from ASBH taking on US$60.72 million debt facility for the amalgamation process in June 2022, it has also consolidated the debt load of the various subsidiaries it has acquired over the years. As a result, ASBH’s consolidated debt has risen from $15.88 billion in 2022 to $26.24 billion at the end of 2025.

Despite the relatively large, consolidated debt load, Seprod’s financial risk profile continues to be recognised as good by the ratings agency based on operating revenue growth, improved capitalisation and adequate liquidity. Management also intends to avoid new debt for the remainder of 2026 as it cuts the debt on its balance sheet. The report noted that Seprod is expected to repay $8 billion in maturing debt from internal cash flows over the next year.

“Notably, Seprod has consistently met its debt obligations in full and on time. Moreover, should the need arise, the Group can comfortably utilise its portfolio of liquid assets which includes short-term marketable securities of circa J $4.9 billion as at December 2025,” the CARICRIS report noted.

Seprod sold its stake in subsidiary International Biscuits Limited (IBL) in February 2026, with an inflow of $1.71 billion from the sale. That sale formed part of its portfolio optimisation strategy as it retained distribution rights for IBL products up to February 2031, with the option to renew. According to documents from the Companies Office of Jamaica, Kevin Donaldson, Wade Mars and Ravi Rochlani were appointed directors of IBL on February 28.

“So, we didn’t consider it sensible over the long term to be in a market that we are competing with our customers. So, strategically we felt divesting it would be a good choice,” Scott explained at Seprod’s July 2026 AGM.

Seprod is now moving to integrate its latest Barbadian acquisitions while leveraging its larger distribution platform across the region to improve product penetration and cross-selling opportunities. The company has implemented artificial intelligence (AI) driven analytics to enhance real time monitoring of the business while ASBH moves towards warehouse consolidation in Trinidad & Tobago. It is also set to benefit from the efficiencies from the recent introduction of its new Benhill machine for its dairy business.

With Seprod receiving shareholder approval at Monday’s EGM, the board is also empowered to issue new Seprod shares as consideration for acquisitions in the future. Seprod previously received permission from shareholders to issue new shares as the directors saw fit at its September 2023 AGM.

Seprod increased its stake in ASBH from 50 to 80 per cent in July 2026 by issuing new Seprod ordinary shares in exchange for the ASBH shares tendered by investors. This move resulted in Seprod director Anthony Mark Hart becoming the 10th largest shareholder in Seprod. Hart was previously issued ASBH shares in December 2024 as consideration for his shares in Caribbean Producers (Jamaica) Limited (CPJ).

“CariCRIS expects continued good performance from Seprod over the next 12 to 15 months supported by continued revenue growth from recent acquisitions, planned new product launches, expected benefits from its operational modernization initiatives and broadly stable macroeconomic conditions across its key markets,” the ratings agency noted.

Seprod’s stock price remains down five per cent in 2026 as of Tuesday, resulting in a market capitalisation of $72.71 billion. It has paid $1.21 in dividends totalling $1.10 billion during 2026.

World.title: Ophthalmologist visit under microscope as Ruel Reid and Co fraud trial continues
World.content:
Former Caribbean Maritime University President Professor Fritz Pinnock (left) and former Education Minister Ruel Reid (second left) about to enter the Corporate Area Parish Court in Half-Way-Tree, St Andrew, in October 2019 for a bail hearing. Both men, along with Reid’s wife Sharen and daughter Sharelle, as well as Jamaica Labour Party Councillor Kim Brown Lawrence, are facing multiple charges in a multimillion-dollar fraud case.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The court is expected to hear details of an August 2018 eye doctor visit by former Education Minister Ruel Reid when his fraud trial resumes on Wednesday as prosecution witness Connie Williams Champagnie continues her testimony on the stand.

Williams Champagnie, during examination-in-chief at the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, detailed the payment and record-keeping systems at her business, Optical Smart Limited, before telling the court that Reid had entered the establishment on August 15, 2018, for an eye exam with another customer known to her. She said he also bought two pairs of eyeglasses using two health cards and a debit card.

When asked how she knew Reid, Williams Champagnie said she had never met Reid prior to that day, but described him as a public figure, telling the court that she had recognised him from the news, as he was the education minister at the time of his visit in 2018.

Reid, his wife Sharen Reid and daughter Sharelle Reid, along with former head of the Caribbean Maritime University (CMU) Fritz Pinnock and Councillor Kim Brown Lawrence are on trial, accused of siphoning off around $25 million from the Ministry of Education and CMU between March 2016 and October 2019.

Williams Champagnie told the court that she, from about arm’s length on the day of his visit, had an unimpeded view of Reid for between five and 10 minutes.

When asked if she saw that same individual in the courtroom, she responded that she did, pointing out a man in the dock in a grey suit, glasses and a blue and red tie. The individual stood and identified himself as Ruel Reid.

The five defendants have pleaded not guilty to a litany of charges including that the former education minister and his family members instructed a domestic worker to set up an account in which millions were deposited.

It is alleged that money was funnelled through transfers to various accounts either owned or controlled by the accused, or handed over in cash, with the recipients either knowing, or reasonably should have known, it was criminal property, resulting in charges of acquisition of criminal property.

Pinnock and Reid are accused of using their roles as public servants to mastermind and effect a scheme in which individuals were being paid on a regular basis by CMU, without knowledge that they were being paid; and in which invoices for goods and services were generated, but not by the individuals being paid, who did not at any time provide the stated services or goods to CMU, resulting in charges of conspiracy to defraud.

The two are also charged with acts of corruption under Section 15 of the Corruption Act — Pinnock for allegedly facilitating the payment of monies from CMU by authorising fraudulent vouchers, and Reid, in his capacity as a minister, for causing money to be paid out from the ministry and CMU for work, goods, and services not provided.

— Dana Malcolm.

World.title: Jamaica’s Kaheem Parris makes history for Sabah in Champions League
World.content:
Sabah FK's Jamaican midfielder #11 Kaheem Parris celebrates after scoring the team's first goal during the UEFA Champions League match between Sabah and Slavia Praha at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Baku on October 13, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

Jamaican winger Kaheem Parris made history for Azerbaijani champions Sabah on Tuesday as he scored the opening goal for the club in their first-ever Champions League win, a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague.

Parris fired home the opener in the 49th-minute from the edge of the box after latching on to a cutback by Ivan Lepinjica. It was the club’s first-ever goal in European competition.

Joy-Lance Mickels clinched victory for the hosts late in comedic fashion, as his weak effort from distance should have been easily cleared by Slavia defender David Moses, but the Nigerian tripped and the ball found its way home.

The victory sees Sabah bouncing back from a heavy 4-0 defeat against Manchester United in their opening match.

Meanwhile, the defeat extends Slavia’s winless run in the Champions League to 21 matches.

World.title: JC booted from Walker Cup for fielding ineligible player Jamone Lyle
World.content:
Jamaica College forward Jamone Lyle (third left) gets away from St Catherine High School’s Caiden Yen (on ground) while his teammates Jaquan Brown and Davill Jarrett (right) look on during their ISSA Manning Cup game at Ashenheim Stadium in St Andrew on Wednesday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Jamaica College (JC) have been booted from the Walker Cup for fielding an ineligible player, bringing their championship hopes crashing down just days before a highly anticipated final showdown against rivals Kingston College (KC).

Additionally, the ‘True Blues’ have been banned from next year’s edition of the knockout tournament, and must forfeit the Manning Cup second round match against St Catherine which they had won 3 – 2, which means the result has been reversed to hand St Catherine a 3 – 0 win over the many-time champions.

The decision was made at an Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) emergency meeting on Tuesday, following the revelation that JC star Jamone Lyle has a professional contract with Waterhouse Football Club, making him ineligible for schoolboy football under ISSA regulations.

Waterhouse, in a disciplinary letter dated October 9, said it had fined Lyle $60,000 for unauthorised participation in a Manning Cup match on October 7. The club alleged that Lyle ignored instructions from head coach Donovan Duckie and General Secretary Richard McCallum not to take the field for JC, in breach of his professional contract and the club’s rules.

ISSA’s decision to boot JC from the Walker Cup means that KC will now face Mona High in the final set for Friday. Mona had lost to JC in the semi-final via a penalty shootout.

World.title: BZR delayed! Concert postponed to December; patrons offered refunds
World.content:
File Photo BZR Weekend logo Cardi B

KINGSTON, Jamaica — BZR WKND Jamaica 2026 has been postponed from October 18 to December 20, following news that American rapper Cardi B will not be headlining the event as originally promoted.

In a statement issued to patrons and supporters, organisers attributed the postponement to circumstances beyond their control, while extending condolences to Cardi B and her family following the death of a loved one.

“First and foremost, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Cardi B and her family on the passing of their loved one. Our thoughts, prayers and deepest sympathies are with Cardi during this difficult time,” the statement read.

It followed days of speculation after the rapper’s publicly announced cancellation on October 8 and a follow-up video in which she maintained she was not at fault for the cancellation.

READ: ‘Just know it wasn’t me’: Cardi B addresses cancelled BZR WKND performance

However, on Tuesday, the promoters insisted they had fulfilled their financial and contractual obligations and made every effort to deliver the highly anticipated event.

“From the outset, BZR WKND has approached this event with the utmost professionalism, good faith and commitment, including fulfilling our financial obligations in full and honouring our contractual commitments,” they said.

Acknowledging the disappointment likely to be felt by patrons, particularly those who had already secured tickets, accommodation and travel arrangements, organisers apologised for the inconvenience.

Despite the setback, the promoters have assured fans that the show will go on, promising an even bigger, star-studded experience when the event returns in December.

“One thing is certain: we will not let you down. A show will happen. Our vision has always been bigger than one artiste,” the statement said.

“BZR WKND is about bringing world-class entertainment, music, culture, and an unforgettable festival experience to Jamaica,” it added.

All tickets purchased for the original October 18 date will remain valid for the rescheduled event on December 20.

However, patrons who are unable to attend on the new date or who no longer wish to attend may request a refund by emailing eventsteamjamaica@kanoopays.com. Refund requests must include the purchaser’s full name, ticket purchase confirmation, order or transaction reference number, and the email address used to purchase the tickets.

Organisers said further instructions regarding refunds and the rescheduled event will be communicated through official channels.

A press conference is also expected to be held later this week to address questions surrounding the postponement and provide additional details about what patrons can expect in December.

“We are using this additional time to build an even bigger, star-studded experience worthy of our fans and the Caribbean stage,” the organisers said.

They thanked supporters for their patience and continued confidence in the event, reiterating their commitment to delivering a world-class entertainment experience in Jamaica.

World.title: TCN deal takes flight
World.content:
NEW YORK, United States — Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents stand guard at the New York ICE field office at the Jacob K Javits Federal Building on July 31, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

THE first batch of third-country nationals (TCNs) should be arriving in the island today, highly placed sources told the Jamaica Observer late Monday evening after the Government signalled the imminent start of the controversial programme agreed between Kingston and Washington.

It was not immediately clear what time the flight carrying the TCNs would arrive or the number making up the first batch; however, Observer sources said they are mostly South Americans and the country will be updated at this week’s post-Cabinet press briefing.

The Government had previously stated that under the agreement Jamaica would accept no more than 25 per fortnight.

A release from the Ministry of National Security and Peace and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade on Monday said that “the first flight transporting third-country nationals under the agreement is expected to arrive in Jamaica shortly”.

According to both ministries, the release was issued to provide a further update on the implementation of the memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed earlier this year between Jamaica and the United States.

The release also stated that the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has agreed to commence support services.

Under the agreement signed in June this year, up to 25 asylum seekers who have unresolved migration cases in the US will temporarily transit through Jamaica en route to their home countries every two weeks.

The MOU was inked amidst US efforts to manage regional structured migration.

According to National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang, the people covered under the MOU are not being permanently settled in Jamaica and would only remain on the island while arrangements are made for their onward movement.

But the programme has attracted flak from various quarters, including the Opposition People’s National Party, which has demanded that the Government table the full MOU in Parliament.

In their release on Monday, the national security and foreign ministries reiterated that both Kingston and Washington “had finalised the operating procedures governing the arrangement, including the necessary safeguards and parameters to ensure its implementation in a safe, orderly, and lawful manner”.

“The Government reiterates that this is a transit arrangement intended to facilitate the return of third-country nationals to their countries of origin or other receiving countries, with the support of the IOM, which has been formally engaged to provide assistance to the individuals while they are in Jamaica and to facilitate their onward movement,” the release said.

The ministries also restated that “the arrangement will not be funded by the Government of Jamaica, that no third-country national with criminal antecedents will be permitted to transit through Jamaica under this programme; and further, that the number of persons anticipated will be a maximum of 25 persons per fortnight”.

The ministries also reminded that the MOU provides for its suspension if 10 third country nationals apply to remain in Jamaica through asylum applications or other humanitarian processes.

“The Government of Jamaica will continue to work closely with the Government of the United States and the IOM to ensure that the implementation of the programme is appropriately managed in accordance with the principles of safe and orderly migration, and consistent with both domestic and international law,” the release stated, adding that the Government “will continue to keep the public informed of significant developments as the programme progresses”.

World.title: Murders down, theft up
World.content:
SAMUELS... the police have responded by increasing patrols in affected communities and asking residents to report unfamiliar people whose presence raised concerns

ST James is far safer than it was a decade ago when murders topped 300 in some years, says police divisional commander Senior Superintendent Eron Samuels.

But Hurricane Melissa has triggered a new crime headache, with larceny and break-ins surging as overseas property owners returned after the Category 5 storm to find their homes burgled.

Speaking on the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good Podcast, Samuels said the absence of electricity and water after the October 28, 2025 hurricane kept many overseas property owners away from their homes in Montego Bay and the wider St James.

“So a lot of them came back in the Christmas to the new year period, and we had a huge surge of reports of break-ins and those sort of crimes in the January/ February period. So that resulted in us getting a large amount of reports,” he said.

He acknowledged that there was a 126 per cent increase in larceny and a 79 per cent rise in break-ins, noting that the aftermath of Hurricane Melissa had contributed to the increases.

“Now, we’re not going to hide these numbers because it tells the true story of what is taking place,” Samuels said. He noted that the police had responded by increasing patrols in affected communities and asking residents to report unfamiliar people whose presence raised concerns.

Samuels added the police also recognised that some people had been left without somewhere to live after the hurricane and had moved into properties that were closed up while their owners were away. “And whilst it’s wrong, they did that.

But we are doing our best to ensure that we increase the patrols within that space… We have had our patrols moving around and identifying these sorts of situations where persons are squatting or, you know, living in these places, and having them removed,” he said.

Samuels said the police had begun to see a decline in these crimes since the start of the year, but warned that vehicle theft was another concern linked to the hurricane’s impact.

“What our intelligence is telling us as well is that a lot of people are stealing vehicles, to fix vehicles that were damaged in the storm.

So we should see a reduction. However, what we have tried to do as well is… trying to get people to understand [the safety of] parking in designated parking areas, trying not to leave their vehicles unattended in areas where these things can happen, and we have been increasing our patrols at large public events, et cetera,” he added.

Despite the rise in property crimes, Samuels argued that St James is considerably safer than it was years ago, when the parish recorded more than 200 murders annually.

He said the current murder figures should be viewed against that longer history, rather than only compared with the previous year. Samuels reported 47 murders in St James from the start of the year to the time of the podcast’s recording, compared with 43 over the same period last year.

He described last year as a record year and said the current total was still far below figures recorded in earlier years. He also said the nature of killings in the parish has changed, with interpersonal disputes now accounting for more than half of murders, based on his recollection, compared with a period when gang-related killings dominated.

According to the senior cop, the improvement in safety is being reflected in how people view and use Montego Bay and the wider parish, including overseas Jamaicans purchasing property and visitors attending events.

“They’re not watching the numbers, they’re watching the feeling of safety and security. People are moving back home.

When we had the Diaspora conference the other day, we had most people saying that they’re purchasing property here in Montego Bay in St James because they’re seeing the safety and security, they’re seeing the developments taking place… You have all these developments taking place here in St James, billion- dollar developments, and this is only done because they are seeing the reduction in crime in St James,” he said.

World.title: Jamaica shines brightly at World Travel Awards
World.content:
embers of the multi-award-winning Sandals Resorts International team at the World Travel Awards held at Princess Hotel in Hanover, Sunday night. (Photo: Horace Hines)

GREEN ISLAND, Hanover — Jamaica captured 39 honours at the 33rd staging of the World Travel Awards, with Sandals Resorts International (SRI) leading the regional winners with an impressive 17.

The accolades were announced during a red-carpet ceremony on Sunday night, hosted by Princess Grand Jamaica and Princess Senses The Mangrove in Green Island, Hanover.

Sandals maintained its position as a leading force in Caribbean hospitality, extending its record as the Caribbean’s Leading Hotel Brand for the 33rd consecutive year.

Among its other major wins, Sandals Ochi was named the Caribbean’s Leading All- Inclusive Resort, while Sandals Dunn’s River secured the Caribbean’s Leading Luxury All-Inclusive Resort title.

Other Sandals and Beaches properties recognised were Sandals St Vincent, Sandals Royal Bahamian, Sandals Royal Barbados, Sandals Royal Curaçao, Beaches Turks and Caicos, Sandals Grenada, Sandals Grand Antigua, and Sandals Grande St Lucian.

Regional director of SRI in Jamaica Jeremy Jones described the company’s sustained recognition as an achievement that reflected positively on the country and its people.

“I think for Sandals Resorts International to be voted Best All-Inclusive Caribbean company for 33 years in a row is a phenomenal achievement for one little company born out of Jamaica 45 years ago,” Jones said.
