World.title: Germany detains Turks suspected of sabotaging Starlink station in Poland on behalf of Russia
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Two Turkish men suspected of carrying out last month’s arson attack on a satellite internet ground station in Poland used by Starlink have been detained in Germany. The Polish authorities say that the sabotage was carried out on behalf of Russia. On Monday evening, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk first announced that the pair had been taken into custody “at the request of the Polish security services”. He said that the Turkish men’s actions had been “a further act of hybrid warfare” – the term used for sabotage and other hostile activity carried out in Europe by Russia – and that “the perpetrators will answer before the Polish justice system”. Na zlecenie polskich służb niemiecka policja zatrzymała dwóch obywateli tureckich podejrzanych o podpalenie stacji Starlink na Mazowszu. To kolejny akt wojny hybrydowej. Sprawcy sabotażu odpowiedzą przed polskim wymiarem sprawiedliwości. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 12, 2026 Shortly afterwards, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński revealed that the arrests had taken place in cooperation between Poland’s police and Internal Security Agency (ABW) and Germany’s Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA). He said that the charge the suspects are likely to face in Poland would be “sabotage on behalf of a foreign intelligence service”, a crime that carries a minimum prison sentence of 10 years, ranging up to life. Later on Monday, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, confirmed that Poland believes the attack was carried out “on behalf of the Russian security services”. The incident in question took place on 23 September at a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company. The facility is used to provide internet services across the region, including in Ukraine, which has relied heavily on Starlink connections since Russia’s full-scale invasion. Firefighters were called out that evening to a fire at the facility, which is owned by Polish state telecommunications operator Exatel. The next day, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gakowski revealed that the blaze had been started deliberately and “the modus operandi is clearly Russian”. Poland has been one of the primary targets for Russian sabotage operations in Europe. Those have included a series of arson attacks, including one that burned down Warsaw’s largest shopping centre and another at a drone factory that is used to supply the Ukrainian military. A fire last night at a Starlink ground station in Poland that is used to provide internet services to Ukraine was caused deliberately and "the modus operandi is clearly Russian", says digital affairs minister @KGawkowski https://t.co/p2DEn7XexF — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 24, 2026 On Monday evening, at a press conference alongside Kierwiński and Siemoniak, the commander of Poland’s police, Marek Boroń, revealed that one of the two Turkish suspects had resident status in Germany while the other did not. He said that the Polish authorities had been able to document their movements in Poland, and had recordings, fingerprints and DNA of the suspects. Simoniak added that there was a “high probability” that other individuals were involved in the attack, but that he could not divulge further information about them currently. He also thanked the German authorities for their cooperation. “We have no doubt that Russian intelligence services are behind this act of sabotage,” said the minister, quoted by the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. “And it’s worth adding that Russian intelligence services are increasingly using people connected to the criminal world. They never use their own citizens.” Russia uses individuals already present in Europe – and often already involved in criminal activity – to carry out most of its hybrid operations. On Monday, in a separate case, three Ukrainians and one Belarusian went on trial in Warsaw accused of being behind a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania. Four men – three Ukrainians and a Belarusian – have gone on trial in Warsaw accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on behalf of Russia https://t.co/i4czRb9DYZ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 12, 2026 On Tuesday morning, German newspaper Handelsblatt reported confirmation from the State Criminal Police Office (LKA) in Baden-Württemberg that two Turkish men had been detained on Monday in the town of Nürtingen at the request of the Polish authorities. The office did not provide further details, but Handelsblatt reports that the two suspects are due to be brought before a judge today. World.title: Four go on trial in Warsaw over arson attacks carried out on Russian orders
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Four men have gone on trial in Warsaw accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on Russian orders. The accused – three Ukrainians and one Belarusian – can be named only as Oleksandr H., Stepan K., Vitalii K. and Pavlo T. under Polish privacy law and their trial is taking place behind closed doors for security reasons. Polish prosecutors say that they were part of an organised group tasked with “committing acts of sabotage and terrorism” on behalf of Russia’s foreign intelligence service in April and May 2024. Those included a fire that burned down Warsaw’s largest shopping centre, Marywilska 44; another at a store in Warsaw belonging to home improvement chain OBI; and a third at an IKEA store in Vilnius. They also allegedly planned an arson attack on an IKEA store in the Latvian capital of Riga. W Sądzie Okręgowym Warszawa-Praga ruszył proces grupy przestępczej, która miała na zlecenie Federacji Rosyjskiej podpalać markety wielkopowierzchniowe, w tym centrum handlowe przy Marywilskiej w Warszawie.https://t.co/0CFl1RyJvq — TVN Warszawa (@tvnwarszawa) October 12, 2026 According to an indictment issued against the men in March this year, Stepan K., the Belarusian, set fire to the OBI store. Oleksandr H. is accused of involvement in the arson attack on the IKEA store in Vilnius and preparations for further attacks. The pair have been indicted under Poland’s espionage law for carrying out acts of sabotage and terrorism on behalf of foreign intelligence. That crime carries a minimum sentence of 10 years in prison, ranging up to life. Another Ukrainian suspect, Daniil B., had also been due to stand trial today on the same charge, with prosecutors finding that he had received an order from a handler in Russia to go to Marywilska on the night the arson attack took place and record footage of the fire and the response of the emergency services. However, Daniil B. was jailed in Lithuania last year for his role in the Vilnius IKEA fire and Poland has not yet managed to secure his extradition for the trial in Warsaw, meaning that it went ahead without his involvement. Polish prosecutors say they have determined that the Marywilska fire was also carried out on the orders of Russian intelligence, but have not been able to identify which individuals actually perpetrated the attack. Stepan K. and Oleksandr H. – as well as Vitalii K., whom prosecutors accuse of helping carry out the arson in Vilnius – are additionally charged with participating in an organised criminal group that aimed to carry out terrorist offences, a crime punishable by up to 10 years in prison. Both Vitalii K. and Pavlo T. were also indicted in relation to an assault in the village of Wólka Kosowska, just outside Warsaw. Pavlo T. was already convicted in Poland last year along with two other Ukrainian men, Serhii R. and Vladyslav Y., over their role in the same criminal group tasked with carrying out acts of sabotage and terrorism by Russia. They were handed jail terms ranging from 16 months to five and a half years. Two other alleged members of the group, Serhii Chalyi and Oleksandr Varyvoda, who prosecutors say were involved in coordinating sabotage activities, remain wanted. Three Ukrainians have been jailed in Poland for their role in a group tasked with carrying out sabotage and terrorism. That included the fire that destroyed Warsaw’s largest shopping centre, which Polish prosecutors say was carried out on Russia’s orders https://t.co/xuFx5T4HH9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2025 In response to evidence that Moscow was behind the Marywilska fire, Poland last year ordered Russia’s consulate in Kraków to close. It has since closed all Russian consulates due to Moscow’s ongoing campaign of sabotage, with Russia responding by shutting down all Polish consulates on its territory. A report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism published earlier this year found that Poland is the “primary focus” of Russian sabotage in Europe. Most recently, Poland has accused Moscow of being behind a fire at a drone factory that supplies the Polish and Ukrainian militaries. Last year, Ukrainian operatives working on behalf of Russia also used explosives in an attempt to derail a train in Poland. Most acts of sabotage ordered by Russia in Poland have been carried out not by Russians themselves, but by Ukrainians and Belarusians, large numbers of whom already live in Poland and other countries in the region. World.title: Israeli producer had access to data harvested by Poland using Pegasus spyware, say prosecutors
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Data harvested from mobile phones by the Polish authorities using Pegasus spyware were transmitted outside Poland and were accessible to the tool’s Israeli producer, Polish prosecutors have revealed as part of an investigation into the use of Pegasus under the former government. Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that the case is “one of the biggest scandals in Polish history since the fall of communism”, and that it is “beyond any doubt” that the Israeli firm behind Pegasus, NSO Group, cooperates with Israeli intelligence. Tego o Pegasusie jeszcze nie słyszeliście. pic.twitter.com/etvhTE9EWa — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 12, 2026 Pegasus is a powerful and controversial tool that allows the extraction of large amounts of data from mobile phones without users’ knowledge. A number of countries have been found to have used it to spy on opposition figures. In 2017, Poland, under the government of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, purchased Pegasus from NSO. The spyware was subsequently used against hundreds of targets, including a number of PiS’s political opponents. Among them was the head of the 2019 election campaign of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party (which was then known as Civic Platform, PO). Last year, Tusk revealed that his own wife and daughter had been among those caught up in the surveillance. PiS, however, has insisted that Pegasus was a necessary tool to fight crime and ensure national security. It says the spyware was only used with court approval against targets legitimately suspected of wrongdoing. After a coalition led by Tusk took power from PiS in December 2023, it launched investigations into the use of Pegasus under the former government. Today, the National Prosecutor’s Office released its latest findings, based on analysis by experts at the forensic research office of Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW). The experts confirmed that Pegasus allowed the harvesting of emails, instant messaging and text messages; the content of telephone conversations, both via mobile networks and internet calls; browsing histories, calendars and contact lists; photos, videos and other files; and location data. “Additionally, Pegasus allowed the use of the device’s built-in microphone and cameras to record audio and video in real time and take screenshots,” reports the National Prosecutor’s Office. Czy to możliwe, że państwo traci kontrolę nad własnym systemem inwigilacji? I to nie była stara konsola… Z opinii biegłych ABW wynika, że CBA kupiło narzędzie, nad którym nie miało pełnej kontroli. Dane opuszczały Polskę, moduł infekujący kontrolował producent, a zagraniczna… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) October 12, 2026 The ABW experts also highlighted serious concerns over management and security of the harvested data, noting that Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA), which was responsible for using the spyware, “did not have full control over the Pegasus system”. “The CBA did not have passwords to access some accounts with administrative privileges and some system components remained under the control of the manufacturer [NSO],” wrote the prosecutor’s office. “The server module responsible for infecting mobile devices remained under the manufacturer’s exclusive control.” Data transmitted through the Pegasus system travelled outside Polish territory, through “servers located in various parts of the world”, in a network managed by NSO and “beyond the CBA’s control”, found the experts. Meanwhile, NSO “had technical access to materials from operational surveillance”, although prosecutors say that the experts “did not determine whether the manufacturer actually obtained access to materials from specific operations”. The former deputy head of Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau has been charged with unlawfully sharing material obtained through surveillance using Pegasus spyware, including communication involving PM @donaldtusk's daughter when Tusk was in opposition https://t.co/LyTuqbq0KQ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 23, 2025 In a video commenting on the latest findings, Tusk said that the investigation into Pegasus was “coming to a head”. He called it “one of the biggest scandals in Polish history after the fall of communism”. The former PIS authorities signed a contract for a spyware system “over which they de facto had no control, because control remained in the hands of Israel and an Israeli company…whose cooperation with Israeli intelligence is, of course, beyond doubt”, said the prime minister. “They paid money for a system that de facto transferred all possible data on Polish citizens, Polish opposition leaders and Polish independent prosecutors…to the Israeli side,” he added. “This is no longer [just] a scandal…We’re talking about a crime against the state.” Two former heads of Polish security agencies have been charged over the use of Pegasus spyware under the former PiS government. The pair, who deny wrongdoing, could be jailed for up to three years if found guilty of unlawfully allowing use of the spyware https://t.co/TWjQR74IYT — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2026 Later on Monday, a separate parliamentary committee set up by the ruling coalition to investigate the use of Pegasus also revealed unclassified sections of a report on its findings. In addition to the information released by prosecutors, the commission also said that the CBA had never obtained the required IT security accreditation for Pegasus, meaning that it was used without meeting requirements for protecting classified information. The commission’s chairwoman, Magdalena Sroka, also said that courts granting authorisation for the use of Pegasus were not informed of its full capabilities, such as the ability to access the entire contents of phones, reports broadcaster RMF. 💬 Jest to dokument o tym, jak władza publiczna w Polsce sięgnęła po narzędzie ingerujące w prawa obywatelskie – powiedziała przewodnicząca komisji śledczej ds. inwigilacji systemem Pegasus @MagdalenaSroka, prezentując raport z prac komisji.https://t.co/MzA9gj4M0Y — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) October 12, 2026 Legal proceedings are already underway against a number of former officials in relation to Pegasus. In February, prosecutors charged the former heads of the AWB and Military Counterintelligence Service (SKW) with abuse of power for approving the use of Pegasus despite being aware of legal shortcomings. Previously, the former head of the CBA was charged with the same offence, while one of his deputies was charged with unlawfully disclosing material from surveillance of Roman Giertych, an MP from Tusk’s KO party who has also worked as a lawyer for Tusk and his family. Last year, a former deputy justice minister from the PiS government, Michał Woś, was indicted to stand trial over his role in the alleged illegal use of justice ministry funds to help the CBA purchase Pegasus. World.title: US wants Poland to join G20 “as soon as possible”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The United States wants Poland to join the G20 “as soon as possible” and intends to raise the issue with other members of the international forum at its forthcoming summit in December in Miami, the US State Department has told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Having previously endorsed Polish membership of the G20 in May, the US now says it intends to “continue discussions with G20 members this year on making Poland a full member as soon as possible”. “Poland’s long-term and steady economic growth, combined with its growing leadership position in the international arena, make it an ideal participant,” the State Department told PAP. Stany Zjednoczone oficjalnie zadeklarowały, że będą zabiegać o stałe członkostwo Polski w G20 https://t.co/lnZ583HIus — Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) October 11, 2026 The G20, a major intergovernmental forum that brings together 19 major countries together with the European Union and the African Union, is set to meet at a golf resort owned by President Donald Trump in Miami on 14-15 December. Poland is also participating this year as a guest of the United States. PAP reports that the US has proposed that one of the points in the final declaration adopted by leaders at the conclusion of the summit refer to Poland’s permanent membership. However, this would require the assent of all current members, including Russia. The issue is likely to be discussed in a pre-summit online meeting of so-called “sherpas” negotiating the text of the declaration, reports PAP. After visiting Washington earlier this month, Marcin Przydacz, the head of President Karol Nawrocki’s international policy office, said that joining the G20 permanently is “Plan A”, but acknowledged that receiving a consensus from existing member states made this variant difficult. He added that Nawrocki would travel to London before the summit to discuss the possibility of continuing Poland’s guest status next year, when the UK will host the G20. At a meeting of G20 trade ministers last week, finance minister Andrzej Domański said that Poland has a good chance of being invited next year. Nawrocki also plans to visit G20 members Saudi Arabia and Argentina to canvass for support for Poland’s membership bid, Przydacz has confirmed. A third option would be for Poland to become a “permanent guest”, a status typically reserved for organisations like the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group, but also held by Spain. The United States has expressed "strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member" following talks in Warsaw, after which it also emphasised "strong and growing" Polish-American relations https://t.co/qTpCACnMfu — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 2, 2026 Poland has long lobbied for membership in the group. In 2010, then-President Lech Kaczyński said “the place of my country is among the members of the G20”. In 2022, following the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Polish government argued that their country should replace Russia. Last December, the US invited Poland to join this year’s summit. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that Poland was “assuming its rightful place” at the forum. Poland has argued that its membership is justified by its economy being on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world. Though G20 membership is not decided solely on that basis, the G20 does include most of the world’s 20 largest economies (only Switzerland and the Netherlands have larger economies than Poland but no G20 membership). Polish President @NawrockiKn “does not like” the fact that Donald Trump has invited Vladimir Putin to the G20 summit in Miami, says his chief foreign policy aide. However, Nawrocki still plans to attend the event, which Poland is invited to as a guest https://t.co/JojsFB4NX6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 26, 2026 In September, the United States provoked criticism from European leaders, including Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, when it announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin would be invited to the Miami summit. Subsequently, Przydacz confirmed that, although Nawrocki, who is a close ally of Trump, “does not like” the fact that Putin has been invited, the Polish president was still planning to attend the summit. Sikorski likewise said he would attend a G20 meeting of foreign ministers in Atlanta in October even if a Russian representative was there and agreed that Poland should not boycott the summit in December. World.title: Independent beats PM Tusk’s candidate in Kraków mayoral election
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Łukasz Gibała, an independent, has won the mayoral election in Kraków, Poland’s second-biggest city, beating Monika Piątkowska, the candidate backed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. With all votes counted by just after 1 a.m. on Monday morning, Gibała had 62.1% against 37.9% for Piątkowska, who had already conceded defeat shortly after 9 p.m. on Sunday night, when exit polls showed a large margin of victory for her opponent. Turnout was 44.3%. “Today in Poland, more and more people realise that we don’t have to live in the reality that politicians in Warsaw project upon us,” declared Gibała as it became clear he had won. “More and more people realise that we, in our own towns and cities, know better what’s good for us than they do in Warsaw.” The victory marks a blow for Tusk – whose Civic Coalition (KO) party has its strongest support in large cities – just a year before he seeks to win another term at parliamentary elections. The prime minister had visited Kraków to campaign alongside Piątkowska. Dziś 11 października 2026 roku, po 24 latach, mieszkańcy odzyskali swoje miasto. Chciałbym podziękować wszystkim Krakowianom, którzy mi zaufali i zdecydowali się oddać ma mnie głos. To nasze wspólne zwycięstwo. Dziękuję mojej partnerce Adzie, sztabowi i współpracownikom ze… pic.twitter.com/0FsNYwjPkj — Łukasz Gibała (@LukaszGibala) October 11, 2026 For Gibała, a wealthy businessman who has largely funded his own political career, this was victory at the fourth attempt, having stood in every mayoral contest since 2014, obtaining a growing share of the vote each time. He stood as an independent, promising to sort out the city’s finances, end cronyism in the appointment of municipal officials, improve public transport and reverse ticket-price increases, and hold a referendum on Kraków’s controversial clean transport zone for vehicles. He also pledged to favour residents over developers in planning decisions and to counteract the negative effects of tourism in what is Poland’s most-visited city, including by restricting short-term-rental properties. Gibała’s victory had been expected after he came top in the first round two weeks ago with 36.4% of the vote among the seven candidates who stood. Piątkowska trailed on 29.9%. The top two candidates then met in today’s run-off. Piątkowska was the joint candidate of Tusk’s centrist KO party and the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which are both part of the national government. She has, since last year, been a member of the Senate in Warsaw. Previously, she worked in Kraków city hall during the mayoralty of Jacek Majchrowski, who held office from 2002 to 2024. Piątkowska received the personal backing of Tusk, who announced her candidacy in June alongside PSL leader and deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (though critics noted that they held the event in Warsaw rather than Kraków). Tusk also visited Kraków before the first round to support his candidate. Among her campaign promises were to seek to locate an AI “gigafactory” in Kraków, to boost the availability of housing for young people, and to implement a package of policies for women, including free mammograms, pram-friendly infrastructure, free menstrual hygiene products, and safer nighttime public transport. Poland’s government has approved legislation that would allow local communities to ban short-term rentals of the type offered through services such as Airbnb. Such accommodation has boomed in recent years, often prompting a backlash from local residents https://t.co/8MRfRWTDxd — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 3, 2026 Kraków’s election was held in unusual circumstances after the previous mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, also from KO, was removed from his position in May, just two years into his term. He had faced accusations of cronyism and poor financial management, as well as criticism over the introduction of the clean transport zone. A petition to hold a recall referendum received more than the 58,355 signatures required. In the subsequent referendum, 97.3% supported removing the mayor (Miszalski had appealed to his supporters not to vote in an unsuccessful effort to keep turnout below the 27% needed for the result to be binding). Before today’s election, both Miszalski and Majchowski had called on Cracovians to vote for Piątkowska. After his victory had become clear, Gibała declared that “11 October 2026 will be remembered as the day when, after 24 years, the inhabitants of Krakow regained their city”. The vote had been particularly closely watched as it came just a year before the parliamentary elections. Gibała’s victory has been celebrated by figures from the right-wing opposition, though the new mayor is not politically aligned with them (and indeed previously served as an MP in Tusk’s party). World.title: Polish security services report alleged assassination plot against PM Tusk
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s security services say they have received “credible” information indicating a “high probability” of an assassination attempt against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. At the time of writing, no details have been released regarding where and how the alleged attacks were expected to take place, who might be behind them, or what the source of the information was. W związku z informacją, która wpłynęła do @PolskaPolicja i dotyczy możliwego zamachu na premiera @donaldtusk oraz wicepremiera, ministra obrony narodowej @KosiniakKamysz, minister koordynator służb specjalnych @TomaszSiemoniak oraz minister spraw wewnętrznych i administracji… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) October 11, 2026 On Sunday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, first announced that the police had received “information…regarding a possible assassination attempt” on Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz, who, as well as serving as defence minister, is also a deputy prime minister. Dobrzyński revealed that the Internal Security Agency (ABW), police and State Protection Service (SOP), which provides security for high-ranking officials, would meet to discuss the potential threat. Speaking after that meeting, interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka confirmed that the threat had first been identified by SOP, which passed the information on to the police. “We are taking this matter extremely seriously,” added Dobrzyński, speaking alongside her. He criticised “pseudo-experts” in the media who had expressed doubt about the announcement of a possible assassination attempt. “We’re talking about threats directed at the most important people in the country,” he added. “This information is so serious and credible that we’ve decided to share it with you now…We are talking about a high probability that these threats will be carried out.” Dobrzyński did not divulge any details about the nature of the attack or where the warnings had come from, but said that he would be able to provide further information once the police and security services had carried out further investigation. "Sprawę traktujemy śmiertelnie poważnie. Mówimy o dużym prawdopodobieństwie spełnienia tych gróźb" Rzecznik prasowy ministra koordynatora służb specjalnych o możliwym zamachu na premiera i szefa MON. pic.twitter.com/2xoWrZJT2w — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 11, 2026 Government spokesman Adam Szłapka, speaking to broadcaster TVN, acknowledged that the authorities constantly receive a “cascade of indications” regarding potential threats. However, “this signal was more disturbing than previous” ones, he added. Szłapka also indicated that one element of the warning had come via email, but added that “it was not just an email” that had raised concern. Like Dobrzyński, he said that further information would be released in due course. Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading daily, reports that an unnamed “official close to the prime minister” had said that the threat came from “right-wing extremists” and that the perpetrators were Poles. Another source within the intelligence services told the newspaper that the threat was treated more seriously than others because it contained information about addresses linked to Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz. Poland has charged a 17-year-old with planning neo-Nazi terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. Two other Polish teenagers who were part of the same online community promoting neo-Nazism and violence have also been detained https://t.co/86AnIHWFe8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 Last month, police detained a 56-year-old man in the city of Przemyśl after he posted a video on social media threatening Tusk. Earlier in September, a 52-year-old man in the town of Oława was likewise arrested for making criminal threats against the prime minister online. Also in September, the security services detained three teenagers who were accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them was additionally charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. This week has also seen Poland facing an unprecedented security challenge after three knife attacks took place on schools, leaving one person dead and many injured. In response, the police have since Friday carried out checks at over 64,000 locations, including many schools, and detained over 100 people, most of them teenagers found to have made threats or been in possession of weapons. World.title: Czech Republic to See Sharp Weekend Cooldown and Possible Snowfall
World.content:
The Czech Republic is set for a change in weather this weekend, with temperatures expected to fall and snow possible in mountain areas, according to the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute (CHMI).

The colder conditions will follow several relatively mild autumn days, when daytime temperatures are forecast to reach 17 to 18 degrees Celsius.



By the weekend, however, increased cloud cover and precipitation could bring the first signs of winter to higher elevations.

The transition will come after a frosty start to the week. Meteorologists expect the coldest night of the week to have already passed, meaning temperatures should remain more moderate over the coming days.

Sunshine is forecast across much of the country during the remainder of the working week, although mornings will stay chilly. Local fog and showers may develop in eastern parts of the Czech Republic.

The outlook for the weekend remains uncertain, but forecasters expect a general cooling trend, accompanied by extensive cloud cover and periods of rain.

Mountain regions are most likely to see wintry conditions. As temperatures fall, rain could turn to snow at higher elevations, particularly in the mountains. Some locations may also experience temperatures below freezing.

However, significant or lasting snowfall is not currently expected. Any snow that falls is likely to be limited to light dustings or scattered flakes, with accumulations unlikely to persist for long.

World.title: David Duchovny Brings New Album to Prague This Thursday
World.content:
David Duchovny, best known for his acting career, will perform in Prague on October 15, 2026, presenting songs from his upcoming album Prince of Pieces at Archa+.

Tickets are on sale through GoOut.

Duchovny has spent the past decade developing his career as a songwriter and recording artist, releasing music that combines melodic rock with introspective lyrics.

Prince of Pieces is his fourth album and brings together a small group of musicians and longtime collaborators.

The new record follows Hell or Highwater, Every Third Thought, released in 2017, and Gestureland, released in 2021. According to the album’s press release, the latest project is his most cohesive and collaborative work to date, reflecting the relationships he has built with fellow musicians over the years.

Duchovny’s music has received positive reviews from critics.

AllMusic described his sound as “eloquent, alt-rock-kissed country-folk in the vein of Wilco and the Wallflowers,” while The Boston Globe praised his voice for its “parched resonance and just a hint of rasp,” adding that he sings with feeling.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by David Duchovny (@davidduchovny)

The actor has said that the arrangements on his records are shaped by the mood and rhythm of each song, rather than following a single formula.

“The arrangements of the songs have always been in service of either the groove or the emotion,” Duchovny said. He added that he looks for sounds that complement the melody, including horns, bells and harmonies, while also experimenting with rhythms and beats.

World.title: Czech Doctors May Soon Prescribe Museum Visits to Prevent Depression
World.content:
Doctors in the Czech Republic could soon recommend museum visits, dance classes, singing and creative workshops to people at risk of depression, anxiety or social isolation.

The program, known as Art on Prescription, aims to connect healthcare providers with museums, galleries, libraries and other cultural institutions.

Rather than replacing medication or psychotherapy, these activities would complement existing treatment and help prevent mental health problems.



The National Institute of Mental Health (NUDZ) is preparing a National Platform for Prevention through Culture to bring together cultural organizations, healthcare providers, social services and schools. The goal is to make existing cultural activities more accessible to people who could benefit from them.

The initiative is not intended to turn cultural institutions into medical facilities. Instead, it seeks to use local resources to support mental well-being and strengthen social connections.

Research highlights benefits of cultural activities

International research suggests that participating in cultural and artistic activities can improve well-being, strengthen social ties and reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety.

According to Dominika Grygarová, a researcher at NUDZ, an analysis combining studies from more than 20 countries found significant reductions in symptoms of both depression and anxiety.

The benefits depend not only on exposure to art but also on active participation, Grygarová said. Creating something, learning a new skill, sharing experiences and interacting with others can help people focus on something beyond their difficulties and develop a sense of belonging.

However, the programs are intended primarily as a preventive and supportive measure, not a substitute for professional treatment. Researchers also want to assess their effectiveness and economic value, with preliminary analyses suggesting that some initiatives could be cost-effective.

Czech project looks to Northern Europe

NUDZ plans to build on similar programs already operating in several countries, particularly the United Kingdom and Northern Europe.

The Czech initiative intends to follow the so-called Baltic model, with researchers planning to work with Danish colleagues next year on a European project to introduce the approach more widely.

World.title: Who Is Petr Hlaváček? The Architect Set to Become Prague’s Next Mayor
World.content:
Petr Hlaváček is seeking to become the Czech capital’s next mayor after his political movement, STAN, won the municipal elections.

STAN received 23.16 percent of the vote, securing 17 seats in the Prague City Assembly and putting the movement in a strong position to negotiate the next governing coalition.



Hlaváček, currently deputy mayor for territorial and strategic development, has indicated that he wants to take the top job at City Hall.

His priorities include expanding housing construction, redeveloping former industrial sites and improving transport infrastructure.

A key role in Prague’s new zoning plan

Hlaváček’s main achievement as deputy mayor has been his involvement in preparing Prague’s new Metropolitan Plan, which replaced the previous zoning document from 1999 when it came into effect in September 2026.

The plan sets out where construction can take place and establishes rules for future development. It identifies capacity for up to 350,000 new homes, primarily through the redevelopment of brownfield sites.

One of the main projects is the transformation of Bubny-Zátory, an underused area expected to provide housing for around 20,000 people.

Hlaváček has also backed the Prague Development Company, which manages municipal land and aims to increase housing construction. According to him, the company could facilitate the development of up to 70,000 homes while helping prevent city-owned land from being sold off.

Transport and housing at the top of his agenda

If appointed mayor, Hlaváček wants to continue work on major transport projects, including Prague’s inner ring road and the Prague Ring Road. He also supports expanding public transport and reforming parking policy, arguing that parking in the city is often too cheap.

Before the elections, he said STAN would welcome continuing the existing coalition at City Hall but wanted a more prominent role, depending on its electoral support.

From architect to deputy mayor

Born in Zlín on July 31, 1961, Hlaváček graduated from the Faculty of Architecture at the Czech Technical University in Prague. He later established his own architectural studio, taught as a visiting professor at the University of Michigan and served as vice-dean at his alma mater.

His professional work includes the renovation of the Czech Embassy in Brasília, Brazil.

In 2015, he became director of the Prague Institute of Planning and Development. He was dismissed the following year amid criticism over delays to the Metropolitan Plan, a decision that prompted protests from institute employees.

Hlaváček entered Prague politics after the 2018 municipal elections and became first deputy mayor for territorial development and spatial planning in November 2021. He remained in the city leadership after the 2022 elections and took responsibility for territorial and strategic development in February 2023.

World.title: Sinatra Tribute Pairs Frank Sinatra Classics With 1930s Dining at Prague’s Mánes
World.content:
Prague’s Art Restaurant Mánes combines live performances of Frank Sinatra’s best-known songs with a three-course dinner inspired by traditional Czech cuisine of the 1930s.

The functionalist building offers views of the Vltava River and nearby Žofín Island, providing the setting for an evening dedicated to the music and style of Sinatra’s era.



The Sinatra’s Tribute musical programme features acclaimed soloists, including baritone Daniel Klánský and jazz singer Sophie Lamoš. They perform some of Sinatra’s best-known songs, including *My Way* and *Fly Me to the Moon*, accompanied by a group of musicians.

Rather than simply imitating the legendary American singer, the Sinatra Tribute offers its own interpretation of his musical legacy.

One of the programme’s highlights is a restored 1897 Steinway & Sons grand piano, an instrument once played by Czech composer and pianist Jaroslav Ježek.

The music is complemented by a three-course dinner served before the concert.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sinatra Tribute Koncert & Večeře / Sinatra Tribute Show & Dinner (@sinatratributeprague)

Created exclusively for the programme by Mánes Restaurant head chef Jaroslav Zahálka, the menu draws inspiration from Prague’s culinary traditions of the 1930s, reflecting the period associated with the evening’s musical theme.

Visitors can contact the venue for current dates, ticket prices and reservations.

World.title: From Lisbon to Hanoi, New Flight Options From Prague This Autumn
World.content:
The autumn school break is approaching, and travelers departing from Prague still have options for trips abroad.

However, those hoping to find cheap flights may struggle to secure a good deal, as fares tend to rise closer to departure and fewer seats remain available at lower prices.

Families face an additional challenge. When booking four tickets together, they may discover that the cheapest fare is available for only one or two passengers, forcing them to pay more for the remaining seats.



Airlines are also dealing with high fuel costs and strong competition, making it important to fill as many seats as possible.

A search conducted on Wednesday, October 7, found that Kraków and Gdańsk were among the cheapest destinations available for the autumn break week.

New flights from Prague and postponed routes

Prague Airport has announced several new connections for the autumn and winter seasons, although some airlines have postponed their planned launches until spring.

Smartwings, for example, has delayed the introduction of flights to Venice, Italy, and Bergen, Norway. Both routes were originally scheduled to begin before the autumn break but are now expected to launch in March.

Despite the changes, Prague Airport continues to list the destinations among its new routes, with their original launch dates still displayed. According to the current schedule, Smartwings’ next new connection is to Lisbon, with flights due to begin on October 23.

Travelers heading farther afield have another option. Vietjet Air launched its Prague–Hanoi service on Saturday, October 10. The route includes a stopover in Kazakhstan, rather than offering a nonstop connection to Vietnam.

Closer to home, easyJet’s new route from Prague to Hamburg provides another option for the break. Return fares were available for around CZK 4,000.

Marrakech joins the network as winter routes target skiers

EasyJet is also scheduled to launch flights from Prague to Marrakech, Morocco, on October 25. The new connection will increase competition on the route, although fares during the autumn break are relatively high.

A return ticket can cost as much as CZK 16,000, excluding baggage. Prices can be considerably lower outside the peak travel period.

Wizz Air is adding flights to Poprad, Slovakia, while Sky Alps is expected to begin services to Bolzano, Italy, in early December. Both destinations provide access to mountain regions popular with winter sports enthusiasts.

Another seasonal option is Eurowings’ planned route to Rovaniemi, Finland, which is scheduled to launch on December 20. Located on the Arctic Circle, the city is closely associated with Santa Claus and attracts visitors during the Christmas season.

World.title: RestaurantWeek Prague Returns With 75 Restaurants and Autumn Menus
World.content:
RestaurantWeek® returns to Prague from October 13 to November 18, offering diners the chance to try menus at around 75 restaurants across the capital at reduced prices.

The three-course menus available for CZK 490 or CZK 790, plus a reservation fee.



The autumn edition features a mix of established Prague restaurants and newcomers to the festival. Among the first-time participants are U Malířů 1543 in Malá Strana and Buddha-Bar Prague, both well-known names on the city’s dining scene.

Participating restaurants are incorporating seasonal ingredients into their menus, including pumpkin, game, poultry, forest fruits, plums and quince. Truffles and shrimp are also expected to feature prominently.

Pumpkin will appear in dishes ranging from soups to mousses, while restaurants focusing on seafood and creative interpretations of Czech ingredients will offer alternatives for diners looking to explore different flavours.

The festival aims to make restaurants more accessible while encouraging people to dine out and meet in person. This year’s edition includes a partnership with Singles Club, an initiative promoting face-to-face social connections as an alternative to app-based dating.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Singles Club (@singlesclubcz)

Connecting Prague restaurants with local producers

RestaurantWeek® is also collaborating with the Regional Food (Regionální potravina) project, which supports small Czech food producers. The partnership aims to connect restaurants with local suppliers and help regional products reach more customers.

For the first time, the festival will also recognise restaurants that work with regional ingredients, adding a new category to its traditional awards for popular and highly rated establishments.

Three-course menus cost CZK 490 or CZK 790, depending on the restaurant, with reservation fees of CZK 49 or CZK 79, respectively. Some venues offer a fourth course, an amuse-bouche, and are marked as premium on the festival website.

World.title: Prague’s SaSaZu Club to Host Central Europe’s Largest Halloween Party
World.content:
Bloody Sexy Halloween festival, described as Central Europe’s largest Halloween event, will return to Prague’s SaSaZu Club for its 2026 edition.

The two-night celebration will take place on Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31, promising an extensive lineup of shows, performances, and music acts.



Founded in 2009, the event has grown into one of the most attended Halloween parties in the region, regularly attracting more than 4,000 visitors each year. Organizers say this year’s edition will feature immersive decorations, live performances, and sets from both Czech and international DJs.

A traditional highlight of the weekend will be the Bloody Sexy Costume Contest, open to all attendees.

Participants can register at SaSaZu between 9 p.m. and midnight, with costumes judged on creativity, originality, and presentation. The winner, selected by audience applause at midnight, will receive a cash prize of CZK 40,000.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bloody Sexy Halloween (@bloodysexyhalloween)

The event will run across both nights with multiple performances and themed productions throughout the venue.

Tickets for Bloody Sexy Halloween 2025 are priced between CZK 510 and CZK 1,450, depending on the category (Regular, Badass Babes, or VIP).

They are available exclusively via the official website www.bloodysexy.cz

World.title: Magyar proposes surprise drug and alcohol tests for Hungarian MPs – Even Fidesz backs the idea
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar has proposed mandatory, unannounced alcohol and drug tests for MPs, and opposition parties Fidesz and Mi Hazánk have both voiced their support. Fidesz, however, added a pointed remark, saying it hopes the rules will apply to Prime Minister Péter Magyar as well.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar has proposed introducing mandatory, unannounced alcohol and drug tests for members of Hungary’s parliament, and the idea has received support from opposition parties Fidesz and Mi Hazánk.

The Fidesz parliamentary group confirmed its position in a response to Telex on Tuesday, adding: “We hope that the rules will apply to Péter Magyar as well.”

Mi Hazánk also backed the initiative, saying the party had previously supported the use of drug and alcohol testing.

The proposal follows a series of confrontations in parliament involving Fidesz MP János Pócs, whose behaviour Magyar criticised during parliamentary proceedings on Monday.

What prompted Magyar’s proposal?

On Tuesday morning, Magyar shared a video from one of his parliamentary speeches the previous day, in which he commented on Pócs’s conduct in the chamber. The Fidesz MP had reportedly been playing bingo during parliamentary proceedings and later held up a sign reading “nausea” after Magyar’s speech.

In the video, the prime minister called attention to Pócs’s behaviour and asked the Tisza parliamentary group to submit a proposal to amend parliament’s rules and the legislation governing its operation.

Magyar suggested that introducing mandatory, unannounced alcohol and drug tests would help establish whether substance use could explain what he described as Pócs’s increasingly poor condition.

Fidesz and Mi Hazánk back the idea

Fidesz’s support comes with a clear political caveat. While endorsing the initiative, the party stressed that Magyar himself should also be subject to any new requirements. Mi Hazánk, meanwhile, said it supported the proposal because it had already advocated drug and alcohol testing in the past.

If you missed it: Hungary passes new child protection law: Magyar slams Fidesz and Mi Hazánk for voting against it

Magyar has taken drug tests before

The prime minister has undergone drug testing several times during his political career, Telex recalls. In June 2024, Magyar took a drug test and challenged Tamás Deutsch, who was then Fidesz’s leading candidate for the European Parliament elections, as well as members of the government at the time, to do the same.

In March 2026, just weeks before Hungary’s parliamentary election, Magyar underwent another comprehensive drug test at a laboratory in Vienna. The results, published later that month, indicated that he had not consumed drugs in the preceding months.

World.title: Hungarian man attempted to rape a woman out running in Vienna
World.content:
A passer-by intervened after witnessing the attack on a 28-year-old woman, helping her escape. Police arrested the 34-year-old Hungarian suspect just 300 metres from the scene.

A 34-year-old Hungarian man has been arrested in Vienna on suspicion of attempting to rape a woman who was out running on Monday morning. The suspect allegedly grabbed the 28-year-old, dragged her to the ground and attempted to sexually assault her after they both fell down an embankment.

According to Austrian newspaper Kronen Zeitung, the attack took place on Brigittenauer Lände, where a passer-by witnessed the incident and intervened when he realised that the woman was being sexually assaulted.

The witness initially believed he had come across a physical altercation. However, after taking a closer look, he recognised the nature of the attack and stepped in to help the victim.

Passer-by’s intervention helped save the woman

The suspect reportedly released the woman when the passer-by intervened and fled the scene. Police launched an immediate search and arrested the man at around 6.45 am, approximately 300 metres from the location of the alleged attack.

Police spokesperson Markus Dittrich confirmed the circumstances of the incident to Kronen Zeitung.

The suspect is a 34-year-old Hungarian citizen without a permanent registered address. Following his arrest, he was questioned by police but denied committing the offence.

He was subsequently taken into custody at a correctional facility pending further proceedings.

If you missed it: Two young Hungarians rescued from Austria’s highest peak after dangerous night-time ordeal

Victim suffered minor injuries; investigation continues

The 28-year-old woman escaped with relatively minor physical injuries, suffering abrasions during the attack. The psychological impact of the incident remains unclear. The investigation is ongoing, and the suspect’s guilt has not yet been established by a court.

World.title: National Geographic reports on Hungarian discovery
World.content:
According to the Hungarian Ornithological and Nature Conservation Society (Magyar Madártani és Természetvédelmi Egyesület, MME), National Geographic has for the first time featured a Hungarian natural science discovery in its international publications. The research, which began in Hungary, tracked the migration of red-footed falcons using satellite transmitters and led researchers to Angola, where they identified a gathering site for birds of prey on a scale previously unknown to science: FALCOPOLIS, ‘home to one million red-footed falcons’.

National Geographic takes notice of the research

The report published in the September international edition was written by Pulitzer Prize-winning author Ed Yong, with photography by Hungarian photographer Ákos Stiller. The Hungarian-language edition will be published in October, potentially bringing this Hungarian conservation success story to an audience of up to 300 million readers worldwide.

FALCOPOLIS (FALCO = falcon; POLIS = city or city-state) was identified by Hungarian researchers in 2019 in central Angola. It is currently the largest known wintering aggregation of birds of prey in the world. Every March, hundreds of thousands of red-footed falcons – potentially as many as one million – gather here before returning to their breeding grounds in Europe and Central Asia. As a significant proportion of the estimated global population of the species converges on this site each year, the future of the entire species depends on what happens to this area. Following the discovery, a Hungarian-led initiative was launched to prepare for the site’s protection.

A research camp for the next 60 years

The MME team members are directly responsible for carrying out the research activities within the project. The expedition in March 2026 brought together an MME staff member, international volunteers from the FALCOPOLIS Foundation, a representative of the University of Veterinary Medicine Budapest, a film and photography crew, and the local partners Orbis Angola and INBAC.

The year’s most significant milestone was the establishment of a research camp. Orbis Angola and the FALCOPOLIS Foundation secured the right to use one hectare of land for conservation purposes for a period of 60 years. The camp was funded by Hungarian-owned A-M Hungary Kft. Ringing, satellite tagging and environmental education for the local community all take place here.

‘Császár’s’ 34,217-kilometre journey

‘Császár’ (‘Emperor’), a male red-footed falcon fitted with a satellite transmitter near Dinnyés in 2025 as part of the LIFE20 NAT/SK/001077 red-footed falcon conservation project, provided particularly valuable data on migration. Researchers successfully downloaded his GPS data at FALCOPOLIS in 2026 using a ground-based antenna, and the bird subsequently returned to its Hungarian breeding grounds after migration.

The data record a full year’s journey from Hungary to its wintering grounds in southern Africa and back – a total of 34,217 kilometres. In September, ‘Császár’ covered 3,676 kilometres in a single uninterrupted flight over four days, spending approximately 98 hours in continuous flight. When ringed, the bird weighed just 150 grams and was roughly the size of a dove.

National Geographic reports on a Hungarian discovery – MME researchers are playing a key role in the FALCOPOLIS project.

Up to one million birds

The median estimates from three population counts conducted with the help of volunteers were 250,000 birds on 18 March, 475,000 on 21 March and 750,000 on 29 March. Based on the range of estimates, the peak gathering may have reached as many as one million birds.

Poaching on the decline, habitat remains vulnerable

During night patrols in 2026, researchers detected no organised poaching, marking a significant change from previous years, when tens of thousands of red-footed falcons may have ended up on the market. Continued protection is nevertheless essential: the team also documented an individual transporting a bird intended for sale.

The greatest long-term risk is the loss of mature mango and eucalyptus trees used by the falcons as communal roosts. These trees are valuable sources of firewood and charcoal, making them vulnerable to felling. The team has therefore begun compiling an inventory of trees and has also mapped the approximately 5 km² area using a drone. These data could provide the basis for future habitat protection decisions.

National Geographic reports on a Hungarian discovery – MME researchers are playing a key role in the FALCOPOLIS project.

Local communities hold the key to conservation

FALCOPOLIS can only be protected successfully in partnership with local communities. Cooperation with INBAC and the local authorities, school programmes, joint tree-planting initiatives and the conservation commitment made by a local football team called the ‘Falcons’ all aim to establish the red-footed falcon as a natural treasure that local people themselves are committed to protecting.

After their matches, young players from the team speak to spectators about why they no longer hunt the falcons.

The public will also have an opportunity to experience the red-footed falcon conservation project’s immersive 360-degree film at the Tata Wild Goose Festival on 28 November.

World.title: New 120-room hotel coming to Hungary’s second-largest city: opening date revealed!
World.content:
International hotel group IHG Hotels & Resorts is bringing its Holiday Inn Express & Suites brand to Debrecen, with a new 120-room hotel scheduled to open in 2029. The project, developed in partnership with Hungarian property group Xanga, will be the chain’s first hotel in eastern Hungary.

A new internationally branded hotel is planned for Debrecen, Hungary’s second-largest city, as the eastern Hungarian economic hub continues to attract major investments and business travellers.

IHG Hotels & Resorts has signed an agreement with the Debrecen-based Xanga Group to develop a 120-room Holiday Inn Express & Suites hotel. The property is expected to open in 2029 and will strengthen IHG’s presence outside Budapest.

The project forms part of a wider mixed-use development that will include residential apartments, offices and retail units, reflecting the city’s ongoing expansion.

Where will the new Holiday Inn hotel be built?

According to Turizmus.com, the hotel will be located approximately one kilometre from Debrecen city centre, making it accessible to visitors travelling for both business and leisure.

Designed around the hotel brand’s Next Generation concept, the property will feature 100 modern standard guest rooms and 20 suites. Guests will also have access to complimentary hot breakfast, free Wi-Fi and the brand’s Express Café & Bar facilities.

The combination of standard rooms and larger suites is intended to cater to different types of visitors, including business travellers staying in the city for investment-related projects and tourists exploring eastern Hungary.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Why is Debrecen attracting more hotels?

Debrecen has emerged as one of Hungary’s most important industrial and investment destinations in recent years. Major domestic and international investments, infrastructure improvements and expanding air connections have helped increase demand for accommodation.

The city is a key economic centre for eastern Hungary, and its rapid development has created a growing need for modern hotels operated by recognised international brands.

Willemijn Geels, IHG Hotels & Resorts’ vice-president of development for Europe, said the company was pleased to bring Holiday Inn Express & Suites to Debrecen. She described the city as one of Central Europe’s most dynamically developing urban centres and highlighted the hotel as IHG’s first project in eastern Hungary.

Geels added that the agreement reflected the company’s ambition to expand beyond Budapest and meet growing demand for quality international hotel brands in rapidly developing regional cities.

She also welcomed the partnership with Xanga, describing it as the two companies’ first joint project and expressing hope for a long-term, successful collaboration.

If you missed it: Two Budapest hotels named among Europe’s favourites by Condé Nast Traveler readers

IHG expands its Hungarian hotel portfolio

The planned Debrecen property will be IHG’s second hotel development outside Budapest in Hungary. Holiday Inn Express is the company’s fastest-growing brand, and the new hotel will become its 57th European property offering suites alongside standard rooms.

IHG currently has five operating hotels in Hungary, with another three in preparation.

The Debrecen development is part of the group’s wider strategy to expand in regional cities across Hungary and Central and Eastern Europe, where economic growth is creating new opportunities for internationally recognised accommodation providers.

World.title: Budapest residents say they fear walking certain streets: anger over crime grows
World.content:
Residents of Budapest’s inner districts say some streets have become places they avoid even during the day, while others feel unsafe after dark. Protesters are demanding hundreds of additional police officers, permanent patrols and tougher measures against drug dealing and public disorder at a demonstration in Józsefváros on Wednesday.

Residents concerned about rising theft, break-ins and open drug use are taking to the streets in central Budapest on Wednesday, 14 October. The demonstration is scheduled to begin at 5 pm in Horváth Mihály Square, in the city’s eighth district, Józsefváros.

According to Hungarian news outlet Reakció, the organisers believe several public areas in Budapest’s inner districts have effectively become “no-go zones”, where drug dealing, drug consumption and harassment of passers-by are recurring problems.

They claim that many residents no longer feel safe walking alone after dark, while some avoid certain streets even during the day. The protesters argue that these concerns extend beyond Józsefváros and affect several inner districts of the Hungarian capital.

Residents demand action over drugs and street crime

The demonstration brings together local residents, legal experts, community organisers and a district councillor, all of whom are expected to address different aspects of the problem.

Marcell Erős, an IT specialist and one of the petition’s authors, is due to speak about conditions in his own neighbourhood. According to the organisers, he regularly encounters reports of break-ins, drug use and drug dealing, as well as what he considers unsuccessful attempts to resolve the problems through discussions with the authorities.

Criminal lawyer, legal expert and university lecturer Dániel Tran will discuss the legal obstacles that can complicate prompt police intervention and the gathering of evidence. Bella Szűcs-Zágoni, founder of the Safe Újlipótváros Facebook group, will share experiences from community efforts to improve safety in Budapest’s 13th district.

Józsefváros councillor Aram Shakkour is also expected to speak about local public safety concerns, residents’ complaints and the social problems connected to policing and street disorder. The organisers say their aim is not simply to assign blame, but to develop solutions that could improve safety in central Budapest regardless of political affiliation.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Petition calls for at least 500 additional police officers

The protesters intend to submit a petition to the Ministry of the Interior setting out a series of demands. One of their central requests is to increase staffing at police headquarters serving Budapest’s fifth to ninth districts by at least 500 officers. They are also calling for a general pay rise for law enforcement personnel.

The petition demands a permanent police presence at several locations that the organisers consider particularly problematic, including Blaha Lujza Square, Nyugati Square, Oktogon, Rákóczi Square and Pope John Paul II Square.

They also want foot patrols throughout the inner districts, including at night, and tougher police action against people who sell or use illegal drugs in central Budapest.

Another proposal is to prohibit the sale of glass pipes, which can be used to consume certain drugs, including synthetic substances commonly referred to as crystal. The full list of demands includes:
